declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:monoid`.

Informal statement: an additive monoid is a set with an associative binary
operation and a two-sided identity element.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `AddMonoid` is exactly this
structure with the identity named `0`; its inherited fields give
`add_assoc`, `zero_add`, and `add_zero`.  The additional natural-scalar field
in Mathlib is canonically generated by repeated addition and does not
strengthen the thesis definition.
declarations.header: abbrev AdditiveMonoid (X : Type u) := AddMonoid X
declarations.name: AdditiveMonoid

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:abelian-monoid`.

Informal statement: an abelian monoid is an additive monoid whose addition is
commutative.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `AddCommMonoid` extends
`AddMonoid` by the law `add_comm`, matching the single extra axiom displayed
in the thesis.
declarations.header: abbrev AbelianMonoid (X : Type u) := AddCommMonoid X
declarations.name: AbelianMonoid

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:cancellation-property`.

Informal statement: a monoid has the cancellation property when adding the
same element on either the left or the right is injective.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `IsCancelAdd` combines
`IsLeftCancelAdd` and `IsRightCancelAdd`.  Its two cancellation laws are
precisely the two implications written in the thesis; the `AddMonoid`
assumption supplies the ambient monoid structure.
declarations.header: abbrev HasCancellationProperty (X : Type u) [AddMonoid X] := IsCancelAdd X
declarations.name: HasCancellationProperty

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:abelian-group`.

Informal statement: an abelian group is an abelian monoid in which every
element has an additive inverse.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `AddCommGroup` extends an
additive commutative monoid with negation and the inverse law.  Its identity
is `0`, corresponding to the thesis element `e`, and `-g` is the thesis
inverse.
declarations.header: abbrev AbelianGroup (G : Type u) := AddCommGroup G
declarations.name: AbelianGroup

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:abelian-group`.
The inverse is unique already in an abelian monoid when it exists.
declarations.header: theorem additiveInverse_unique {G : Type u} [AddCommMonoid G] {g h k : G} (hh : g + h = 0) (hk : g + k = 0) : h = k :=
declarations.name: additiveInverse_unique

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:real-vector-space`.

Informal statement: a real vector space is an abelian group equipped with a
real scalar action satisfying the identity, distributivity, scalar-addition,
and scalar-associativity laws.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: under the explicitly required
`AddCommGroup V`, Mathlib's `Module ℝ V` packages exactly the four scalar laws
listed in the thesis.  In particular they are available as `one_smul`,
`smul_add`, `add_smul`, and `mul_smul`.
declarations.header: abbrev RealVectorSpace (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] := Module ℝ V
declarations.name: RealVectorSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:vector-space-extension`.

Informal statement: if `V` is a real vector space and `X` is any type, then
the function space `X → V`, with pointwise addition and pointwise scalar
multiplication, is a real vector space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof follows the thesis exactly.
The additive group of `X → V` is Mathlib's pointwise `Pi` group, the scalar
multiplication is defined pointwise, `(a • f) x = a • f x`, and every required
equality (the four thesis axioms and Mathlib's two further `Module` fields) is
checked by evaluating the corresponding equality in `V` at an arbitrary
`x : X`.  The resulting structure is definitionally Mathlib's `Pi` module
instance (`functionSpaceRealVectorSpace_eq_pi`). The current thesis explicitly
includes the empty domain.
declarations.header: def functionSpaceRealVectorSpace (X : Type u) (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] : RealVectorSpace (X → V)
declarations.name: functionSpaceRealVectorSpace

declarations.docComment: The pointwise structure is definitionally Mathlib's `Pi` module instance.
declarations.header: theorem functionSpaceRealVectorSpace_eq_pi (X : Type u) (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] : functionSpaceRealVectorSpace X V = Pi.module X (fun _ => V) ℝ := rfl
declarations.name: functionSpaceRealVectorSpace_eq_pi

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:vector-space-extension`.
The empty-domain function space is exactly the zero vector space.
declarations.header: theorem emptyDomain_function_eq_zero (X : Type u) (V : Type v) [IsEmpty X] [AddCommGroup V] (f : X → V) : f = 0 :=
declarations.name: emptyDomain_function_eq_zero

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:group-completion-scope`.
Transport of formal differences targets the span, with no assertion that
this is the whole ambient vector space. The completed object instead
targets the metric completion of that span.
declarations.header: theorem formal_difference_and_metric_completion_targets {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) : Nonempty (GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ ≃ₗ[ℝ] Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ)) ∧ Nonempty (CompletedGrothendieckVectorization φ hφ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] UniformSpace.Completion (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ))) ∧ CompleteSpace (CompletedGrothendieckVectorization φ hφ) :=
declarations.name: formal_difference_and_metric_completion_targets

declarations.header: theorem encoding_quotient_injective {X : Type u} {V : Type v} (φ : X → V) : Function.Injective (functionKernelExtension φ) :=
declarations.name: encoding_quotient_injective

declarations.docComment:
An isometric embedding into a complete metric space extends to an
isometry from the completion onto exactly the closure of its original range.
declarations.header: theorem completion_extension_range {E F : Type*} [MetricSpace E] [MetricSpace F] [CompleteSpace F] (f : E → F) (hf : Isometry f) : Set.range (UniformSpace.Completion.extension f) = closure (Set.range f) :=
declarations.name: completion_extension_range

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:group-completion-scope`.
The actual map to the closure is the canonical continuous extension of the
kernel encoding isometry. This gives the explicit completion-to-closure
isometry (and surjectivity) missing from the earlier evidence inventory.
declarations.header: def completedKernelEquivImageClosure {X : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X H) (hφ : WeaklyLinearOperator ℝ X H φ) : CompletedKernelSpace φ hφ ≃ᵢ closure (Set.range φ) :=
declarations.name: completedKernelEquivImageClosure

declarations.header: theorem completedKernelEquivImageClosure_coe {X : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X H) (hφ : WeaklyLinearOperator ℝ X H φ) (x : InnerProductKernelSpace φ hφ) : ((completedKernelEquivImageClosure φ hφ (x : CompletedKernelSpace φ hφ)) : H) = innerProductKernelLinearIsometryEquivRange φ hφ x :=
declarations.name: completedKernelEquivImageClosure_coe

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:field`.
declarations.header: abbrev FieldStructure (K : Type u) := Field K
declarations.name: FieldStructure

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:real-vector-space`.
The current definition is over an arbitrary field; real spaces are a
specialization of this general construction.
declarations.header: abbrev VectorSpace (K : Type u) (V : Type v) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] := Module K V
declarations.name: VectorSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:vector-space-extension`.

The source now quantifies over every field and includes the empty domain. The
scalar multiplication is pointwise, `(a • f) x = a • f x`, and each vector-space
axiom (together with Mathlib's two further `Module` fields) is checked by
evaluating the corresponding identity of `V` at every `x : X`; the additive
group of `X → V` is the pointwise `Pi` group.
declarations.header: @[implicit_reducible] def functionSpaceVectorSpace (K : Type u) (X : Type v) (V : Type w) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] : Module K (X → V)
declarations.name: functionSpaceVectorSpace

declarations.docComment: The pointwise structure is definitionally Mathlib's `Pi` module instance.
declarations.header: theorem functionSpaceVectorSpace_eq_pi (K : Type u) (X : Type v) (V : Type w) [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] : functionSpaceVectorSpace K X V = Pi.module X (fun _ ↦ V) K := rfl
declarations.name: functionSpaceVectorSpace_eq_pi

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-relation`.
The simplified relation respects addition of representatives.
declarations.header: theorem completionRelation_add_compatible [IsCancelAdd M] {p q r s : M × M} (hpq : p.1 + q.2 = q.1 + p.2) (hrs : r.1 + s.2 = s.1 + r.2) : (p.1 + r.1) + (q.2 + s.2) = (q.1 + s.1) + (p.2 + r.2) :=
declarations.name: completionRelation_add_compatible

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:grothendieck-group`.
declarations.header: def completionEmbedding : M →+ GroupCompletion M :=
declarations.name: completionEmbedding

declarations.header: theorem completionEmbedding_apply (x : M) : completionEmbedding x = completionPair (x, 0) :=
declarations.name: completionEmbedding_apply

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem completionPair_eq_sub_embedding (x y : M) : completionPair (x, y) = completionEmbedding x - completionEmbedding y :=
declarations.name: completionPair_eq_sub_embedding

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).
Every extending homomorphism has the asserted difference formula: a monoid
homomorphism between abelian groups preserves inverses, and clause (ii) gives
`χ([(x,y)]) = χ(ι(x)) − χ(ι(y)) = ψ(x) − ψ(y)`.
declarations.header: theorem completion_extension_pair_formula {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) (Ψ : GroupCompletion M →+ G) (hΨ : Ψ.comp completionEmbedding = ψ) (x y : M) : Ψ (completionPair (x, y)) = ψ x - ψ y :=
declarations.name: completion_extension_pair_formula

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).
Well-definedness step of `ψ̄([(x,y)]) = ψ(x) − ψ(y)`: from
`ψ(x) + ψ(y′) = ψ(x′) + ψ(y)` it follows that `ψ(x) − ψ(y) = ψ(x′) − ψ(y′)`.
declarations.header: theorem completionLift_well_defined {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) {x y x' y' : M} (h : ψ x + ψ y' = ψ x' + ψ y) : ψ x - ψ y = ψ x' - ψ y' :=
declarations.name: completionLift_well_defined

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).
The underlying function of the thesis extension, `ψ̄([(x,y)]) = ψ(x) − ψ(y)`,
defined on classes. If `(x,y) ∼ (x′,y′)`, that is `x + y′ = x′ + y` (in
Mathlib's quotient up to a common summand `k`, whose image `ψ(k)` cancels in the
group `G`; under cancellation no such `k` is needed), applying `ψ` gives
`ψ(x) + ψ(y′) = ψ(x′) + ψ(y)`, so the value does not depend on the
representative.
declarations.header: def completionLiftFun {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) (g : GroupCompletion M) : G :=
declarations.name: completionLiftFun

declarations.header: theorem completionLiftFun_pair {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) (x y : M) : completionLiftFun ψ (completionPair (x, y)) = ψ x - ψ y := rfl
declarations.name: completionLiftFun_pair

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).
The thesis extension `ψ̄` as a homomorphism: it is additive because `ψ` is
additive, `ψ̄([(x,y)] + [(x′,y′)]) = ψ(x + x′) − ψ(y + y′)
= (ψ(x) − ψ(y)) + (ψ(x′) − ψ(y′))`, and `ψ̄([(e,e)]) = ψ(e) − ψ(e) = 0`.
declarations.header: def completionLift {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) : GroupCompletion M →+ G
declarations.name: completionLift

declarations.header: theorem completionLift_pair {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) (x y : M) : completionLift ψ (completionPair (x, y)) = ψ x - ψ y := rfl
declarations.name: completionLift_pair

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).
The extension restricts to `ψ` along the canonical map:
`ψ̄(ι(x)) = ψ(x) − ψ(e) = ψ(x)`.
declarations.header: theorem completionLift_comp_embedding {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) : (completionLift ψ).comp completionEmbedding = ψ :=
declarations.name: completionLift_comp_embedding

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:grothendieck-universal`, clause (iii).

The universal property, including uniqueness of the extension, along the thesis
route. Existence is the thesis extension `completionLift`,
`ψ̄([(x,y)]) = ψ(x) − ψ(y)`, which restricts to `ψ` along `ι`. Uniqueness: any
`χ` with `χ ∘ ι = ψ` satisfies `χ([(x,y)]) = χ(ι(x)) − χ(ι(y)) = ψ(x) − ψ(y)` by
clause (ii), so `χ = ψ̄` on every class, and every element is a class. Only the
quotient object itself remains Mathlib's `AddLocalization`.
declarations.header: theorem completion_universal {G : Type v} [AddCommGroup G] (ψ : M →+ G) : ∃! Ψ : GroupCompletion M →+ G, Ψ.comp completionEmbedding = ψ :=
declarations.name: completion_universal

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `rem:group-completion-scope`, `defn:grothendieck-group`,
`prop:grothendieck-universal`.
The quotient object `G(X) = (X × X)/∼`, as Mathlib's Grothendieck group: the
actual abelian group of formal differences (clause (i) of the universal-property
proposition). Cancellation is needed for the faithful embedding and the
manuscript's simplified pair relation.
declarations.header: abbrev GroupCompletion (M : Type u) [AddCommMonoid M] :=
declarations.name: GroupCompletion

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:grothendieck-group`.
The class `[(x,y)]` of the pair `(x,y)`, interpreted as a formal difference.
declarations.header: def completionPair (p : M × M) : GroupCompletion M :=
declarations.name: completionPair

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:group-completion-scope`.
Without cancellation the congruence includes an extra common summand.
declarations.header: theorem completionPair_eq_iff_exists (p q : M × M) : completionPair p = completionPair q ↔ ∃ c : M, c + (p.1 + q.2) = c + (q.1 + p.2) :=
declarations.name: completionPair_eq_iff_exists

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:group-completion-scope`.
An idempotent element collapses to zero on introducing formal inverses. Thus
faithfulness cannot be asserted for arbitrary commutative monoids.
declarations.header: theorem completionEmbedding_eq_zero_of_idempotent (x : M) (hx : x + x = x) : completionPair (x, 0) = 0 :=
declarations.name: completionEmbedding_eq_zero_of_idempotent

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `rem:group-completion-scope`, `defn:grothendieck-group`,
`prop:grothendieck-universal`.
The quotient relation is exactly the displayed cross-addition relation `∼`.
declarations.header: theorem completionPair_eq_iff [IsCancelAdd M] (p q : M × M) : completionPair p = completionPair q ↔ p.1 + q.2 = q.1 + p.2 :=
declarations.name: completionPair_eq_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `prop:grothendieck-relation`, `rem:group-completion-scope`.

The thesis proof that the cross-addition relation `∼` is an equivalence.
Reflexivity and symmetry are immediate. For transitivity, add the middle second
component `y′` to `x + y″`, reassociate, substitute the two defining equalities,
reassociate again, and cancel `y′` (this is where cancellation enters).
declarations.header: theorem completionRelation_equivalence [IsCancelAdd M] : Equivalence (fun p q : M × M ↦ p.1 + q.2 = q.1 + p.2) :=
declarations.name: completionRelation_equivalence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:group-completion-scope`.
Every group element has a pair representative.
declarations.header: theorem completionPair_surjective : Function.Surjective (completionPair (M := M)) :=
declarations.name: completionPair_surjective

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `rem:group-completion-scope`, `prop:grothendieck-universal`.
Clause (i): the addition, identity, and inverse are precisely the source's pair
formulas.
declarations.header: theorem completionPair_laws (x y z w : M) : completionPair (x, y) + completionPair (z, w) = completionPair (x + z, y + w) ∧ completionPair ((0 : M), 0) = 0 ∧ -completionPair (x, y) = completionPair (y, x) :=
declarations.name: completionPair_laws

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `rem:group-completion-scope`, `prop:grothendieck-universal`.
Clause (ii): the canonical map `x ↦ [(x,0)]` is additive and injective under
cancellation.
declarations.header: theorem completionEmbedding_faithful [IsCancelAdd M] : Function.Injective (fun x : M ↦ completionPair (x, 0)) ∧ ∀ x y : M, completionPair (x + y, 0) = completionPair (x, 0) + completionPair (y, 0) :=
declarations.name: completionEmbedding_faithful

declarations.docComment:
Separability for the logarithmic-distortion Skorokhod metric, proved using
finite step paths with cuts and values in countable dense sets.
declarations.header: theorem skorokhodDistance_separable {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) : IsSeparableFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) :=
declarations.name: skorokhodDistance_separable

declarations.docComment:
Compatibility theorem for the former combined external obligation.
Both completeness and separability are now proved internally.
declarations.header: theorem skorokhodDistance_complete_separable {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) : IsCompleteFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) ∧ IsSeparableFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) :=
declarations.name: skorokhodDistance_complete_separable

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:skorokhod-metric`.
The metric, finiteness, completeness, and separability clauses are all proved
internally for the thesis's exact logarithmic-distortion formula.
declarations.header: theorem skorokhodDistance_metric_complete_separable {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) : IsExtendedMetric (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) ∧ (∀ f g, @skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side f g ≠ ∞) ∧ IsCompleteFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) ∧ IsSeparableFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) :=
declarations.name: skorokhodDistance_metric_complete_separable

declarations.docComment:
Uniformly small time changes and vanishing aligned path error imply
convergence for logarithmic distortion. The proof uses finite oscillation
cuts and Lipschitz interpolation, with no project-specific axiom.
declarations.header: theorem skorokhodConvergence_of_timeChanges {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) (fseq : ℕ → RegularPath a b X side) (f : RegularPath a b X side) (timeChanges : ℕ → IncreasingIntervalBijection a b) (hshift : Tendsto (fun n => timeShiftNorm (timeChanges n)) atTop (𝓝 0)) (herror : Tendsto (fun n => alignedPathError (fseq n) f (timeChanges n)) atTop (𝓝 0)) : ConvergesFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) fseq f :=
declarations.name: skorokhodConvergence_of_timeChanges

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:504:prop:39`.
Both implications are proved internally, using the thesis's exact logarithmic
distortion formula and its uniform-displacement convergence criterion.
declarations.header: theorem skorokhodConvergence_iff_timeChanges {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) (fseq : ℕ → RegularPath a b X side) (f : RegularPath a b X side) : ConvergesFor (@skorokhodEDistance a b X _ side) fseq f ↔ ∃ timeChanges : ℕ → IncreasingIntervalBijection a b, Tendsto (fun n => timeShiftNorm (timeChanges n)) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun n => alignedPathError (fseq n) f (timeChanges n)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: skorokhodConvergence_iff_timeChanges

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:9:defn:1`

Informal statement: a topology is a family of subsets containing the empty
and whole sets and closed under finite intersections and arbitrary unions.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `TopologicalSpace` structure
packages exactly these closure laws for typed sets.
declarations.header: abbrev ThesisTopology (X : Type u) := TopologicalSpace X
declarations.name: ThesisTopology

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:20:defn:2`

Informal statement: a topological base covers every point and refines the
intersection of any two basic neighborhoods at each point of that intersection.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the two thesis clauses are stored
directly, before any ambient topology has been chosen.  This distinction is
important for the later proposition that constructs a topology from the base.
declarations.header: structure IsTopologicalBase {X : Type u} (B : Set (Set X)) : Prop
declarations.name: IsTopologicalBase

declarations.docComment: The product family appearing in the manuscript.
declarations.header: def productBase {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (BX : Set (Set X)) (BY : Set (Set Y)) : Set (Set (X × Y)) :=
declarations.name: productBase

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:29:prop:3`

Informal statement: Cartesian products of members of bases on `X` and `Y`
form a topological base on `X × Y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof coordinate by
coordinate, carried out directly on the two pre-topological base clauses: for
covering, choose one basic neighbourhood in each coordinate and take their
product; for refinement, refine the intersection in each coordinate with the
given bases and take the product of the two refining sets.  No Mathlib
product-basis theorem is used.
declarations.header: theorem productBase_isTopologicalBase {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} {BX : Set (Set X)} {BY : Set (Set Y)} (hX : IsTopologicalBase BX) (hY : IsTopologicalBase BY) : IsTopologicalBase (productBase BX BY) :=
declarations.name: productBase_isTopologicalBase

declarations.docComment: The topology generated by a pre-topological basis.
declarations.header: def topologyGeneratedByBase {X : Type u} (B : Set (Set X)) : TopologicalSpace X :=
declarations.name: topologyGeneratedByBase

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:topology-base`.

Informal statement: the topology associated with a base consists of unions of
basic sets, equivalently it is the topology generated by that base.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: install `generateFrom B`, then build
Mathlib's topology-relative basis certificate from the two pre-topological
clauses proved above.  Its `open_iff_eq_sUnion` theorem gives exactly the
manuscript's explicit union representation, without assuming the conclusion.
declarations.header: theorem topologyGeneratedByBase_open_iff {X : Type u} {B : Set (Set X)} (hB : IsTopologicalBase B) : letI := topologyGeneratedByBase B
declarations.name: topologyGeneratedByBase_open_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:64:defn:5`

Informal statement: a map is continuous when the preimage of every open set
in the codomain is open in the domain.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the displayed open-preimage condition
is stated directly; Mathlib's `continuous_def` identifies it with `Continuous`.
declarations.header: def IsContinuousByOpenPreimages {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] (f : X → Y) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsContinuousByOpenPreimages

declarations.header: theorem isContinuousByOpenPreimages_iff {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : X → Y} : IsContinuousByOpenPreimages f ↔ Continuous f :=
declarations.name: isContinuousByOpenPreimages_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:Hausdorff`.

Informal statement: a space is Hausdorff when distinct points admit disjoint
open neighborhoods.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `T2Space` is precisely the
Hausdorff separation property used by the thesis.
declarations.header: abbrev HausdorffSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] := T2Space X
declarations.name: HausdorffSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:second-countable`.

Informal statement: a space is second-countable when its topology has a
countable base.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `SecondCountableTopology` is Mathlib's
propositional mixin asserting the existence of such a countable basis.
declarations.header: abbrev IsSecondCountable (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :=
declarations.name: IsSecondCountable

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:96:defn:8`

Informal statement: the subspace topology on `Y ⊆ X` consists of intersections
of `Y` with open subsets of `X`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the topology induced by the subtype
inclusion is Mathlib's subspace topology; preimages under that inclusion are
exactly the intersections displayed in the thesis.
declarations.header: def subspaceTopology {X : Type u} [t : TopologicalSpace X] (Y : Set X) : TopologicalSpace Y :=
declarations.name: subspaceTopology

declarations.docComment: An open cover in the exact set-family formulation used in the thesis.
declarations.header: def IsOpenCover {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (U : Set (Set X)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsOpenCover

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:104:defn:9`

Informal statement: an open cover is a family of open sets whose union is the
whole space, and a subcover is a subfamily that still covers.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `IsOpenCover` records openness and the
union equation, while this predicate adds the two subcover requirements
verbatim.
declarations.header: def IsOpenSubcover {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (V U : Set (Set X)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsOpenSubcover

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:113:defn:10`

Informal statement: a subset is compact when every open cover in its subspace
topology has a finite subcover.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `IsCompact` is the standard
cover/filter-equivalent notion for subsets and specializes to the thesis
definition on the subtype.
declarations.header: abbrev IsCompactSet {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] := @IsCompact X _
declarations.name: IsCompactSet

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:metric`.

Informal statement: an extended metric is an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued distance that
vanishes exactly on equal points, is symmetric, and satisfies the triangle
inequality.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this predicate spells out the thesis's
three numbered axioms without imposing Mathlib's finiteness convention for
ordinary `MetricSpace` distances.
declarations.header: def IsExtendedMetric {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsExtendedMetric

declarations.docComment: The bounded truncation from the extended-metric convention.
declarations.header: def truncatedEDistance {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ℝ≥0∞) (x y : X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: truncatedEDistance

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:extended-metric-convention`

Informal statement: truncating an extended metric by `1` is again a metric and
leaves every ball of radius at most `1` unchanged, so all local metric notions
are unchanged.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the equality of small balls is the local
calculation used in the manuscript's argument for equal topology, convergence,
Cauchy sequences, completeness, and separability.  The metric axioms for the
truncation are verified explicitly as well.
declarations.header: theorem truncatedEDistance_properties {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ℝ≥0∞) (hd : IsExtendedMetric d) : IsExtendedMetric (truncatedEDistance d) ∧ ∀ x : X, ∀ {ε : ℝ≥0∞}, ε ≤ 1 → {y | truncatedEDistance d x y < ε} = {y | d x y < ε} :=
declarations.name: truncatedEDistance_properties

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:pseudometric`.

Informal statement: an extended pseudometric is symmetric, satisfies the
triangle inequality, and has zero self-distance, but need not separate points.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the three clauses are recorded directly
for an `ℝ≥0∞`-valued function, preserving the thesis's extended convention.
declarations.header: def IsExtendedPseudometric {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsExtendedPseudometric

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `cor:pseudometric-metric-relation`.

Informal statement: every metric is a pseudometric, and a pseudometric is a
metric exactly when zero distance forces equality.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: unfolding the two preceding predicates
reduces the first part to the metric zero axiom at `(x,x)` and the second part
to adjoining the missing separation clause.
declarations.header: theorem extendedMetric_pseudometric_relation {X : Type u} {d ρ : X → X → ℝ≥0∞} (hd : IsExtendedMetric d) (hρ : IsExtendedPseudometric ρ) : IsExtendedPseudometric d ∧ (IsExtendedMetric ρ ↔ ∀ x y, ρ x y = 0 → x = y) :=
declarations.name: extendedMetric_pseudometric_relation

declarations.docComment: The family of all positive-radius extended-metric balls.
declarations.header: def metricBallFamily (X : Type u) [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : Set (Set X) :=
declarations.name: metricBallFamily

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:topology-extended-pseudometric` (refinement step).

The manuscript's explicit radius: for `x ∈ B(c,ε) ∩ B(c′,δ)` the half-minimum
slack `r = ½ min{ε − d(c,x), δ − d(c′,x)}` is strictly positive, and the
triangle inequality `d(c,y) ≤ d(c,x) + d(x,y) < d(c,x) + r ≤ ε` (and likewise
for `c′`) puts `B(x,r)` inside both balls.  Extended radii are harmless because
both centre distances are finite.
declarations.header: theorem half_slack_refinement {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (c d x : X) (ε δ : ℝ≥0∞) (hx : x ∈ Metric.eball c ε ∩ Metric.eball d δ) : let r := min (ε - edist c x) (δ - edist d x) / 2
declarations.name: half_slack_refinement

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:topology-extended-pseudometric`.

Informal statement: positive-radius balls of a pseudometric form a topological
base for the topology induced by that pseudometric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the manuscript proof.  Covering:
`d(x,x) = 0 < 1` puts `x` in `B(x,1)`.  Refinement: for
`x ∈ B(c,ε) ∩ B(c′,δ)`, the half-minimum slack radius of
`half_slack_refinement` yields a ball `B(x,r)` of the family inside the
intersection, by the triangle inequality.  No Mathlib neighbourhood basis or
topology-relative basis certificate is used.
declarations.header: theorem metricBalls_isTopologicalBase (X : Type u) [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : IsTopologicalBase (metricBallFamily X) :=
declarations.name: metricBalls_isTopologicalBase

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:distance-to-set`.

Informal statement: the extended distance from `x` to `B` is the infimum of
the distances from `x` to points of `B`, with distance to the empty set equal
to infinity.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is Mathlib's `Metric.infEDist`, whose
definition is the required infimum and whose theorem `infEDist_empty` supplies
the empty-set convention.
declarations.header: def distanceToSet {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (x : X) (B : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: distanceToSet

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:232:defn:17`

Informal statement: Hausdorff distance is the maximum of the two directed
supremum distances between subsets, with the stated empty-set conventions.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `Metric.hausdorffEDist` uses
`infEDist` and the same two directed suprema, including the manuscript's
extended-valued empty-set behavior.
declarations.header: def hausdorffDistance {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (A B : Set X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: hausdorffDistance

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:hausdorff-distance`.

Informal statement: Hausdorff distance is an extended pseudometric on the
power set of a metric space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib proves self-distance, symmetry,
and the Hausdorff triangle inequality and packages them in
`PseudoEMetricSpace.hausdorff`; returning that structure verifies all three
axioms at once.
declarations.header: def powerSetHausdorffPseudoEMetricSpace (X : Type u) [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : PseudoEMetricSpace (Set X) :=
declarations.name: powerSetHausdorffPseudoEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:255:prop:19` (separation step).

Two balls of radius `ε = ½ min{d(x,y), 1}` around points at positive distance
are disjoint: a common point `z` would give
`d(x,y) ≤ d(x,z) + d(z,y) < 2ε = min{d(x,y),1} ≤ d(x,y)`, exactly as in the
manuscript.
declarations.header: theorem half_distance_balls_disjoint {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (x y : X) (hxy : 0 < edist x y) : let r := min (edist x y) 1 / 2
declarations.name: half_distance_balls_disjoint

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:255:prop:19`

Informal statement: the topology of a pseudometric is Hausdorff exactly when
zero distance separates points.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: both directions follow the manuscript.
If zero distance separates points, two distinct points have positive distance
and the disjoint half-distance balls of `half_distance_balls_disjoint` are the
required open neighbourhoods.  Conversely, if the space is Hausdorff but
`d(x,y) = 0` with `x ≠ y`, pick disjoint open neighbourhoods `U ∋ x`, `V ∋ y`;
the centred-ball characterisation of open sets gives a ball `B(x,ε) ⊆ U`, and
`d(x,y) = 0 < ε` puts `y` in `U`, contradicting disjointness.
declarations.header: theorem pseudoEMetricTopology_hausdorff_iff {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : Nonempty (T2Space X) ↔ ∀ x y : X, edist x y = 0 → x = y :=
declarations.name: pseudoEMetricTopology_hausdorff_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:Cauchy-sequence`.

Informal statement: a sequence is Cauchy when all sufficiently late pairs of
terms are arbitrarily close.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's filter definition `CauchySeq`
is equivalent to the displayed epsilon-tail condition in a metric space.
declarations.header: abbrev IsCauchySequence {X : Type u} [UniformSpace X] (x : ℕ → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCauchySequence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:convergent-sequence`.

Informal statement: a sequence converges when it tends to some point of the
space; that point is its limit.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Tendsto x atTop (𝓝 limit)` is Mathlib's
filter form of the manuscript's epsilon-and-eventual-tail quantifiers.
declarations.header: def IsConvergentSequence {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (x : ℕ → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsConvergentSequence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:complete-space`.

Informal statement: a metric space is complete when every Cauchy sequence has
a limit in the space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `CompleteSpace` is the
uniform-space version of this condition and is equivalent to sequential
completeness for metric spaces.
declarations.header: abbrev IsCompleteMetricSpace (X : Type u) [UniformSpace X] := CompleteSpace X
declarations.name: IsCompleteMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:separable`.

Informal statement: a metric space is separable when it has a countable dense
subset.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `SeparableSpace` is exactly the
existence of a countable dense set; metric density unfolds to the displayed
epsilon approximation property.
declarations.header: abbrev IsSeparableMetricSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] :=
declarations.name: IsSeparableMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:327:defn:25`

Informal statement: a Polish space has a compatible complete separable metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `PolishSpace` combines second
countability with complete metrizability, an equivalent topological
formulation of the thesis definition.
declarations.header: abbrev IsPolishSpace (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] := PolishSpace X
declarations.name: IsPolishSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:376:defn:32`

Informal statement: a map between metric spaces is continuous when every
epsilon at every base point admits a delta controlling the image distance.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the predicate transcribes the displayed
epsilon-delta formula literally; Mathlib's metric continuity lemmas identify
it with topological `Continuous`.
declarations.header: def EpsilonDeltaContinuous {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} [PseudoMetricSpace X] [PseudoMetricSpace Y] (f : X → Y) : Prop :=
declarations.name: EpsilonDeltaContinuous

declarations.docComment: The compact real interval used as the path domain.
declarations.header: abbrev ClosedInterval (a b : ℝ) := Set.Icc a b
declarations.name: ClosedInterval

declarations.docComment: A rational window `[s, s′]` together with the index of its centre.
declarations.header: abbrev Window := ℚ × ℚ × ℕ
declarations.name: Window

declarations.docComment: The times of `[a,b]` lying in the rational window.
declarations.header: def region {a b : ℝ} (w : Window) : Set (ClosedInterval a b) :=
declarations.name: region

declarations.docComment: A finite window family covers `[a,b]`.
declarations.header: def Covers {a b : ℝ} (s : Finset Window) : Prop :=
declarations.name: Covers

declarations.docComment:
The constraint cell: the windows cover `[a,b]`, and on every window the
path stays within the rational radius `i.2` of the window's centre.
declarations.header: def constraint {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] (d : ℕ → X) (i : Finset Window × ℚ) : Set C(ClosedInterval a b, X) :=
declarations.name: constraint

declarations.docComment:
The manuscript's approximation step: uniform continuity of `f` on the
compact interval gives a finite cover by rational windows on each of which `f`
stays within `2ε` of a centre `d n`; with a rational radius `q ∈ (2ε, 3ε)`, `f`
lies in the resulting cell, and every member `g` of that cell satisfies
`d(f(t), g(t)) ≤ d(f(t), y_k) + d(y_k, g(t)) < 5ε` on every window, hence
`d_∞(f,g) < 6ε`.
declarations.header: theorem exists_constraint {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] (d : ℕ → X) (hd : DenseRange d) (f : C(ClosedInterval a b, X)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : ∃ i : Finset Window × ℚ, f ∈ constraint d i ∧ ∀ g ∈ constraint d i, dist f g < ε :=
declarations.name: exists_constraint

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:spc-continuous`.

Informal statement: continuous maps from `[a,b]` to a metric space carry the
supremum metric `d_∞(f,g) = sup_t d(f(t),g(t))`; if the target is complete and
separable, so is this path space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the first conjunct records the
manuscript's supremum formula for the distance on `C([a,b];X)`
(`ContinuousMap.dist_eq_iSup`, Mathlib's sup metric on continuous maps from a
compact domain).  Completeness is Mathlib's uniform-limit theorem for
continuous maps on a compact domain.  Separability follows the manuscript's
rational-window construction in `ContinuousPathSeparability`: one path is
chosen from each nonempty cell of covering rational windows, dense-sequence
centres and rational radius; the cells are countable, and
`ContinuousPathSeparability.exists_constraint` places every `f` in a cell all
of whose members are uniformly within `ε` of `f`.  (An empty target makes the
path space a subsingleton, which is trivially separable.)
declarations.header: theorem continuousPathSpace_metric_complete_separable (a b : ℝ) (X : Type u) [MetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : (∀ f g : C(ClosedInterval a b, X), dist f g = ⨆ t, dist (f t) (g t)) ∧ Nonempty (CompleteSpace C(ClosedInterval a b, X)) ∧ Nonempty (TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace C(ClosedInterval a b, X)) :=
declarations.name: continuousPathSpace_metric_complete_separable

declarations.docComment: The graph of a continuous path.
declarations.header: def continuousGraph {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (f : C(ClosedInterval a b, X)) : Set (ClosedInterval a b × X) :=
declarations.name: continuousGraph

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:408:prop:34`

Informal statement: the graph of a continuous map on a closed bounded interval
is compact, hence closed and bounded in the product metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this follows the thesis proof verbatim:
`t ↦ (t,f t)` is continuous, the interval subtype is compact, and its range is
therefore compact.  Mathlib then derives closedness and metric boundedness.
declarations.header: theorem continuousGraph_compact_closed_bounded {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] (f : C(ClosedInterval a b, X)) : IsCompact (continuousGraph f) ∧ IsClosed (continuousGraph f) ∧ Bornology.IsBounded (continuousGraph f) :=
declarations.name: continuousGraph_compact_closed_bounded

declarations.docComment: Right continuity on a closed interval, in the one-sided epsilon form.
declarations.header: def IsRightContinuousOnIcc {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsRightContinuousOnIcc

declarations.docComment: Left continuity on a closed interval, in the one-sided epsilon form.
declarations.header: def IsLeftContinuousOnIcc {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsLeftContinuousOnIcc

declarations.docComment: Existence of right limits at all nonterminal times.
declarations.header: def HasRightLimitsOnIcc {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: HasRightLimitsOnIcc

declarations.docComment: Existence of left limits at all noninitial times.
declarations.header: def HasLeftLimitsOnIcc {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: HasLeftLimitsOnIcc

declarations.docComment: The two one-sided path orientations used below.
declarations.header: inductive PathOrientation | cadlag | caglad deriving DecidableEq /-- Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35` Informal statement: càdlàg paths are right-continuous with left limits, while càglàd paths are left-continuous with right limits, with all four one-sided conditions interpreted on `[a,b]` as displayed in the thesis. Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the four auxiliary predicates above are literal epsilon-delta transcriptions. This definition combines the correct two predicates for each orientation and therefore also makes endpoint clauses explicit. -/ def IsOneSidedRegularPath {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (side : PathOrientation) (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: PathOrientation

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`

Informal statement: càdlàg paths are right-continuous with left limits, while
càglàd paths are left-continuous with right limits, with all four one-sided
conditions interpreted on `[a,b]` as displayed in the thesis.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the four auxiliary predicates above are
literal epsilon-delta transcriptions.  This definition combines the correct
two predicates for each orientation and therefore also makes endpoint clauses
explicit.
declarations.header: def IsOneSidedRegularPath {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] {a b : ℝ} (side : PathOrientation) (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsOneSidedRegularPath

declarations.docComment: The subtype of càdlàg or càglàd paths.
declarations.header: abbrev RegularPath (a b : ℝ) (X : Type u) [PseudoMetricSpace X] (side : PathOrientation) :=
declarations.name: RegularPath

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:478:defn:37`

Informal statement: `Λ([a,b])` consists of strictly increasing bijections of
the interval to itself; their logarithmic distortion is the supremum of the
logarithm of all secant-slope ratios.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: strict monotonicity and bijectivity are
stored as fields.  The companion `timeDistortion` definition immediately below
is the exact supremum formula from the formal block.
declarations.header: structure IncreasingIntervalBijection (a b : ℝ)
declarations.name: IncreasingIntervalBijection

declarations.docComment: The secant-slope ratio of an interval time change.
declarations.header: def timeChangeSecantSlope {a b : ℝ} (timeChange : IncreasingIntervalBijection a b) (s t : ClosedInterval a b) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: timeChangeSecantSlope

declarations.docComment: The logarithmic time distortion `‖λ‖∘`, allowing the value `∞`.
declarations.header: def timeDistortion {a b : ℝ} (timeChange : IncreasingIntervalBijection a b) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: timeDistortion

declarations.docComment: Extended supremum distance between two interval paths.
declarations.header: def supPathEDistance {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (f g : ClosedInterval a b → X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: supPathEDistance

declarations.docComment: The Skorokhod infimum formula from the thesis.
declarations.header: def skorokhodEDistance {a b : ℝ} {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] {side : PathOrientation} (f g : RegularPath a b X side) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: skorokhodEDistance

declarations.docComment: Cauchy sequences for an explicit extended-valued distance.
declarations.header: def IsCauchyFor {Z : Type u} (d : Z → Z → ℝ≥0∞) (x : ℕ → Z) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCauchyFor

declarations.docComment: Completeness for an explicit extended-valued distance.
declarations.header: def IsCompleteFor {Z : Type u} (d : Z → Z → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCompleteFor

declarations.docComment: Separability for an explicit extended-valued distance.
declarations.header: def IsSeparableFor {Z : Type u} (d : Z → Z → ℝ≥0∞) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsSeparableFor

declarations.docComment: Convergence for an explicit distance.
declarations.header: def ConvergesFor {Z : Type u} (d : Z → Z → ℝ≥0∞) (x : ℕ → Z) (limit : Z) : Prop :=
declarations.name: ConvergesFor

declarations.header: def timeShiftNorm {a b : ℝ} (timeChange : IncreasingIntervalBijection a b) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: timeShiftNorm

declarations.docComment: Uniform state-space error after applying a time change.

declarations.header: private def rawTruncatedEMetricSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : EMetricSpace X
declarations.name: rawTruncatedEMetricSpace

declarations.header: private theorem truncation_uniformity (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : (inferInstance : UniformSpace X).uniformity = (rawTruncatedEMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace.uniformity :=
declarations.name: truncation_uniformity

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:extended-metric-convention`.
The bounded metric `min(edist,1)` retains exactly the original uniformity and
topology. Consequently Cauchy filters, limits, continuity, and Borel sets are
unchanged, including when the original distance can be infinite.
declarations.header: def truncatedMetricSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : MetricSpace X :=
declarations.name: truncatedMetricSpace

declarations.header: theorem truncated_edist (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] (x y : X) : @edist X (truncatedMetricSpace X).toEDist x y = min (edist x y) 1 := rfl
declarations.name: truncated_edist

declarations.docComment: Original label: `rem:extended-metric-convention`.
declarations.header: theorem truncated_complete (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] : @CompleteSpace X (truncatedMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace := inferInstance
declarations.name: truncated_complete

declarations.docComment: Original label: `rem:extended-metric-convention`.
declarations.header: theorem truncated_separable (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X (truncatedMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace := inferInstance
declarations.name: truncated_separable

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `prop:spc-continuous` (not the mapped proof): the
separability clause as an instance, for a nonempty separable metric target and
without a completeness hypothesis.  One selected continuous path per nonempty
countable rational-constraint cell of `Analysis.ContinuousPathSeparability`
forms the dense set; no compact-open second-countability theorem is used.  The
mapped proof is `Analysis.continuousPathSpace_metric_complete_separable`.
declarations.header: theorem continuousPath_separable_source (a b : ℝ) (X : Type*) [MetricSpace X] [Nonempty X] [SeparableSpace X] : SeparableSpace C(Icc a b, X) :=
declarations.name: continuousPath_separable_source

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `prop:spc-continuous` (not the mapped proof):
separability in the extended-distance scope.  Separability is topological; the
capped compatible metric retains the original topology and lets the same
rational-constraint construction apply.  The mapped statement
`Analysis.continuousPathSpace_extended_complete_separable` obtains this clause
from Mathlib's instance instead.
declarations.header: theorem continuousPath_extended_separable_source (a b : ℝ) (X : Type*) [d : EMetricSpace X] [Nonempty X] [SeparableSpace X] : letI := continuousPathSpaceEMetricSpace a b X
declarations.name: continuousPath_extended_separable_source

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:g-delta`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsGDelta {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (s : Set X) : Prop := IsGδ s
declarations.name: IsGDelta

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:g-delta`.
Natural indexing starts at zero in Lean, a harmless reindexing of the
positive-natural sequence in the source.
declarations.header: theorem isGDelta_iff {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] (s : Set X) : IsGDelta s ↔ ∃ U : ℕ → Set X, (∀ n, IsOpen (U n)) ∧ s = ⋂ n, U n :=
declarations.name: isGDelta_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
In a pseudometric topology, topological inseparability is precisely zero
distance, so the standard separation quotient is the exact stated quotient.
declarations.header: abbrev ZeroDistanceQuotient (X : Type u) [PseudoEMetricSpace X] := SeparationQuotient X
declarations.name: ZeroDistanceQuotient

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistance_equivalence {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : Equivalence (fun x y : X => edist x y = 0) :=
declarations.name: zeroDistance_equivalence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
Well-definedness of the quotient distance, by the manuscript's four-term
triangle inequality: if `x ∼ y` and `x* ∼ y*`, then
`d(x,x*) ≤ d(x,y) + d(y,y*) + d(y*,x*) = d(y,y*)`, and exchanging the two
representative pairs gives the reverse inequality.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistance_edist_congr {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] {x y x' y' : X} (hxy : edist x y = 0) (hxy' : edist x' y' = 0) : edist x x' = edist y y' :=
declarations.name: zeroDistance_edist_congr

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
The quotient distance `d∼([x],[x*]) = d(x,x*)`, defined through representatives;
`zeroDistance_edist_congr` is the independence of the representatives
(inseparability in a pseudometric space is zero distance).
declarations.header: def zeroDistanceQuotientEDist {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : ZeroDistanceQuotient X → ZeroDistanceQuotient X → ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: zeroDistanceQuotientEDist

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
The displayed formula `d∼([x],[x*]) = d(x,x*)`.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistanceQuotientEDist_mk {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (x y : X) : zeroDistanceQuotientEDist (SeparationQuotient.mk x) (SeparationQuotient.mk y) = edist x y := rfl
declarations.name: zeroDistanceQuotientEDist_mk

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
Mathlib's separation-quotient distance is the same quotient distance.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistanceQuotient_edist {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (x y : X) : edist (SeparationQuotient.mk x) (SeparationQuotient.mk y) = edist x y := rfl
declarations.name: zeroDistanceQuotient_edist

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistanceQuotient_mk_eq_iff {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (x y : X) : SeparationQuotient.mk x = SeparationQuotient.mk y ↔ edist x y = 0 :=
declarations.name: zeroDistanceQuotient_mk_eq_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pseudometric-quotient`.
The quotient distance is an extended metric on `X_∼`: symmetry and the triangle
inequality descend directly from `d` through representatives, and
`d∼([x],[x*]) = 0` means `d(x,x*) = 0`, i.e. `x ∼ x*`, i.e. `[x] = [x*]`.
declarations.header: theorem zeroDistanceQuotient_metric (X : Type u) [PseudoEMetricSpace X] : Analysis.IsExtendedMetric (zeroDistanceQuotientEDist (X := X)) :=
declarations.name: zeroDistanceQuotient_metric

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The manuscript's maximum metric `(x, x′) ↦ max_i d_i(x(i), x′(i))` on a finite
product, written as the finite supremum of the coordinate distances (the empty
product has distance zero).
declarations.header: def maximumEDist {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] (x y : (i : I) → X i) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: maximumEDist

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The indexed supremum over a finite set is its maximum. The empty product
has distance zero, consistent with the source's later empty-product use.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_edist {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] (x y : (i : I) → X i) : edist x y = Finset.univ.sup (fun i => edist (x i) (y i)) := edist_pi_def x y
declarations.name: finite_maximum_edist

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
Mathlib's product distance is the maximum metric.
declarations.header: theorem maximumEDist_eq_edist {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] (x y : (i : I) → X i) : maximumEDist x y = edist x y := (finite_maximum_edist x y).symm
declarations.name: maximumEDist_eq_edist

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The maximum metric is a pseudometric: it vanishes on the diagonal and is
symmetric because every `d_i` is, and the triangle inequality holds in each
coordinate and therefore for the maximum.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_pseudometric {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (X : I → Type v) [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] : Analysis.IsExtendedPseudometric (maximumEDist (X := X)) :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_pseudometric

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
If every `d_i` is a metric, vanishing of the maximum forces equality in every
coordinate, so the maximum metric is a metric.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_metric {I : Type u} [Fintype I] (X : I → Type v) [∀ i, EMetricSpace (X i)] : Analysis.IsExtendedMetric (maximumEDist (X := X)) :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_metric

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The ball of radius `ε` around `x` for the maximum metric is the product
`∏ B^{d_i}_ε(x(i))` of the coordinate balls.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_ball {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] (x : (i : I) → X i) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : 0 < ε) : {y | maximumEDist x y < ε} = Set.univ.pi fun i => {z | edist (x i) z < ε} :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_ball

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The maximum metric induces the product topology, via the centred-ball
characterisation of open sets: a maximum ball is a product of coordinate balls,
hence open in the product topology; conversely a basic product open set
`∏ O_i ∋ x` contains the maximum ball of radius `min_i ε_i` as soon as
`B^{d_i}_{ε_i}(x(i)) ⊆ O_i` for every `i`.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_isOpen_iff {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {X : I → Type v} [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] (s : Set ((i : I) → X i)) : (∀ x ∈ s, ∃ ε > 0, {y | maximumEDist x y < ε} ⊆ s) ↔ IsOpen s :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_isOpen_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
The product extended-metric instance retains the coordinate product
topology, rather than introducing a merely equivalent unrelated topology.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_product_topology {I : Type u} [Finite I] (X : I → Type v) [∀ i, PseudoEMetricSpace (X i)] : (inferInstance : TopologicalSpace ((i : I) → X i)) = Pi.topologicalSpace := rfl
declarations.name: finite_maximum_product_topology

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
Completeness by coordinates: a Cauchy sequence for the maximum metric is Cauchy
in every coordinate because `d_i ≤ d_max`; if every factor is complete, the
coordinate limits form a point `x` of the product, and convergence in every
coordinate gives `d_max(x_m, x) < ε` for all large `m`.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_complete {I : Type u} [Finite I] (X : I → Type v) [∀ i, EMetricSpace (X i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (X i)] : CompleteSpace ((i : I) → X i) :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_complete

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-metric-products`.
Separability by coordinates: if `D_i ⊆ X_i` is countable and dense for every
`i`, then `∏ D_i` is countable, and it is dense because choosing `y_i ∈ D_i`
with `d_i(x(i), y_i) < ε` for every `i` gives `d_max(x, y) < ε`.
declarations.header: theorem finite_maximum_separable {I : Type u} [Finite I] (X : I → Type v) [∀ i, EMetricSpace (X i)] [∀ i, TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (X i)] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace ((i : I) → X i) :=
declarations.name: finite_maximum_separable

declarations.header: theorem smallError_truncated_iff {I : Type v} {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (P : ℝ → I → Prop) (f g : I → X) : (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ i, P δ i → @dist X (BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X).toDist (f i) (g i) < ε) ↔ (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ i, P δ i → edist (f i) (g i) < ENNReal.ofReal ε) :=

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`.
The same one-sided paths, represented using a bounded metric with the

declarations.docComment: Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`.
declarations.header: theorem extended_rightContinuous_iff (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : @IsRightContinuousOnIcc X (BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X).toPseudoMetricSpace a b f ↔ ∀ t₀ : ClosedInterval a b, (t₀ : ℝ) < b → ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ t : ClosedInterval a b, (t₀ : ℝ) < t → (t : ℝ) < min ((t₀ : ℝ) + δ) b → edist (f t) (f t₀) < ENNReal.ofReal ε :=
declarations.name: extended_rightContinuous_iff

declarations.docComment: Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`.
declarations.header: theorem extended_leftContinuous_iff (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : @IsLeftContinuousOnIcc X (BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X).toPseudoMetricSpace a b f ↔ ∀ t₀ : ClosedInterval a b, a < (t₀ : ℝ) → ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ t : ClosedInterval a b, max a ((t₀ : ℝ) - δ) < t → (t : ℝ) < t₀ → edist (f t) (f t₀) < ENNReal.ofReal ε :=
declarations.name: extended_leftContinuous_iff

declarations.docComment: Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`.
declarations.header: theorem extended_rightLimits_iff (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : @HasRightLimitsOnIcc X (BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X).toPseudoMetricSpace a b f ↔ ∀ t₀ : ClosedInterval a b, (t₀ : ℝ) < b → ∃ R : X, ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ t : ClosedInterval a b, (t₀ : ℝ) < t → (t : ℝ) < min ((t₀ : ℝ) + δ) b → edist (f t) R < ENNReal.ofReal ε :=
declarations.name: extended_rightLimits_iff

declarations.docComment: Original block id: `source:A - appendices/analysis.tex:425:defn:35`.
declarations.header: theorem extended_leftLimits_iff (f : ClosedInterval a b → X) : @HasLeftLimitsOnIcc X (BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X).toPseudoMetricSpace a b f ↔ ∀ t₀ : ClosedInterval a b, a < (t₀ : ℝ) → ∃ L : X, ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ δ > (0 : ℝ), ∀ t : ClosedInterval a b, max a ((t₀ : ℝ) - δ) < t → (t : ℝ) < t₀ → edist (f t) L < ENNReal.ofReal ε :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`A - appendices/analysis.tex`, Lemma `lem:regular-paths-bounded-borel`.

Original label: `lem:regular-paths-bounded-borel`, Borel-measurability clause.

Informal statement: a right-continuous map from a second-countable linearly
ordered space into a Borel space is Borel measurable (càdlàg paths; càglàd
paths follow by order reversal, continuous paths as a special case).

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis approximates `f` by step
functions on a uniform grid and takes the pointwise limit; Lean reaches the
same conclusion directly through the right-neighbourhood measurability
criterion `MeasurableSet.of_mem_nhdsGT`, which is the measure-theoretic
content of that limit argument.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_of_right_continuous {α : Type u} {V : Type v} [TopologicalSpace α] [LinearOrder α] [OrderTopology α] [SecondCountableTopology α] [MeasurableSpace α] [BorelSpace α] [TopologicalSpace V] [MeasurableSpace V] [BorelSpace V] {f : α → V} (hf : ∀ x, ContinuousWithinAt f (Ici x) x) : Measurable f :=
declarations.name: measurable_of_right_continuous

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`A - appendices/analysis.tex`, Lemma `lem:regular-paths-bounded-borel`.

Original label: `lem:regular-paths-bounded-borel`, boundedness clause.

Informal statement: on a compact linearly ordered space, a map with one-sided
limits on both sides (right-continuous with left limits, as for càdlàg paths)
into a pseudometric space has bounded range.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis argues by contradiction
along a monotone subsequence and its one-sided limit; Lean uses the equivalent
local-boundedness criterion on a compact space, with the two one-sided limits
supplying bounded images of a left and a right neighbourhood of each point.

declarations.docComment:
The returned checkpoint is the earliest validation minimizer among all
visited models, even when the final visited model is worse.
declarations.header: theorem checkpoint_spec (score : ℕ → ℝ) (maxRounds patience : ℕ) : checkpoint score maxRounds patience ≤ stopRound score maxRounds patience ∧ (∀ i ≤ stopRound score maxRounds patience, score (checkpoint score maxRounds patience) ≤ score i) ∧ (∀ i ≤ stopRound score maxRounds patience, score i = score (checkpoint score maxRounds patience) → checkpoint score maxRounds patience ≤ i) :=
declarations.name: checkpoint_spec

declarations.name: validationScore_congr

declarations.docComment:
For a fixed candidate-model sequence, changing outcomes outside validation
cannot change the checkpoint. This is not a claim that prior preprocessing or
training was independent of test data.

declarations.header: theorem continuous_threshold (a b : ℝ) : Continuous (threshold a b) :=
declarations.name: continuous_threshold

declarations.header: theorem norm_threshold_le (a b r : ℝ) : ‖threshold a b r‖ ≤ (intervalMeasure a b).real univ ^ (1 / (2 : ℝ)) :=
declarations.name: norm_threshold_le

declarations.header: theorem integrable_threshold (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] : Integrable (threshold a b) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_threshold

declarations.docComment: The actual kernel barycentre belongs to the actual constraint set.
declarations.header: theorem kernel_average_mem (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : (∫ r, threshold a b r ∂μ) ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: kernel_average_mem

declarations.header: def cdfClass (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ :=
declarations.name: cdfClass

declarations.header: theorem cdfClass_ae (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : ⇑(cdfClass a b μ) =ᵐ[intervalMeasure a b] cdf μ :=
declarations.name: cdfClass_ae

declarations.docComment:
The scalar test of the thesis proof of clause (ii): for `u ∈ L²([a,b])` and the
kernel law `μ`, Fubini for `h_u(y) = ∫_a^b u(x) 1{y ≤ x} dx` gives
`∫ ⟪u, χ_r⟫ dμ(r) = ∫_a^b u(x) G(x) dx = ⟪u, [G|_{[a,b]}]⟫`.
declarations.header: theorem scalar_kernel_fubini (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (u : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : (∫ r, ⟪u, threshold a b r⟫_ℝ ∂μ) = ⟪u, cdfClass a b μ⟫_ℝ :=
declarations.name: scalar_kernel_fubini

declarations.docComment:
Fubini identifies the Hilbert barycentre with the CDF's actual restriction
class, rather than with an arbitrary pointwise version of a conditional mean.
declarations.header: theorem kernel_average_eq_cdfClass (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : (∫ r, threshold a b r ∂μ) = cdfClass a b μ :=
declarations.name: kernel_average_eq_cdfClass

declarations.docComment: Each `G(ω, ·)` is a distribution function, so its restriction class lies in `𝒞`.
declarations.header: theorem cdfClass_mem (a b : ℝ) (μ : Measure ℝ) : cdfClass a b μ ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: cdfClass_mem

declarations.docComment:
One scalar test `u` of the thesis proof: `⟪E[χ_t | 𝓕_s], u⟫ = E[⟪χ_t, u⟫ | 𝓕_s]`
almost surely (conditional expectation commutes with the continuous linear functional
`⟪u, ·⟫`), then the scalar conditional-law identity and `scalar_kernel_fubini`.
declarations.header: theorem scalar_conditional_cdf {Ω T : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace T] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → ℝ) (Y : Ω → T) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (a b : ℝ) (u : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : (fun ω ↦ ⟪u, P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] ω⟫_ℝ) =ᵐ[P] fun ω ↦ ⟪u, cdfClass a b (condDistrib X Y P (Y ω))⟫_ℝ :=
declarations.name: scalar_conditional_cdf

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (ii).
The thesis route: apply the scalar test identity to a countable dense subset of
`L²([a,b])`, discard the countably many null sets, and conclude
`E[χ_t | 𝓕_s] = [G_s(·,·)|_{[a,b]}]` almost surely; since each `G_s(ω, ·)` is a
distribution function, the conditional expectation lies in `𝒞` almost surely.
The same fixed conditional law supplies the CDF class at every outcome outside a
single null set; there is no family of pointwise exceptional sets.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_cdf {Ω T : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace T] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → ℝ) (Y : Ω → T) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (a b : ℝ) : P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] =ᵐ[P] (fun ω ↦ cdfClass a b (condDistrib X Y P (Y ω))) ∧ ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] ω ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: conditional_cdf

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (ii), kernel-barycentre form.
The L²-valued conditional expectation is the barycentre of the single regular
conditional-law kernel. This is `conditional_cdf` (the scalar-test proof) combined
with the Fubini identification `kernel_average_eq_cdfClass` of that barycentre with
the CDF class; membership in the original constraint is inherited, without selecting
values of an L² representative at individual arguments.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_threshold {Ω T : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace T] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → ℝ) (Y : Ω → T) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (a b : ℝ) : P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] =ᵐ[P] (fun ω ↦ ∫ r, threshold a b r ∂condDistrib X Y P (Y ω)) ∧ ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] ω ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: conditional_threshold

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (ii) for an
arbitrary information sigma-algebra, using its identity conditioning map.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_cdf_subsigma {Ω : Type*} [m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω] (m : MeasurableSpace Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) (P : @Measure Ω m₀) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → ℝ) (hX : @Measurable Ω ℝ m₀ _ X) (a b : ℝ) : ∃ G : Ω → (ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ), P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | m] =ᵐ[P] G ∧ (∀ ω, ∃ κ : Measure ℝ, IsProbabilityMeasure κ ∧ G ω = cdfClass a b κ) ∧ ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, P[fun ω ↦ threshold a b (X ω) | m] ω ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: conditional_cdf_subsigma

declarations.header: def intervalMeasure (a b : ℝ) : Measure ℝ := volume.restrict (Icc a b)
declarations.name: intervalMeasure

declarations.docComment:

declarations.name: constraint

declarations.header: theorem zero_mem (a b : ℝ) : (0 : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) ∈ constraint a b :=
declarations.name: zero_mem

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`.
Non-emptiness of the literal constraint set.
declarations.header: theorem nonempty (a b : ℝ) : (constraint a b).Nonempty := ⟨0, zero_mem a b⟩
declarations.name: nonempty

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`.
Convexity of the actual monotone representative constraint, without assuming
closedness or defining it to be the closure of a smaller substitute.
declarations.header: theorem convex (a b : ℝ) : Convex ℝ (constraint a b) :=
declarations.name: convex

declarations.docComment:
Extend a bounded monotone function on an arbitrary subset, without
requiring that subset to be closed or contain either interval endpoint.
declarations.header: def monotoneExtension (f : ℝ → ℝ) (S : Set ℝ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: monotoneExtension

declarations.header: theorem monotoneExtension_properties {f : ℝ → ℝ} {S : Set ℝ} (hmono : MonotoneOn f S) (hb : ∀ x ∈ S, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) : Monotone (monotoneExtension f S) ∧ (∀ x, 0 ≤ monotoneExtension f S x ∧ monotoneExtension f S x ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, monotoneExtension f S x = f x) :=
declarations.name: monotoneExtension_properties

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:cdf-constraint-selection`.
The pointwise-bounded representative interface is exactly equivalent to the
source's a.e. bounds together with an arbitrary monotone representative.
Clamping changes no L² class and preserves monotonicity.
declarations.header: theorem mem_constraint_iff {a b : ℝ} (f : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : f ∈ constraint a b ↔ (∀ᵐ x ∂intervalMeasure a b, 0 ≤ f x ∧ f x ≤ 1) ∧ ∃ g : ℝ → ℝ, MonotoneOn g (Icc a b) ∧ g =ᵐ[intervalMeasure a b] f :=
declarations.name: mem_constraint_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, closedness in clause (i).
The proof uses a genuinely convergent L² subsequence and a bounded monotone
extension of its full-measure pointwise limit, rather than replacing the
source's constraint by its closure.
declarations.header: theorem isClosed (a b : ℝ) : IsClosed (constraint a b) :=
declarations.name: isClosed

declarations.header: theorem minimizers_nonexpansive {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] {C : Set H} (hC : Convex ℝ C) {u v p q : H} (hp : p ∈ C) (hq : q ∈ C) (hpmin : ‖u - p‖ = ⨅ w : C, ‖u - (w : H)‖) (hqmin : ‖v - q‖ = ⨅ w : C, ‖v - (w : H)‖) : ‖p - q‖ ≤ ‖u - v‖ :=
declarations.name: minimizers_nonexpansive

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (i).
declarations.header: theorem projection_existsUnique (a b : ℝ) (f : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : ∃! p, p ∈ constraint a b ∧ ‖f - p‖ = ⨅ w : constraint a b, ‖f - (w : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ)‖ :=
declarations.name: projection_existsUnique

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (i).
declarations.header: def projection (a b : ℝ) (f : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : constraint a b :=
declarations.name: projection

declarations.header: theorem projection_spec (a b : ℝ) (f : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ) : ‖f - (projection a b f : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ)‖ = ⨅ w : constraint a b, ‖f - (w : ℝ →₂[intervalMeasure a b] ℝ)‖ :=
declarations.name: projection_spec

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (i).
The projection is nonexpansive in the actual L² metric.
declarations.header: theorem projection_lipschitz (a b : ℝ) : LipschitzWith 1 (projection a b) :=
declarations.name: projection_lipschitz

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (iii).
Every literal constraint class admits the supported right-continuous CDF
representative. The only altered values are at monotone discontinuities and
the endpoints, a Lebesgue-null set.
declarations.header: theorem supportedCDF_exists {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (f : constraint a b) : ∃ F : SupportedCDF a b, F.toL2 = f.val :=
declarations.name: supportedCDF_exists

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:cdf-constraint-selection`.
The source's selected CDF, constructed from the actual L² constraint class.
declarations.header: def selection {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (f : constraint a b) : SupportedCDF a b :=
declarations.name: selection

declarations.header: theorem selection_toL2 {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (f : constraint a b) : (selection hab f).toL2 = f.val := (supportedCDF_exists hab f).choose_spec
declarations.name: selection_toL2

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (iii).
declarations.header: theorem selection_inverse {a b : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (F : SupportedCDF a b) : selection hab ⟨F.toL2, F.toL2_mem⟩ = F :=

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (iii).
The Cramér distance is exactly the L² distance of the restricted classes.
declarations.header: theorem cramerDistance_eq_norm {a b : ℝ} (F G : SupportedCDF a b) : cramerDistance F G = ‖F.toL2 - G.toL2‖ :=
declarations.name: cramerDistance_eq_norm

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:cdf-constraint-properties`, clause (iii).

declarations.name: selection_isometry

Original label: `defn:frechet-martingale`.
Adjacent-time Fréchet minimization, with all admissibility conditions explicit.

declarations.docComment:
The squared-norm minimum characterizes the projection uniquely. This is
the Hilbert-space reduction following `defn:frechet-martingale`.
declarations.header: theorem hilbert_minimizer_iff_condExpL2 (hm : m ≤ m₀) (f : Ω →₂[μ] H) (g : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ) : (∀ y : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ, ‖f - (g : Ω →₂[μ] H)‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖f - (y : Ω →₂[μ] H)‖ ^ 2) ↔ g = condExpL2 H ℝ hm f :=
declarations.name: hilbert_minimizer_iff_condExpL2

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:regression-theorem`.
Uniqueness clause: in expected squared-error form the unique minimizer is the
same L² class, namely the conditional expectation.
declarations.header: theorem hilbert_meanSquare_minimizer_iff (hm : m ≤ m₀) (f : Ω →₂[μ] H) (g : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ) : (∀ y : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ, (∫ ω, ‖f ω - (g : Ω →₂[μ] H) ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤ ∫ ω, ‖f ω - (y : Ω →₂[μ] H) ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ↔ g = condExpL2 H ℝ hm f :=
declarations.name: hilbert_meanSquare_minimizer_iff

declarations.docComment:
Finite original-distance second moments imply a finite measurable loss;
the real expectation agrees with this nonnegative integral after `toReal`.

declarations.name: extended_squared_loss_integrable

declarations.docComment:
The extended nonnegative expectation is the ordinary real expectation
used by the source once finite second moments have been established.
declarations.header: theorem extended_squared_loss_expectation [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace E] (μ : Measure Ω) (X Y : Ω → E) (z₀ : E) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (hXm : (∫⁻ ω, edist (X ω) z₀ ^ 2 ∂μ) < ∞) (hYm : (∫⁻ ω, edist (Y ω) z₀ ^ 2 ∂μ) < ∞) : (∫ ω, (edist (X ω) (Y ω) ^ 2).toReal ∂μ) = (∫⁻ ω, edist (X ω) (Y ω) ^ 2 ∂μ).toReal :=
declarations.name: extended_squared_loss_expectation

The source's valid horizon-spaced independence claim. The proof peels off

declarations.docComment:
