declarations.name: hilbertProduct_inner

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
The manuscript's comparison between the `ℓ²` product norm and the maximum norm
of `prop:finite-metric-products`: `max_i ‖v_i‖ ≤ ‖v‖ ≤ |I|^{1/2} max_i ‖v_i‖`.
The maximum norm is Mathlib's supremum norm on the plain product `∀ i, H i`
(`Pi.norm_def`), reached through `WithLp.ofLp`.
declarations.header: theorem hilbertProduct_norm_comparison {I : Type u} [Fintype I] {H : I → Type v} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace ℝ (H i)] (v : HilbertProduct H) : ‖WithLp.ofLp v‖ ≤ ‖v‖ ∧ ‖v‖ ≤ Real.sqrt (Fintype.card I) * ‖WithLp.ofLp v‖ :=
declarations.name: hilbertProduct_norm_comparison

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
Completeness from `prop:finite-metric-products` through the norm comparison:
the lower bound makes `WithLp.ofLp` `1`-Lipschitz, so a Cauchy sequence of the
`ℓ²` product is Cauchy for the maximum metric and converges coordinatewise by
`DoctoralAnalysis.finite_maximum_complete`; the upper bound makes
`WithLp.toLp` `|I|^{1/2}`-Lipschitz, so that limit is also the `ℓ²` limit.
This includes the empty index type.
declarations.header: theorem hilbertProduct_complete {I : Type u} [Finite I] {H : I → Type v} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace ℝ (H i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (H i)] : CompleteSpace (HilbertProduct H) :=
declarations.name: hilbertProduct_complete

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
Separability from `prop:finite-metric-products` through the norm comparison:
`WithLp.toLp` is continuous (upper bound) and surjective, so the countable dense
subset of the maximum-metric product given by
`DoctoralAnalysis.finite_maximum_separable` maps onto a countable dense subset
of the `ℓ²` product.
declarations.header: theorem hilbertProduct_separable {I : Type u} [Finite I] {H : I → Type v} [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace ℝ (H i)] [∀ i, TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (H i)] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (HilbertProduct H) :=
declarations.name: hilbertProduct_separable

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:adjoint-compact-operators`.
declarations.header: abbrev adjoint {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →L[ℝ] H) := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint T
declarations.name: adjoint

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:adjoint-compact-operators`.
declarations.header: theorem adjoint_identity {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →L[ℝ] H) (u v : H) : ⟪T u, v⟫ = ⟪u, adjoint T v⟫ :=
declarations.name: adjoint_identity

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:adjoint-compact-operators`.
declarations.header: def IsSelfAdjoint {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (T : H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop := adjoint T = T
declarations.name: IsSelfAdjoint

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:adjoint-compact-operators`.
declarations.header: def HasFiniteRank {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (T : H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop := FiniteDimensional ℝ (LinearMap.range T.toLinearMap)
declarations.name: HasFiniteRank

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:adjoint-compact-operators`.
declarations.header: def IsCompact {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (T : H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCompact

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The manuscript's expansion of the increment:
`𝔣(ŷ+h) − 𝔣(ŷ) − 2⟨ŷ−y,h⟩ = ‖y − ŷ − h‖² − ‖y − ŷ‖² − 2⟨ŷ−y,h⟩ = ‖h‖²`,
before taking any limit.
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_remainder {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y p h : H) : ‖y - (p + h)‖ ^ 2 - ‖y - p‖ ^ 2 - (2 • innerSL ℝ (p - y)) h = ‖h‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_remainder

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The manuscript's Cauchy--Schwarz bound `|Ah| ≤ 2‖ŷ−y‖‖h‖` for the candidate
derivative `Ah = 2⟨ŷ−y,h⟩`, which shows that `A` is bounded.
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_linear_bound {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y p h : H) : |(2 • innerSL ℝ (p - y)) h| ≤ 2 * ‖p - y‖ * ‖h‖ :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_linear_bound

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The manuscript's normalised remainder `|𝔣(ŷ+h) − 𝔣(ŷ) − Ah| / ‖h‖ = ‖h‖`
(including the harmless totalised value `0` at `h = 0`).
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_remainder_ratio {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y p h : H) : |‖y - (p + h)‖ ^ 2 - ‖y - p‖ ^ 2 - (2 • innerSL ℝ (p - y)) h| / ‖h‖ = ‖h‖ :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_remainder_ratio

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The normalised remainder `‖h‖` tends to `0` as `h → 0`.
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_remainder_ratio_tendsto {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y p : H) : Tendsto (fun h => |‖y - (p + h)‖ ^ 2 - ‖y - p‖ ^ 2 - (2 • innerSL ℝ (p - y)) h| / ‖h‖) (𝓝 (0 : H)) (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_remainder_ratio_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The manuscript's direct verification of the Fréchet-derivative definition: by
`squared_loss_remainder` the increment minus the bounded linear candidate
`Ah = 2⟨ŷ−y,h⟩` (`squared_loss_linear_bound`) is exactly `‖h‖²`, so the
normalised remainder `‖h‖⁻¹ · ‖h‖² = ‖h‖` tends to `0` as `h → 0`.  No chain
rule for `‖·‖²` is used, and no completeness is needed.
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_hasFDerivAt {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y prediction : H) : HasFDerivAt (fun z : H => ‖y - z‖ ^ 2) (2 • innerSL ℝ (prediction - y)) prediction :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_hasFDerivAt

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:squared-loss-gradient`.
The derivative is represented by the claimed gradient.
declarations.header: theorem squared_loss_gradient {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (y prediction h : H) : (2 • innerSL ℝ (prediction - y)) h = ⟪(2 : ℝ) • (prediction - y), h⟫ :=
declarations.name: squared_loss_gradient

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
The bounded linear first-order approximation in the current source.
declarations.header: abbrev HasFrechetDerivative {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] (f : H → G) (A : H →L[ℝ] G) (x : H) : Prop := HasFDerivAt f A x
declarations.name: HasFrechetDerivative

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
declarations.header: def frechetDerivative {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] (f : H → G) (x : H) : H →L[ℝ] G :=
declarations.name: frechetDerivative

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
Every existing approximation agrees with the named derivative, making the
operator-valued derivative function well-defined on differentiable inputs.
declarations.header: theorem frechetDerivative_eq {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] {f : H → G} {A : H →L[ℝ] G} {x : H} (hA : HasFrechetDerivative f A x) : frechetDerivative f x = A := hA.fderiv
declarations.name: frechetDerivative_eq

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
Finite products of real Banach spaces are Banach for every standard finite
product `p`-norm, including the maximum norm at `p = ∞`.
declarations.header: theorem finiteProductBanach {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (V : ι → Type v) [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (V i)] [∀ i, NormedSpace ℝ (V i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (V i)] (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] : Nonempty (NormedSpace ℝ (PiLp p V)) ∧ CompleteSpace (PiLp p V) :=
declarations.name: finiteProductBanach

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
Finite Hilbert products are complete and have exactly the coordinate-sum
inner product. The `PiLp 2` instance provides the Hilbert axioms.
declarations.header: theorem finiteProductHilbert {ι : Type u} [Fintype ι] (H : ι → Type v) [∀ i, NormedAddCommGroup (H i)] [∀ i, InnerProductSpace ℝ (H i)] [∀ i, CompleteSpace (H i)] : CompleteSpace (PiLp 2 H) ∧ ∀ f g : PiLp 2 H, inner ℝ f g = ∑ i, inner ℝ (f i) (g i) :=
declarations.name: finiteProductHilbert

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-products`.
Separability is preserved by the product topology and hence by all of these
finite-product norms. No completeness assumption is needed.
declarations.header: theorem finiteProductSeparable {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (V : ι → Type v) [∀ i, TopologicalSpace (V i)] [∀ i, TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (V i)] (p : ℝ≥0∞) : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (PiLp p V) :=
declarations.name: finiteProductSeparable

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:norm`.

Informal statement: a real normed space is a real vector space equipped with
a nonnegative size function that vanishes exactly at zero, is homogeneous
under real scalar multiplication, and satisfies the triangle inequality.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `NormedAddCommGroup V` supplies the
definite norm and triangle inequality, while `NormedSpace ℝ V` extends the
real module structure and supplies scalar compatibility.  Over `ℝ`, Mathlib's
`norm_smul` is precisely the thesis identity `‖a • v‖ = |a| ‖v‖`.
declarations.header: abbrev RealNormedSpace (V : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup V] := NormedSpace ℝ V
declarations.name: RealNormedSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:inner-product`.

Informal statement: a real inner product is symmetric, real-linear, positive
semidefinite, and positive definite; a vector space carrying it is a real
inner-product space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `InnerProductSpace.Core ℝ V` is
Mathlib's raw inner-product structure on an additive real module; importantly,
it assumes no pre-existing norm.  Over `ℝ`, its Hermitian symmetry and
conjugate-linearity fields are exactly the symmetry and real-linearity in the
thesis, while `re_inner_nonneg` and `definite` are its two positivity clauses.
declarations.header: abbrev RealInnerProductSpace (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] :=
declarations.name: RealInnerProductSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:norm-induced-by-inner-product`.

Informal statement: in a real inner-product space, the formula
`v ↦ sqrt ⟨v,v⟩` defines a norm.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the dependent pair returned below
contains both the induced `Norm V` (`‖v‖ = sqrt ⟪v, v⟫`) and a
`NormedSpace.Core ℝ V` proof of the textbook norm facts; no norm is assumed in
the input.  Nonnegativity, definiteness and real homogeneity (conditions (i)
and (ii) of `defn:norm`) are immediate from the inner-product axioms and are
taken from Mathlib's core verification.  The triangle inequality (iii) is
proved here along the thesis's route: Cauchy--Schwarz `⟪u,v⟫ ≤ ‖u‖‖v‖`
(`InnerProductSpace.Core.norm_inner_le_norm`) gives
`‖u+v‖² = ‖u‖² + 2⟪u,v⟫ + ‖v‖² ≤ (‖u‖ + ‖v‖)²`, and taking square roots
(`nonneg_le_nonneg_of_sq_le_sq`) yields `‖u+v‖ ≤ ‖u‖ + ‖v‖`.  The following
helper theorem records that the constructed norm is definitionally the
thesis's square-root formula.
declarations.header: noncomputable def inducedNormOfInnerProduct (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] (core : RealInnerProductSpace V) : { inducedNorm : Norm V // @NormedSpace.Core ℝ V _ _ _ inducedNorm } :=
declarations.name: inducedNormOfInnerProduct

declarations.header: theorem inducedNormOfInnerProduct_apply {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] (core : RealInnerProductSpace V) (v : V) : @norm V (inducedNormOfInnerProduct V core).1 v = Real.sqrt (core.inner v v) :=
declarations.name: inducedNormOfInnerProduct_apply

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:metric-induced-by-norm`.

Informal statement: for a normed space `(V, ‖·‖)`, the formula
`d(u, v) = ‖u - v‖` defines a metric on `V`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the input is a bare real vector space
with a norm function and the norm axioms of `defn:norm` (`NormedSpace.Core`:
nonnegativity, definiteness, real homogeneity, triangle inequality), with no
pre-existing distance, uniformity or topology.  The metric space is built from
the thesis's three verifications: `d(u,v) = ‖u − v‖ = 0 ↔ u − v = 0 ↔ u = v`
by definiteness; symmetry from `‖u − v‖ = ‖(−1)•(v − u)‖ = |−1| ‖v − u‖` by
homogeneity; and the triangle inequality from
`‖u − v‖ = ‖(u − w) + (w − v)‖ ≤ ‖u − w‖ + ‖w − v‖`.  The companion lemma
`metricSpaceOfNorm_dist` records that the constructed distance is
definitionally the displayed formula.
declarations.header: noncomputable def metricSpaceOfNorm (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Norm V] (core : NormedSpace.Core ℝ V) : MetricSpace V
declarations.name: metricSpaceOfNorm

declarations.header: theorem metricSpaceOfNorm_dist {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Norm V] (core : NormedSpace.Core ℝ V) (u v : V) : letI := metricSpaceOfNorm V core
declarations.name: metricSpaceOfNorm_dist

declarations.docComment:
Bundled-instance corollary of `prop:metric-induced-by-norm` (not the mapped
proof, which is `metricSpaceOfNorm`): on a Mathlib `NormedAddCommGroup` the
pre-installed distance is the thesis formula `d(u, v) = ‖u - v‖`
(`dist_eq_norm`), so downstream uses of the formula on bundled types remain
valid.
declarations.header: theorem dist_eq_norm_sub {V : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup V] (u v : V) : dist u v = ‖u - v‖ :=
declarations.name: dist_eq_norm_sub

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `cor:metric-induced-by-inner-product`.

Informal statement: in a real inner-product space,
`d(u, v) = sqrt ⟪u - v, u - v⟫` defines a metric on `V`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: exactly the thesis's two-step
composition.  `inducedNormOfInnerProduct` (`prop:norm-induced-by-inner-product`)
turns the inner product into the norm `‖v‖ = sqrt ⟪v, v⟫` together with its
norm axioms, and `metricSpaceOfNorm` (`prop:metric-induced-by-norm`) turns that
norm into the metric `d(u, v) = ‖u - v‖`.  The companion lemma
`metricSpaceOfInnerProduct_dist` records that the resulting distance is
definitionally the displayed square-root formula.
declarations.header: noncomputable def metricSpaceOfInnerProduct (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] (core : RealInnerProductSpace V) : MetricSpace V :=
declarations.name: metricSpaceOfInnerProduct

declarations.header: theorem metricSpaceOfInnerProduct_dist {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] (core : RealInnerProductSpace V) (u v : V) : letI := metricSpaceOfInnerProduct V core
declarations.name: metricSpaceOfInnerProduct_dist

declarations.docComment:
Bundled-instance corollary of `cor:metric-induced-by-inner-product` (not the
mapped proof, which is `metricSpaceOfInnerProduct`): on a Mathlib real
inner-product space, rewrite the bundled metric using `dist_eq_norm`, then the
norm using `norm_eq_sqrt_real_inner`.
declarations.header: theorem dist_eq_sqrt_inner_sub {V : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] (u v : V) : dist u v = Real.sqrt (⟪u - v, u - v⟫) :=
declarations.name: dist_eq_sqrt_inner_sub

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:banach-hilbert-separable`.

Informal statement: a normed space is Banach when its induced metric is
complete, an inner-product space is Hilbert when that same metric is complete,
and either kind of space is separable when its induced metric is separable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: use a normed type `B` for the Banach
clause and an inner-product type `H` for the Hilbert clause, so the words cannot
be applied to a bare pseudometric space.  Their completeness predicates are
both Mathlib's `CompleteSpace` after the appropriate induced metric has been
fixed.  The final pair records separability for each of the two ambient
structures.
declarations.header: def banachHilbertSeparablePredicates (B : Type u) (H : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup B] [NormedSpace ℝ B] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] : Prop × Prop × (Prop × Prop) :=
declarations.name: banachHilbertSeparablePredicates

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bounded-linear-operator`.

Informal statement: a bounded linear operator from real normed space `V` to
real normed space `W` is a linear map `T` for which some nonnegative constant
`C` satisfies `‖T v‖ ≤ C ‖v‖` for every `v`; the collection is denoted
`𝓛(V, W)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `ContinuousLinearMap`, written
`V →L[ℝ] W`, bundles a real linear map with continuity and exposes the thesis
bound through `ContinuousLinearMap.bound`.  The later mapped proposition
`prop:bounded-iff-continuous` verifies that this is equivalent to the thesis's
boundedness formulation.
declarations.header: abbrev BoundedLinearOperator (V : Type u) (W : Type v) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W] :=
declarations.name: BoundedLinearOperator

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:operator-norm`.

Informal statement: the operator norm of a bounded linear operator `T` is the
supremum of `‖T v‖` over `‖v‖ ≤ 1`; on a nonzero domain it is equivalently the
supremum over `‖v‖ = 1`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the norm on `V →L[ℝ] W` is Mathlib's
operator norm.  The two conjuncts invoke its closed-unit-ball and unit-sphere
supremum theorems.  Mathlib's sphere formula also covers the zero space by its
`sSup ∅ = 0` convention, so it slightly strengthens the thesis's second clause,
which assumes `V ≠ {0}`.
declarations.header: theorem operatorNorm_eq_sSup {V : Type u} {W : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W] (T : V →L[ℝ] W) : ‖T‖ = sSup ((fun v : V => ‖T v‖) '' Metric.closedBall 0 1) ∧ ‖T‖ = sSup ((fun v : V => ‖T v‖) '' Metric.sphere 0 1) :=
declarations.name: operatorNorm_eq_sSup

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:bounded-iff-continuous`.

Informal statement: a real linear map between normed spaces admits a global
bound `‖T v‖ ≤ C ‖v‖` if and only if its underlying function is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `IsBoundedLinearMap ℝ T` is Mathlib's
predicate consisting of linearity together with such a norm bound.  The
forward implication uses its `continuous` theorem.  Conversely, the linearity
already bundled in `T : V →ₗ[ℝ] W`, together with continuity, is converted by
`isLinearMap_and_continuous_iff_isBoundedLinearMap`.
declarations.header: theorem linearMap_bounded_iff_continuous {V : Type u} {W : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [NormedAddCommGroup W] [NormedSpace ℝ W] (T : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) : IsBoundedLinearMap ℝ T ↔ Continuous T :=
declarations.name: linearMap_bounded_iff_continuous

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:dual-space`.

Informal statement: the continuous dual `V*` of a real normed space `V` is the
real vector space `𝓛(V, ℝ)` of bounded linear functionals from `V` to `ℝ`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: specialise the continuous-linear-map
type used for bounded operators to codomain `ℝ`.  Mathlib supplies its real
vector-space operations pointwise and its operator norm automatically.
declarations.header: abbrev DualSpace (V : Type u) [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] :=
declarations.name: DualSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:riesz-representation`.

Informal statement: for every continuous real linear functional `φ` on a real
Hilbert space `H`, there is a unique vector `hφ` such that
`φ u = ⟪u, hφ⟫` for every `u`, and the operator norm of `φ` equals `‖hφ‖`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's Fréchet--Riesz theorem is the
surjective linear isometry `InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ H`.  Take its inverse
at `φ`, use real-inner-product symmetry to match the thesis's argument order,
use injectivity for uniqueness, and use the inverse isometry's `norm_map` for
the norm identity.  This is entirely Mathlib-verified; no external assumption is
introduced.
declarations.header: theorem rieszRepresentation {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (φ : DualSpace H) : ∃! hφ : H, (∀ u : H, φ u = ⟪u, hφ⟫) ∧ ‖φ‖ = ‖hφ‖ :=
declarations.name: rieszRepresentation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:atom-diffuse`.
A positive measurable set is an atom if every measurable cut has a null side.
declarations.header: def IsMeasureAtom {Ω : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) (A : Set Ω) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom

declarations.docComment: Every positive measurable set contains a measurable atom.
declarations.header: def IsPurelyAtomic {Ω : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic

declarations.docComment: A diffuse measure has no measurable positive-mass atom.
declarations.header: def IsDiffuse {Ω : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsDiffuse

declarations.docComment: The distinct support points and their positive singleton weights.
declarations.header: def HasCountablePointMassRepresentation {Ω : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (β : Measure Ω) : Prop :=
declarations.name: HasCountablePointMassRepresentation

declarations.header: theorem IsMeasureAtom.cut_zero (hA : IsMeasureAtom μ A) (hB : MeasurableSet B) : μ (A ∩ B) = 0 ∨ μ (A \ B) = 0 :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom.cut_zero

declarations.header: theorem IsMeasureAtom.of_absolutelyContinuous (hA : IsMeasureAtom μ A) (hνμ : ν ≪ μ) (hpos : 0 < ν A) : IsMeasureAtom ν A :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom.of_absolutelyContinuous

declarations.header: theorem IsMeasureAtom.subset (hA : IsMeasureAtom μ A) (hBA : B ⊆ A) (hB : MeasurableSet B) (hpos : 0 < μ B) : IsMeasureAtom μ B :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom.subset

declarations.header: theorem IsMeasureAtom.of_restrict (hA : IsMeasureAtom (μ.restrict s) A) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : IsMeasureAtom μ (A ∩ s) :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom.of_restrict

declarations.header: theorem IsDiffuse.restrict (hμ : IsDiffuse μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : IsDiffuse (μ.restrict s) :=
declarations.name: IsDiffuse.restrict

declarations.header: theorem IsPurelyAtomic.restrict (hμ : IsPurelyAtomic μ) (hs : MeasurableSet s) : IsPurelyAtomic (μ.restrict s) :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic.restrict

declarations.header: theorem IsPurelyAtomic.eq_zero_of_diffuse (hμ : IsPurelyAtomic μ) (hd : IsDiffuse μ) : μ = 0 :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic.eq_zero_of_diffuse

declarations.docComment:
Diffuseness descends along absolute continuity. The density's positive set
allows a hypothetical atom to be transferred back to the reference measure.
declarations.header: theorem IsDiffuse.of_absolutelyContinuous [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] (hμ : IsDiffuse μ) (hνμ : ν ≪ μ) : IsDiffuse ν :=
declarations.name: IsDiffuse.of_absolutelyContinuous

declarations.docComment:
A countable measurable union captures every atom up to a null set. Its
complement is diffuse and its restriction is purely atomic.
declarations.header: theorem exists_atomic_support [SFinite μ] : ∃ B : Set Ω, MeasurableSet B ∧ IsDiffuse (μ.restrict Bᶜ) ∧ IsPurelyAtomic (μ.restrict B) ∧ ∀ ν : Measure Ω, ν ≪ μ → IsDiffuse ν → ν B = 0 :=
declarations.name: exists_atomic_support

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:atomic`.
Every sigma-finite measure on an arbitrary measurable space has a unique
decomposition into a diffuse measure and a purely atomic measure.
declarations.header: theorem atomicDecomposition_general (μ : Measure Ω) [SigmaFinite μ] : ∃! p : Measure Ω × Measure Ω, μ = p.1 + p.2 ∧ IsDiffuse p.1 ∧ IsPurelyAtomic p.2 :=
declarations.name: atomicDecomposition_general

declarations.docComment:
On a countably separated measurable space, a measurable atom contains
a point of positive mass.
declarations.header: theorem IsMeasureAtom.exists_positive_singleton [MeasurableSpace.CountablySeparated Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (hA : IsMeasureAtom μ A) : ∃ x ∈ A, 0 < μ ({x} : Set Ω) :=
declarations.name: IsMeasureAtom.exists_positive_singleton

declarations.docComment:
Purely atomic s-finite measures on countably separated spaces are
countable weighted sums of their positive singleton masses.
declarations.header: theorem IsPurelyAtomic.countablePointMassRepresentation [SFinite μ] [MeasurableSpace.CountablySeparated Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (hμ : IsPurelyAtomic μ) : HasCountablePointMassRepresentation μ :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic.countablePointMassRepresentation

declarations.header: theorem IsPurelyAtomic.exists_countable_dirac_sum [SigmaFinite μ] [MeasurableSpace.CountablySeparated Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (hμ : IsPurelyAtomic μ) : ∃ (I : Set Ω) (a : I → ℝ≥0), I.Countable ∧ (∀ x, 0 < a x) ∧ (∀ x : I, IsMeasureAtom μ ({x.1} : Set Ω)) ∧ μ = Measure.sum (fun x : I => a x • Measure.dirac x.1) :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic.exists_countable_dirac_sum

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:atomic`.
The Polish Borel specialization includes the countable point-mass formula.
declarations.header: theorem atomicDecomposition {Ω : Type u} [TopologicalSpace Ω] [PolishSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω] [BorelSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [SigmaFinite μ] : ∃! p : Measure Ω × Measure Ω, μ = p.1 + p.2 ∧ IsDiffuse p.1 ∧ IsPurelyAtomic p.2 ∧ HasCountablePointMassRepresentation p.2 :=
declarations.name: atomicDecomposition

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:atomic`.
The revised statement's literal indexing by a subset of the natural numbers,
with distinct support points and coefficients equal to singleton masses.
The empty atomic part is included without adding a dummy support point.
declarations.header: theorem IsPurelyAtomic.exists_nat_dirac_sum [SigmaFinite μ] [MeasurableSpace.CountablySeparated Ω] [MeasurableSingletonClass Ω] (hμ : IsPurelyAtomic μ) : ∃ (I : Set ℕ) (x : I → Ω) (a : I → ℝ≥0), Function.Injective x ∧ (∀ i, 0 < a i) ∧ (∀ i, (a i : ℝ≥0∞) = μ ({x i} : Set Ω)) ∧ (∀ i, IsMeasureAtom μ ({x i} : Set Ω)) ∧ μ = Measure.sum (fun i => a i • Measure.dirac (x i)) :=
declarations.name: IsPurelyAtomic.exists_nat_dirac_sum

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:bochner-integrability`.
The literal finite-norm-integral criterion under the manuscript's measurable,
separable Banach hypotheses.
declarations.header: theorem bochnerIntegrable_iff_finite_norm_integral (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → V) (hf : Measurable f) : Integrable f μ ↔ (∫⁻ ω, ‖f ω‖ₑ ∂μ) < ∞ :=
declarations.name: bochnerIntegrable_iff_finite_norm_integral

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
Every integrable measurable Banach-valued function has integrable simple
approximants converging in integrated norm, whose integrals converge in `V`.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_simple_approximation (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → V) (hf : Measurable f) (hfi : Integrable f μ) : ∃ s : ℕ → SimpleFunc Ω V, (∀ n, Integrable (s n) μ) ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫⁻ ω, ‖f ω - s n ω‖ₑ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫ ω, s n ω ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (bochnerIntegral μ f)) :=
declarations.name: bochner_simple_approximation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`; this equivalence is also the
content of `prop:bochner-integrability` (the simple-approximation criterion
versus the finite-norm-integral criterion).
The simple-approximation criterion is equivalent to integrability. The
converse uses a finite integrated error at one index; it does not assume
integrability of the target or of every approximation error in advance.
declarations.header: theorem bochnerIntegrable_iff_simple_approximation (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → V) (hf : Measurable f) : Integrable f μ ↔ ∃ s : ℕ → SimpleFunc Ω V, (∀ n, Integrable (s n) μ) ∧ Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫⁻ ω, ‖f ω - s n ω‖ₑ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: bochnerIntegrable_iff_simple_approximation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
Every sequence satisfying the manuscript's approximation criterion gives the
same integral limit, so the definition is independent of the selected sequence.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_integral_tendsto_of_simple_approximation (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → V) (hf : Measurable f) (s : ℕ → SimpleFunc Ω V) (hs : ∀ n, Integrable (s n) μ) (hlim : Tendsto (fun n ↦ ∫⁻ ω, ‖f ω - s n ω‖ₑ ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 0)) : Tendsto (fun n ↦ bochnerIntegral μ (s n)) atTop (𝓝 (bochnerIntegral μ f)) :=
declarations.name: bochner_integral_tendsto_of_simple_approximation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
The finite weighted-sum formula on the measurable level-set partition. Any
other integrable simple presentation defining the same function has the same
integral, as proved by `bochner_simple_integral_congr` below.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_simple_integral_eq_sum (μ : Measure Ω) (s : SimpleFunc Ω V) (hs : Integrable s μ) : bochnerIntegral μ s = ∑ v ∈ s.range, μ.real (s ⁻¹' {v}) • v :=
declarations.name: bochner_simple_integral_eq_sum

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
Independence of the simple-function presentation, including equality only
almost everywhere.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_simple_integral_congr (μ : Measure Ω) (s t : SimpleFunc Ω V) (hs : Integrable s μ) (ht : Integrable t μ) (hst : (s : Ω → V) =ᵐ[μ] t) : (∑ v ∈ s.range, μ.real (s ⁻¹' {v}) • v) = ∑ v ∈ t.range, μ.real (t ⁻¹' {v}) • v :=
declarations.name: bochner_simple_integral_congr

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:simple-function`.
Linearity for nonnegative indicator presentations does not require disjoint
sets. Overlaps are counted in the represented function; the current source
equivalently refines the sets and combines coefficients on each cell.
declarations.header: theorem lintegral_finite_indicator_sum {ι : Type*} (μ : Measure Ω) (I : Finset ι) (E : ι → Set Ω) (a : ι → ℝ≥0∞) (hE : ∀ i ∈ I, MeasurableSet (E i)) : (∫⁻ ω, ∑ i ∈ I, (E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ a i) ω ∂μ) = ∑ i ∈ I, a i * μ (E i) :=
declarations.name: lintegral_finite_indicator_sum

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
The finite weighted-sum formula holds for any measurable indicator
presentation whose individual terms are integrable, including partitions.
Neither disjointness nor distinct vector values are needed for this identity.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_finite_indicator_sum {ι : Type*} (μ : Measure Ω) (I : Finset ι) (E : ι → Set Ω) (v : ι → V) (hE : ∀ i ∈ I, MeasurableSet (E i)) (hfi : ∀ i ∈ I, Integrable ((E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ v i)) μ) : bochnerIntegral μ (fun ω ↦ ∑ i ∈ I, (E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ v i) ω) = ∑ i ∈ I, μ.real (E i) • v i :=
declarations.name: bochner_finite_indicator_sum

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
The source's finite weighted norm condition suffices for each indicator term,
including zero vectors on cells of infinite measure.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_finite_indicator_sum_of_norm_sum_lt_top {ι : Type*} (μ : Measure Ω) (I : Finset ι) (E : ι → Set Ω) (v : ι → V) (hE : ∀ i ∈ I, MeasurableSet (E i)) (hfinite : (∑ i ∈ I, ‖v i‖ₑ * μ (E i)) < ∞) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ ∑ i ∈ I, (E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ v i) ω) μ ∧ bochnerIntegral μ (fun ω ↦ ∑ i ∈ I, (E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ v i) ω) = ∑ i ∈ I, μ.real (E i) • v i :=
declarations.name: bochner_finite_indicator_sum_of_norm_sum_lt_top

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.
For disjoint measurable cells, the integrated norm is exactly the weighted
norm sum in the source. The cells need not exhaust the domain: outside them
the represented simple function is zero.
declarations.header: theorem bochner_partition_norm_integral {ι : Type*} (μ : Measure Ω) (I : Finset ι) (E : ι → Set Ω) (v : ι → V) (hE : ∀ i ∈ I, MeasurableSet (E i)) (hd : (I : Set ι).PairwiseDisjoint E) : (∫⁻ ω, ‖∑ i ∈ I, (E i).indicator (fun _ ↦ v i) ω‖ₑ ∂μ) = ∑ i ∈ I, ‖v i‖ₑ * μ (E i) :=
declarations.name: bochner_partition_norm_integral

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:lp-banach`.
The representative-level inner-product formula is invariant under changes
on null sets in either argument.
declarations.header: theorem integral_inner_congr_ae {H : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (μ : Measure Ω) {f f' g g' : Ω → H} (hf : f =ᵐ[μ] f') (hg : g =ᵐ[μ] g') : (∫ ω, inner ℝ (f ω) (g ω) ∂μ) = ∫ ω, inner ℝ (f' ω) (g' ω) ∂μ :=
declarations.name: integral_inner_congr_ae

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:regular-conditional-distribution`.

The conditional-expectation identity is proved for every bounded measurable
test function using the same kernel as the joint-law disintegration. Uniqueness
is with respect to the law of the conditioning random element.
declarations.header: theorem regularConditionalDistribution_full {Ω : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] [StandardBorelSpace S] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → S) (Y : Ω → T) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) : ∃ Q : Kernel T S, IsMarkovKernel Q ∧ (P.map Y) ⊗ₘ Q = P.map (fun ω ↦ (Y ω, X ω)) ∧ (∀ A B, MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → P (X ⁻¹' A ∩ Y ⁻¹' B) = ∫⁻ y in B, Q y A ∂P.map Y) ∧ (∀ g : S → ℝ, Measurable g → (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ s, ‖g s‖ ≤ C) → P[fun ω ↦ g (X ω) | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace T).comap Y] =ᵐ[P] fun ω ↦ ∫ s, g s ∂Q (Y ω)) ∧ (∀ R : Kernel T S, IsMarkovKernel R → (P.map Y) ⊗ₘ R = P.map (fun ω ↦ (Y ω, X ω)) → R =ᵐ[P.map Y] Q) :=
declarations.name: regularConditionalDistribution_full

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:measure-disintegration`.
The exact empty-space condition in the current statement: the target must be
inhabited when the source is inhabited. If the source is empty the unique
kernel is vacuously Markov, even when the target is empty too.
declarations.header: theorem measureDisintegration_including_empty {S : Type u} {T : Type v} [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] [StandardBorelSpace T] (h : Nonempty S → Nonempty T) (Λ : Measure (S × T)) [IsFiniteMeasure Λ] : ∃ Q : Kernel S T, IsMarkovKernel Q ∧ Λ.fst ⊗ₘ Q = Λ ∧ ∀ R : Kernel S T, IsFiniteKernel R → Λ.fst ⊗ₘ R = Λ → R =ᵐ[Λ.fst] Q :=
declarations.name: measureDisintegration_including_empty

declarations.header: noncomputable def extendedIntegral (μ : Measure S) (f : S → EReal) : EReal :=
declarations.name: extendedIntegral

declarations.header: theorem measurable_abs : Measurable EReal.abs :=
declarations.name: measurable_abs

declarations.header: theorem toENNReal_le_abs (x : EReal) : x.toENNReal ≤ x.abs :=
declarations.name: toENNReal_le_abs

declarations.header: theorem enorm_toReal_le_abs (x : EReal) : ‖x.toReal‖ₑ ≤ x.abs :=
declarations.name: enorm_toReal_le_abs

declarations.header: theorem ae_coe_toReal_of_lintegral_abs_lt_top (μ : Measure S) {f : S → EReal} (hf : Measurable f) (hfinite : ∫⁻ s, (f s).abs ∂μ < ∞) : (fun s ↦ ((f s).toReal : EReal)) =ᵐ[μ] f :=
declarations.name: ae_coe_toReal_of_lintegral_abs_lt_top

declarations.header: theorem integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_abs_lt_top (μ : Measure S) {f : S → EReal} (hf : Measurable f) (hfinite : ∫⁻ s, (f s).abs ∂μ < ∞) : Integrable (fun s ↦ (f s).toReal) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_abs_lt_top

declarations.header: theorem extendedIntegral_congr_ae (μ : Measure S) {f g : S → EReal} (hfg : f =ᵐ[μ] g) : extendedIntegral μ f = extendedIntegral μ g :=
declarations.name: extendedIntegral_congr_ae

declarations.header: theorem extendedIntegral_coe (μ : Measure S) {f : S → ℝ} (hf : Integrable f μ) : extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ (f s : EReal)) = (∫ s, f s ∂μ : ℝ) :=
declarations.name: extendedIntegral_coe

declarations.header: theorem extendedIntegral_eq_integral_toReal (μ : Measure S) {f : S → EReal} (hf : Measurable f) (hfinite : ∫⁻ s, (f s).abs ∂μ < ∞) : extendedIntegral μ f = ((∫ s, (f s).toReal ∂μ : ℝ) : EReal) :=
declarations.name: extendedIntegral_eq_integral_toReal

declarations.header: theorem extendedIntegral_of_nonneg (μ : Measure S) {f : S → EReal} (hf : ∀ s, 0 ≤ f s) : extendedIntegral μ f = ((∫⁻ s, (f s).toENNReal ∂μ) : EReal) :=
declarations.name: extendedIntegral_of_nonneg

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:tonelli-fubini`.
Tonelli's nonnegative clause for extended-real inputs, with measurable partial
integrals and both orders of integration, including infinite integrals.
declarations.header: theorem tonelli_extendedReal (μ : Measure S) (ν : Measure T) [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] (f : S × T → EReal) (hf : Measurable f) (hnonneg : ∀ z, 0 ≤ f z) : Measurable (fun s ↦ extendedIntegral ν (fun t ↦ f (s, t))) ∧ Measurable (fun t ↦ extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ f (s, t))) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ extendedIntegral ν (fun t ↦ f (s, t))) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = extendedIntegral ν (fun t ↦ extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ f (s, t))) :=
declarations.name: tonelli_extendedReal

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:tonelli-fubini`.
The signed clause in the full extended-real scope of the thesis. The absolute
integrability assumption yields almost-everywhere integrable sections and
justifies both iterated signed integrals.
declarations.header: theorem fubini_extendedReal (μ : Measure S) (ν : Measure T) [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] (f : S × T → EReal) (hf : Measurable f) (hfinite : ∫⁻ z, (f z).abs ∂μ.prod ν < ∞) : (∀ᵐ s ∂μ, Measurable (fun t ↦ f (s, t)) ∧ ∫⁻ t, (f (s, t)).abs ∂ν < ∞) ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂ν, Measurable (fun s ↦ f (s, t)) ∧ ∫⁻ s, (f (s, t)).abs ∂μ < ∞) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ extendedIntegral ν (fun t ↦ f (s, t))) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = extendedIntegral ν (fun t ↦ extendedIntegral μ (fun s ↦ f (s, t))) :=
declarations.name: fubini_extendedReal

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:tonelli-fubini`.
The signed partial integrals are explicitly zeroed on the measurable null sets
of non-integrable sections. These versions are measurable and integrable;
both of their ordinary integrals equal the full signed extended integral.
declarations.header: theorem fubini_zeroed_partial_versions (μ : Measure S) (ν : Measure T) [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] (f : S × T → EReal) (hf : Measurable f) (hfinite : ∫⁻ z, (f z).abs ∂μ.prod ν < ∞) : ∃ g : S → ℝ, ∃ h : T → ℝ, Measurable g ∧ Measurable h ∧ Integrable g μ ∧ Integrable h ν ∧ (∀ s, g s = if (∫⁻ t, (f (s, t)).abs ∂ν) < ∞ then ∫ t, (f (s, t)).toReal ∂ν else 0) ∧ (∀ t, h t = if (∫⁻ s, (f (s, t)).abs ∂μ) < ∞ then ∫ s, (f (s, t)).toReal ∂μ else 0) ∧ ((fun s => (g s : EReal)) =ᵐ[μ] fun s => extendedIntegral ν (fun t => f (s, t))) ∧ ((fun t => (h t : EReal)) =ᵐ[ν] fun t => extendedIntegral μ (fun s => f (s, t))) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = (∫ s, g s ∂μ : ℝ) ∧ extendedIntegral (μ.prod ν) f = (∫ t, h t ∂ν : ℝ) :=
declarations.name: fubini_zeroed_partial_versions

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric`.
The library neighborhood is the existential open neighborhood of the source,
including its empty-set convention. Apply this with the truncated metric.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorov_neighborhood_formula {X : Type*} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (B : Set X) (ε : ℝ) : Metric.thickening ε B = {x | ∃ b ∈ B, dist x b < ε} ∧ Metric.thickening ε (∅ : Set X) = ∅ :=
declarations.name: prokhorov_neighborhood_formula

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric`.
All four assertions apply to the literal min(d,1) metric specified by the
current source. Its topology, Borel sets and complete uniformity agree with
the original extended metric, as proved in BoundedMetric.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovMetricTheorem_extended {X : Type*} [d : EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : letI bounded := @BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X d
declarations.name: prokhorovMetricTheorem_extended

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric`.
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.
Restricting the infimum to finite strictly positive radii leaves the library
distance unchanged. This matches the radius convention of the source.
declarations.header: theorem levyProkhorovEDist_eq_positive_inf {X : Type*} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] (μ ν : Measure X) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [IsFiniteMeasure ν] : levyProkhorovEDist μ ν = sInf {ε : ℝ≥0∞ | 0 < ε ∧ ε < ∞ ∧ ∀ B, MeasurableSet B → μ B ≤ ν (Metric.thickening ε.toReal B) + ε ∧ ν B ≤ μ (Metric.thickening ε.toReal B) + ε} :=
declarations.name: levyProkhorovEDist_eq_positive_inf

declarations.docComment:

The metric used for Prokhorov's distance is exactly the source's capped
extended metric. Its topology and Borel sets agree with those of the original
extended metric; no finiteness of the original base distance is required.
declarations.header: theorem randomMeasure_iff_prokhorovMeasurable_extended {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [d : EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] (Ξ : Ω → FiniteMeasure X) : letI bounded := @BoundedMetric.truncatedMetricSpace X d
declarations.name: randomMeasure_iff_prokhorovMeasurable_extended

Original label: `defn:standard-borel-space`.
Being standard Borel asserts existence of a compatible Polish topology; it
does not equip the measurable space with a preferred topology.
declarations.header: theorem standardBorel_iff_exists_polish (X : Type u) [m : MeasurableSpace X] : StandardBorelSpace X ↔ ∃ t : TopologicalSpace X, @PolishSpace X t ∧ m = @borel X t :=
declarations.name: standardBorel_iff_exists_polish

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:borel-subset-standard-borel`.
The subtype measurable space is exactly the trace sigma algebra.
declarations.header: theorem borelSubset_standardBorel {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] {Y : Set X} (hY : MeasurableSet Y) : StandardBorelSpace Y :=
declarations.name: borelSubset_standardBorel

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:measurable-space`.

Informal statement: a measurable space on a nonempty set `Ω` is a collection
of subsets containing `Ω` and closed under complements and countable unions;
that collection is its sigma-algebra.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `MeasurableSpace Ω` packages
exactly this sigma-algebra.  Its primitive fields use the equivalent axioms
`∅` measurable, complement closure, and countable-union closure; `univ` follows
from the first two.  The thesis's nonemptiness assumption is retained at use
sites when probability mass one is needed, but is not required to define a
sigma-algebra.
declarations.header: abbrev SigmaAlgebra (Ω : Type u) := MeasurableSpace Ω
declarations.name: SigmaAlgebra

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:measure`.

Informal statement: a measure is an extended-nonnegative-valued, countably
additive set function that vanishes on the empty set; it is a probability
measure exactly when its total mass is one.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Measure Ω` already bundles the empty-set
and disjoint-countable-additivity axioms.  The displayed equivalence records
the thesis's additional probability clause using Mathlib's
`IsProbabilityMeasure` class.
declarations.header: theorem probabilityMeasure_iff {Ω : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) : IsProbabilityMeasure μ ↔ μ univ = 1 :=
declarations.name: probabilityMeasure_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:measurable-function`.

Informal statement: a function `f : Ω → S` is measurable when the inverse
image of every measurable subset of `S` is measurable in `Ω`; on a probability
space it is a random element, and a real-valued one is a random variable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `Measurable f` is exactly the
inverse-image condition.  The probability measure changes terminology, not
the underlying predicate, so no additional field is needed for random
elements or variables.
declarations.header: abbrev MeasurableFunction {Ω : Type u} {S : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace S] (f : Ω → S) : Prop :=
declarations.name: MeasurableFunction

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:trace-sigma-algebra`.

Informal statement: the trace sigma-algebra on a subset `E ⊆ Ω` consists of
the intersections `F ∩ E` with measurable `F ⊆ Ω`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib represents the restricted set
as the subtype `E` and equips it with the pullback (`comap`) of the ambient
measurable space along `Subtype.val`.  Its measurable subsets are precisely
the thesis traces, including when `E` itself is not measurable.
declarations.header: abbrev traceSigmaAlgebra {Ω : Type u} [mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω] (E : Set Ω) : MeasurableSpace E :=
declarations.name: traceSigmaAlgebra

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:measurable-restrictions`.

Informal statement: if measurable sets `E n` cover `Ω`, then `f : Ω → S` is
measurable if and only if every restriction `f|E n : E n → S` is measurable
for the trace sigma-algebra.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the forward direction composes with the
measurable subtype inclusion.  For the converse, the preimage of a measurable
set is reconstructed as the countable union of its intersections with `E n`;
`MeasurableSet.subtype_image` is the Lean counterpart of the thesis sets
`A_n ∩ E_n`.  This follows the manuscript proof rather than invoking a
black-box pasting theorem.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_iff_restrictions {Ω : Type u} {S : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace S] (f : Ω → S) (E : ℕ → Set Ω) (hE : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (E n)) (hcover : ⋃ n, E n = univ) : Measurable f ↔ ∀ n, Measurable (fun x : E n => f x) :=
declarations.name: measurable_iff_restrictions

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:push-forward`.

Informal statement: a measurable map `f : Ω → S` transports a measure `μ` to
the measure `μ ∘ f⁻¹`, whose value on measurable `B` is `μ (f⁻¹ B)`; for a
probability measure this push-forward is the law of `f`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib calls the push-forward
`Measure.map f μ`.  `Measure.map_apply` proves the displayed evaluation
identity, and Mathlib automatically transports `IsProbabilityMeasure` through
a measurable map.
declarations.header: theorem pushForward_apply {Ω : Type u} {S : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace S] (μ : Measure Ω) {f : Ω → S} (hf : Measurable f) {B : Set S} (hB : MeasurableSet B) : μ.map f B = μ (f ⁻¹' B) :=
declarations.name: pushForward_apply

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:product-measure`.

Informal statement: for finite measures `μ` and `ν`, their product is the
unique measure on the product sigma-algebra satisfying
`(μ ⊗ ν)(A × B) = μ(A)ν(B)` for measurable rectangles.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: choose Mathlib's `μ.prod ν`; its theorem
`Measure.prod_prod` supplies the rectangle identity.  Uniqueness is proved
with `Measure.ext_prod`.  The candidate measure is finite because its mass on
`univ × univ` is the product of two finite masses.
declarations.header: theorem productMeasure_existsUnique {S : Type u} {T : Type v} [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] (μ : Measure S) (ν : Measure T) [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] : ∃! ρ : Measure (S × T), ∀ A : Set S, ∀ B : Set T, MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → ρ (A ×ˢ B) = μ A * ν B :=
declarations.name: productMeasure_existsUnique

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:tonelli-fubini`.

Informal statement: a nonnegative measurable function on a product has
measurable partial integrals and equal product and iterated integrals in both
orders; an integrable real function has integrable sections almost everywhere
and satisfies the analogous two Fubini identities.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the nonnegative clause is Mathlib's
`lintegral_prod` and `lintegral_prod_symm` for `ℝ≥0∞`, together with the two
partial-integral measurability theorems.  The signed clause uses the Bochner
integral specialised to `ℝ`, `Integrable.prod_right_ae`,
`Integrable.prod_left_ae`, `integral_prod`, and `integral_prod_symm`.
The full extended-real-valued statement, including infinite values on null
sets, is proved separately in `ExtendedFubini.lean`.
declarations.header: theorem tonelliFubini {S : Type u} {T : Type v} [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] (μ : Measure S) (ν : Measure T) [SigmaFinite μ] [SigmaFinite ν] (g : S × T → ℝ≥0∞) (hg : Measurable g) (f : S × T → ℝ) (hf : Integrable f (μ.prod ν)) : (Measurable (fun s => ∫⁻ t, g (s, t) ∂ν) ∧ Measurable (fun t => ∫⁻ s, g (s, t) ∂μ) ∧ (∫⁻ z, g z ∂μ.prod ν) = ∫⁻ s, ∫⁻ t, g (s, t) ∂ν ∂μ ∧ (∫⁻ z, g z ∂μ.prod ν) = ∫⁻ t, ∫⁻ s, g (s, t) ∂μ ∂ν) ∧ ((∀ᵐ s ∂μ, Integrable (fun t => f (s, t)) ν) ∧ (∀ᵐ t ∂ν, Integrable (fun s => f (s, t)) μ) ∧ (∫ z, f z ∂μ.prod ν) = ∫ s, ∫ t, f (s, t) ∂ν ∂μ ∧ (∫ z, f z ∂μ.prod ν) = ∫ t, ∫ s, f (s, t) ∂μ ∂ν) :=
declarations.name: tonelliFubini

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:markov-kernel`.

Informal statement: a Markov kernel from `S` to `T` is a measurable family
`s ↦ Q(s, ·)` of probability measures on `T`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `Kernel S T` makes every
evaluation `s ↦ Q s B` measurable for measurable `B`, and
`IsMarkovKernel Q` asserts that every fibre is a probability measure.  The
subtype below bundles exactly those two thesis clauses.
declarations.header: abbrev MarkovKernel (S : Type u) (T : Type v) [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] :=
declarations.name: MarkovKernel

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:measure-disintegration`.

Informal statement: a finite measure `Λ` on `S × T`, with standard-Borel
target `T`, admits a Markov kernel `Q` such that the first marginal composed
with `Q` recovers `Λ`; the kernel is unique almost everywhere for the first
marginal.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib constructs `Λ.condKernel` for a
finite product measure with standard-Borel second coordinate.  Its
`disintegrate` theorem is equality of whole measures, stronger than checking
rectangles one at a time.  `eq_condKernel_of_measure_eq_compProd` supplies the
thesis's almost-everywhere uniqueness clause.
declarations.header: theorem measureDisintegration {S : Type u} {T : Type v} [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] [StandardBorelSpace T] [Nonempty T] (Λ : Measure (S × T)) [IsFiniteMeasure Λ] : IsMarkovKernel Λ.condKernel ∧ Λ.fst ⊗ₘ Λ.condKernel = Λ ∧ ∀ Q : Kernel S T, IsFiniteKernel Q → Λ.fst ⊗ₘ Q = Λ → Q =ᵐ[Λ.fst] Λ.condKernel :=
declarations.name: measureDisintegration

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:regular-conditional-distribution`.

Informal statement: standard-Borel random elements `X : Ω → S` and
`Y : Ω → T` have a regular conditional distribution of `X` given `Y`, unique
up to the law of `Y`; its kernel disintegrates the joint law of `(Y, X)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: apply Mathlib's standard-Borel
conditional-kernel construction to the pushed-forward joint law
`P.map (Y, X)`.  The resulting equality of measures implies the thesis's
rectangle probability formula and, by integration, the bounded-measurable
conditional-expectation identity. `ConditionalDistribution.lean` proves those
two consequences explicitly together with almost-everywhere uniqueness.
declarations.header: theorem regularConditionalDistribution {Ω : Type u} {S : Type v} {T : Type w} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace S] [MeasurableSpace T] [StandardBorelSpace S] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → S) (Y : Ω → T) (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) : ∃ Q : Kernel T S, IsMarkovKernel Q ∧ (P.map fun ω => (Y ω, X ω)).fst ⊗ₘ Q = P.map fun ω => (Y ω, X ω) :=
declarations.name: regularConditionalDistribution

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:simple-function`.

Informal statement: a simple measurable function takes finitely many vector
values on measurable fibres, equivalently it can be written as a finite sum of
measurable-set indicators times those values.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `SimpleFunc Ω V` is a
measurable function with finite range.  Its fibre decomposition gives the
indicator-sum representation in the thesis, while repeated values or
overlapping presentations are canonically refined to measurable fibres.
declarations.header: abbrev SimpleMeasurableFunction (Ω : Type u) (V : Type v) [MeasurableSpace Ω] :=
declarations.name: SimpleMeasurableFunction

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:bochner-integral`.

Informal statement: the Bochner integral of an integrable Banach-valued
function is the limit of the integrals of simple functions converging in
integrated norm; for a simple partition it is the corresponding weighted
finite sum.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.integral` is
the Bochner integral.  Its implementation passes through `L¹`, built as the
completion of integrable simple functions, and proves partition independence
and convergence.  The wrapper keeps the thesis name; Mathlib totalises it to
zero outside `Integrable f`, while the thesis uses it only under integrability.
`BochnerConstruction.lean` proves the simple-approximation criterion, existence
and independence of the limit, and the finite indicator-sum formulas explicitly.
declarations.header: noncomputable def bochnerIntegral {Ω : Type u} {V : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (μ : Measure Ω) (f : Ω → V) : V :=
declarations.name: bochnerIntegral

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:bochner-integrability`.

Informal statement: for a measurable function into a separable Banach space,
Bochner integrability is equivalent to scalar integrability of its norm.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `AEStronglyMeasurable f μ` is the exact
measurability hypothesis used in Mathlib's Bochner theory; ordinary Borel
measurability into a separable Banach space implies it.  Mathlib's
`integrable_norm_iff` then gives the norm criterion directly, with scalar
`Integrable` equivalent to finiteness of the integral of the nonnegative norm.
declarations.header: theorem bochnerIntegrable_iff_norm {Ω : Type u} {V : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup V] (μ : Measure Ω) {f : Ω → V} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) : Integrable f μ ↔ Integrable (fun ω => ‖f ω‖) μ :=
declarations.name: bochnerIntegrable_iff_norm

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:expected-value`.

Informal statement: the expected value of a Bochner-integrable Banach-valued
random element `X` is its Bochner integral with respect to the probability
measure.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: expectation is definitionally the same
Mathlib Bochner integral used above, specialised to a measure carrying
`IsProbabilityMeasure`.  The `Integrable X P` hypothesis is accepted to retain
the thesis's domain of definition even though Mathlib totalises the integral.
declarations.header: noncomputable def expectedValue {Ω : Type u} {V : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (X : Ω → V) (_hX : Integrable X P) : V :=
declarations.name: expectedValue

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:lp-spaces`.
Mathlib's carrier is the a.e. quotient; it uses the essential supremum at
exponent infinity and inherits pointwise linear operations.
declarations.header: abbrev LpSpace {Ω : Type u} {V : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup V] (μ : Measure Ω) (p : ℝ≥0∞) := Lp V p μ
declarations.name: LpSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:lp-banach`.

Informal statement: `L^p(Ω, μ; V)` is Banach for every `1 ≤ p ≤ ∞` when `V`
is Banach; if `H` is a real Hilbert space, then `L²(Ω, μ; H)` is Hilbert with
inner product equal to the integral of the pointwise inner product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `Lp V p μ` is already the
almost-everywhere quotient from the thesis.  Its `CompleteSpace` instance
proves the Banach clause for every extended exponent with `1 ≤ p`, including
`∞`.  `MeasureTheory.L2.innerProductSpace` and `L2.inner_def` give the Hilbert
structure and exact displayed inner-product formula.
declarations.header: theorem lpBanach_l2Hilbert {Ω : Type u} {V : Type v} {H : Type w} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] : CompleteSpace (Lp V p μ) ∧ ∀ f g : Lp H 2 μ, inner ℝ f g = ∫ ω, inner ℝ (f ω) (g ω) ∂μ :=
declarations.name: lpBanach_l2Hilbert

declarations.docComment: Right-continuity with left limits on a set, the path regularity called càdlàg.
declarations.header: def IsCadlagOn {V : Type v} [TopologicalSpace V] (f : ℝ → V) (s : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCadlagOn

declarations.docComment: Left-continuity with right limits on a set, the path regularity called càglàd.
declarations.header: def IsCagladOn {V : Type v} [TopologicalSpace V] (f : ℝ → V) (s : Set ℝ) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCagladOn

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:cadlag-caglad-l2`.

Informal statement: a continuous, càdlàg, or càglàd path with values in a
separable real Banach space belongs to `L²` on every compact real interval.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc a b))`
is the thesis membership statement, expressed on `ℝ` with the measure
restricted to `[a,b]` rather than changing to a subtype. One-sided continuity
makes inverse images of open sets measurable. The two one-sided limits give
local boundedness, and compactness gives a uniform bound. These facts imply
`MemLp` for any exponent on this finite measure space. The càglàd case uses
the same argument with the order reversed.
declarations.header: theorem regularPath_memLp_two {V : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V] [CompleteSpace V] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace V] {a b : ℝ} (_hab : a < b) (f : ℝ → V) : (ContinuousOn f (Icc a b) ∨ IsCadlagOn f (Icc a b) ∨ IsCagladOn f (Icc a b)) → MemLp f 2 (volume.restrict (Icc a b)) :=
declarations.name: regularPath_memLp_two

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:finite-integer-valued-measures`.

Informal statement: `𝓜(X)` is the type of finite Borel measures, `𝓝(X)` its
integer-valued subspace, `𝓟(X)` the probability measures, and a Borel measure
is locally finite when every point has an open neighbourhood of finite mass.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Mathlib's `FiniteMeasure X` and
`ProbabilityMeasure X` are the first and third spaces.  The companion
definitions immediately below form the natural-number-valued subtype and
alias `IsLocallyFiniteMeasure`, whose neighbourhood definition is exactly the
thesis clause and which has an equivalent open-neighbourhood theorem.
declarations.header: abbrev FiniteMeasures (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X] := FiniteMeasure X
declarations.name: FiniteMeasures

declarations.docComment: A finite measure whose value on every measurable set is a natural number.
declarations.header: def IsIntegerValuedFiniteMeasure {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : FiniteMeasures X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsIntegerValuedFiniteMeasure

declarations.docComment: The thesis space `𝓝(X)` of finite integer-valued measures.
declarations.header: abbrev FiniteIntegerMeasures (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X] :=
declarations.name: FiniteIntegerMeasures

declarations.docComment: The thesis space `𝓟(X)` of probability measures.
declarations.header: abbrev ProbabilityMeasures (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X] := ProbabilityMeasure X
declarations.name: ProbabilityMeasures

declarations.docComment: Mathlib's neighbourhood formulation of local finiteness.
declarations.header: abbrev IsLocallyFiniteBorelMeasure {X : Type u} [TopologicalSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] (μ : Measure X) :=
declarations.name: IsLocallyFiniteBorelMeasure

declarations.docComment: The finite-measure space equipped with Mathlib's Lévy--Prokhorov distance.
declarations.header: abbrev ProkhorovFiniteMeasures (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X] :=
declarations.name: ProkhorovFiniteMeasures

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric`.

Informal statement: on a complete separable metric space, the Prokhorov
distance is a genuine complete separable metric on finite Borel measures and
metrises weak convergence; it restricts to probability and integer-valued
finite measures.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the exact Prokhorov distance separates
finite Borel measures, metrizes weak convergence, and has a separable space
of finite measures. Uniform tightness of Cauchy sequences and Prokhorov
compactness prove completeness. This wrapper combines the four proved
clauses without any project-specific axioms.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovMetricTheorem {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : (∀ μ ν : ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X, dist μ ν = 0 ↔ μ = ν) ∧ CompleteSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) ∧ TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) ∧ ∀ (μ : ℕ → FiniteMeasures X) (ν : FiniteMeasures X), Tendsto (fun n => _root_.MeasureTheory.LevyProkhorov.ofMeasure (μ n)) atTop (𝓝 (_root_.MeasureTheory.LevyProkhorov.ofMeasure ν)) ↔ Tendsto μ atTop (𝓝 ν) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovMetricTheorem

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:prokhorov-metric`, restrictions to probability and
integer-valued finite measures. The probability subspace is the closed
mass-one level set; the integer subspace uses compact atomic parameters.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovMetricTheorem_restrictions {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : CompleteSpace (_root_.MeasureTheory.LevyProkhorov (ProbabilityMeasure X)) ∧ TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (_root_.MeasureTheory.LevyProkhorov (ProbabilityMeasure X)) ∧ CompleteSpace (Stochastic.PointProcesses.ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) ∧ TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (Stochastic.PointProcesses.ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovMetricTheorem_restrictions

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:kallenberg-random-measure`.

Informal statement: a finite random measure is a family of finite measures
`ω ↦ ξ(ω, ·)` whose evaluation `ω ↦ ξ(ω,B)` is measurable for every measurable
`B`; it is integer-valued when every fibre has natural-number set masses.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: a Mathlib `Kernel Ω X` is exactly a
measurable family of measures, and its `measurable_coe` theorem is the first
thesis clause.  The field `finite` imposes pointwise finiteness without the
stronger uniform bound required by Mathlib's `IsFiniteKernel`.  The companion
predicate below records integer-valuedness fibre by fibre.
declarations.header: structure RandomFiniteMeasure (Ω : Type u) (X : Type v) [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X]
declarations.name: RandomFiniteMeasure

declarations.docComment: A random finite measure whose every fibre is integer-valued.
declarations.header: def IsIntegerValuedRandomMeasure {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] (ξ : RandomFiniteMeasure Ω X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsIntegerValuedRandomMeasure

declarations.docComment: Pointwise conversion of a random finite measure into `FiniteMeasure X`.
declarations.header: def RandomFiniteMeasure.toFiniteMeasure {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] (ξ : RandomFiniteMeasure Ω X) (ω : Ω) : FiniteMeasure X :=
declarations.name: RandomFiniteMeasure.toFiniteMeasure

declarations.docComment: Evaluation measurability of a finite-measure-valued function.
declarations.header: def IsEvaluationMeasurable {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] (Ξ : Ω → FiniteMeasure X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsEvaluationMeasurable

declarations.docComment: Measurability into the Borel space generated by the Prokhorov metric.
declarations.header: def IsProkhorovBorelMeasurable {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [PseudoMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] (Ξ : Ω → FiniteMeasure X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsProkhorovBorelMeasurable

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:A - appendices/measure.tex:438:prop:25`.

Informal statement: on finite Borel measures over a Polish space, a
measure-valued map is measurable for the Prokhorov Borel sigma-algebra if and
only if every measurable-set evaluation is measurable; hence the kernel and
random-element formulations of a finite random measure are equivalent.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `IsEvaluationMeasurable` is the Giry
evaluation sigma-algebra used by Mathlib's `FiniteMeasure`, while
`IsProkhorovBorelMeasurable` explicitly installs the Borel sigma-algebra of
Mathlib's Lévy--Prokhorov pseudometric. The proof first identifies weak and
Prokhorov topologies and establishes separability. A basis of bounded
continuous integral tests makes weak open sets evaluation-measurable.
Portmanteau gives Borel measurability of closed-set evaluations; a pi-system
argument extends this to every Borel set.
declarations.header: theorem randomMeasure_iff_prokhorovMeasurable {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] (Ξ : Ω → FiniteMeasure X) : IsEvaluationMeasurable Ξ ↔ IsProkhorovBorelMeasurable Ξ :=
declarations.name: randomMeasure_iff_prokhorovMeasurable

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:mean-measure`.

Informal statement: if a finite random measure has integrable total mass,
then `B ↦ E[ξ(B)]` is a finite measure, called its mean measure.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: compose the kernel `ξ.toKernel` with the
probability measure using Mathlib's measure--kernel composition `∘ₘ`.  The
`Measure.bind_apply` formula is exactly expectation of each evaluation.  The
assumed finite integral of the total mass proves finiteness at `univ`, allowing
the result to be bundled as `FiniteMeasure X`.
declarations.header: theorem meanMeasure_exists {Ω : Type u} {X : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] (P : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure P] (ξ : RandomFiniteMeasure Ω X) (htotal : (∫⁻ ω, ξ.toKernel ω univ ∂P) < ∞) : ∃ ν : FiniteMeasure X, ∀ B : Set X, MeasurableSet B → (ν : Measure X) B = ∫⁻ ω, ξ.toKernel ω B ∂P :=
declarations.name: meanMeasure_exists

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:lp-point-evaluation`.
Continuity recovers both endpoints on a nondegenerate interval.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq (hab : a < b) (hf : ContinuousOn f (Icc a b)) (hg : ContinuousOn g (Icc a b)) (h : f =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] g) : EqOn f g (Icc a b) :=
declarations.name: continuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq

declarations.docComment: Right continuity recovers every point except the terminal point.
declarations.header: theorem rightContinuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ContinuousWithinAt f (Icc a b ∩ Ici x) x) (hg : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ContinuousWithinAt g (Icc a b ∩ Ici x) x) (h : f =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] g) : EqOn f g (Ico a b) :=
declarations.name: rightContinuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq

declarations.docComment: Left continuity recovers every point except the initial point.
declarations.header: theorem leftContinuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq (hf : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ContinuousWithinAt f (Icc a b ∩ Iic x) x) (hg : ∀ x ∈ Icc a b, ContinuousWithinAt g (Icc a b ∩ Iic x) x) (h : f =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] g) : EqOn f g (Ioc a b) :=
declarations.name: leftContinuous_eqOn_of_ae_eq

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:lp-point-evaluation`.
A càdlàg representative and its terminal value determine the entire path.
declarations.header: theorem cadlag_eqOn_of_ae_eq_of_terminal (hf : IsCadlagOn f (Icc a b)) (hg : IsCadlagOn g (Icc a b)) (h : f =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] g) (hb : f b = g b) : EqOn f g (Icc a b) :=
declarations.name: cadlag_eqOn_of_ae_eq_of_terminal

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:lp-point-evaluation`.
A càglàd representative and its initial value determine the entire path.
declarations.header: theorem caglad_eqOn_of_ae_eq_of_initial (hf : IsCagladOn f (Icc a b)) (hg : IsCagladOn g (Icc a b)) (h : f =ᵐ[volume.restrict (Icc a b)] g) (ha : f a = g a) : EqOn f g (Icc a b) :=
declarations.name: caglad_eqOn_of_ae_eq_of_initial
