Separation inside an arbitrary ambient set `I` cuts out the elements lying in
every inductive set.  The primary `naturals` is the instance in which `I` is the
inductive set supplied by the Infinity axiom.
declarations.header: def leastInductiveZF (I : ZFSet.{u}) : ZFSet.{u} :=
declarations.name: leastInductiveZF

declarations.header: theorem leastInductiveZF_inductive {I : ZFSet.{u}} (hI : IsInductive I) : IsInductive (leastInductiveZF I) :=
declarations.name: leastInductiveZF_inductive

declarations.header: theorem leastInductiveZF_subset {I S : ZFSet.{u}} (hS : IsInductive S) : leastInductiveZF I ⊆ S :=
declarations.name: leastInductiveZF_subset

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `prop:induction` (not the mapped proof): the same two
inclusions for the least inductive set cut out of an arbitrary ambient set `I`.
The mapped set-universe proof is `induction_naturals` in `ZFCFoundations`.
declarations.header: theorem induction_by_leastZF {I S : ZFSet.{u}} (hS : S ⊆ leastInductiveZF I) (hzero : (∅ : ZFSet.{u}) ∈ S) (hstep : ∀ n, n ∈ S → n ∪ ({n} : ZFSet.{u}) ∈ S) : S = leastInductiveZF I :=
declarations.name: induction_by_leastZF

declarations.docComment:
Inductivity of a subset for a specified zero and successor on an arbitrary
type.  The primary typed clause is `univ_subset_of_inductive` in
`DoctoralSetTheory`, for `X := ℕ`, `zero := 0` and `succ := (· + 1)`.
declarations.header: def IsInductiveSet {X : Type u} (zero : X) (succ : X → X) (S : Set X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsInductiveSet

declarations.docComment: Intersection construction of the least inductive set.
declarations.header: def leastInductiveSet {X : Type u} (zero : X) (succ : X → X) : Set X :=
declarations.name: leastInductiveSet

declarations.header: theorem leastInductiveSet_inductive {X : Type u} (zero : X) (succ : X → X) : IsInductiveSet zero succ (leastInductiveSet zero succ) :=
declarations.name: leastInductiveSet_inductive

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `prop:induction` (not the mapped proof): for an
arbitrary zero and successor, an inductive subset of the least inductive set
equals it, by the two inclusions and without any natural-number recursor.  The
mapped proofs are `ZFC.induction_naturals` in `ZFCFoundations` (set universe)
and `induction_set` in `DoctoralSetTheory` (typed `ℕ`).
declarations.header: theorem induction_by_least_inductive_set {X : Type u} (zero : X) (succ : X → X) (S : Set X) (hS : IsInductiveSet zero succ S) (hsub : S ⊆ leastInductiveSet zero succ) : S = leastInductiveSet zero succ :=
declarations.name: induction_by_least_inductive_set

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:bijection`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsInjective {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (f : X → Y) : Prop := Function.Injective f
declarations.name: IsInjective

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:bijection`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsSurjective {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (f : X → Y) : Prop := Function.Surjective f
declarations.name: IsSurjective

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:bijection`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsBijective {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (f : X → Y) : Prop := Function.Bijective f
declarations.name: IsBijective

declarations.docComment:
`ℕ₀ = Set.univ` is contained in every inductive subset of `ℕ`. This is the
typed form of the Infinity clause that `ℕ₀` is the least inductive set; it is
the one place where Lean's natural-number recursor enters.
declarations.header: theorem univ_subset_of_inductive (S : Set ℕ) (hzero : 0 ∈ S) (hstep : ∀ n, n ∈ S → n + 1 ∈ S) : Set.univ ⊆ S :=
declarations.name: univ_subset_of_inductive

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:induction`.

Typed restatement over Lean's `ℕ`, following the thesis inclusions: `S ⊆ ℕ₀`
holds trivially, and `ℕ₀ ⊆ S` because `S` is inductive and `ℕ₀` is the least
inductive set (`univ_subset_of_inductive`); the two inclusions give `S = ℕ₀`.
The mapped set-universe proof, in which `ℕ₀` is literally constructed as the
least inductive set, is `ZFC.induction_naturals` in `ZFCFoundations`.
declarations.header: theorem induction_set (S : Set ℕ) (hzero : 0 ∈ S) (hstep : ∀ n, n ∈ S → n + 1 ∈ S) : S = Set.univ :=
declarations.name: induction_set

declarations.docComment: The finite history before the next recursion step.
declarations.header: def recursiveHistory {X : Type u} (G : Tuple X → X) : (n : ℕ) → Fin n → X | 0 => Fin.elim0 | n + 1 => Fin.snoc (recursiveHistory G n) (G ⟨n, recursiveHistory G n⟩) /-- Original label: `thm:recursion`. Lean's value at n corresponds to the manuscript's value at n+1. -/ def recursiveSequence {X : Type u} (G : Tuple X → X) (n : ℕ) : X :=
declarations.name: recursiveHistory

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:recursion`.
Lean's value at n corresponds to the manuscript's value at n+1.
declarations.header: def recursiveSequence {X : Type u} (G : Tuple X → X) (n : ℕ) : X :=
declarations.name: recursiveSequence

declarations.header: theorem recursiveHistory_eq_sequence {X : Type u} (G : Tuple X → X) (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) : recursiveHistory G n i = recursiveSequence G i.val :=
declarations.name: recursiveHistory_eq_sequence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:recursion`.
The displayed history-dependent rule has exactly one solution, including
rules whose next value depends on every earlier value.
declarations.header: theorem recursion_existsUnique {X : Type u} (G : Tuple X → X) : ∃! f : ℕ → X, ∀ n, f n = G ⟨n, fun i : Fin n => f i.val⟩ :=
declarations.name: recursion_existsUnique

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: abbrev CardinalLE (X : Type u) (Y : Type v) : Prop := Nonempty (X ↪ Y)
declarations.name: CardinalLE

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: abbrev Equinumerous (X : Type u) (Y : Type v) : Prop := Nonempty (X ≃ Y)
declarations.name: Equinumerous

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsFiniteType (X : Type u) : Prop := Finite X
declarations.name: IsFiniteType

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: abbrev IsCountableType (X : Type u) : Prop := Countable X
declarations.name: IsCountableType

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: abbrev HasContinuumCardinality (X : Type u) : Prop := Equinumerous X ℝ
declarations.name: HasContinuumCardinality

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
The finite-type predicate is equivalent to exactly the source's finite
initial-segment criterion, including the empty type and n=0.
declarations.header: theorem isFiniteType_iff (X : Type u) : IsFiniteType X ↔ ∃ n : ℕ, Nonempty (X ≃ Fin n) :=
declarations.name: isFiniteType_iff

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:cardinality`.
declarations.header: theorem isCountableType_iff (X : Type u) : IsCountableType X ↔ CardinalLE X ℕ :=
declarations.name: isCountableType_iff

declarations.docComment: Original label: `thm:cantor-schroeder-bernstein`.
declarations.header: theorem cantorSchroederBernstein {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (hXY : CardinalLE X Y) (hYX : CardinalLE Y X) : Equinumerous X Y :=
declarations.name: cantorSchroederBernstein

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:well-ordering`.
The conclusion uses the exact non-strict well-order definition in the appendix.
declarations.header: theorem wellOrderingTheorem_explicit (α : Type u) : ∃ O : PartialOrderRelation α, O.IsWellOrdered :=
declarations.name: wellOrderingTheorem_explicit

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:zorns-lemma`.
Chain upper bounds and maximality use the literal quantified source conditions.
declarations.header: theorem zornsLemma_explicit {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] (h : ∀ C : Set α, (∀ x ∈ C, ∀ y ∈ C, x ≤ y ∨ y ≤ x) → ∃ z : α, ∀ c ∈ C, c ≤ z) : ∃ m : α, ∀ x, m ≤ x → x = m :=
declarations.name: zornsLemma_explicit

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:arbitrary-product-space`.
The dependent product is equivalent to the source's compatible functions with
codomain the ordinary union of the component sets.
declarations.header: def arbitraryProductUnionEquiv {ι : Type u} {α : Type v} (X : ι → Set α) : ArbitraryProduct X ≃ {f : ι → (⋃ i, X i) // ∀ i, (f i : α) ∈ X i}
declarations.name: arbitraryProductUnionEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:bijection-not-homeomorphism`.
Two identical infinite component sets overlap but their ordinary and tagged
unions still have a bijection. Thus an arbitrary bijection cannot replace
injectivity of the canonical tag-forgetting map.
declarations.header: theorem overlapping_family_has_union_bijection : ∃ S : Bool → Set ℕ, ¬ MarketRepresentation.PairwiseDisjoint S ∧ Nonempty (MarketRepresentation.SetDisjointUnion S ≃ {x : ℕ // ∃ i, x ∈ S i}) :=
declarations.name: overlapping_family_has_union_bijection

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:existence`.

Informal statement: there exists a set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: for every ambient type, its empty subset
is already a set, so the typed analogue of existence is constructive.
declarations.header: theorem setExistence (α : Type u) : ∃ x : Set α, x = x :=
declarations.name: setExistence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:extensionality`.

Informal statement: two sets with exactly the same elements are equal.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is Mathlib's extensionality theorem
for typed sets, applied directly to the pointwise membership equivalence.
declarations.header: theorem setExtensionality {α : Type u} {x y : Set α} (h : ∀ z, z ∈ x ↔ z ∈ y) : x = y :=
declarations.name: setExtensionality

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:scheme-of-comprehension`.

Informal statement: a property cuts out a subset of any existing set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean's set-builder notation is a predicate,
so restricted comprehension is the set whose predicate is membership in `z`
conjoined with `φ`; no new axiom is required.
declarations.header: theorem separation {α : Type u} (z : Set α) (φ : α → Prop) : ∃ x : Set α, ∀ y, y ∈ x ↔ y ∈ z ∧ φ y :=
declarations.name: separation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:empty-set-unique`.

Informal statement: there exists a unique set having no elements.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: typed restatement of the thesis argument.
Existence (`setExistence`) supplies a set `x`; Separation (`separation`) with
the formula `y ≠ y` cuts out of `x` a set with no elements; Extensionality
(`setExtensionality`) identifies any two sets with no elements, because both
membership predicates are everywhere false. The literal set-universe version is
`ZFC.unique_empty` in `ZFCFoundations`.
declarations.header: theorem existsUniqueEmptySet (α : Type u) : ∃! x : Set α, ∀ z, z ∉ x :=
declarations.name: existsUniqueEmptySet

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:empty-set`.

Informal statement: `emptySet α` denotes the set with no elements of `α`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis notation `∅` is represented by
Mathlib's empty typed set and exposed under a descriptive bridge name.
declarations.header: def emptySet (α : Type u) : Set α :=
declarations.name: emptySet

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:no-universal-set`.

Informal statement: an untyped membership universe closed under separation
cannot contain an object that contains every object.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean has a typed universal subset
`Set.univ`, so the literal untyped ZF sentence would be false after naïve
translation.  We instead formalise the thesis's Russell proof over an abstract
self-membership relation and its separation principle; the diagonal object is
in itself exactly when it is not in itself.
declarations.header: theorem noUniversalObjectOfSeparation {U : Type u} (mem : U → U → Prop) (separate : ∀ z : U, ∀ φ : U → Prop, ∃ x : U, ∀ y : U, mem y x ↔ mem y z ∧ φ y) : ¬ ∃ universal : U, ∀ x : U, mem x universal :=
declarations.name: noUniversalObjectOfSeparation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:foundation`.

Informal statement: every nonempty set has an element with no predecessor from
that set under membership.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the ZF membership relation is abstracted
as a well-founded relation `r`; `WellFounded.has_min` supplies precisely the
minimal element asserted by Foundation.
declarations.header: theorem foundation {α : Type u} (r : α → α → Prop) (hr : WellFounded r) (x : Set α) (hx : x.Nonempty) : ∃ y ∈ x, ¬ ∃ z, z ∈ x ∧ r z y :=
declarations.name: foundation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:pairing`.

Informal statement: for any two elements there is a set containing exactly
those two elements.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the pair set `{x, y}` is a primitive
finite-set notation in Mathlib, and simplification proves its membership law.
declarations.header: theorem pairing {α : Type u} (x y : α) : ∃ z : Set α, ∀ w, w ∈ z ↔ w = x ∨ w = y :=
declarations.name: pairing

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:union`.

Informal statement: a family of sets has a union containing exactly the
elements that occur in one of its members.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the witness is the typed predicate
`x ↦ ∃ X ∈ F, x ∈ X`, which is Mathlib's set-theoretic union construction.
declarations.header: theorem unionFamily {α : Type u} (F : Set (Set α)) : ∃ U : Set α, ∀ x, x ∈ U ↔ ∃ X ∈ F, x ∈ X :=
declarations.name: unionFamily

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:product-space`.

Informal statement: the product space consists of the ordered pairs whose first
coordinate is in `X` and whose second coordinate is in `Y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean uses its typed ordered-pair type
instead of the Kuratowski encoding; Mathlib's set product has the same
membership condition used throughout the thesis.
declarations.header: def productSpace {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (X : Set α) (Y : Set β) : Set (α × β) :=
declarations.name: productSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:relation`.

Informal statement: a relation from `X` to `Y` is a subset of `X × Y`, with a
domain and range obtained by existential projection.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the graph and its subset certificate are
bundled; the definitions `Relation.domain` and `Relation.range` below implement
the two projections in the displayed thesis formulas.
declarations.header: structure Relation {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (X : Set α) (Y : Set β)
declarations.name: Relation

declarations.header: def domain {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {X : Set α} {Y : Set β} (R : Relation X Y) : Set α :=
declarations.name: domain

declarations.header: def range {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {X : Set α} {Y : Set β} (R : Relation X Y) : Set β :=
declarations.name: range

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:equivalence-relation`.

Informal statement: an equivalence relation on `X` is supported on `X × X` and
is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive there.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: each of the three thesis clauses is
recorded explicitly, together with the subset-of-product condition implicit in
the manuscript's notation `∼ ⊆ X × X`.
declarations.header: def IsEquivalenceRelationOn {α : Type u} (X : Set α) (r : α → α → Prop) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsEquivalenceRelationOn

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:equivalence-class`.

Informal statement: the equivalence class of `x` contains the elements of `X`
related to `x`; the quotient is the collection of all such classes.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the class is a set-builder predicate,
while `equivalenceClassSpace` below takes its range over representatives in
`X`, matching the two displayed constructions in the thesis.
declarations.header: def equivalenceClass {α : Type u} (X : Set α) (r : α → α → Prop) (x : α) : Set α :=
declarations.name: equivalenceClass

declarations.header: def equivalenceClassSpace {α : Type u} (X : Set α) (r : α → α → Prop) : Set (Set α) :=
declarations.name: equivalenceClassSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:function`.

Informal statement: a function from the set `X` to the set `Y` assigns exactly
one element of `Y` to each element of `X`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the subtype function type `X → Y`
builds totality, uniqueness, and codomain membership into the type itself.
declarations.header: abbrev FunctionBetween {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (X : Set α) (Y : Set β) :=
declarations.name: FunctionBetween

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:graph`.

Informal statement: the graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs
`(x, f x)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the graph is represented as the predicate
on subtype pairs whose second coordinate equals the function value.
declarations.header: def graph {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {X : Set α} {Y : Set β} (f : FunctionBetween X Y) : Set (X × Y) :=
declarations.name: graph

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:graph-defines`.

Informal statement: a function is completely determined by its graph.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: functions and graphs have different
types in Lean, so the thesis's set-theoretic equality becomes injectivity of
the graph construction; the proof evaluates graph equality at `(x, f x)`.
declarations.header: theorem graph_injective {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {X : Set α} {Y : Set β} : Function.Injective (fun f : FunctionBetween X Y => graph f) :=
declarations.name: graph_injective

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:empty-domain-function`.

Informal statement: functions with empty domain have the same empty graph,
even when their codomains differ.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: equality of differently typed functions
is not a well-formed Lean proposition.  Both graphs are therefore embedded in
the common codomain sum; their ranges are equal because an `Empty` input cannot
exist, which is the graph argument used in the thesis proof.
declarations.header: theorem emptyDomainFunctionsHaveEqualGraphs {β : Type v} {γ : Type w} (f : Empty → β) (g : Empty → γ) : Set.range (fun x : Empty => (x, @Sum.inl β γ (f x))) = Set.range (fun x : Empty => (x, @Sum.inr β γ (g x))) :=
declarations.name: emptyDomainFunctionsHaveEqualGraphs

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:replacement`.

Informal statement: the outputs assigned uniquely to the elements of `X` form
a set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: dependent type theory already permits
the image predicate `{y | ∃ x ∈ X, φ x y}`; the functional premise is retained
to match the thesis scheme, but no additional axiom is needed to form the set.
declarations.header: theorem replacement {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (X : Set α) (φ : α → β → Prop) (_hfunctional : ∀ x ∈ X, ∃! y, φ x y) : ∃ Y : Set β, ∀ y, y ∈ Y ↔ ∃ x ∈ X, φ x y :=
declarations.name: replacement

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:infinity`.

Informal statement: there is a set containing zero and closed under successor,
and hence an infinite set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the natural-number type is primitive in
Lean; its universal subset witnesses the inductive-set formulation used by the
thesis and is closed under `n ↦ n + 1`.
declarations.header: theorem infinity : ∃ X : Set ℕ, 0 ∈ X ∧ ∀ n ∈ X, n + 1 ∈ X :=
declarations.name: infinity

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:subset`.

Informal statement: `Y` is a subset of `X` when membership in `Y` implies
membership in `X`; it is strict when some element of `X` is absent from `Y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `IsSubset` spells out Mathlib's `Y ⊆ X`
predicate, and `IsStrictSubset` below follows the thesis's explicit witness
formulation rather than relying only on notation.
declarations.header: def IsSubset {α : Type u} (Y X : Set α) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsSubset

declarations.header: def IsStrictSubset {α : Type u} (Y X : Set α) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsStrictSubset

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:power-set`.

Informal statement: for every set `X`, the collection of all subsets of `X`
is itself a set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: a set of sets is a predicate on `Set α`;
restricted comprehension with predicate `Z ⊆ X` constructs the witness.
declarations.header: theorem powerSetExistence {α : Type u} (X : Set α) : ∃ P : Set (Set α), ∀ Z, Z ∈ P ↔ Z ⊆ X :=
declarations.name: powerSetExistence

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:power-set`.

Informal statement: `powerSet X` is the set of all subsets of `X`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the direct typed set-builder
version of the thesis notation `℘(X)`.
declarations.header: def powerSet {α : Type u} (X : Set α) : Set (Set α) :=
declarations.name: powerSet

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:choice`.

Informal statement: every family of nonempty sets admits a function selecting
one member from each set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: each member of the family is represented
by a subtype element carrying its membership proof; `Classical.choose` selects
from the supplied nonemptiness proof.  This uses Lean's standard classical
choice principle, not a project-specific axiom.
declarations.header: theorem choiceForFamily {α : Type u} (𝒳 : Set (Set α)) (hne : ∀ A ∈ 𝒳, A.Nonempty) : ∃ f : 𝒳 → α, ∀ A : 𝒳, f A ∈ (A : Set α) :=
declarations.name: choiceForFamily

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:ordered-sets`.

Informal statement: a partial order is reflexive, antisymmetric, and
transitive; totality compares distinct elements, and a well-order gives every
nonempty subset a least element.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `PartialOrderRelation` records the three
displayed axioms for an explicit relation.  The predicates `IsTotal` and
`IsWellOrdered` below add the manuscript's remaining clauses without changing
its order convention.
declarations.header: structure PartialOrderRelation (α : Type u)
declarations.name: PartialOrderRelation

declarations.header: def IsTotal {α : Type u} (O : PartialOrderRelation α) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsTotal

declarations.header: def IsWellOrdered {α : Type u} (O : PartialOrderRelation α) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsWellOrdered

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:well-ordering`.

Informal statement: every set can be equipped with a well-order.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: a thesis set is represented by its
subtype; Mathlib's `WellOrderingRel` supplies a well-founded strict total order
on every type, which is the standard type-theoretic well-ordering theorem.
declarations.header: theorem wellOrderingTheorem (α : Type u) : ∃ r : α → α → Prop, IsWellOrder α r :=
declarations.name: wellOrderingTheorem

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:zorns-lemma`.

Informal statement: if every chain in a partially ordered set has an upper
bound, then the set has a maximal element.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is Mathlib's `zorn_le` with the
thesis hypotheses written using `IsChain`, `BddAbove`, and `IsMax` for the
ambient partial order.
declarations.header: theorem zornsLemma {α : Type u} [PartialOrder α] (h : ∀ C : Set α, IsChain (· ≤ ·) C → BddAbove C) : ∃ maximal : α, IsMax maximal :=
declarations.name: zornsLemma

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:arbitrary-product-space`.

Informal statement: the arbitrary product of a family `(X i)` is the type of
choice functions whose `i`th value lies in `X i`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: returning an element of the subtype
`X i` enforces the displayed membership condition at every index, including
for dependent families.
declarations.header: abbrev ArbitraryProduct {ι : Type u} {α : Type v} (X : ι → Set α) :=
declarations.name: ArbitraryProduct

declarations.header: def binaryFamily {α : Type u} (X Y : Set α) : Bool → Set α | false => X | true => Y /-- Original label: `prop:binary-product-space`. Informal statement: the binary Cartesian product is equivalent to the two-index arbitrary product. Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Bool` is a two-element index type; the equivalence sends a pair to the dependent function taking `false` to its first coordinate and `true` to its second, with the inverse given
declarations.name: binaryFamily

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:binary-product-space`.

Informal statement: the binary Cartesian product is equivalent to the
two-index arbitrary product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Bool` is a two-element index type; the
equivalence sends a pair to the dependent function taking `false` to its first
coordinate and `true` to its second, with the inverse given by evaluation.
declarations.header: def binaryProductEquiv {α : Type u} (X Y : Set α) : X × Y ≃ ArbitraryProduct (binaryFamily X Y)
declarations.name: binaryProductEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:sequence`.

Informal statement: an `X`-sequence is a function from the natural numbers to
`X`, written `(xₙ)ₙ` instead of ordinary function notation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: a sequence in the thesis set `X` is the
function type `ℕ → X`, where the subtype codomain records membership in `X`.
declarations.header: abbrev Sequence {α : Type u} (X : Set α) :=
declarations.name: Sequence

declarations.docComment: Original label: `axiom:existence`.
declarations.header: theorem existence : ∃ x : ZFSet.{u}, x = x := ⟨∅, rfl⟩
declarations.name: existence

declarations.docComment: Original label: `axiom:extensionality`.
declarations.header: theorem extensionality (x y : ZFSet.{u}) (h : ∀ z, z ∈ x ↔ z ∈ y) : x = y :=
declarations.name: extensionality

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:scheme-of-comprehension`.
External parameters in the formula are included in the predicate.
declarations.header: theorem separation (z : ZFSet.{u}) (φ : ZFSet.{u} → Prop) : ∃ x : ZFSet.{u}, ∀ y, y ∈ x ↔ y ∈ z ∧ φ y :=
declarations.name: separation

declarations.docComment:
Original labels: `prop:empty-set-unique`, `defn:empty-set`.

The thesis argument: Existence supplies a set `x`; Separation with the formula
`y ≠ y` cuts out of `x` a set with no elements; Extensionality identifies any
two sets with no elements, since they vacuously have the same elements.
declarations.header: theorem unique_empty : ∃! x : ZFSet.{u}, ∀ z, z ∉ x :=
declarations.name: unique_empty

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:no-universal-set`.
The manuscript's Russell argument, with its separation premise discharged.
declarations.header: theorem no_universal_set : ¬ ∃ y : ZFSet.{u}, ∀ x : ZFSet.{u}, x ∈ y :=
declarations.name: no_universal_set

declarations.docComment: Original label: `axiom:foundation`.
declarations.header: theorem foundation (x : ZFSet.{u}) (hx : x ≠ ∅) : ∃ y, y ∈ x ∧ ¬ ∃ z, z ∈ x ∧ z ∈ y :=
declarations.name: foundation

declarations.header: theorem not_self_member (x : ZFSet.{u}) : x ∉ x := ZFSet.mem_irrefl x
declarations.name: not_self_member

declarations.docComment: Original label: `axiom:pairing`.
declarations.header: theorem pairing (x y : ZFSet.{u}) : ∃ z : ZFSet.{u}, ∀ w, w ∈ z ↔ w = x ∨ w = y :=
declarations.name: pairing

declarations.docComment: Original label: `axiom:union`.
declarations.header: theorem union (F : ZFSet.{u}) : ∃ U : ZFSet.{u}, ∀ x, x ∈ U ↔ ∃ X, X ∈ F ∧ x ∈ X :=
declarations.name: union

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `axiom:replacement`.
The functional image is a member of the same set universe, not merely an

by Extensionality.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: convergence clause of
`thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Informal statement: on a Polish Borel space, weak convergence of finite
measures is equivalent to convergence to zero in the Prokhorov metric.

Proof: total mass is 1-Lipschitz in the Prokhorov metric and rescaling is
jointly continuous. Away from zero, normalize and use Mathlib's probability
topology theorem. At zero, total mass controls convergence directly. The
helper establishes an identity homeomorphism and arbitrary-filter convergence;
this wrapper preserves the thesis's sequence formulation and Polish hypotheses.
declarations.header: theorem finiteMeasure_prokhorov_metrizes_weakConvergence_polish {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] {μ : ℕ → FiniteMeasures X} {ν : FiniteMeasures X} : WeakConvergesFiniteMeasures μ ν ↔ ProkhorovConvergesFiniteMeasures μ ν :=
declarations.name: finiteMeasure_prokhorov_metrizes_weakConvergence_polish

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: complete/separable clause for `\mathcal{M}(X)`.

Informal statement: if `X` is Polish, then the finite-measure space
`(\mathcal{M}(X),ρ)` is complete.

Proof: finite atomic approximations give uniform finite mass covers for
a Cauchy sequence. Intersections of closed covers at decreasing scales are
compact on the complete base and prove tightness. Bounded total masses and
Mathlib's finite-measure Prokhorov compactness theorem give a weakly
convergent subsequence. The proved topology equivalence and the Cauchy
property give convergence of the whole sequence in the Prokhorov metric.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovFiniteMeasures_complete_polish {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : CompleteSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovFiniteMeasures_complete_polish

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: complete/separable clause for `\mathcal{M}(X)`.

Informal statement: if `X` is Polish, then the finite-measure space
`(\mathcal{M}(X),ρ)` is separable.

Proof: finite atomic measures are dense by a measurable small-diameter
partition and a finite truncation with a small mass tail. Their parameter
spaces form a countable union of separable finite products, and the atomic
maps are continuous. No completeness assumption is used by the helper.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovFiniteMeasures_separable_polish {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovFiniteMeasures_separable_polish

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: complete/separable clause for `\mathcal{N}(X)`.

Informal statement: if `X` is Polish, then the finite integer-valued measure
space `(\mathcal{N}(X),ρ)` is complete.

Proof: a Cauchy sequence is uniformly tight. A common compact set with mass
tail less than one contains every positive integer atom. Bounded total mass
bounds both the number of atoms and their multiplicities. Atomic decompositions
place the whole sequence in a compact image of finitely many finite products
of that compact set. A convergent subsequence and the Cauchy property give
convergence in the integer-valued subspace.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures_complete_polish {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : CompleteSpace (ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures_complete_polish

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: complete/separable clause for `\mathcal{N}(X)`.

Informal statement: if `X` is Polish, then the finite integer-valued measure
space `(\mathcal{N}(X),ρ)` is separable.

Proof: fixed natural multiplicities define a Lipschitz map from each finite
product of the base space. The countable union of these separable layers maps
onto every finite integer measure by the proved atomic decomposition.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures_separable_polish {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures_separable_polish

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Original label: full summary of
`thm:prokhorov-metric-weak-convergence-polish`.

Informal statement: under Polish Borel hypotheses, the Prokhorov metric
metrizes weak convergence of finite measures, and the Prokhorov finite-measure
and finite-integer-measure spaces are complete and separable.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: the Prokhorov distance definition, metric carrier, and
distance-identification theorem are in `Stochastic.PointProcesses`.
All clauses, including both completeness conclusions, are proved above.
This wrapper records the theorem as one audit-friendly declaration while
keeping each dependency separately named. Its historical name is retained.
declarations.header: theorem prokhorovMetricWeakConvergencePolish_externalSummary {X : Type u} [MetricSpace X] [MeasurableSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [BorelSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] {μ : ℕ → FiniteMeasures X} {ν : FiniteMeasures X} : (WeakConvergesFiniteMeasures μ ν ↔ ProkhorovConvergesFiniteMeasures μ ν) ∧ CompleteSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) ∧ TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (ProkhorovFiniteMeasures X) ∧ CompleteSpace (ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) ∧ TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (ProkhorovFiniteIntegerMeasures X) :=
declarations.name: prokhorovMetricWeakConvergencePolish_externalSummary

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Original label: `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Informal statement: on a standard Borel space, every finite integer-valued
measure has a finite atomic representation
`\sum_{k \leq \kappa} β_k δ_{x_k}`, with positive natural multiplicities and
distinct atoms; such representations are unique up to permutation of the finite
atom index set.

Proof note: `AtomicDecompositionProof.exists_atomicDecomposition` proves
that integer-valued mass and outer regularity concentrate the measure on
finitely many positive-mass singletons. Classical choice selects one of the
proved decompositions. This declaration no longer introduces an axiom.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `StandardBorelSpace X` is mathlib's measurable-space analogue
of the thesis' standard Borel hypothesis. The conclusion is the previously
defined `AtomicDecomposition`, so the result is aligned with the
formal target used in `prop:tuple-measure-surjective`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] (μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X) : AtomicDecomposition μ :=
declarations.name: finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Original label: uniqueness clause of `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Informal statement: two finite atomic decompositions of the same finite
integer-valued measure have the same number of atoms, and after reindexing one
finite atom list by a permutation, the atoms and multiplicities agree.

Proof note: singleton masses identify corresponding atoms and their weights.
The atom correspondence is a bijection of the finite index sets, hence a
permutation after identifying their cardinalities.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: the thesis treats uniqueness as equality
up to permutation of `{1, ..., κ}`. Lean represents the finite index set as
`Fin d.length`; once the two lengths are equal, `Fin.cast` transports a
permuted index into the second decomposition's domain.
declarations.header: theorem finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition_unique_up_to_permutation {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] {μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X} (d e : AtomicDecomposition μ) : ∃ length_equality : d.length = e.length, ∃ atom_index_permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin d.length), ∀ i : Fin d.length, e.atom (Fin.cast length_equality (atom_index_permutation i)) = d.atom i ∧ e.multiplicity (Fin.cast length_equality (atom_index_permutation i)) = d.multiplicity i :=
declarations.name: finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition_unique_up_to_permutation

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Original label: existence clause of `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Informal statement: every finite integer-valued measure on a standard Borel
space admits a finite atomic decomposition with positive integer
multiplicities and distinct atoms.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: existence and uniqueness are both proved
in `Stochastic.AtomicDecompositionProof`; the older interface names are kept
so downstream theorem statements remain stable.
declarations.header: theorem finiteIntegerMeasure_exists_atomicDecomposition {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] (μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X) : Nonempty (AtomicDecomposition μ) :=
declarations.name: finiteIntegerMeasure_exists_atomicDecomposition

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Original label: full checked summary of `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Informal statement: every finite integer-valued measure on a standard Borel
space admits an atomic decomposition, and any two such decompositions are the
same after a finite permutation of the atom index set.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: the proved existence and uniqueness
clauses are bundled here for trace review. The historical declaration name is
retained, but this theorem no longer depends on a project-specific axiom.
declarations.header: theorem finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition_externalSummary {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] (μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X) : Nonempty (AtomicDecomposition μ) ∧ ∀ d e : AtomicDecomposition μ, ∃ length_equality : d.length = e.length, ∃ atom_index_permutation : Equiv.Perm (Fin d.length), ∀ i : Fin d.length, e.atom (Fin.cast length_equality (atom_index_permutation i)) = d.atom i ∧ e.multiplicity (Fin.cast length_equality (atom_index_permutation i)) = d.multiplicity i :=
declarations.name: finiteIntegerMeasure_atomicDecomposition_externalSummary
