declarations.header: theorem loss_decomposition (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (y : F) (x : E) : ‖y - A x‖ ^ 2 = ‖y - A (inverse A y)‖ ^ 2 + ‖A (inverse A y) - A x‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: loss_decomposition

declarations.header: theorem minimizer_iff (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (y : F) (x : E) : (∀ z, ‖y - A x‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖y - A z‖ ^ 2) ↔ A x = A (inverse A y) :=
declarations.name: minimizer_iff

declarations.header: theorem unique_minimum_norm_minimizer (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (y : F) (x : E) (hx : ∀ z, ‖y - A x‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖y - A z‖ ^ 2) (hn : ‖x‖ ≤ ‖inverse A y‖) : x = inverse A y :=
declarations.name: unique_minimum_norm_minimizer

declarations.header: theorem coefficient_norm_decomposition (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] F) (y : F) (x : E) (hx : A x = A (inverse A y)) : ‖x‖ ^ 2 = ‖inverse A y‖ ^ 2 + ‖x - inverse A y‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: coefficient_norm_decomposition

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `cor:unique-sorting-map-total-order`.
Both outputs are sorted and have the same multiplicities. Uniqueness of a
sorted representative therefore makes any sorting rule permutation invariant,
as in the source proof.
declarations.header: theorem sortingRule_permutation_invariant {X : Type*} [LinearOrder X] (σ : SortingRule X) (x : Tuple X) (π : FinitePermutation x.length) : σ.sort (permute x π) = σ.sort x :=
declarations.name: sortingRule_permutation_invariant

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/1_economics.tex`.

Original label: `prin:agent-actions`.

Informal statement: an action is admissible for an agent in a state exactly
when resources, authority over the affected orders, and venue rules permit it.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: all three constraints are explicit
state-dependent predicates. No rationality or utility condition is imposed.
declarations.header: def AdmissibleAction {Agent : Type u} {State : Type v} {Action : Type w} (resourcePermitted authorityPermitted venuePermitted : Agent → State → Action → Prop) (agent : Agent) (state : State) (action : Action) : Prop :=
declarations.name: AdmissibleAction

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/1_economics.tex`.

Original label: `prin:finitism`.

Informal statement: a market observed on one finite interval carries a finite
set of participating agents and, for each participant, a finite set of
actions performed during that interval.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Finset` records both finiteness claims
as data and leaves the agent and action types otherwise unrestricted.
declarations.header: structure FiniteMarketInterval (Agent : Type u) (Action : Type v)
declarations.name: FiniteMarketInterval

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/1_economics.tex`.

Original label: `prin:clearing`.

Informal statement: a market is cleared precisely when there is no exchange
that is both admissible and jointly acceptable to the involved agents.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis biconditional is used as the
definition of `IsCleared`; the existential packages a remaining exchange and
the two required properties.
declarations.header: def IsCleared {Exchange : Type u} (admissible jointlyWilling : Exchange → Prop) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsCleared

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:52:rem:2`

Informal statement: two components of a dependent sum with different tags
are disjoint, even when their payload types or underlying sets overlap.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: applying `Sigma.fst` to an alleged
equality of tagged elements would identify the tags, contradicting the
hypothesis that they differ.
declarations.header: theorem sigma_mk_ne_of_tag_ne {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {a b : A} (hab : a ≠ b) (x : X a) (y : X b) : Sigma.mk a x ≠ Sigma.mk b y :=
declarations.name: sigma_mk_ne_of_tag_ne

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:adm-static`.

Informal statement: unrestricted tagged static orders are canonically
equivalent to price/quantity/direction triples.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the equivalence merely reassociates and
reorders the coordinates of the dependent sum; its inverse restores the
direction tag.
declarations.header: def unrestrictedStaticOrdersEquiv : (Σ _ : OrderSide, ℝ × Quantity) ≃ ((ℝ × Quantity) × OrderSide)
declarations.name: unrestrictedStaticOrdersEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: an agent-constrained static order stores its direction and
agent together with proofs that its price and quantity are admissible for
that pair.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this dependent-sum type is the literal
Lean counterpart of the restricted disjoint union used in the thesis.
declarations.header: abbrev AgentStaticOrder (Agent : Type u) (P : OrderSide → Agent → Set ℝ) (Q : OrderSide → Agent → Set Quantity) : Type u :=
declarations.name: AgentStaticOrder

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: forgetting admissibility proofs embeds a constrained
static order into the unrestricted price/quantity/direction/agent product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the tag and both subtype values are
retained, so equality in the target determines equality in the source.
declarations.header: def agentStaticOrderEmbedding {Agent : Type u} {P : OrderSide → Agent → Set ℝ} {Q : OrderSide → Agent → Set Quantity} : AgentStaticOrder Agent P Q → ((ℝ × Quantity) × (OrderSide × Agent)) :=
declarations.name: agentStaticOrderEmbedding

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:agent-adm-static`.

Informal statement: the canonical map from agent-constrained static orders to
the unrestricted product is injective, though it need not be surjective.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: injectivity follows because the map
forgets only proof fields; subtype proof irrelevance reconstructs the original
dependent-sum element.
declarations.header: theorem agentStaticOrderEmbedding_injective {Agent : Type u} {P : OrderSide → Agent → Set ℝ} {Q : OrderSide → Agent → Set Quantity} : Function.Injective (agentStaticOrderEmbedding (P := P) (Q := Q)) :=
declarations.name: agentStaticOrderEmbedding_injective

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:adm-dyn`.

Informal statement: unrestricted tagged dynamic orders are canonically
equivalent to price/quantity/time/direction tuples.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: as in the static example, the map is a
coordinate reassociation; time is represented by the nonnegative-real type.
declarations.header: def unrestrictedDynamicOrdersEquiv : (Σ _ : OrderSide × Quantity, ℝ × Quantity) ≃ (((ℝ × Quantity) × Quantity) × OrderSide)
declarations.name: unrestrictedDynamicOrdersEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: a dynamically constrained order stores direction, agent,
and submission time together with an admissible price and quantity.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the admissible sets depend on all three
indices exactly as in the thesis disjoint union.
declarations.header: abbrev AgentDynamicOrder (Agent : Type u) (P : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set ℝ) (Q : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set Quantity) : Type u :=
declarations.name: AgentDynamicOrder

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: forgetting the admissibility proofs maps a dynamically
constrained order into the unrestricted coordinate product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: all mathematical coordinates are kept;
only membership proofs are erased.
declarations.header: def agentDynamicOrderEmbedding {Agent : Type u} {P : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set ℝ} {Q : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set Quantity} : AgentDynamicOrder Agent P Q → (((ℝ × Quantity) × (OrderSide × Agent)) × Quantity) :=
declarations.name: agentDynamicOrderEmbedding

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:agent-adm-dyn`.

Informal statement: the canonical map from time-varying constrained orders to
the unrestricted dynamic-order product is injective.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: equality of the retained coordinates
fixes the dependent tag and both subtype values; proof irrelevance then gives
equality of the original orders.
declarations.header: theorem agentDynamicOrderEmbedding_injective {Agent : Type u} {P : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set ℝ} {Q : OrderSide → Agent → Quantity → Set Quantity} : Function.Injective (agentDynamicOrderEmbedding (P := P) (Q := Q)) :=
declarations.name: agentDynamicOrderEmbedding_injective

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the thesis priority relation on static orders first
compares price (decreasing for buys, increasing for sells) and then compares
quantity decreasingly when prices tie.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the definition follows the displayed
buy and sell formulas verbatim, using the direction tag to choose the branch.
declarations.header: def staticPriority (side : OrderSide) (x y : ℝ × Quantity) : Prop :=
declarations.name: staticPriority

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: tagged static orders are comparable only when their buy
or sell tags agree, in which case the side-specific priority is used.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the explicit tag equality is what turns
two total side orders into a partial order on their disjoint union.
declarations.header: def taggedStaticPriority (x y : OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: taggedStaticPriority

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: any two price/quantity payloads on the same side are
comparable by the thesis static priority.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: trichotomy of prices decides the first
coordinate; when prices agree, totality of nonnegative quantities decides the
tie-breaker.
declarations.header: theorem staticPriority_total (side : OrderSide) (x y : ℝ × Quantity) : staticPriority side x y ∨ staticPriority side y x :=
declarations.name: staticPriority_total

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:partial-order-static-market`.

Informal statement: two tagged static orders are comparable in at least one
direction exactly when their direction tags agree.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: same-side comparability uses
`staticPriority_total`; the reverse implication reads the tag equality from
either possible comparison.
declarations.header: theorem taggedStaticPriority_comparable_iff_same_side (x y : OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) : (taggedStaticPriority x y ∨ taggedStaticPriority y x) ↔ x.1 = y.1 :=
declarations.name: taggedStaticPriority_comparable_iff_same_side

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Supplementary definition for the price-time-priority prose at source line 194.

Informal statement: price-time priority ranks a better price first and, when
prices tie, an earlier submission time first.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this definition records the market
convention mentioned in the prose independently of the quantity tie-breaker
used in the preceding static example.
declarations.header: def priceTimePriority (side : OrderSide) (x y : ℝ × Quantity) : Prop :=
declarations.name: priceTimePriority

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:249:rem:12`

Informal statement: for a partial order, the associated strict relation is
the non-strict relation with its diagonal removed, and adjoining the diagonal
recovers the non-strict relation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean's `<` and `≤` are predicates rather
than sets of pairs; antisymmetry supplies the two equivalences pointwise.
declarations.header: theorem strict_and_nonstrict_order_differ_by_diagonal {X : Type u} [PartialOrder X] (x y : X) : (x < y ↔ x ≤ y ∧ x ≠ y) ∧ (x ≤ y ↔ x < y ∨ x = y) :=
declarations.name: strict_and_nonstrict_order_differ_by_diagonal

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: a static total priority first puts all buys before all
sells and otherwise uses the side-specific static priority.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the displayed lexicographic
construction with the arbitrary convention `buy < sell`.
declarations.header: def staticTotalPriority (x y : OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: staticTotalPriority

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:total-order-static-market`.

Informal statement: the lexicographic static priority compares every pair of
tagged orders.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: different sides are decided by the
chosen buy-before-sell order; equal sides reduce to
`staticPriority_total`.
declarations.header: theorem staticTotalPriority_total (x y : OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) : staticTotalPriority x y ∨ staticTotalPriority y x :=
declarations.name: staticTotalPriority_total

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: dynamic price-time-quantity priority compares price first,
then submission time, and then quantity, reversing only the price direction
between buys and sells.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the two branches transcribe the two
displayed formulas from the thesis example.
declarations.header: def dynamicPriority (side : OrderSide) (x y : (ℝ × Quantity) × Quantity) : Prop :=
declarations.name: dynamicPriority

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: any two dynamic payloads on a fixed side are comparable
by price, time, and quantity priority.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: nested trichotomy follows exactly the
three successive tie-breakers in `dynamicPriority`.
declarations.header: theorem dynamicPriority_total (side : OrderSide) (x y : (ℝ × Quantity) × Quantity) : dynamicPriority side x y ∨ dynamicPriority side y x :=
declarations.name: dynamicPriority_total

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: dynamic total priority orders sides lexicographically and
uses dynamic price-time-quantity priority within each side.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: it is the dynamic analogue of
`staticTotalPriority`.
declarations.header: def dynamicTotalPriority (x y : OrderSide × ((ℝ × Quantity) × Quantity)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: dynamicTotalPriority

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:total-order-dynamic-market`.

Informal statement: the lexicographic dynamic priority compares every pair of
tagged dynamic orders.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: side comparison handles mixed tags,
while `dynamicPriority_total` handles matching tags.
declarations.header: theorem dynamicTotalPriority_total (x y : OrderSide × ((ℝ × Quantity) × Quantity)) : dynamicTotalPriority x y ∨ dynamicTotalPriority y x :=
declarations.name: dynamicTotalPriority_total

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: an agent-labelled order consists of its market-visible
price/quantity/direction payload and the submitting agent.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: putting the visible payload first makes
the market-view projection the ordinary first projection.
declarations.header: abbrev AgentLabelledOrder (Agent : Type u) : Type u :=
declarations.name: AgentLabelledOrder

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the market view forgets which agent submitted an order
while retaining price, quantity, and direction.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis quotient map before
passing to its kernel equivalence classes.
declarations.header: def marketView {Agent : Type u} : AgentLabelledOrder Agent → OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity) :=
declarations.name: marketView

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:completing-order-agent-based-static-market`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:350:rem:18`.

Informal statement: quotienting agent-labelled orders by equality of their
market view is canonically equivalent to the range of visible orders.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: mathlib's kernel-quotient equivalence
implements the thesis map from equivalence classes to price/quantity/direction
orders and proves well-definedness and bijectivity at once.
declarations.header: noncomputable def agentOrderQuotientEquivMarketViewRange (Agent : Type u) : Quotient (Setoid.ker (marketView (Agent := Agent))) ≃
declarations.name: agentOrderQuotientEquivMarketViewRange

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: truncate an extended distance at one, producing a finite
extended-real value even when the original distance is infinite.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the pointwise formula
`min (d x y) 1` used in the thesis remark.
declarations.header: def truncatedEDistance {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ENNReal) (x y : X) : ENNReal :=
declarations.name: truncatedEDistance

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:368:rem:20`

Informal statement: truncation at one is bounded and it agrees with the
original extended distance whenever that distance is below one.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the local agreement on every ball of
radius less than one is the precise small-scale fact behind the thesis claim
that truncation does not change the induced topology.
declarations.header: theorem truncatedEDistance_bounded_and_locally_equal {X : Type u} (d : X → X → ENNReal) (x y : X) : truncatedEDistance d x y ≤ 1 ∧ (d x y < 1 → truncatedEDistance d x y = d x y) :=
declarations.name: truncatedEDistance_bounded_and_locally_equal

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:498:rem:25`

Informal statement: the measurable direct sum of an indexed family of spaces
has the dependent-sum carrier `Σ a, X a`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean's measurable-space instance for a
dependent sum is the standard direct-sum sigma algebra; this abbreviation
records the terminology used by the remark without duplicating the instance.
declarations.header: abbrev MeasurableDirectSum (A : Type u) (X : A → Type v) [∀ a, MeasurableSpace (X a)] : Type (max u v) :=
declarations.name: MeasurableDirectSum

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `rem:unordered-configuration-space`.

Informal statement: the unordered finite-configuration space over `X` is the
type of finite subsets of `X`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: finite subsets carry no enumeration or
ordering, matching the configuration-space terminology exactly.
declarations.header: abbrev UnorderedFiniteConfiguration (X : Type u) : Type u :=
declarations.name: UnorderedFiniteConfiguration

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the empty finite subset is a point of every finite-subset
space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: its finiteness proof is the standard
finiteness theorem for the empty set.
declarations.header: def emptyFiniteSubset (X : Type u) : FiniteSubsets X :=
declarations.name: emptyFiniteSubset

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `rem:hausdorff-convention`.

Informal statement: the extended Hausdorff distance from the empty set is
zero for the empty set and infinity for every nonempty finite set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof invokes mathlib's extended
Hausdorff empty-set theorem after splitting on whether the second finite set
is empty.
declarations.header: theorem hausdorffEDistance_empty_convention {X : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace X] (s : FiniteSubsets X) : hausdorffEDistance (emptyFiniteSubset X) s = if (s : Set X) = ∅ then 0 else ∞ :=
declarations.name: hausdorffEDistance_empty_convention

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `rem:hausdorff-infinite-values`.

Informal statement: in a finite-valued metric space, the Hausdorff extended
distance between two nonempty finite subsets is not infinite.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: finite subsets of a metric space are
bounded, so the standard bounded-nonempty Hausdorff theorem excludes `∞`;
the preceding convention accounts for the remaining empty-set cases.
declarations.header: theorem hausdorffEDistance_ne_top_of_nonempty_finite {X : Type u} [PseudoMetricSpace X] (s t : FiniteSubsets X) (hs : (s : Set X).Nonempty) (ht : (t : Set X).Nonempty) : hausdorffEDistance s t ≠ ∞ :=
declarations.name: hausdorffEDistance_ne_top_of_nonempty_finite

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:903:rem:45`

Informal statement: the graph/range of the empty tuple is the empty set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean represents the empty tuple as a
map from `Fin 0`; eliminating a hypothetical index proves its range empty,
which is the typed analogue of the ZFC graph observation in the thesis.
declarations.header: theorem range_emptyTuple {X : Type u} : Set.range (Tuple.empty X).2 = ∅ :=
declarations.name: range_emptyTuple

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:985:rem:50`

Informal statement: the length stored with a finite permutation is the
cardinality of its finite domain.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: a finite permutation is indexed by
`Fin n`, whose cardinality is definitionally the thesis domain size `n`.
declarations.header: theorem finitePermutation_domain_card (permutation : FinitePermutations) : Fintype.card (Fin permutation.1) = permutation.1 :=
declarations.name: finitePermutation_domain_card

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:985:rem:50`
The source's inclusion of permutations into natural-valued tuples. Adding one
translates Lean's zero-based indices to the thesis's positive naturals.
declarations.header: def finitePermutationTuple (permutation : FinitePermutations) : Tuple ℕ :=
declarations.name: finitePermutationTuple

declarations.header: theorem finitePermutationTuple_injective : Function.Injective finitePermutationTuple :=
declarations.name: finitePermutationTuple_injective

declarations.header: @[simp] theorem finitePermutationTuple_length (permutation : FinitePermutations) : (finitePermutationTuple permutation).length = permutation.1 := rfl
declarations.name: finitePermutationTuple_length

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1048:cor:54`

Informal statement: every partially ordered type admits at least one sorting
rule on all finite tuples.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Alias for `cor:54` (the mapped
construction is TuplesSorting.choiceSortingRule). The construction itself lives
in `TuplesSorting`: `chosenSortingPermutation` selects one sorting permutation
for each tuple, `choiceSortingRule` packages those selections as a sorting
rule, and `sortingRule_exists` records the resulting existence statement; those
declarations carry the thesis label `thm:sorting-exists`. This one-line bridge
only re-exposes `sortingRule_exists` under the stable block ID, which is
necessary because the thesis labels this corollary with a theorem prefix.
declarations.header: theorem context_sortingRule_exists (X : Type u) [PartialOrder X] : Nonempty (SortingRule X) :=
declarations.name: context_sortingRule_exists

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1899:rem:95`

Informal statement: over a total order, any two sorting permutations produce
the same sorted tuple even if the permutations themselves differ on repeated
entries.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the chapter's uniqueness theorem for
sorted permutations compares the resulting tuples, deliberately not the
witnessing permutations.
declarations.header: theorem sorting_output_unique_despite_permutation_choice {X : Type u} [LinearOrder X] (x : Tuple X) (pi rho : SortingPermutations x) : permute x pi.1 = permute x rho.1 :=
declarations.name: sorting_output_unique_despite_permutation_choice

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1386:rem:65`

Informal statement: relational composition connects `x` to `z` when some
intermediate `y` is related to `x` by the first relation and to `z` by the
second.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: relations are predicates in Lean, so
the thesis set-builder definition becomes this existential predicate.
declarations.header: def relationComposition {X : Type u} (R S : X → X → Prop) (x z : X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: relationComposition

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: concatenate a finite list of tuples from left to right,
using the empty tuple as the zero-length base case.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: recursion fixes the parenthesization of
the thesis shorthand and preserves the displayed order of the tuple factors.
declarations.header: def concatList {X : Type u} : List (Tuple X) → Tuple X | [] => Tuple.empty X | [x] => x | x :: y :: xs => concat x (concatList (y :: xs)) /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`. Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1550:rem:77` Informal statement: the three-term concatenation shorthand expands in the listed order to `x ⊕ (y ⊕ z)`. Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is a definitional unfolding of `concatList`; no commutativity is introduced or assumed. -/ theorem concatList_three {X : Type u} (x y z : Tuple X) : concatList [x, y, z] = concat x (concat y z) :=
declarations.name: concatList

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1550:rem:77`

Informal statement: the three-term concatenation shorthand expands in the
listed order to `x ⊕ (y ⊕ z)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is a definitional unfolding of
`concatList`; no commutativity is introduced or assumed.
declarations.header: theorem concatList_three {X : Type u} (x y z : Tuple X) : concatList [x, y, z] = concat x (concat y z) :=
declarations.name: concatList_three

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: lexicographic order on pairs first compares the first
coordinate strictly and uses the non-strict second-coordinate order on ties.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is exactly the order relation used
in the discontinuity example.
declarations.header: def lexicographicPairLE (x y : ℝ × ℝ) : Prop :=
declarations.name: lexicographicPairLE

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the discontinuity witness is the two-entry tuple
`((0,1),(1/(n+1),0))`; the shift by one makes every denominator positive.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: using `n+1` makes explicit the positive
natural-number indexing intended by the thesis formula `1/n`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def lexSortingWitness (n : ℕ) : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ) :=
declarations.name: lexSortingWitness

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the pointwise limit of the discontinuity witness is the
pair `((0,1),(0,0))`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this names the exact limiting tuple
displayed in the thesis.
declarations.header: def lexSortingLimit : (ℝ × ℝ) × (ℝ × ℝ) :=
declarations.name: lexSortingLimit

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `exmp:sort-discont`.

Informal statement: every shifted reciprocal witness is lexicographically
sorted, the sequence converges to `((0,1),(0,0))`, and that limit is not
sorted.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: positivity proves sortedness, the
standard reciprocal limit proves convergence, and the tie at first coordinate
with `1 ≤ 0` false proves failure of sortedness at the limit.  This is the
closed-graph obstruction used by the thesis to show sorting discontinuous.
declarations.header: theorem lexSorting_discontinuity_witness : (∀ n, lexicographicPairLE (lexSortingWitness n).1 (lexSortingWitness n).2) ∧ Tendsto lexSortingWitness atTop (nhds lexSortingLimit) ∧ ¬ lexicographicPairLE lexSortingLimit.1 lexSortingLimit.2 :=
declarations.name: lexSorting_discontinuity_witness

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Original label: `rem:sorting-permutations-not-unique`.

Informal statement: a constant real tuple of length two is fixed by both the
identity permutation and the transposition, although those permutations are
distinct.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the swap moves the two indices, while
constant-function extensionality shows that both reindexings yield the same
tuple values.
declarations.header: theorem equalRealPair_has_distinct_sortingPermutations (x : ℝ) : ∃ pi rho : Equiv.Perm (Fin 2), pi ≠ rho ∧ (fun _ : Fin 2 => x) ∘ pi = (fun _ : Fin 2 => x) ∘ rho :=
declarations.name: equalRealPair_has_distinct_sortingPermutations

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`.

Original label: `rem:concat-empty-tuples`.

Informal statement: concatenating two empty tuples produces the empty tuple.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: both input domains are `Fin 0`; after
unfolding concatenation, function extensionality eliminates the impossible
output index.
declarations.header: theorem concat_empty_empty (X : Type u) : concat (Tuple.empty X) (Tuple.empty X) = Tuple.empty X :=
declarations.name: concat_empty_empty

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`.

Original label: `defn:sorted-tuple-add`.

Informal statement: fix one sorting rule for a partially ordered type.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `choiceSortingRule` chooses one sorting
permutation for each finite tuple, providing the globally well-defined rule
that the market convention requires.
declarations.header: noncomputable def fixedSortingRule (X : Type u) [PartialOrder X] : SortingRule X :=
declarations.name: fixedSortingRule

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`.

Original label: `rem:reindex-bracket-notation`.

Informal statement: whenever the selected-index set has strictly fewer
members than the original tuple domain, reindexing strictly shortens the
tuple and hence cannot be a permutation of that domain.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the exact length formula for `reindex`
turns the cardinality hypothesis directly into the claimed strict inequality.
declarations.header: theorem reindex_shortens_when_indices_discarded {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (indices : FiniteSubsets ℕ) (hcard : (FiniteSubsets.toFinset (finiteSubsetInter indices (tupleDomain x))).card < x.length) : (reindex x indices).length < x.length :=
declarations.name: reindex_shortens_when_indices_discarded

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the empty modification contains no index/value pairs and
therefore satisfies the distinct-index condition.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the condition is immediate because
membership in the underlying empty finite subset is impossible.
declarations.header: def emptyModification (X : Type u) : DistinctFiniteSubsets X :=
declarations.name: emptyModification

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: applying the empty modification leaves every tuple
unchanged.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: every coordinate falls into the
no-replacement branch of `modificationValue`.
declarations.header: theorem modify_emptyModification {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) : modify x (emptyModification X) = x :=
declarations.name: modify_emptyModification

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`.

Original label: `rem:void-modification`.

Informal statement: a void modification leaves the ordinary tuple fixed,
while sorted modification returns the chosen sorting of that same tuple.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the first equality is
`modify_emptyModification`; unfolding `sortedModify` and rewriting by it
gives the second equality.
declarations.header: theorem voidModification_behavior {X : Type u} [Preorder X] (sortingRule : SortingRule X) (x : Tuple X) : modify x (emptyModification X) = x ∧ (sortedModify sortingRule x (emptyModification X)).1 = sortingRule.sort x :=
declarations.name: voidModification_behavior

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`.

Original label: `rem:tuple-projection-operator-notation`.

Informal statement: tuple decomposition is exactly the map sending each
coordinate tag to the corresponding tuple projection.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the operator-style and function-style
notations are definitionally equal in the dependent-product representation.
declarations.header: theorem tupleDecomposition_eq_projectionMap {A : Type v} {X : A → Type u} (x : Tuple ((a : A) → X a)) : tupleDecomposition x = fun a => tupleProjection a x :=
declarations.name: tupleDecomposition_eq_projectionMap

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`.

Original label: `rem:separation-element-projection`.

Informal statement: separating the entries tagged by `a` and projecting away
their tags yields a tuple in the untagged component type `X a`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `separationComponent` performs both the
index filtering and the proof-carrying dependent projection, so its result
type formally enforces the codomain claimed in the remark.
declarations.header: noncomputable def untaggedSeparation {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} (a : A) (x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) : Tuple (X a) :=
declarations.name: untaggedSeparation

declarations.docComment:
Supporting lemma for empty atomic decompositions: a sum indexed by the empty
finite type is zero. The current stochastic-market chapter explicitly uses
this convention inside its atomic-representation lemma.
declarations.header: theorem sum_fin_zero {M : Type u} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : Fin 0 → M) : ∑ i, f i = 0 :=
declarations.name: sum_fin_zero

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`.

Original label: `rem:permuted-tuple-notation`.

Informal statement: every permuted-tuple quotient class has a tuple
representative whose quotient is the original class.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the existing quotient choice function
supplies the representative; its `Quot.out_eq` theorem certifies the chosen
notation without pretending the representative map is injective.
declarations.header: theorem permutedTupleClass_has_representative {X : Type u} (q : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : ∃ x : Tuple X, Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) x = q :=
declarations.name: permutedTupleClass_has_representative

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`.

Original label: `rem:measurable-enumeration-adaptation`.

Informal statement: repeating the atoms of a finite atomic decomposition by
their multiplicities produces a tuple whose induced counting measure is the
original finite integer-valued measure.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the constructive tuple bridge
used when adapting a measurable atom enumeration; it invokes no new axiom and
is independent of the cited measurability theorem itself.
declarations.header: theorem atomicEnumeration_corresponds_to_tuple {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] {μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X} (decomposition : AtomicDecomposition μ) : tupleInducedIntegerMeasure (tupleOfAtomicDecomposition decomposition) = μ :=
declarations.name: atomicEnumeration_corresponds_to_tuple

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the fiber of a group action over `y` consists of the
group elements that move a fixed point `x` to `y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: for the thesis application, the group
is the finite permutation group and these fibers are the cosets of the tuple
stabilizer.
declarations.header: abbrev OrbitFiber (G : Type u) (X : Type v) [Group G] [MulAction G X] (x y : X) : Type u :=
declarations.name: OrbitFiber

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: left multiplication by `g` bijects the action fiber over
`y` with the action fiber over `g • y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: multiplication by `g⁻¹` is the inverse;
the action laws prove both fiber-membership conditions and inverse laws.
declarations.header: def orbitFiberLeftMulEquiv {G : Type u} {X : Type v} [Group G] [MulAction G X] (x y : X) (g : G) : OrbitFiber G X x y ≃ OrbitFiber G X x (g • y)
declarations.name: orbitFiberLeftMulEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`.

Informal statement: all fibers lying in one finite group orbit have equal
cardinality; in particular, every tuple in a permutation orbit is produced by
the same number of permutations.

Supporting group-action lemma: `orbitFiberLeftMulEquiv` gives the explicit
coset bijection. The current tuple multiplicity and uniform point-process
sampling results specialize this orbit-counting argument.
declarations.header: theorem orbitFiber_card_eq {G : Type u} {X : Type v} [Group G] [Finite G] [MulAction G X] (x y : X) (g : G) : Nat.card (OrbitFiber G X x y) = Nat.card (OrbitFiber G X x (g • y)) :=
declarations.name: orbitFiber_card_eq

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the kernel equivalence relation of a map identifies
exactly the inputs having the same image.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: mathlib's `Setoid.ker` is the typed
quotient relation meant by "kernel" outside the linear-algebra null-space
sense.
declarations.header: def kernelEquivalence {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (f : X → Y) : Setoid X :=
declarations.name: kernelEquivalence

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`.

Original label: `rem:kernel-quotient-terminology`.

Informal statement: two elements are related by the kernel equivalence of
`f` if and only if `f` maps them to the same value.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: unfolding `Setoid.ker` distinguishes
this fiber relation from the null space of a linear operator.
declarations.header: theorem kernelEquivalence_apply {X : Type u} {Y : Type v} (f : X → Y) (x y : X) : kernelEquivalence f x y ↔ f x = f y :=
declarations.name: kernelEquivalence_apply

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`.

Original block id: `source:1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex:1296:cor:45`

Informal statement: for a nonempty domain and weakly convex real-vector-space
operator, the map `T([(x,z)]) = Φ(x) - Φ(z)` is a linear isomorphism from the
Grothendieck vectorization onto the span of the operator image.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the witness is
`KernelHilbert.grothendieckVectorizationLinearEquivSpan`, and the displayed
formula for `T` on pair representatives is
`grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan_pairRepresentative_formula`; the stable ID
is needed because the thesis corollary carries a theorem-prefixed label.
declarations.header: theorem context_grothendieck_vectorization_linearEquiv_span {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (phi : Operator X V) (hphi : WeaklyConvexOperator X V phi) : ∃ T : GrothendieckVectorization phi hphi ≃ₗ[ℝ] Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range phi), ∀ p : GrothendieckPair phi hphi, ((T (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid phi hphi) p) : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range phi)) : V) = weakConvexKernelImage phi hphi p.1 - weakConvexKernelImage phi hphi p.2 :=
declarations.name: context_grothendieck_vectorization_linearEquiv_span

declarations.docComment:
Existence wrapper for the corollary at line 1296 of
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex` (not the mapped
statement): the linear isomorphism of
`context_grothendieck_vectorization_linearEquiv_span`, forgetting the formula
for `T`. Kept under its former name for interface stability.
declarations.header: theorem context_grothendieck_vectorization_is_span {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (phi : Operator X V) (hphi : WeaklyConvexOperator X V phi) : Nonempty (GrothendieckVectorization phi hphi ≃ₗ[ℝ] Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range phi)) :=
declarations.name: context_grothendieck_vectorization_is_span

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `2 - day-ahead/2_clearing_operator_price_curves.tex`.

Original label: `rem:lp-point-evaluation`.

Informal statement: the thesis `ℒ²` convention is the type of actual
functions together with a square-integrability proof, before identifying
functions that agree almost everywhere.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the subtype retains pointwise function
values; mathlib's separate `Lp E 2 μ` type below is the almost-everywhere
quotient.  Thus the distinction in the thesis is visible in the Lean types.
declarations.header: abbrev L2Representatives (Domain : Type u) (E : Type v) [MeasurableSpace Domain] [NormedAddCommGroup E] (measure : Measure Domain) : Type (max u v) :=
declarations.name: L2Representatives

declarations.docComment:
Informal statement: the conventional Hilbert `L²` space is the
almost-everywhere quotient of square-integrable functions.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this abbreviation names the quotient
type used by mathlib and contrasts it with `L2Representatives`.
declarations.header: abbrev L2EquivalenceClasses (Domain : Type u) (E : Type v) [MeasurableSpace Domain] [NormedAddCommGroup E] (measure : Measure Domain) : Type (max u v) :=
declarations.name: L2EquivalenceClasses

declarations.header: structure Efficiency
declarations.name: Efficiency

declarations.header: def gridEnergy (η : Efficiency) (change : ℝ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: gridEnergy

declarations.header: theorem gridEnergy_zero (η : Efficiency) : gridEnergy η 0 = 0 :=
declarations.name: gridEnergy_zero

declarations.header: theorem gridEnergy_of_charge (η : Efficiency) {change : ℝ} (h : 0 ≤ change) : gridEnergy η change = change / η.charge := if_neg (not_lt.mpr h)
declarations.name: gridEnergy_of_charge

declarations.header: theorem gridEnergy_of_discharge (η : Efficiency) {change : ℝ} (h : change < 0) : gridEnergy η change = η.discharge * change := if_pos h
declarations.name: gridEnergy_of_discharge

declarations.header: theorem gridEnergy_pos_iff (η : Efficiency) (change : ℝ) : 0 < gridEnergy η change ↔ 0 < change :=
declarations.name: gridEnergy_pos_iff

declarations.header: theorem gridEnergy_parts (η : Efficiency) (change : ℝ) : gridEnergy η change = max change 0 / η.charge - η.discharge * max (-change) 0 :=
declarations.name: gridEnergy_parts

declarations.header: def increment (a : Fin 51) : ℝ := 4 * (a.val : ℝ) - 100
declarations.name: increment

declarations.header: theorem increment_bounds (a : Fin 51) : -100 ≤ increment a ∧ increment a ≤ 100 :=
declarations.name: increment_bounds

declarations.header: theorem increment_strictMono : StrictMono increment :=
declarations.name: increment_strictMono

declarations.docComment: Exactly `4 ℤ ∩ [-100,100]`, including both endpoints and idle.
declarations.header: theorem increment_range (r : ℝ) : (∃ a : Fin 51, increment a = r) ↔ (∃ k : ℤ, r = 4 * (k : ℝ)) ∧ -100 ≤ r ∧ r ≤ 100 :=
declarations.name: increment_range

declarations.header: abbrev Action := Lex (Fin 24 → Fin 51)
declarations.name: Action

declarations.header: def storageGrid : Finset ℝ := univ.image (fun i : Fin 101 => 4 * (i.val : ℝ))
declarations.name: storageGrid

declarations.header: theorem storageGrid_bounds {q : ℝ} (hq : q ∈ storageGrid) : 0 ≤ q ∧ q ≤ 400 :=
declarations.name: storageGrid_bounds

declarations.header: def storedAfter (start : ℝ) (a : Action) (k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: storedAfter

declarations.header: theorem storedAfter_zero (start : ℝ) (a : Action) : storedAfter start a 0 = start :=
declarations.name: storedAfter_zero

declarations.header: theorem storedAfter_full (start : ℝ) (a : Action) : storedAfter start a 24 = start + ∑ h, increment (a h) :=
declarations.name: storedAfter_full

declarations.header: def feasible (η : Efficiency) (start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) : Finset Action :=
declarations.name: feasible

declarations.header: theorem mem_feasible (η : Efficiency) (start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) (a : Action) : a ∈ feasible η start stop domain ↔ (∀ h : Fin 24, storedAfter start a (h.val + 1) ∈ storageGrid) ∧ storedAfter start a 24 = stop ∧ ∀ h : Fin 24, gridEnergy η (increment (a h)) ∈ domain h :=
declarations.name: mem_feasible

declarations.header: def payoff (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (a : Action) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: payoff

declarations.header: def maximizers (s : Finset Action) (f : Action → ℝ) : Finset Action :=
declarations.name: maximizers

declarations.header: theorem maximizers_nonempty {s : Finset Action} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) : (maximizers s f).Nonempty :=
declarations.name: maximizers_nonempty

declarations.header: def select (s : Finset Action) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) : Action :=
declarations.name: select

declarations.header: theorem select_mem_maximizers (s : Finset Action) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) : select s hs f ∈ maximizers s f := min'_mem _ _
declarations.name: select_mem_maximizers

declarations.header: theorem select_mem (s : Finset Action) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) : select s hs f ∈ s := (mem_filter.mp (select_mem_maximizers s hs f)).1
declarations.name: select_mem

declarations.header: theorem select_max (s : Finset Action) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) {b : Action} (hb : b ∈ s) : f b ≤ f (select s hs f) :=
declarations.name: select_max

declarations.header: theorem select_lex_first (s : Finset Action) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : Action → ℝ) {b : Action} (hb : b ∈ s) (hbmax : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ≤ f b) : select s hs f ≤ b :=
declarations.name: select_lex_first

declarations.header: def predictedAction (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (P : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) (hne : (feasible η start stop domain).Nonempty) : Action :=
declarations.name: predictedAction

declarations.header: theorem predictedAction_optimal (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (P : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) (hne : (feasible η start stop domain).Nonempty) : predictedAction η cost start stop P domain hne ∈ feasible η start stop domain ∧ ∀ a ∈ feasible η start stop domain, payoff η cost P a ≤ payoff η cost P (predictedAction η cost start stop P domain hne) :=
declarations.name: predictedAction_optimal

declarations.docComment: Evaluation against realized curves requires a fresh domain check on the selected schedule.
declarations.header: def realizedPayoff (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) (a : Action) (_hreal : ∀ h, gridEnergy η (increment (a h)) ∈ domain h) : ℝ := payoff η cost P a
declarations.name: realizedPayoff

declarations.header: theorem payoff_congr_on_submission (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P R : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (a : Action) (h : ∀ j, P j (gridEnergy η (increment (a j))) = R j (gridEnergy η (increment (a j)))) : payoff η cost P a = payoff η cost R a :=
declarations.name: payoff_congr_on_submission

declarations.docComment: Internal-throughput costs cancel when comparing the same selected schedule.
declarations.header: theorem payoff_forecast_error (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P predicted : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (a : Action) : payoff η cost P a - payoff η cost predicted a = ∑ h, (-gridEnergy η (increment (a h)) * (P h (gridEnergy η (increment (a h))) - predicted h (gridEnergy η (increment (a h))))) :=
declarations.name: payoff_forecast_error

declarations.header: theorem net_internal_change (η : Efficiency) (start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin 24 → Set ℝ) {a : Action} (ha : a ∈ feasible η start stop domain) : ∑ h, increment (a h) = stop - start :=
declarations.name: net_internal_change

declarations.header: def charged (a : Action) : ℝ := ∑ h, max (increment (a h)) 0
declarations.name: charged

declarations.header: def discharged (a : Action) : ℝ := ∑ h, max (-increment (a h)) 0
declarations.name: discharged

declarations.header: theorem charged_sub_discharged (a : Action) : charged a - discharged a = ∑ h, increment (a h) :=
declarations.name: charged_sub_discharged

declarations.header: theorem net_grid_withdrawal (η : Efficiency) (a : Action) : ∑ h, gridEnergy η (increment (a h)) = charged a / η.charge - η.discharge * discharged a :=
declarations.name: net_grid_withdrawal

declarations.header: theorem payoff_common_shift (η : Efficiency) (cost c : ℝ) (P : Fin 24 → ℝ → ℝ) (a : Action) : payoff η cost (fun h q => P h q + c) a = payoff η cost P a - c * (charged a / η.charge - η.discharge * discharged a) :=
declarations.name: payoff_common_shift

declarations.docComment: The source's upper bound on the extra cycling margin at the declared settings.
declarations.header: theorem illustrated_cycle_margin {buy sell : ℝ} (hbuy : 40 ≤ buy) (hsell : sell ≤ 80) : sell * (0.925 : ℝ) - buy / (0.925 : ℝ) - 2 * 25 ≤ -(712 / 37 : ℝ) :=
declarations.name: illustrated_cycle_margin

declarations.header: abbrev OrderedSchedule (n : ℕ) := Lex (Schedule n)

declarations.header: def schedules {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) : Finset (OrderedSchedule n) :=

declarations.header: theorem maximizers_nonempty {n : ℕ} {s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)} (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) : (maximizers s f).Nonempty :=
declarations.name: maximizers_nonempty

declarations.header: def select {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) : OrderedSchedule n :=
declarations.name: select

declarations.header: theorem select_mem_maximizers {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) : select s hs f ∈ maximizers s f := Finset.min'_mem _ _
declarations.name: select_mem_maximizers

declarations.header: theorem select_mem {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) : select s hs f ∈ s :=
declarations.name: select_mem

declarations.header: theorem select_max {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) {b : OrderedSchedule n} (hb : b ∈ s) : f b ≤ f (select s hs f) :=

declarations.header: theorem select_lex_first {n : ℕ} (s : Finset (OrderedSchedule n)) (hs : s.Nonempty) (f : OrderedSchedule n → ℝ) {b : OrderedSchedule n} (hb : b ∈ s) (hbmax : ∀ a ∈ s, f a ≤ f b) : select s hs f ≤ b := Finset.min'_le _ _ (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hb, hbmax⟩)
declarations.name: select_lex_first

declarations.docComment:
The chronological lexicographically first maximizer, for arbitrary finite
grids and arbitrary horizon (the source uses `n = 24`).
declarations.header: def predictedAction {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hne : (schedules G R η start stop domain).Nonempty) : OrderedSchedule n :=
declarations.name: predictedAction

declarations.header: theorem predictedAction_optimal {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hne : (schedules G R η start stop domain).Nonempty) : Feasible G R η start stop domain (predictedAction G R η cost start stop domain P hne) ∧ ∀ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a → BatteryValuation.payoff η cost P a ≤ BatteryValuation.payoff η cost P (predictedAction G R η cost start stop domain P hne) :=

declarations.header: theorem predictedAction_lex_first {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hne : (schedules G R η start stop domain).Nonempty) (b : OrderedSchedule n) (hb : Feasible G R η start stop domain b) (hbmax : ∀ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a → BatteryValuation.payoff η cost P a ≤ BatteryValuation.payoff η cost P b) : predictedAction G R η cost start stop domain P hne ≤ b :=

declarations.name: realizedSelectedValue

declarations.header: theorem selected_transition_error {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (forecastDomain realizedDomain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (predicted realized : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hne : (schedules G R η start stop forecastDomain).Nonempty) (hreal : Feasible G R η start stop realizedDomain (predictedAction G R η cost start stop forecastDomain predicted hne)) : realizedSelectedValue G R η cost start stop forecastDomain realizedDomain predicted realized hne hreal - plugInValue G R η cost start stop forecastDomain predicted hne = transitionValueError η cost realized predicted (predictedAction G R η cost start stop forecastDomain predicted hne) := rfl
declarations.name: selected_transition_error

declarations.header: theorem transitionValueError_eq {n : ℕ} (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (realized predicted : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (a : Schedule n) : transitionValueError η cost realized predicted a = ∑ h, -gridEnergy η (a h) * (realized h (gridEnergy η (a h)) - predicted h (gridEnergy η (a h))) :=

declarations.name: rescale_mem_grid

declarations.docComment:
Every feasible enlarged schedule rescales to a feasible original one.
The interval and zero assumptions on each price domain are essential.
declarations.header: theorem feasible_rescale {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) (hd : ∀ h, Convex ℝ (domain h)) (hz : ∀ h, 0 ∈ domain h) (a : Schedule n) (ha : Feasible (scaledGrid α G) (scaledGrid α R) η (α * start) (α * stop) domain a) : Feasible G R η start stop domain (scale α⁻¹ a) :=
declarations.name: feasible_rescale

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:battery-value-functions`, objective for any horizon.

declarations.name: payoff

declarations.docComment:
A nonempty feasible transition attains its plug-in value for arbitrary
finite grids, without any continuity assumption on its price functions.
declarations.header: theorem exists_optimal_schedule {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hne : ∃ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a) : ∃ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a ∧ ∀ b, Feasible G R η start stop domain b → payoff η cost P b ≤ payoff η cost P a :=
declarations.name: exists_optimal_schedule

declarations.docComment:
The hourly cash comparison of the thesis proof, with the price function only
non-decreasing on its declared interval domain `D`: the comparison involves the two
feasible points `q = τ(Δq̃_h)` and `α q = τ(Δq_h)` of `D` and nothing else. The
sign split on `q` is exactly the thesis's two cases.
declarations.header: theorem cash_scale_le_of_monotoneOn (P : ℝ → ℝ) (D : Set ℝ) (hP : MonotoneOn P D) (q α : ℝ) (hα : 1 ≤ α) (hqD : q ∈ D) (haD : α * q ∈ D) : -(α * q) * P (α * q) ≤ α * (-q * P q) :=
declarations.name: cash_scale_le_of_monotoneOn

declarations.docComment: Globally monotone special case of `cash_scale_le_of_monotoneOn`.
declarations.header: theorem monotone_cash_scale (P : ℝ → ℝ) (hP : Monotone P) (q α : ℝ) (hα : 1 ≤ α) : -(α * q) * P (α * q) ≤ α * (-q * P q) :=
declarations.name: monotone_cash_scale

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:battery-sublinear-scaling`, schedule inequality.
Thesis proof, hourly inequality: for a schedule `a` whose grid energies lie in the
declared interval domains, and whose `α`-scaled grid energies do too, compare the two
feasible interval points, split by sign, cancel the positively homogeneous throughput
cost `λ|·|`, then sum over the hours.
declarations.header: theorem payoff_scale_le_of_monotoneOn {n : ℕ} (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (hP : ∀ h, MonotoneOn (P h) (domain h)) (a : Schedule n) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) (ha : ∀ h, gridEnergy η (a h) ∈ domain h) (hlarge : ∀ h, gridEnergy η (scale α a h) ∈ domain h) : payoff η cost P (scale α a) ≤ α * payoff η cost P a :=
declarations.name: payoff_scale_le_of_monotoneOn

declarations.docComment:
Special case of `payoff_scale_le_of_monotoneOn` under global monotonicity of every
hourly price function (kept for downstream users); not the mapped proof of
`prop:battery-sublinear-scaling`.
declarations.header: theorem payoff_scale_le {n : ℕ} (η : Efficiency) (cost : ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hP : ∀ h, Monotone (P h)) (a : Schedule n) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) : payoff η cost P (scale α a) ≤ α * payoff η cost P a :=
declarations.name: payoff_scale_le

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:battery-sublinear-scaling`.
Thesis proof, for arbitrary finite state and increment grids `G`, `R` and hourly price
functions that are non-decreasing on interval domains containing `0`: rescale the
enlarged feasible schedule by `α⁻¹` (interval convexity and `0 ∈ domain` give its
feasibility for the original grids), bound its payoff by the hourly sign comparison,
and conclude with the attained small-grid maximum.
declarations.header: theorem optimalValue_scale_le_of_monotoneOn {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hP : ∀ h, MonotoneOn (P h) (domain h)) (hd : ∀ h, Convex ℝ (domain h)) (hz : ∀ h, 0 ∈ domain h) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) (aLarge aSmall : Schedule n) (hlarge : Feasible (scaledGrid α G) (scaledGrid α R) η (α * start) (α * stop) domain aLarge) (hsmallmax : ∀ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a → payoff η cost P a ≤ payoff η cost P aSmall) : payoff η cost P aLarge ≤ α * payoff η cost P aSmall :=
declarations.name: optimalValue_scale_le_of_monotoneOn

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:battery-sublinear-scaling`.
The proposition as stated: if the enlarged feasible set is non-empty, then the original
feasible set is non-empty (by rescaling), its maximum is attained, and every enlarged
schedule is bounded by `α` times that maximum.
declarations.header: theorem sublinear_scaling_of_monotoneOn {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hP : ∀ h, MonotoneOn (P h) (domain h)) (hd : ∀ h, Convex ℝ (domain h)) (hz : ∀ h, 0 ∈ domain h) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) (hne : ∃ a, Feasible (scaledGrid α G) (scaledGrid α R) η (α * start) (α * stop) domain a) : ∃ aSmall, Feasible G R η start stop domain aSmall ∧ (∀ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a → payoff η cost P a ≤ payoff η cost P aSmall) ∧ ∀ aLarge, Feasible (scaledGrid α G) (scaledGrid α R) η (α * start) (α * stop) domain aLarge → payoff η cost P aLarge ≤ α * payoff η cost P aSmall :=
declarations.name: sublinear_scaling_of_monotoneOn

declarations.docComment:
Special case of `optimalValue_scale_le_of_monotoneOn` under global monotonicity of
every hourly price function (kept for downstream users); not the mapped proof of
`prop:battery-sublinear-scaling`.
declarations.header: theorem optimalValue_scale_le {n : ℕ} (G R : Finset ℝ) (η : Efficiency) (cost start stop : ℝ) (domain : Fin n → Set ℝ) (P : Fin n → ℝ → ℝ) (hP : ∀ h, Monotone (P h)) (hd : ∀ h, Convex ℝ (domain h)) (hz : ∀ h, 0 ∈ domain h) (α : ℝ) (hα : 1 < α) (aLarge aSmall : Schedule n) (hlarge : Feasible (scaledGrid α G) (scaledGrid α R) η (α * start) (α * stop) domain aLarge) (hsmallmax : ∀ a, Feasible G R η start stop domain a → payoff η cost P a ≤ payoff η cost P aSmall) : payoff η cost P aLarge ≤ α * payoff η cost P aSmall :=
declarations.name: optimalValue_scale_le

declarations.docComment:

declarations.name: everett_lagrangian_separation

On the interior of a segment of positive quantity width, the actual
midpoint inverse is precisely the transposed affine interpolation.
declarations.header: theorem midpoint_eq_interpolate {lo hi : ℝ} {E : ℝ → ℝ} (hE : Monotone E) {a b : ℝ × ℝ} (hp : a.1 ≤ b.1) (hq : a.2 < b.2) (hsub : segment ℝ a b ⊆ completedGraph lo hi E) {q : ℝ} (hqq : q ∈ Ioo a.2 b.2) : midpointPrice lo hi E q = interpolate a.2 b.2 a.1 b.1 q :=
declarations.name: midpoint_eq_interpolate

declarations.docComment:
A quantity interval containing no polygon vertex lies on one transposed
positive-width piece. The hypotheses refer to the actual completed graph,
not to a certificate assuming the inverse is affine.
declarations.header: theorem midpoint_affine_on_vertex_gap {ι : Type*} {lo hi u v : ℝ} {E : ℝ → ℝ} (hE : Monotone E) (a b : ι → ℝ × ℝ) (hp : ∀ i, (a i).1 ≤ (b i).1) (hq : ∀ i, (a i).2 ≤ (b i).2) (hgraph : completedGraph lo hi E = ⋃ i, segment ℝ (a i) (b i)) (huv : u < v) (hvertices : ∀ i, (a i).2 ∉ Ioo u v ∧ (b i).2 ∉ Ioo u v) (hne : (levelSet lo hi E ((u + v) / 2)).Nonempty) : ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ q ∈ Ioo u v, midpointPrice lo hi E q = A * q + B :=
declarations.name: midpoint_affine_on_vertex_gap

declarations.name: polygon

declarations.header: theorem polygon_eq_iUnion {n : ℕ} (x : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ) (E : ℝ → ℝ) : polygon x E = (⋃ i : Fin (n + 1), segment ℝ (lower E (x i)) (upper E (x i))) ∪ ⋃ j : Fin n, segment ℝ (upper E (x j.castSucc)) (lower E (x j.succ)) :=
declarations.name: polygon_eq_iUnion

declarations.docComment:

declarations.name: uniform_block_exists

declarations.header: theorem uniform_cell_fraction {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (j : Fin n) (s u : ℝ) : (u - ((j : ℝ) / n + s)) / ((((j : ℝ) + 1) / n + s) - ((j : ℝ) / n + s)) = (n : ℝ) * (u - s) - j :=

declarations.header: theorem uniform_block_unique {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (j k : Fin n) {t : ℝ} (hj : (j : ℝ) / n < t ∧ t < ((j : ℝ) + 1) / n) (hk : (k : ℝ) / n < t ∧ t ≤ ((k : ℝ) + 1) / n) : k = j :=

declarations.header: theorem left_cell_unique {L R : ℕ} (hL : 0 < L) (hR : 0 < R) (j : Fin L) (u : Parameter) (hu : (j : ℝ) / L < (u : ℝ) + 1 ∧ (u : ℝ) + 1 < ((j : ℝ) + 1) / L) (hu0 : (u : ℝ) < 0) (i : Fin (L + R)) (hi : u ∈ cell (leftBoundary L R) (rightBoundary L R) i) : i = Fin.castAdd R j :=
declarations.name: left_cell_unique

declarations.name: right_cell_unique

declarations.header: theorem graph_of_affine_piece (price : ℝ → ℝ) {a b q t : ℝ} (hab : a < b) (hq : q ∈ Ioo a b) (haff : ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo a b, price x = A * x + B) (hqt : q = (1 - t) * a + t * b) : pairEquiv (q, price q) = (1 - t) • (pieceEndpoints price a b).1 + t • (pieceEndpoints price a b).2 :=

declarations.header: theorem canonical_eq_endpoint_pointwise (f : Curve) (hL : 0 < leftCount f) (hR : 0 < rightCount f) (hl : ∀ j : Fin (leftCount f), ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (leftKnot f j.castSucc) (leftKnot f j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) (hr : ∀ j : Fin (rightCount f), ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (rightKnot f j.castSucc) (rightKnot f j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) (u : Parameter) (hu : u ∉ parameterKnots (leftCount f) (rightCount f)) : pairEquiv (PLCanonicalEncoding.encoding f u) = representative (leftBoundary (leftCount f) (rightCount f)) (rightBoundary (leftCount f) (rightCount f)) (endpointData f.price (leftKnot f) (rightKnot f)) u :=

declarations.docComment:

declarations.header: theorem canonical_eq_endpoint_actual_counts (μ : Measure Parameter) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [NoAtoms μ] (f : Curve) (hL : 0 < leftCount f) (hR : 0 < rightCount f) (hl : ∀ j : Fin (leftCount f), ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (leftKnot f j.castSucc) (leftKnot f j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) (hr : ∀ j : Fin (rightCount f), ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (rightKnot f j.castSucc) (rightKnot f j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) : PLCanonicalEncoding.encodingLp μ f = endpointContinuousLinearMap μ (leftBoundary (leftCount f) (rightCount f)) (rightBoundary (leftCount f) (rightCount f)) (endpointData f.price (leftKnot f) (rightKnot f)) :=
declarations.name: canonical_eq_endpoint_actual_counts

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:pl-encoding-measurable`.
Fixed comparison-cell coordinates may be substituted for the actual
canonical node arrays. No conclusion identifying the encoding is assumed.
declarations.header: theorem canonical_eq_endpoint_fixed_counts (μ : Measure Parameter) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] [NoAtoms μ] (f : Curve) {L R : ℕ} (kl : Fin (L + 1) → ℝ) (kr : Fin (R + 1) → ℝ) (hL : leftCount f = L) (hR : rightCount f = R) (hLpos : 0 < L) (hRpos : 0 < R) (hkl : ∀ j : Fin (leftCount f + 1), leftKnot f j = kl (Fin.cast (congrArg (fun n ↦ n + 1) hL) j)) (hkr : ∀ j : Fin (rightCount f + 1), rightKnot f j = kr (Fin.cast (congrArg (fun n ↦ n + 1) hR) j)) (hl : ∀ j : Fin L, ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (kl j.castSucc) (kl j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) (hr : ∀ j : Fin R, ∃ A B : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ Ioo (kr j.castSucc) (kr j.succ), f.price x = A * x + B) : PLCanonicalEncoding.encodingLp μ f = endpointContinuousLinearMap μ (leftBoundary L R) (rightBoundary L R) (endpointData f.price kl kr) :=
declarations.name: canonical_eq_endpoint_fixed_counts

Original label: `prop:price-impact-curve-properties`, clause (ii).
The actual midpoint inverse of a completed monotone finite polygonal graph
has a finite disjoint interval partition of affine pieces, along the thesis's
clause-(ii) argument: on the open core of a piece the completed graph is the
affine graph, so the inverse is its affine inverse (or constant on a flat); the
piece endpoints contribute singleton cells.  Nonemptiness of the level sets is a
hypothesis here; on the thesis route it comes from the finite polygonal segment
cover of the completed graph (`FinitePricePathSource.actual_levelSet_nonempty`
for the actual book), while `CompletedInverse.levelSet_nonempty` is an alternative
sup-based route.  No inverse-affinity assumption occurs in this theorem.

`CompletedInverse.levelSet_nonempty` rather than by the thesis's finite polygonal
segment cover (`FinitePricePathSource.actual_levelSet_nonempty`).

Thesis source: analytic membership clause following Definition
`defn:admissible-price-curve-parametrisation` in the replacement price-curve
chapter.

Original label: `defn:admissible-price-curve-parametrisation`.

Every admissible parametrised graph belongs to `L²` on the common compact
parameter interval.  The theorem is measure-agnostic and applies in
particular to restricted Lebesgue measure.

Informal statement: graph-admissible actual representatives are closed under

representative with every admissibility field proved.  It deliberately makes
no claim that this result is the canonical sided encoding of its decoded
curve.

closed under every pointwise combination with nonnegative coefficients.

the price coordinate. The endpoint of the combination is proved to be the
same nonnegative combination of the original endpoints, matching the
manuscript construction of the decoded curve `h`.

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `cor:sided-parametrisation-not-weakly-convex` (not the
mapped proof): Hilbert-valued (almost-everywhere quotient) clause of the corollary
in `2 - day-ahead/2_clearing_operator_price_curves.tex`, proved here by an
exhaustive case split over the possible block counts.  The mapped proof, which
follows the thesis's explicit example with the continuity and graph-recovery
argument (quarter knot `5/6` versus `5/8`), is
`SidedSourceExclusion.canonicalLp_not_weaklyConvex_source` /
`canonical_not_weaklyConvexAE_source` in `CanonicalSidedSourceExclusion.lean`.

Proof note: equality in the `L²([-1,1]; ℝ × ℝ)` quotient is represented by
equality almost everywhere with respect to restricted Lebesgue measure.  The
two/three-block midpoint has four positive-measure price levels.  Any canonical
encoding equal to it almost everywhere therefore has at most four strictly
