declarations.header: theorem sampleCoalition_full {M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → H) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (z : Fin M → (Fin n → ℝ)) : sampleCoalition M f x univ z = f x :=
declarations.name: sampleCoalition_full

declarations.header: theorem sampleCoalition_unbiased {M : ℕ} (hM : 0 < M) (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → H) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) (ν : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (hf : Measurable f) (hint : Integrable (fun z => f (completeInput x A z)) ν) (z : Fin M → Ω → (Fin n → ℝ)) (hlaw : ∀ m, HasLaw (z m) ν μ) : ∫ ω, sampleCoalition M f x A (fun m => z m ω) ∂μ = coalitionValue f x A ν :=
declarations.name: sampleCoalition_unbiased

declarations.docComment: An actual first-moment condition on the selected conditional law is explicit.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCoalition_tendsto_ae (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → H) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (A : Finset (Fin n)) (ν : Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (hf : Measurable f) (hint : Integrable (fun z => f (completeInput x A z)) ν) (z : ℕ → Ω → (Fin n → ℝ)) (hlaw : ∀ m, HasLaw (z m) ν μ) (hindep : Pairwise fun b c => z b ⟂ᵢ[μ] z c) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun M => sampleCoalition M f x A (fun m => z m.val ω)) atTop (𝓝 (coalitionValue f x A ν)) :=
declarations.name: sampleCoalition_tendsto_ae

declarations.docComment:
Subtracting the two sample averages is exactly the displayed average of paired differences.
The pairing is algebraic and does not assume independence between the two coalitions.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCoalition_sub (M : ℕ) (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → H) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (A B : Finset (Fin n)) (z w : Fin M → (Fin n → ℝ)) : sampleCoalition M f x A z - sampleCoalition M f x B w = (M : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ m, (f (completeInput x A (z m)) - f (completeInput x B (w m))) :=
declarations.name: sampleCoalition_sub

declarations.header: theorem value_tendsto {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {V : ι → Finset (Fin n) → H} {W : Finset (Fin n) → H} (hV : ∀ A, Tendsto (fun m => V m A) l (𝓝 (W A))) (i : Fin n) : Tendsto (fun m => Shapley.value (V m) i) l (𝓝 (Shapley.value W i)) :=
declarations.name: value_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
All finitely many simulated coalition values can be substituted into the Shapley formula.
Different coalitions may share randomness; each coalition's sequence must satisfy its own law
and independence assumptions.
declarations.header: theorem simulation_attribution_tendsto_ae (f : (Fin n → ℝ) → H) (x : Fin n → ℝ) (ν : Finset (Fin n) → Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) (hf : Measurable f) (hint : ∀ A, Integrable (fun z => f (completeInput x A z)) (ν A)) (z : Finset (Fin n) → ℕ → Ω → (Fin n → ℝ)) (hlaw : ∀ A m, HasLaw (z A m) (ν A) μ) (hindep : ∀ A, Pairwise fun b c => z A b ⟂ᵢ[μ] z A c) (i : Fin n) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun M => Shapley.value (fun A => sampleCoalition M f x A (fun m => z A m.val ω)) i) atTop (𝓝 (Shapley.value (fun A => coalitionValue f x A (ν A)) i)) :=
declarations.name: simulation_attribution_tendsto_ae

declarations.docComment:
The current tree interpolation claim assumes pairwise distinct inputs.
This lemma records why that qualification is needed.
declarations.header: theorem duplicate_input_prevents_interpolation {X Y : Type*} (f : X → Y) {x₁ x₂ : X} {y₁ y₂ : Y} (hx : x₁ = x₂) (hy : y₁ ≠ y₂) : ¬(f x₁ = y₁ ∧ f x₂ = y₂) :=
declarations.name: duplicate_input_prevents_interpolation

declarations.docComment:
Even an unrestricted real-valued predictor has strictly positive loss on
two equal inputs with responses zero and one.
declarations.header: theorem conflicting_pair_loss_lower_bound (prediction : ℝ) : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ (0 - prediction) ^ 2 + (1 - prediction) ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: conflicting_pair_loss_lower_bound

declarations.header: def coordinateScale (a b : ℝ) (x : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ × ℝ := (a * x.1, b * x.2)
declarations.name: coordinateScale

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `eq:standardizing-operator`.
The claimed inverse is an inverse when both scales are nonzero.
declarations.header: theorem coordinateScale_inverse (a b : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (x : ℝ × ℝ) : coordinateScale a b (coordinateScale a⁻¹ b⁻¹ x) = x :=
declarations.name: coordinateScale_inverse

declarations.docComment: Zero empirical scales cannot define inverse operators on the ambient space.
declarations.header: theorem zero_coordinateScale_not_injective (b : ℝ) : ¬Function.Injective (coordinateScale 0 b) :=
declarations.name: zero_coordinateScale_not_injective

declarations.docComment:
The paired-lag normalization in Chapter 4 is bounded by one. The index
set is the actual common-observation set; no regular calendar is required.
declarations.header: theorem paired_autocorrelation_bound {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (x y : ι → ℝ) (hx : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, x i ^ 2) (hy : 0 < ∑ i ∈ s, y i ^ 2) : |(∑ i ∈ s, x i * y i) / (Real.sqrt (∑ i ∈ s, x i ^ 2) * Real.sqrt (∑ i ∈ s, y i ^ 2))| ≤ 1 :=
declarations.name: paired_autocorrelation_bound

declarations.docComment: The cell mean used by the current recursive regression-tree model.
declarations.header: def cellMean {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (y : ι → H) : H :=
declarations.name: cellMean

declarations.header: theorem sum_sub_cellMean {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (y : ι → H) : ∑ i ∈ s, (y i - cellMean s y) = 0 :=
declarations.name: sum_sub_cellMean

declarations.docComment:
The sum-of-squares decomposition displayed in Chapter 5, lines 336–342.

Original label: `lem:cell-risk-minimiser`.
declarations.header: theorem cell_sum_squares {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (y : ι → H) (z : H) : ∑ i ∈ s, ‖y i - z‖ ^ 2 = (∑ i ∈ s, ‖y i - cellMean s y‖ ^ 2) + (s.card : ℝ) * ‖z - cellMean s y‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: cell_sum_squares

declarations.docComment:
The empirical mean is the unique minimizer; completeness is unnecessary.

Original label: `lem:cell-risk-minimiser`.
declarations.header: theorem cellMean_unique_minimizer {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (y : ι → H) (z : H) : (∑ i ∈ s, ‖y i - z‖ ^ 2) ≤ (∑ i ∈ s, ‖y i - cellMean s y‖ ^ 2) ↔ z = cellMean s y :=
declarations.name: cellMean_unique_minimizer

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: Definition `defn:frechet-derivative`.

Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.

Mathlib's `HasFDerivAt` is the little-o formulation of the displayed
norm-quotient limit.
declarations.header: def IsFrechetDerivativeAt {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace G] (f : H → G) (x : H) (A : H →L[ℝ] G) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsFrechetDerivativeAt

declarations.docComment:
Fréchet differentiability is existence of a bounded linear derivative.

Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
declarations.header: def FrechetDifferentiableAt {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace G] (f : H → G) (x : H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: FrechetDifferentiableAt

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
The library's little-o derivative is equivalent to the manuscript's exact
increment and norm-quotient limit. At zero the real quotient is totalized to
zero, so including the zero increment does not change the limit.
declarations.header: theorem isFrechetDerivativeAt_iff_norm_quotient {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace G] (f : H → G) (x : H) (A : H →L[ℝ] G) : IsFrechetDerivativeAt f x A ↔ Tendsto (fun h => ‖f (x + h) - f x - A h‖ / ‖h‖) (𝓝 0) (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: isFrechetDerivativeAt_iff_norm_quotient

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
The derivative notation denotes a unique bounded linear operator.
declarations.header: theorem frechetDerivative_unique {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [InnerProductSpace ℝ G] [CompleteSpace G] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace G] {f : H → G} {x : H} {A B : H →L[ℝ] G} (hA : IsFrechetDerivativeAt f x A) (hB : IsFrechetDerivativeAt f x B) : A = B :=
declarations.name: frechetDerivative_unique

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:frechet-derivative`.
The derivative field is the actual bounded-linear-operator-valued function.
Its values are asserted only under the source's differentiability hypothesis.
declarations.header: noncomputable def frechetDerivative {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] (f : H → G) : H → H →L[ℝ] G :=
declarations.name: frechetDerivative

declarations.header: theorem frechetDerivative_spec {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] {f : H → G} {x : H} {A : H →L[ℝ] G} (h : HasFDerivAt f A x) : frechetDerivative f x = A :=
declarations.name: frechetDerivative_spec

declarations.header: theorem frechetDerivative_hasFDerivAt {H : Type u} {G : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace ℝ G] {f : H → G} (h : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : H) : HasFDerivAt f (frechetDerivative f x) x :=
declarations.name: frechetDerivative_hasFDerivAt

declarations.header: structure Settings
declarations.name: Settings

declarations.header: def fitDirection (cfg : Settings) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : Finset ι) (current : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : Tree p H :=
declarations.name: fitDirection

declarations.header: theorem fitDirection_spec (cfg : Settings) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : Finset ι) (current : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) (hrows : cfg.minimum ≤ fitRows.card) : let t := fitDirection cfg cuts x y fitRows current
declarations.name: fitDirection_spec

declarations.docComment:
Moving any fraction of the way to a squared-loss line-search minimizer
does not increase the loss. This also covers a zero fitted direction.
declarations.header: theorem lineLoss_shrink_le (s : Finset ι) (residual direction : ι → H) (ν : ℝ) (hν : 0 ≤ ν) (hν1 : ν ≤ 1) : lineLoss s residual direction (ν * lineSearchStep s residual direction) ≤ lineLoss s residual direction 0 :=
declarations.name: lineLoss_shrink_le

declarations.header: def update (current direction : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) (step : ℝ) : (Fin p → ℝ) → H :=
declarations.name: update

declarations.header: theorem empiricalRisk_update (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (current direction : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) (γ : ℝ) : empiricalRisk s x y (update current direction γ) = (s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ * lineLoss s (fun i => y i - current (x i)) (fun i => direction (x i)) γ :=
declarations.name: empiricalRisk_update

declarations.header: def roundStep (cfg : Settings) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows lineRows : Finset ι) (current : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: roundStep

declarations.header: def roundUpdate (cfg : Settings) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (current : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : (Fin p → ℝ) → H :=
declarations.name: roundUpdate

declarations.header: theorem roundUpdate_nonincrease (cfg : Settings) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (hν : 0 ≤ ν) (hν1 : ν ≤ 1) (current : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : empiricalRisk lineRows x y (roundUpdate cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν current) ≤ empiricalRisk lineRows x y current :=
declarations.name: roundUpdate_nonincrease

declarations.header: def boost (cfg : Settings) (cuts : ℕ → Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : ℕ → Finset ι) (lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (initial : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : ℕ → (Fin p → ℝ) → H | 0 => initial | n + 1 => roundUpdate cfg (cuts n) x y (fitRows n) lineRows ν (boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial n) theorem boost_risk_antitone (cfg : Settings) (cuts : ℕ → Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : ℕ → Finset ι) (lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (hν : 0 ≤ ν) (hν1 : ν ≤ 1) (initial : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : Antitone (fun n => empiricalRisk lineRows x y (boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial n)) :=
declarations.name: boost

declarations.header: theorem boost_risk_antitone (cfg : Settings) (cuts : ℕ → Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : ℕ → Finset ι) (lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (hν : 0 ≤ ν) (hν1 : ν ≤ 1) (initial : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) : Antitone (fun n => empiricalRisk lineRows x y (boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial n)) :=
declarations.name: boost_risk_antitone

declarations.docComment:
The stored directions are fitted to each current ensemble, not supplied
independently in advance. Their sum is the exact resulting prediction.
declarations.header: theorem boost_eq_sum (cfg : Settings) (cuts : ℕ → Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (fitRows : ℕ → Finset ι) (lineRows : Finset ι) (ν : ℝ) (initial : (Fin p → ℝ) → H) (n : ℕ) (z : Fin p → ℝ) : boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial n z = initial z + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, (ν * roundStep cfg (cuts k) x y (fitRows k) lineRows (boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial k)) • (fitDirection cfg (cuts k) x y (fitRows k) (boost cfg cuts x y fitRows lineRows ν initial k)).eval z :=
declarations.name: boost_eq_sum

declarations.header: def loss (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (t : Tree p H) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: loss

declarations.header: theorem loss_split (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (j : Fin p) (c : ℝ) (l r : Tree p H) : loss s x y (.split j c l r) = loss (leftCell s x j c) x y l + loss (rightCell s x j c) x y r :=
declarations.name: loss_split

declarations.header: theorem loss_mean_eq_impurity (s : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) : loss s x y (.leaf (cellMean s y)) = (s.card : ℝ) * impurity s y :=
declarations.name: loss_mean_eq_impurity

declarations.docComment:
The global sum-of-squares reduction of a leaf split is its sample count
times the thesis's local impurity reduction. Thus best-first selection by
training loss uses the sample-weighted version of the displayed local gain.
declarations.header: theorem leaf_split_reduction [DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (j : Fin p) (c : ℝ) (hl : (leftCell s x j c).Nonempty) (hr : (rightCell s x j c).Nonempty) : loss s x y (.leaf (cellMean s y)) - loss s x y (.split j c (.leaf (cellMean (leftCell s x j c) y)) (.leaf (cellMean (rightCell s x j c) y))) = (s.card : ℝ) * impurityGain (leftCell s x j c) (rightCell s x j c) y :=
declarations.name: leaf_split_reduction

declarations.docComment: Leaf means and minimum sample sizes are checked on the actual routed rows.
declarations.header: def FitsOn (minimum : ℕ) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) : Finset ι → Tree p H → Prop | s, .leaf value => minimum ≤ s.card ∧ value = cellMean s y | s, .split j c l r => FitsOn minimum x y (leftCell s x j c) l ∧ FitsOn minimum x y (rightCell s x j c) r def legalCuts (minimum : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) : Finset (Fin p × ℝ) :=
declarations.name: FitsOn

declarations.header: def legalCuts (minimum : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (s : Finset ι) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) : Finset (Fin p × ℝ) :=
declarations.name: legalCuts

declarations.docComment: Enumerate all single-leaf expansions, retaining every other branch.
declarations.header: def expansions (minimum : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) : Finset (Tree p H) :=
declarations.name: expansions

declarations.header: theorem expansion_leafCount (minimum : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) {u : Tree p H} (hu : u ∈ expansions minimum cuts x y s t) : u.leafCount = t.leafCount + 1 :=
declarations.name: expansion_leafCount

declarations.header: theorem expansion_fitsOn (minimum : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) (ht : FitsOn minimum x y s t) {u : Tree p H} (hu : u ∈ expansions minimum cuts x y s t) : FitsOn minimum x y s u :=
declarations.name: expansion_fitsOn

declarations.header: theorem fitsOn_nonempty (minimum : ℕ) (hm : 0 < minimum) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) (ht : FitsOn minimum x y s t) : s.Nonempty :=
declarations.name: fitsOn_nonempty

declarations.docComment: Positive leaf sample sizes imply nonempty geometric terminal regions.
declarations.header: theorem fitsOn_validOn (minimum : ℕ) (hm : 0 < minimum) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) (ht : FitsOn minimum x y s t) (R : Set (Fin p → ℝ)) (hR : ∀ i ∈ s, x i ∈ R) : t.ValidOn R :=
declarations.name: fitsOn_validOn

declarations.header: def admissible (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) : Finset (Tree p H) :=
declarations.name: admissible

declarations.header: def improving (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) : Finset (Tree p H) :=
declarations.name: improving

declarations.docComment:
A best admissible expansion is selected only if it clears the threshold.
The source does not specify how equal-gain cuts are ordered; choice fixes one.
declarations.header: def step (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) : Option (Tree p H) :=
declarations.name: step

declarations.header: theorem step_spec (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) {u : Tree p H} (hu : step minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t = some u) : u ∈ improving minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t ∧ ∀ v ∈ improving minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t, loss s x y u ≤ loss s x y v :=
declarations.name: step_spec

declarations.header: theorem step_none_iff (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) : step minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t = none ↔ improving minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t = ∅ :=
declarations.name: step_none_iff

declarations.header: theorem step_constraints (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) {u : Tree p H} (hu : step minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t = some u) : u ∈ expansions minimum cuts x y s t ∧ u.leafCount ≤ maxLeaves ∧ u.depth ≤ maxDepth ∧ threshold < loss s x y t - loss s x y u :=
declarations.name: step_constraints

declarations.docComment:
Minimization over all admissible single-leaf expansions, including those
that do not clear the improvement threshold.
declarations.header: theorem step_best (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (t : Tree p H) {u v : Tree p H} (hu : step minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t = some u) (hv : v ∈ admissible minimum maxLeaves maxDepth cuts x y s t) : loss s x y u ≤ loss s x y v :=
declarations.name: step_best

declarations.header: def grow (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) : ℕ → Tree p H → Tree p H | 0, t => t | n + 1, t => match step minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s t with | none => t | some u => grow minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s n u theorem grow_spec (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ threshold) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (n : ℕ) (t : Tree p H) (ht : FitsOn minimum x y s t) (hleaves : t.leafCount ≤ maxLeaves) (hdepth : t.depth ≤ maxDepth) : let u := grow minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s n t
declarations.name: grow

declarations.header: theorem grow_spec (minimum maxLeaves maxDepth : ℕ) (threshold : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ threshold) (cuts : Finset (Fin p × ℝ)) (x : ι → Fin p → ℝ) (y : ι → H) (s : Finset ι) (n : ℕ) (t : Tree p H) (ht : FitsOn minimum x y s t) (hleaves : t.leafCount ≤ maxLeaves) (hdepth : t.depth ≤ maxDepth) : let u := grow minimum maxLeaves maxDepth threshold cuts x y s n t
declarations.name: grow_spec

declarations.docComment:
The leaf budget supplies enough iterations to reach the actual stopping
condition. The fuel bound does not mask an unperformed legal expansion.

Original label: `defn:hilbert-shapley-value`.
Chosen predictor-space versions, with their actual coordinate-projection
domains and their almost-sure conditional-expectation specification.
declarations.header: structure LocalConditionalVersions [MeasurableSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (F : Ω → H) (X : Ω → α → ℝ)
declarations.name: LocalConditionalVersions

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:hilbert-shapley-value`.
The local coalition game evaluates the supplied version at the actual
retained predictor coordinates. Its full endpoint is not forced pointwise.
declarations.header: def localCoalitionGame [MeasurableSpace H] {μ : Measure Ω} {F : Ω → H} {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (versions : LocalConditionalVersions μ F X) (x : α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : H := versions.value S (fun i : S => x i)
declarations.name: localCoalitionGame

declarations.header: theorem conditionalMean_empty (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (F : Ω → H) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) : conditionalMean μ F X ∅ = fun _ => ∫ ω, F ω ∂μ :=
declarations.name: conditionalMean_empty

declarations.header: theorem conditionalMean_memLp (μ : Measure Ω) {F : Ω → H} (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : MemLp (conditionalMean μ F X S) 2 μ := hF.condExp
declarations.name: conditionalMean_memLp

declarations.docComment: This is a specific full-information version. Arbitrary versions agree only almost surely.
declarations.header: theorem conditionalMean_full [Fintype α] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {f : (α → ℝ) → H} (hf : Measurable f) (hF : Integrable (fun ω => f (X ω)) μ) : conditionalMean μ (fun ω => f (X ω)) X univ = fun ω => f (X ω) :=
declarations.name: conditionalMean_full

declarations.header: theorem prediction_efficiency [Fintype α] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {f : (α → ℝ) → H} (hf : Measurable f) (hF : Integrable (fun ω => f (X ω)) μ) (ω : Ω) : ∑ i, Shapley.value (fun S => conditionalMean μ (fun ω => f (X ω)) X S ω) i = f (X ω) - ∫ u, f (X u) ∂μ :=
declarations.name: prediction_efficiency

declarations.docComment:
Corrected forecasting efficiency prose (DA26-04): arbitrary chosen
predictor-space conditional versions give the forecast endpoint only almost
surely. The proof follows finite-game efficiency and then substitutes the two
conditional-version endpoint identities.
declarations.header: theorem localVersions_prediction_efficiency_ae [Fintype α] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {f : (α → ℝ) → H} (hf : Measurable f) (hF : Integrable (fun ω => f (X ω)) μ) (versions : LocalConditionalVersions μ (fun ω => f (X ω)) X) : (fun ω => ∑ i, Shapley.value (localCoalitionGame versions (X ω)) i) =ᵐ[μ] (fun ω => f (X ω) - ∫ u, f (X u) ∂μ) :=
declarations.name: localVersions_prediction_efficiency_ae

declarations.docComment: The retained loss is a genuinely integrable function, not just a totalized integral.
declarations.header: def conditionalLoss (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : {g : Ω → ℝ // Integrable g μ} :=
declarations.name: conditionalLoss

declarations.header: def risk (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: risk

declarations.header: def lossGame (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: lossGame

declarations.header: theorem risk_nonneg (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) : 0 ≤ risk μ hY hF X S :=
declarations.name: risk_nonneg

declarations.header: theorem lossGame_empty (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) : lossGame μ hY hF X ∅ = 0 := sub_self _
declarations.name: lossGame_empty

declarations.header: theorem marginal_loss_reduction (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) (S : Finset α) (i : α) : Shapley.marginal (lossGame μ hY hF X) S i = risk μ hY hF X S - risk μ hY hF X (insert i S) :=
declarations.name: marginal_loss_reduction

declarations.header: theorem efficiency [Fintype α] (μ : Measure Ω) {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) : ∑ i, Shapley.value (lossGame μ hY hF X) i = risk μ hY hF X ∅ - risk μ hY hF X univ :=
declarations.name: efficiency

declarations.header: theorem risk_empty (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Y F : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (hF : MemLp F 2 μ) (X : Ω → α → ℝ) : risk μ hY hF X ∅ = ∫ ω, ‖Y ω - ∫ u, F u ∂μ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: risk_empty

declarations.header: theorem risk_full [Fintype α] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Y : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {f : (α → ℝ) → H} (hf : Measurable f) (hF : MemLp (fun ω => f (X ω)) 2 μ) : risk μ hY hF X univ = ∫ ω, ‖Y ω - f (X ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: risk_full

declarations.header: theorem efficiency_original_loss [Fintype α] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {Y : Ω → H} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) {X : Ω → α → ℝ} (hX : Measurable X) {f : (α → ℝ) → H} (hf : Measurable f) (hF : MemLp (fun ω => f (X ω)) 2 μ) : ∑ i, Shapley.value (lossGame μ hY hF X) i = (∫ ω, ‖Y ω - ∫ u, f (X u) ∂μ‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) - ∫ ω, ‖Y ω - f (X ω)‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: efficiency_original_loss

declarations.name: weight

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:hilbert-shapley-value`.
declarations.header: def marginal (V : Finset α → H) (S : Finset α) (i : α) : H := V (insert i S) - V S
declarations.name: marginal

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:hilbert-shapley-value`.
declarations.header: def value (V : Finset α → H) (i : α) : H :=
declarations.name: value

declarations.header: theorem weight_nonneg (n k : ℕ) : 0 ≤ weight n k :=
declarations.name: weight_nonneg

declarations.header: theorem subsets_without (i : α) : (univ.erase i).powerset = (univ : Finset (Finset α)).filter (fun S => i ∉ S) :=
declarations.name: subsets_without

declarations.header: theorem sum_insert_without (i : α) (f : Finset α → H) : (∑ S ∈ (univ : Finset (Finset α)).filter (fun S => i ∉ S), f (insert i S)) = ∑ T ∈ (univ : Finset (Finset α)).filter (fun T => i ∈ T), f T :=
declarations.name: sum_insert_without

declarations.header: theorem positive_contributions (V : Finset α → H) (i : α) : (∑ S ∈ (univ.erase i).powerset, weight (Fintype.card α) S.card • V (insert i S)) = ∑ T ∈ (univ : Finset (Finset α)).filter (fun T => i ∈ T), weight (Fintype.card α) (T.card - 1) • V T :=
declarations.name: positive_contributions

declarations.header: theorem value_coefficient_formula (V : Finset α → H) : ∑ i, value V i = ∑ T : Finset α, ((T.card : ℝ) * weight (Fintype.card α) (T.card - 1) - ((Fintype.card α - T.card : ℕ) : ℝ) * weight (Fintype.card α) T.card) • V T :=
declarations.name: value_coefficient_formula

declarations.header: theorem weight_balance {n k : ℕ} (hk : 0 < k) (hkn : k < n) : (k : ℝ) * weight n (k - 1) = ((n - k : ℕ) : ℝ) * weight n k :=
declarations.name: weight_balance

declarations.header: theorem weight_endpoint {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) : (n : ℝ) * weight n 0 = 1 ∧ (n : ℝ) * weight n (n - 1) = 1 :=
declarations.name: weight_endpoint

declarations.docComment: Efficiency for the actual factorial-weighted coalition formula.
declarations.header: theorem efficiency_nonempty [Nonempty α] (V : Finset α → H) : ∑ i, value V i = V univ - V ∅ :=
declarations.name: efficiency_nonempty

declarations.header: theorem efficiency (V : Finset α → H) : ∑ i, value V i = V univ - V ∅ :=
declarations.name: efficiency

declarations.docComment: Pointwise prediction efficiency needs explicit endpoint values.
declarations.header: theorem efficiency_of_endpoints (V : Finset α → H) (prediction baseline : H) (hfull : V univ = prediction) (hempty : V ∅ = baseline) : ∑ i, value V i = prediction - baseline :=
declarations.name: efficiency_of_endpoints

declarations.header: theorem value_add (V W : Finset α → H) (i : α) : value (fun S => V S + W S) i = value V i + value W i :=
declarations.name: value_add

declarations.header: theorem value_smul (r : ℝ) (V : Finset α → H) (i : α) : value (fun S => r • V S) i = r • value V i :=
declarations.name: value_smul

declarations.docComment: A feature with zero marginal contribution on every eligible coalition has zero value.
declarations.header: theorem value_dummy (V : Finset α → H) (i : α) (h : ∀ S : Finset α, i ∉ S → V (insert i S) = V S) : value V i = 0 :=
declarations.name: value_dummy

declarations.header: def membershipGame (i : α) (S : Finset α) : ℝ := if i ∈ S then 1 else 0
declarations.name: membershipGame

declarations.header: theorem value_membership_other {i j : α} (hij : i ≠ j) : value (membershipGame i) j = 0 :=
declarations.name: value_membership_other

declarations.header: theorem value_membership_self (i : α) : value (membershipGame i) i = ∑ S ∈ (univ.erase i).powerset, weight (Fintype.card α) S.card :=
declarations.name: value_membership_self

declarations.docComment: The factorial coefficients are a probability weight on eligible coalitions.
declarations.header: theorem weight_sum (i : α) : ∑ S ∈ (univ.erase i).powerset, weight (Fintype.card α) S.card = 1 :=
declarations.name: weight_sum

declarations.header: def stage (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (k : ℕ) : Finset (Fin n) :=
declarations.name: stage

declarations.header: def predecessors (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : Finset (Fin n) :=
declarations.name: predecessors

declarations.header: theorem stage_zero (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : stage π 0 = ∅ :=
declarations.name: stage_zero

declarations.header: theorem stage_full (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : stage π n = univ :=
declarations.name: stage_full

declarations.header: theorem stage_succ (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (k : Fin n) : stage π (k.val + 1) = insert (π.symm k) (stage π k.val) :=
declarations.name: stage_succ

declarations.header: theorem predecessors_eq_stage (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : predecessors π i = stage π (π i).val := rfl
declarations.name: predecessors_eq_stage

declarations.header: def contribution (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : H :=
declarations.name: contribution

declarations.header: theorem efficiency (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ∑ i, contribution V π i = V univ - V ∅ :=
declarations.name: efficiency

declarations.header: def sampleValue (B : ℕ) (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (permutations : Fin B → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : H :=
declarations.name: sampleValue

declarations.docComment: Exact marginal evaluations retain efficiency for every nonempty sample of permutations.
declarations.header: theorem sample_efficiency {B : ℕ} (hB : 0 < B) (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (permutations : Fin B → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ∑ i, sampleValue B V permutations i = V univ - V ∅ :=
declarations.name: sample_efficiency

declarations.header: def uniformMeasure (n : ℕ) [MeasurableSpace (Equiv.Perm (Fin n))] : Measure (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) := (PMF.uniformOfFintype _).toMeasure
declarations.name: uniformMeasure

declarations.header: instance uniformMeasure_probability : IsProbabilityMeasure (uniformMeasure n) :=
declarations.name: uniformMeasure_probability

declarations.header: theorem integral_uniform_contribution (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (i : Fin n) : ∫ π, contribution V π i ∂uniformMeasure n = Shapley.value V i :=
declarations.name: integral_uniform_contribution

declarations.header: theorem contribution_unbiased (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (i : Fin n) {π : Ω → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)} (hπ : HasLaw π (uniformMeasure n) μ) : ∫ ω, contribution V (π ω) i ∂μ = Shapley.value V i :=
declarations.name: contribution_unbiased

declarations.docComment: No moment hypothesis on a fixed finite game is needed: its contribution range is finite.
declarations.header: theorem sampleValue_tendsto_ae (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (i : Fin n) (π : ℕ → Ω → Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (hlaw : ∀ b, HasLaw (π b) (uniformMeasure n) μ) (hindep : Pairwise fun b c => π b ⟂ᵢ[μ] π c) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun B => sampleValue B V (fun b => π b.val ω) i) atTop (𝓝 (Shapley.value V i)) :=
declarations.name: sampleValue_tendsto_ae

declarations.header: theorem notMem_predecessors (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : i ∉ predecessors π i :=
declarations.name: notMem_predecessors

declarations.header: theorem card_predecessors (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (i : Fin n) : (predecessors π i).card = (π i).val :=
declarations.name: card_predecessors

declarations.docComment: The three fibers are the predecessors, the feature itself, and its successors.
declarations.header: def coalitionTag (i : Fin n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) (j : Fin n) : Fin 3 :=
declarations.name: coalitionTag

declarations.header: def positionTag (k j : Fin n) : Fin 3 :=
declarations.name: positionTag

declarations.header: theorem coalitionTag_zero {i j : Fin n} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hi : i ∉ S) : coalitionTag i S j = 0 ↔ j ∈ S :=
declarations.name: coalitionTag_zero

declarations.header: theorem coalitionTag_one (i j : Fin n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : coalitionTag i S j = 1 ↔ j = i :=
declarations.name: coalitionTag_one

declarations.header: theorem coalitionTag_two (i j : Fin n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : coalitionTag i S j = 2 ↔ j ∉ insert i S :=
declarations.name: coalitionTag_two

declarations.header: theorem positionTag_zero (k j : Fin n) : positionTag k j = 0 ↔ j < k :=
declarations.name: positionTag_zero

declarations.header: theorem positionTag_one (k j : Fin n) : positionTag k j = 1 ↔ j = k :=
declarations.name: positionTag_one

declarations.header: theorem positionTag_two (k j : Fin n) : positionTag k j = 2 ↔ k < j :=
declarations.name: positionTag_two

declarations.header: theorem card_coalitionTag {i : Fin n} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hi : i ∉ S) (c : Fin 3) : Fintype.card {j // coalitionTag i S j = c} = if c = 0 then S.card else if c = 1 then 1 else n - S.card - 1 :=
declarations.name: card_coalitionTag

declarations.header: theorem card_positionTag (k : Fin n) (c : Fin 3) : Fintype.card {j // positionTag k j = c} = if c = 0 then k.val else if c = 1 then 1 else n - k.val - 1 :=
declarations.name: card_positionTag

declarations.header: theorem tag_composition_iff {i : Fin n} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hi : i ∉ S) (k : Fin n) (π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : positionTag k ∘ π = coalitionTag i S ↔ predecessors π i = S ∧ π i = k :=
declarations.name: tag_composition_iff

declarations.header: theorem exists_tag_permutation {i : Fin n} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hi : i ∉ S) (k : Fin n) (hk : k.val = S.card) : ∃ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), positionTag k ∘ π = coalitionTag i S :=
declarations.name: exists_tag_permutation

declarations.docComment: Exact multiplicity, including the empty and full predecessor coalitions.
declarations.header: theorem card_predecessor_fiber {i : Fin n} {S : Finset (Fin n)} (hi : i ∉ S) : Fintype.card {π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n) // predecessors π i = S} = S.card.factorial * (n - S.card - 1).factorial :=
declarations.name: card_predecessor_fiber

declarations.header: theorem sum_contributions_by_coalition (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (i : Fin n) : ∑ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), contribution V π i = ∑ S ∈ (univ.erase i).powerset, (S.card.factorial * (n - S.card - 1).factorial) • Shapley.marginal V S i :=
declarations.name: sum_contributions_by_coalition

declarations.docComment: Enumerating all permutations gives the actual factorial-weighted formula.
declarations.header: theorem uniform_average_eq_value (V : Finset (Fin n) → H) (i : Fin n) : (Fintype.card (Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), contribution V π i = Shapley.value V i :=
declarations.name: uniform_average_eq_value

declarations.header: def gramOperator (y : ι → H) : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι →ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ ι :=
declarations.name: gramOperator

declarations.header: theorem gram_positive (y : ι → H) : (gramOperator y).IsPositive :=
declarations.name: gram_positive

declarations.header: def eigenBasis (y : ι → H) : OrthonormalBasis (Fin (Fintype.card ι)) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) :=
declarations.name: eigenBasis

declarations.header: def eigenvalue (y : ι → H) : Fin (Fintype.card ι) → ℝ :=
declarations.name: eigenvalue

declarations.header: theorem eigenvalue_antitone (y : ι → H) : Antitone (eigenvalue y) :=
declarations.name: eigenvalue_antitone

declarations.header: theorem eigenvalue_nonneg (y : ι → H) (i : Fin (Fintype.card ι)) : 0 ≤ eigenvalue y i :=
declarations.name: eigenvalue_nonneg

declarations.header: def truncatedQuadratic (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: truncatedQuadratic

declarations.header: def tailEigenvalue (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: tailEigenvalue

declarations.header: theorem tail_nonneg (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) : 0 ≤ tailEigenvalue y r :=
declarations.name: tail_nonneg

declarations.header: theorem quadratic_eigen_expansion (y : ι → H) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : inner ℝ w (gramOperator y w) = ∑ i : Fin (Fintype.card ι), eigenvalue y i * inner ℝ (eigenBasis y i) w ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: quadratic_eigen_expansion

declarations.docComment:
A genuine residual Rayleigh bound, for the sorted spectral truncation of
the actual response Gram operator. The `r ≥ n` tail is exactly zero.
declarations.header: theorem spectral_error_bound (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : 0 ≤ inner ℝ w (gramOperator y w) - truncatedQuadratic y r w ∧ inner ℝ w (gramOperator y w) - truncatedQuadratic y r w ≤ tailEigenvalue y r * ‖w‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: spectral_error_bound

declarations.header: def contrast (s t : Finset ι) : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι :=
declarations.name: contrast

declarations.header: def splitScale (s t : Finset ι) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: splitScale

declarations.header: def splitWeights (s t : Finset ι) : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι := splitScale s t • contrast s t
declarations.name: splitWeights

declarations.header: theorem contrast_norm_sq (s t : Finset ι) (hd : Disjoint s t) : ‖contrast s t‖ ^ 2 = (s.card : ℝ) * (s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ 2 + (t.card : ℝ) * (t.card : ℝ)⁻¹ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: contrast_norm_sq

declarations.header: theorem splitWeights_norm_sq (s t : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint s t) : ‖splitWeights s t‖ ^ 2 = ((s ∪ t).card : ℝ)⁻¹ :=
declarations.name: splitWeights_norm_sq

declarations.header: theorem weighted_response (s t : Finset ι) (y : ι → H) : (∑ i, splitWeights s t i • y i) = splitScale s t • (EmpiricalGeometry.cellMean s y - EmpiricalGeometry.cellMean t y) :=
declarations.name: weighted_response

declarations.header: theorem quadratic_eq_impurityGain (s t : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint s t) (y : ι → H) : inner ℝ (splitWeights s t) (gramOperator y (splitWeights s t)) = impurityGain s t y :=
declarations.name: quadratic_eq_impurityGain

declarations.docComment:
The retained largest-eigenvalue surrogate's gain, in its exact quadratic
form with the source's actual contrast vector.
declarations.header: def truncatedSplitGain (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (s t : Finset ι) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: truncatedSplitGain

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:gram-split-gain-bound`.
The actual spectral residual is nonnegative and bounded by the first omitted
eigenvalue divided by the parent cell size. Rank at least n has zero error.
declarations.header: theorem splitGain_spectral_bound (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (s t : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint s t) : 0 ≤ impurityGain s t y - truncatedSplitGain y r s t ∧ impurityGain s t y - truncatedSplitGain y r s t ≤ tailEigenvalue y r / (s ∪ t).card :=
declarations.name: splitGain_spectral_bound

declarations.docComment:
The columns of the retained square-root spectral factor. Keeping zero
coordinates for omitted directions has exactly the same Gram matrix as the
source's r-row factor.
declarations.header: def spectralVectors (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (i : ι) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (Fintype.card ι)) :=
declarations.name: spectralVectors

declarations.header: theorem spectralVectors_gram (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (i j : ι) : inner ℝ (spectralVectors y r i) (spectralVectors y r j) = ∑ k : Fin (Fintype.card ι), if k.val < r then eigenvalue y k * eigenBasis y k i * eigenBasis y k j else 0 :=
declarations.name: spectralVectors_gram

declarations.header: theorem spectralVectors_weighted_norm (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (w : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : ‖∑ i, w i • spectralVectors y r i‖ ^ 2 = truncatedQuadratic y r w :=
declarations.name: spectralVectors_weighted_norm

declarations.header: theorem weighted_norm_eq_gain (s t : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint s t) (y : ι → H) : ‖∑ i, splitWeights s t i • y i‖ ^ 2 = impurityGain s t y :=
declarations.name: weighted_norm_eq_gain

declarations.docComment:
The surrogate gain in the bound is exactly the tree gain of the
square-root factor columns whose Gram matrix is U_r Λ_r U_rᵀ.
declarations.header: theorem truncatedSplitGain_eq_factor_gain (y : ι → H) (r : ℕ) (s t : Finset ι) (hs : s.Nonempty) (ht : t.Nonempty) (hd : Disjoint s t) : truncatedSplitGain y r s t = impurityGain s t (spectralVectors y r) :=

declarations.header: theorem scoreDomain_score_measurable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (n : ℕ) : Measurable (fun x : ScoreDomain b => score b n x.toH) :=

declarations.header: noncomputable def scorePartialSum {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) (x : ScoreDomain b) : H :=
declarations.name: scorePartialSum

declarations.header: theorem scorePartialSum_measurable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) : Measurable (scorePartialSum b N) :=
declarations.name: scorePartialSum_measurable

declarations.header: theorem scorePartialSum_tendsto {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (x : ScoreDomain b) : Tendsto (fun N => scorePartialSum b N x) atTop (𝓝 x.toH) :=
declarations.name: scorePartialSum_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
Alternative (vector-reconstruction) route to `σ(X) ⊆ G_∞`: the identity is the
pointwise limit of the measurable finite partial sums.  Not used by the mapped proof
of `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`, which goes through `scoreDomain_toH_measurable_from_balls`.
declarations.header: theorem scoreDomain_toH_measurable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) : Measurable (@ScoreDomain.toH H _ _ b) :=
declarations.name: scoreDomain_toH_measurable

declarations.docComment:
Parseval's identity applied to `x - c`, as in the thesis:
`‖x - c‖² = ∑ₙ (θₙ(x) - θₙ(c))²` with `θₙ(c) = ⟪c, eₙ⟫`.
declarations.header: theorem squaredDistance_hasSum {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (x c : H) : HasSum (fun n => (score b n x - score b n c) ^ 2) (‖x - c‖ ^ 2) :=
declarations.name: squaredDistance_hasSum

declarations.docComment:
The squared distance to a fixed centre is measurable for the score-generated
sigma-algebra: each finite Parseval sum `S_N = ∑_{n<N} (θₙ - xₙ)²` is a measurable
function of the first `N` scores, and `S_N → ‖x - c‖²` pointwise.
declarations.header: theorem squaredDistance_measurable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (c : H) : Measurable (fun x : ScoreDomain b => ‖x.toH - c‖ ^ 2) :=
declarations.name: squaredDistance_measurable

declarations.docComment:
The preimage of an open ball, `X⁻¹(B_ε(c)) = {‖X - c‖² < ε²}`, is measurable for
the score sigma-algebra; no measurable vector reconstruction is evaluated.
declarations.header: theorem ball_preimage_measurable {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (c : H) (ε : ℝ) : MeasurableSet ((ScoreDomain.toH (b := b)) ⁻¹' Metric.ball c ε) :=
declarations.name: ball_preimage_measurable

declarations.docComment:
The thesis's countable family `𝒞 = {B_q(d) | d ∈ D, q ∈ ℚ_{>0}}` of balls with
centres in a dense set `D` and positive rational radii is a basis of the norm topology.
declarations.header: theorem dense_rational_ball_basis {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] {D : Set H} (hD : Dense D) : TopologicalSpace.IsTopologicalBasis (Set.range (fun z : D × {r : ℚ // 0 < r} => Metric.ball (z.1 : H) (z.2 : ℝ))) :=
declarations.name: dense_rational_ball_basis

declarations.docComment:
The reverse inclusion `σ(X) ⊆ G_∞` along the thesis route: fix a countable dense
`D ⊆ H`; every ball `B_q(d)` with `d ∈ D`, `q ∈ ℚ_{>0}` has a score-measurable
preimage by the Parseval argument (`ball_preimage_measurable`); these balls form a
countable base, so every open set is a countable union of them and the identity
`ScoreDomain b → H` is measurable for the Borel sigma-algebra.  (The index type
`D × ℚ_{>0}` is countable; mathlib's `IsTopologicalBasis.borel_eq_generateFrom`
performs the countable-union step.)
declarations.header: theorem scoreDomain_toH_measurable_from_balls {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [mH : MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) : Measurable (@ScoreDomain.toH H _ _ b) :=
declarations.name: scoreDomain_toH_measurable_from_balls

declarations.docComment:
The Borel sigma-algebra of a separable Hilbert space is generated by the
countable family of basis scores.  `G_∞ ⊆ σ(X)` because each score is a continuous
linear functional of `X`; `σ(X) ⊆ G_∞` by the Parseval/ball/countable-base argument
of `scoreDomain_toH_measurable_from_balls`.
declarations.header: theorem scoreMeasurableSpace_eq_borel {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) : scoreMeasurableSpace b = (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace H) :=
declarations.name: scoreMeasurableSpace_eq_borel

declarations.docComment:
Pulling the score-generated sigma-algebra back along a random element is
the same as pulling back its Borel sigma-algebra.
declarations.header: theorem comap_borel_eq_iSup_comap_scores {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) : (borel H).comap X = ⨆ n, (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace ℝ).comap (fun ω => score b n (X ω)) :=
declarations.name: comap_borel_eq_iSup_comap_scores

declarations.docComment:
The sigma-algebra generated by the first `N` scores of `X`. With Lean's
zero-based indexing, level `N` contains scores `0, ..., N - 1`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def scoreFiltration {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) : Filtration ℕ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)
declarations.name: scoreFiltration

declarations.docComment:
The union of the finite-score filtration is the sigma-algebra generated by
the Hilbert-valued random element itself.
declarations.header: theorem iSup_scoreFiltration_eq_comap_borel {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) : (⨆ N, scoreFiltration b X hX N) = (borel H).comap X :=
declarations.name: iSup_scoreFiltration_eq_comap_borel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, first clause of
Theorem `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

Original label: `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

The manuscript states equality only up to null sets. In a separable Hilbert
space, the Borel sigma-algebra itself is generated by the countable score maps,
so Lean proves exact equality before a measure is chosen.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the inclusion `G_∞ ⊆ σ(X)` is the
continuity of each score functional; the inclusion `σ(X) ⊆ G_∞` follows the
thesis proof (Parseval `‖X - x‖² = ∑ (θₙ - xₙ)²` makes every ball preimage
`G_∞`-measurable, and a countable base of rational balls around a countable dense
set passes to all open sets), see `scoreDomain_toH_measurable_from_balls` and
`scoreMeasurableSpace_eq_borel`.  The pull-back along `X` and the identification of
`⨆ N, G_N` with `σ(θₙ, n ∈ ℕ)` are `comap_borel_eq_iSup_comap_scores` and
`iSup_scoreFiltration_eq_comap_borel`.
declarations.header: theorem scores_generate_random_element {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) : (⨆ N, scoreFiltration b X hX N) = (borel H).comap X :=
declarations.name: scores_generate_random_element

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, almost-sure
convergence clause of Theorem `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

Original label: `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

This is Levy's upward theorem from mathlib after identifying the supremum of
the finite-score filtration.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) (Y : Ω → ℝ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun N => μ[Y | scoreFiltration b X hX N] ω) atTop (𝓝 (μ[Y | (borel H).comap X] ω)) :=
declarations.name: condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_ae

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, `L¹`
convergence clause of Theorem `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

Original label: `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.

Lévy's upward theorem in `L¹` (mathlib's `tendsto_eLpNorm_condExp`) for the
increasing score filtration, after the Parseval identification
`⨆ N, G_N = σ(X)`.  The thesis assumes `Y ∈ L¹`; mathlib's statement holds for
every `Y` because conditional expectation vanishes on non-integrable inputs, so
the hypothesis is recorded but not needed.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_L1 {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) (Y : Ω → ℝ) (_hY : Integrable Y μ) : Tendsto (fun N => eLpNorm (μ[Y | scoreFiltration b X hX N] - μ[Y | (borel H).comap X]) 1 μ) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_L1

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `thm:scores-sigma-algebra` (not the mapped proof): the
Hilbert projection core.  Conditional expectations onto an increasing filtration
converge in `L²` once the closure of the union of its measurable subspaces is
identified with the target measurable subspace.  The mapped `L²` clause is
`condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_eLpNorm_two`, proved by Lévy's upward theorem.
declarations.header: theorem condExpL2_tendsto_of_lpMeas_closure {Ω : Type u} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m₀) (hm : m ≤ m₀) (hclosure : (⨆ N, lpMeas ℝ ℝ (ℱ N) 2 μ).topologicalClosure = lpMeas ℝ ℝ m 2 μ) (f : Ω →₂[μ] ℝ) : Tendsto (fun N => (condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (ℱ.le' N) f : Ω →₂[μ] ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (condExpL2 ℝ ℝ hm f : Ω →₂[μ] ℝ)) :=
declarations.name: condExpL2_tendsto_of_lpMeas_closure

declarations.docComment:
For a finite measure, the union of the `L²` subspaces measurable with
respect to an increasing filtration is dense in the subspace measurable with
respect to the supremum sigma-algebra.
declarations.header: theorem lpMeas_iSup_filtration_topologicalClosure {Ω : Type u} {m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m₀) : (⨆ N, lpMeas ℝ ℝ (ℱ N) 2 μ).topologicalClosure = lpMeas ℝ ℝ (⨆ N, ℱ N) 2 μ :=
declarations.name: lpMeas_iSup_filtration_topologicalClosure

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `thm:scores-sigma-algebra` (not the mapped proof): the
general finite-measure filtration density theorem above applies after
identifying the supremum of the score filtration with the sigma-algebra
generated by the random element.  The mapped `L²` clause is
`condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_eLpNorm_two`, proved by Lévy's upward theorem.
declarations.header: theorem scoreFiltration_lpMeas_closure {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) : (⨆ N, lpMeas ℝ ℝ (scoreFiltration b X hX N) 2 μ).topologicalClosure = lpMeas ℝ ℝ ((borel H).comap X) 2 μ :=
declarations.name: scoreFiltration_lpMeas_closure

declarations.header: theorem scoreTarget_le {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) : (borel H).comap X ≤ (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω) :=
declarations.name: scoreTarget_le

declarations.docComment:
The `L²` conditional-expectation classes converge in extended distance
once the isolated density statement is supplied.
declarations.header: theorem condExpL2_scoreFiltration_tendsto_edist {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) (Y : Ω → ℝ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Tendsto (fun N => edist (condExpL2 ℝ ℝ ((scoreFiltration b X hX).le' N) (hY.toLp Y) : Ω →₂[μ] ℝ) (condExpL2 ℝ ℝ (scoreTarget_le b X hX) (hY.toLp Y) : Ω →₂[μ] ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: condExpL2_scoreFiltration_tendsto_edist

declarations.docComment:
The square identity transfers small-set `L¹` bounds for squared functions
into small-set `L²` bounds for the original functions.
declarations.header: theorem eLpNorm_square {Ω : Type u} {m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} (f : Ω → ℝ) : eLpNorm (fun ω => (f ω) ^ 2) 1 μ = (eLpNorm f 2 μ) ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: eLpNorm_square

declarations.docComment: Conditional Jensen preserves a squared integrable majorant.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_square_le {Ω : Type u} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hm : m ≤ m₀) {Y : Ω → ℝ} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : (fun ω => (μ[Y | m] ω) ^ 2) ≤ᵐ[μ] μ[(fun ω => (Y ω) ^ 2) | m] :=
declarations.name: conditional_square_le

declarations.docComment:
The full family of scalar conditional expectations of a square-integrable
variable is uniformly integrable in `L²`.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_uniformIntegrable_two {Ω : Type u} {m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] {ι : Type*} (ℱ : ι → MeasurableSpace Ω) (hℱ : ∀ i, ℱ i ≤ m₀) {Y : Ω → ℝ} (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : UnifIntegrable (fun i => μ[Y | ℱ i]) 2 μ :=
declarations.name: conditional_uniformIntegrable_two

declarations.docComment:
Lévy's upward theorem in `L²`, along the martingale-convergence route: the
almost-everywhere Lévy theorem plus the uniform integrability of the conditional
means in `L²` (Vitali).
declarations.header: theorem levy_upward_L2 {Ω : Type u} {m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (ℱ : Filtration ℕ m₀) (Y : Ω → ℝ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Tendsto (fun N => eLpNorm (μ[Y | ℱ N] - μ[Y | ⨆ n, ℱ n]) 2 μ) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: levy_upward_L2

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:scores-sigma-algebra`.
The `L²` convergence clause: `E[Y | G_N] → E[Y | σ(X)]` in `L²` for `Y ∈ L²`, by
Lévy's upward theorem (`levy_upward_L2`: almost-sure convergence plus uniform
integrability) for the increasing score filtration, after the Parseval
identification `⨆ N, G_N = σ(X)`.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_eLpNorm_two {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : Measurable X) (Y : Ω → ℝ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Tendsto (fun N => eLpNorm (μ[Y | scoreFiltration b X hX N] - μ[Y | (borel H).comap X]) 2 μ) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: condExp_scoreFiltration_tendsto_eLpNorm_two

declarations.docComment: Conditional expectation commutes with each scalar score functional.
declarations.header: theorem score_condExp_ae_eq {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) {X : Ω → H} (hX : Integrable X μ) (n : ℕ) : (fun ω => score b n (μ[X | m] ω)) =ᵐ[μ] μ[(fun ω => score b n (X ω)) | m] :=
declarations.name: score_condExp_ae_eq

declarations.docComment:
The thesis partial sum `S_N(x) = ∑_{n<N} θₙ(x) eₙ`, as the finite orthogonal
projection of `x` onto `span{e₀, …, e_{N-1}}`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def scoreProjection {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) : H →L[ℝ] H :=
declarations.name: scoreProjection

declarations.header: theorem scoreProjection_apply {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) (x : H) : scoreProjection b N x = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, score b n x • b n :=
declarations.name: scoreProjection_apply

declarations.docComment: Bessel's inequality: the projection is a contraction, `‖S_N(x)‖ ≤ ‖x‖`.
declarations.header: theorem norm_scoreProjection_le {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) (x : H) : ‖scoreProjection b N x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ :=
declarations.name: norm_scoreProjection_le

declarations.docComment:
Orthogonality gives the exact squared residual `‖x - S_N(x)‖² = ‖x‖² - ∑_{n<N} θₙ(x)²`,
hence the decreasing error envelope used by conditional dominated convergence.
declarations.header: theorem scoreProjection_residual_sq {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (N : ℕ) (x : H) : ‖x - scoreProjection b N x‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2 - ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (score b n x) ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: scoreProjection_residual_sq

declarations.header: theorem scoreProjection_residual_antitone {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (x : H) : Antitone (fun N => ‖x - scoreProjection b N x‖) :=
declarations.name: scoreProjection_residual_antitone

declarations.docComment:
Conditional dominated convergence for a nonnegative decreasing envelope, in the
almost-sure form used by the thesis.  Mathlib's `L¹` dominated convergence theorem for
`condExpL1` gives convergence in measure, hence a subsequence converging almost
everywhere; monotonicity of conditional expectation upgrades that subsequence to the
full sequence.
declarations.header: theorem conditional_antitone_dominated_zero {Ω : Type u} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (r : ℕ → Ω → ℝ) (bound : Ω → ℝ) (hrmeas : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (r n) μ) (hbound : Integrable bound μ) (hrbound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, ‖r n ω‖ ≤ bound ω) (hranti : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Antitone (fun n => r n ω)) (hrzero : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => r n ω) atTop (𝓝 0)) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => μ[r n | m] ω) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: conditional_antitone_dominated_zero

declarations.docComment:
The thesis's conditional dominated convergence step: `S_N ∘ X → X` pointwise with
`‖S_N ∘ X‖ ≤ ‖X‖`, and `‖X‖` is integrable, so `E[S_N ∘ X | G] → E[X | G]` almost
surely.  The residual envelope `‖S_N ∘ X - X‖ ≤ 2‖X‖` is decreasing by
`scoreProjection_residual_antitone`.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_scoreProjection_tendsto {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) {X : Ω → H} (hX : Integrable X μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun N => μ[(fun u => scoreProjection b N (X u)) | m] ω) atTop (𝓝 (μ[X | m] ω)) :=
declarations.name: condExp_scoreProjection_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
The thesis's linearity step: `E[S_N | G] = ∑_{n<N} E[θₙ | G] eₙ` almost surely, by
linearity of conditional expectation and `E[θₙ eₙ | G] = E[θₙ | G] eₙ` for the fixed
deterministic basis vector `eₙ`.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_scoreProjection_eq_finite_scores {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) {X : Ω → H} (hX : Integrable X μ) (N : ℕ) : μ[(fun u => scoreProjection b N (X u)) | m] =ᵐ[μ] (fun ω => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, μ[(fun u => score b n (X u)) | m] ω • b n) :=
declarations.name: condExp_scoreProjection_eq_finite_scores

declarations.docComment:
In a Hilbert basis, convergence of the partial sums `∑_{n<N} cₙ eₙ` to `z` identifies
each coefficient `cₙ` as the score `⟪eₙ, z⟫` (the scores of the partial sums are
eventually constant and continuous in the limit), so the series is the unconditionally
convergent basis expansion of `z`.
declarations.header: theorem hasSum_of_tendsto_partialSums_smul_basis {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) (c : ℕ → ℝ) {z : H} (h : Tendsto (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, c n • b n) atTop (𝓝 z)) : HasSum (fun n => c n • b n) z :=
declarations.name: hasSum_of_tendsto_partialSums_smul_basis

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Series-convergence clause of Theorem `thm:conditional-expect-Hilbert`.

Original label: `thm:conditional-expect-Hilbert`.

Informal statement: the finite score reconstructions converge almost surely
to the Hilbert-valued conditional expectation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof.  With
`S_N = ∑_{n<N} θₙ eₙ` (`scoreProjection`), linearity of conditional expectation and
pulling out the deterministic vectors give `E[S_N | G] = ∑_{n<N} E[θₙ | G] eₙ`
(`condExp_scoreProjection_eq_finite_scores`); `S_N → X` with `‖S_N‖ ≤ ‖X‖` and
`E‖X‖ < ∞`, so conditional dominated convergence gives `E[S_N | G] → E[X | G]`
almost surely (`condExp_scoreProjection_tendsto`).  The thesis assumes square
integrability on a probability space; the argument only needs Bochner
integrability, so the Lean theorem is slightly stronger.  Lean uses zero-based
natural-number indexing for the Hilbert basis.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_partialSums_tendsto {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) {X : Ω → H} (hX : Integrable X μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, μ[(fun η => score b n (X η)) | m] ω • b n) atTop (𝓝 (μ[X | m] ω)) :=
declarations.name: condExp_partialSums_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Theorem `thm:conditional-expect-Hilbert`.

Original label: `thm:conditional-expect-Hilbert`.

Informal statement: the conditional expectation of a Hilbert-valued random
variable is almost surely the convergent sum of the conditional expectations
of its scalar basis scores.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis proves the almost-sure
convergence of the partial sums `∑_{n<N} E[θₙ | G] eₙ` to `E[X | G]`
(`condExp_partialSums_tendsto`, by the `S_N` / conditional dominated convergence
argument).  The `HasSum` form recorded here is the unconditional-convergence
packaging of that limit: the partial-sum limit identifies the coefficients as the
scores of `E[X | G]`, whose basis expansion converges unconditionally
(`hasSum_of_tendsto_partialSums_smul_basis`).  Lean uses zero-based natural-number
indexing for the Hilbert basis.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_hasSum_scores {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure[m₀] Ω) (hm : m ≤ m₀) [SigmaFinite (μ.trim hm)] (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) {X : Ω → H} (hX : Integrable X μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, HasSum (fun n => μ[(fun η => score b n (X η)) | m] ω • b n) (μ[X | m] ω) :=
declarations.name: condExp_hasSum_scores

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Theorem `thm:regression-theorem`.

Original label: `thm:regression-theorem`.

Informal statement: conditional expectation is the least-squares predictor
among square-integrable random variables measurable with respect to the
conditioning sigma-algebra.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the current manuscript uses membership
in the argmin set. This theorem supplies the orthogonal-projection core: the
distance is the infimum over the measurable subspace. `RegressionMeanSquare`
connects it to the displayed expected squared error for actual random variables.
The Doob--Dynkin factorization through a predictor variable is a separate clause;
the corrected final sentence minimizes over that predictor's sigma-algebra.
declarations.header: theorem condExpL2_minimizes {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} {m m₀ : MeasurableSpace Ω} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] {μ : Measure[m₀] Ω} (hm : m ≤ m₀) (f : Ω →₂[μ] H) : ‖f - (condExpL2 H ℝ hm f : Ω →₂[μ] H)‖ = ⨅ g : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ, ‖f - (g : Ω →₂[μ] H)‖ :=
declarations.name: condExpL2_minimizes

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, predictor-factorisation clause
of Theorem `thm:regression-theorem`.

Original label: `thm:regression-theorem`.

Informal statement: conditioning on a random element `Y` produces a predictor
of the form `g(Y)` for a measurable function `g` on the state space of `Y`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the Doob--Dynkin lemma. The
manuscript assumes the predictor state space is standard Borel; Mathlib's
strong-measurability form only needs the Hilbert-valued codomain to be complete.
The equality is pointwise for Mathlib's chosen conditional-expectation version,
and hence is stronger than the manuscript's almost-sure equality.
declarations.header: theorem condExp_factorsThrough_predictor {Ω : Type u} {E : Type v} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace E] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (Y : Ω → E) (_hY : Measurable Y) (X : Ω → H) : ∃ g : E → H, StronglyMeasurable g ∧ μ[X | (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace E).comap Y] = g ∘ Y :=
declarations.name: condExp_factorsThrough_predictor

declarations.docComment: Matrix coefficients in a Hilbert basis determine a bounded linear operator.
declarations.header: theorem continuousLinearMap_eq_of_basis_matrix_eq {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) {A B : H →L[ℝ] H} (h : ∀ n m, score b m (A (b n)) = score b m (B (b n))) : A = B :=
declarations.name: continuousLinearMap_eq_of_basis_matrix_eq

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Definition `defn:weak-stationarity`.

Original label: `defn:weak-stationarity`.

Informal statement: a process is weakly stationary when its Hilbert-valued
mean is constant and its cross-covariance operator depends only on the lag.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this definition isolates the moment
objects used in the thesis proposition.  Measurability and integrability are
the hypotheses that ensure the supplied `mean` and `crossCov` functions exist;
the coordinate characterization itself is deterministic once those moments
have been formed. `ProcessStationarity.WeaklyStationaryProcess` constructs them
from an actual process and includes the Hilbert--Schmidt lag condition.
declarations.header: def WeaklyStationaryMoments {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (mean : ℕ → H) (crossCov : ℕ → ℕ → H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: WeaklyStationaryMoments

declarations.docComment: Coordinate version of weak stationarity, anchored at time zero.
declarations.header: def CoordinatewiseStationaryMoments {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (mean : ℕ → H) (crossCov : ℕ → ℕ → H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: CoordinatewiseStationaryMoments

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Proposition `prop:weak-stationarity`.

Original label: `prop:weak-stationarity`.

Informal statement: Hilbert-valued weak stationarity is equivalent to
constancy of every coordinate mean and dependence of every coordinate
cross-covariance only on the lag.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the reverse implication deliberately
defines the mean as `mean 0`, rather than first postulating a formal series
`∑ n, μ_n e_n`.  This is the corrected argument noted in `THESIS_ERRORS.md` and
automatically supplies the required square summability. The theorem
`ProcessStationarity.weaklyStationaryProcess_iff_scalar` applies this argument to
actual stochastic moments and discharges their analytic hypotheses.
declarations.header: theorem weaklyStationaryMoments_iff_coordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (mean : ℕ → H) (crossCov : ℕ → ℕ → H →L[ℝ] H) : WeaklyStationaryMoments mean crossCov ↔ CoordinatewiseStationaryMoments b mean crossCov :=
declarations.name: weaklyStationaryMoments_iff_coordinates

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, central-limit clause of
Theorem `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

The complete separable Hilbert-space theorem follows from uniform tightness,
scalar projection CLTs, and uniqueness of the Gaussian characteristic
function. No project-specific axiom is used.
declarations.header: theorem hilbert_central_limit {Ω : Type u} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∃ ν : ProbabilityMeasure H, IsGaussian (ν : Measure H) ∧ FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation (ν : Measure H) id = 0 ∧ FunctionalData.covarianceOperator (ν : Measure H) id = FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0) ∧ TendstoInDistribution (normalizedHilbertSum μ X) atTop id (fun _ : ℕ => μ) (ν : Measure H) :=
declarations.name: hilbert_central_limit

declarations.header: theorem matrixBilin_eq_inner {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (h k : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : h.ofLp ⬝ᵥ ((LinearMap.toMatrix (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis) A.toLinearMap).mulVec k.ofLp = inner ℝ h (A k) :=
declarations.name: matrixBilin_eq_inner

declarations.header: theorem gaussian_covarianceOperator_eq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (A : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι →L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (hA : A.IsPositive) : FunctionalData.covarianceOperator (multivariateGaussian 0 ((LinearMap.toMatrix (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis) A.toLinearMap)) id = A :=
declarations.name: gaussian_covarianceOperator_eq

declarations.docComment:
The normalised empirical sum appearing in the central-limit clause of
Theorem `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def normalizedHilbertSum {Ω : Type*} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : H :=
declarations.name: normalizedHilbertSum

declarations.header: theorem scalarProjection_normalizedHilbertSum {Ω : Type*} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h : H) : scalarProjection h (normalizedHilbertSum μ X n ω) = (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X k ω) - n * μ[fun ω => scalarProjection h (X 0 ω)]) :=
declarations.name: scalarProjection_normalizedHilbertSum

declarations.header: theorem matrixQuad_covariance_eq_variance {Ω : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (t : EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) : t.ofLp ⬝ᵥ ((LinearMap.toMatrix (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun ι ℝ).toBasis) (FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ X).toLinearMap).mulVec t.ofLp = Var[(fun ω => scalarProjection t (X ω)); μ] :=
declarations.name: matrixQuad_covariance_eq_variance

declarations.header: theorem charFun_map_eq_scalarProjection_one {Ω : Type*} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (Y : Ω → H) (hY : AEMeasurable Y μ) (t : H) : charFun (μ.map Y) t = charFun (μ.map (fun ω => scalarProjection t (Y ω))) 1 :=
declarations.name: charFun_map_eq_scalarProjection_one

declarations.header: theorem memLp_comp_linearIsometryEquiv {Ω : Type*} {H K : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℝ K] (μ : Measure Ω) (e : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] K) {X : Ω → H} (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) : MemLp (fun ω => e (X ω)) 2 μ :=
declarations.name: memLp_comp_linearIsometryEquiv

declarations.header: theorem covarianceOperator_comp_linearIsometryEquiv {Ω : Type*} {H K : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (e : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] K) (X : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) : FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (fun ω => e (X ω)) = e.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap.comp ((FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ X).comp e.symm.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap) :=
declarations.name: covarianceOperator_comp_linearIsometryEquiv

declarations.header: theorem covarianceOperator_map_eq {Ω : Type*} {H : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) : FunctionalData.covarianceOperator (μ.map X) id = FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ X :=
declarations.name: covarianceOperator_map_eq

declarations.header: theorem normalizedHilbertSum_comp_linearIsometryEquiv {Ω : Type*} {H K : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℝ K] [CompleteSpace K] (μ : Measure Ω) (e : H ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] K) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : normalizedHilbertSum μ (fun i ω => e (X i ω)) n ω = e (normalizedHilbertSum μ X n ω) :=
declarations.name: normalizedHilbertSum_comp_linearIsometryEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Euclidean form of the central-limit clause of Theorem `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

The limit is constructed as the centred multivariate Gaussian whose covariance
matrix represents the source covariance operator.  Lévy's continuity theorem
upgrades the already formalised scalar projection CLTs to weak convergence of
the vector-valued laws.
declarations.header: theorem euclidean_central_limit {Ω : Type u} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [MeasurableSpace Ω] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → EuclideanSpace ℝ ι) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∃ ν : ProbabilityMeasure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι), IsGaussian (ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)) ∧ FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation (ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)) id = 0 ∧ FunctionalData.covarianceOperator (ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)) id = FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0) ∧ TendstoInDistribution (normalizedHilbertSum μ X) atTop id (fun _ : ℕ => μ) (ν : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ ι)) :=
declarations.name: euclidean_central_limit

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

An orthonormal basis transports the internally proved Euclidean CLT, including
the Gaussian law, zero mean, covariance operator, and weak convergence.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.
The central limit theorem in every real separable Hilbert space, proved

declarations.name: separable_hilbert_central_limit

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.
The former external boundary, retained under its historical name for existing
source links. The full Hilbert-space result now has an internal proof.
declarations.header: theorem hilbert_central_limit_external (_hInfinite : ¬ FiniteDimensional ℝ H) (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∃ ν : ProbabilityMeasure H, IsGaussian (ν : Measure H) ∧ FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation (ν : Measure H) id = 0 ∧ FunctionalData.covarianceOperator (ν : Measure H) id = FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0) ∧ TendstoInDistribution (fun (n : ℕ) ω => Real.sqrt n • ((n : ℝ)⁻¹ • (∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) - FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation μ (X 0))) atTop id (fun _ : ℕ => μ) (ν : Measure H) :=
