declarations.docComment:
Square-summable real matrices, used as the coordinate model for
Hilbert--Schmidt operators.
declarations.header: abbrev HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn (ι : Type*) :=
declarations.name: HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn

declarations.docComment: Compatibility name for the natural-number coordinate model.
declarations.header: abbrev HilbertSchmidtCoordinates := HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ℕ
declarations.name: HilbertSchmidtCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
Coordinates of the rank-one operator `u ⊗ v` in a Hilbert basis.  The
index order matches
`inner (b i) ((u ⊗ v) (b j)) = inner (b i) v * inner (b j) u`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def tensorCoordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v : H) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_apply {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v : H) (ij : ι × ι) : tensorCoordinates b u v ij = b.repr v ij.1 * b.repr u ij.2 :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_apply

declarations.header: theorem summable_basisCoefficient_norm_sq {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (x : H) : Summable (fun i ↦ ‖b.repr x i‖ ^ 2) :=
declarations.name: summable_basisCoefficient_norm_sq

declarations.header: theorem tsum_basisCoefficient_norm_sq {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (x : H) : ∑' i, ‖b.repr x i‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: tsum_basisCoefficient_norm_sq

declarations.docComment:
The coordinate norm of a rank-one operator is the product of the two
vector norms.
declarations.header: theorem norm_tensorCoordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v : H) : ‖tensorCoordinates b u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ :=
declarations.name: norm_tensorCoordinates

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_add_left {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u₁ u₂ v : H) : tensorCoordinates b (u₁ + u₂) v = tensorCoordinates b u₁ v + tensorCoordinates b u₂ v :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_add_left

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_smul_left {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (a : ℝ) (u v : H) : tensorCoordinates b (a • u) v = a • tensorCoordinates b u v :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_smul_left

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_add_right {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v₁ v₂ : H) : tensorCoordinates b u (v₁ + v₂) = tensorCoordinates b u v₁ + tensorCoordinates b u v₂ :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_add_right

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_smul_right {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (a : ℝ) (u v : H) : tensorCoordinates b u (a • v) = a • tensorCoordinates b u v :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_smul_right

declarations.docComment: The rank-one coordinate construction as a continuous bilinear map.
declarations.header: noncomputable def tensorCoordinatesBilinear {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) : H →L[ℝ] H →L[ℝ] (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinatesBilinear

declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinatesBilinear_apply {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v : H) : tensorCoordinatesBilinear b u v = tensorCoordinates b u v :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinatesBilinear_apply

declarations.docComment: Coordinates of `x ⊗ x`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def rankOneCoordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (x : H) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: rankOneCoordinates

declarations.header: theorem norm_rankOneCoordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (x : H) : ‖rankOneCoordinates b x‖ = ‖x‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: norm_rankOneCoordinates

declarations.header: theorem continuous_rankOneCoordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) : Continuous (rankOneCoordinates b) :=
declarations.name: continuous_rankOneCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
The coordinate tensor of two square-integrable Hilbert-valued random
elements is Bochner integrable in `ℓ²(ι×ι)`.
declarations.header: theorem integrable_tensorCoordinates_of_memLp_two {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ tensorCoordinates b (X ω) (Y ω)) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_tensorCoordinates_of_memLp_two

declarations.header: theorem integrable_rankOneCoordinates_of_memLp_two {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ rankOneCoordinates b (X ω)) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_rankOneCoordinates_of_memLp_two

declarations.docComment:
Centred cross-covariance represented as a square-summable matrix of basis
coefficients.
declarations.header: noncomputable def crossCovarianceCoordinates {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: crossCovarianceCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: analytic Hilbert--Schmidt clause used by Proposition
`prop:weak-stationarity` in
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`.

Original label: `prop:weak-stationarity`.

Square-integrability of the two random elements makes their centred
cross-covariance integrable in Hilbert--Schmidt coordinates.  In particular,
the operator-valued lag covariance invoked in the manuscript has a
square-summable matrix, rather than merely coordinatewise finite entries.
declarations.header: theorem integrable_centered_tensorCoordinates_of_memLp_two {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ tensorCoordinates b (X ω - FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation μ X) (Y ω - FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation μ Y)) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_centered_tensorCoordinates_of_memLp_two

declarations.docComment: Empirical raw second-moment coordinates.
declarations.header: noncomputable def rawSecondMomentCoordinates {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: rawSecondMomentCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
The raw rank-one second moment satisfies the Banach-valued strong law in
the Hilbert--Schmidt coordinate space under only a second moment of `X`.
declarations.header: theorem rawSecondMomentCoordinates_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n ↦ rawSecondMomentCoordinates b X n ω) atTop (𝓝 (∫ ω, rankOneCoordinates b (X 0 ω) ∂μ)) :=
declarations.name: rawSecondMomentCoordinates_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment:
Population covariance represented in Hilbert--Schmidt coordinates as raw
second moment minus the rank-one mean correction.
declarations.header: noncomputable def covarianceCoordinates {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: covarianceCoordinates

declarations.docComment: Biased empirical covariance in Hilbert--Schmidt coordinates.
declarations.header: noncomputable def biasedCovarianceCoordinates {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: biasedCovarianceCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
The biased covariance coordinates converge almost surely in their
`ℓ²(ι×ι)` norm.
declarations.header: theorem biasedCovarianceCoordinates_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n ↦ biasedCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω) atTop (𝓝 (covarianceCoordinates μ b (X 0))) :=
declarations.name: biasedCovarianceCoordinates_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment:
The thesis's unbiased covariance estimator in Hilbert--Schmidt
coordinates.
declarations.header: noncomputable def sampleCovarianceCoordinates {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovarianceCoordinates

declarations.docComment:
A tensor coordinate is the corresponding matrix coefficient of the
rank-one continuous operator.
declarations.header: theorem tensorCoordinates_eq_matrixCoefficient {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (u v : H) (i j : ι) : tensorCoordinates b u v (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (FunctionalData.tensorProduct u v (b j)) :=
declarations.name: tensorCoordinates_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.header: theorem rankOneCoordinates_eq_matrixCoefficient {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (x : H) (i j : ι) : rankOneCoordinates b x (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (FunctionalData.tensorProduct x x (b j)) :=
declarations.name: rankOneCoordinates_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.header: theorem sampleCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (i j : ι) : sampleCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (LimitTheorems.sampleCovariance X n ω (b j)) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.header: theorem rawSecondMomentCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (i j : ι) : rawSecondMomentCoordinates b X n ω (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (LimitTheorems.rawSecondMomentOperator X n ω (b j)) :=
declarations.name: rawSecondMomentCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.header: theorem biasedCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (i j : ι) : biasedCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (LimitTheorems.biasedCovarianceOperator X n ω (b j)) :=
declarations.name: biasedCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.docComment:
The same exact `n/(n-1)` correction identity holds in Hilbert--Schmidt
coordinates.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovarianceCoordinates_eq_unbiasedFactor_smul_biased {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (hn : 0 < n) : sampleCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω = ((n : ℝ) * (((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹)) • biasedCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω :=
declarations.name: sampleCovarianceCoordinates_eq_unbiasedFactor_smul_biased

declarations.docComment:
The exact unbiased covariance estimator converges almost surely in the
`ℓ²(ι×ι)` Hilbert--Schmidt coordinate norm.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovarianceCoordinates_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun k ↦ sampleCovarianceCoordinates b X (k + 2) ω) atTop (𝓝 (covarianceCoordinates μ b (X 0))) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovarianceCoordinates_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment:
The population coordinate object is exactly the matrix of the population
covariance operator in the chosen Hilbert basis.
declarations.header: theorem covarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (i j : ι) : covarianceCoordinates μ b X (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ X (b j)) :=
declarations.name: covarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.docComment:
Coordinate differences agree pointwise with the matrix coefficients of
the corresponding operator difference.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovarianceCoordinates_sub_covariance_apply {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (i j : ι) : (sampleCovarianceCoordinates b X n ω - covarianceCoordinates μ b (X 0)) (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) ((LimitTheorems.sampleCovariance X n ω - FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0)) (b j)) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovarianceCoordinates_sub_covariance_apply

declarations.docComment:
Any bounded operator whose matrix coefficients are represented by an
`ℓ²(ι×ι)` element has extended Hilbert--Schmidt norm equal to the
ordinary norm of that coordinate element.
declarations.header: theorem hilbertSchmidtENorm_eq_of_coordinates {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (C : (HilbertSchmidtCoordinatesOn ι)) (hC : ∀ i j, C (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (A (b j))) : LimitTheorems.hilbertSchmidtENorm b A = ENNReal.ofReal ‖C‖ :=
declarations.name: hilbertSchmidtENorm_eq_of_coordinates

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`,
Theorem `thm:lln-covariance`.

Original label: `thm:lln-covariance`.

The exact unbiased sample covariance converges almost surely to the population
covariance in Hilbert--Schmidt norm.  The proof realises rank-one operators in
the complete coordinate space `ℓ²(ι×ι)`, applies Mathlib's Banach-valued
strong law there, and then identifies the coordinate norm with the basis
definition of the extended Hilbert--Schmidt norm.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovariance_hilbertSchmidt_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun k ↦ LimitTheorems.hilbertSchmidtENorm b (LimitTheorems.sampleCovariance X (k + 2) ω - FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0))) atTop (𝓝 0) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovariance_hilbertSchmidt_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, strong-law clause of
Theorem `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Informal statement: empirical means of independent identically distributed
integrable Hilbert-valued random variables converge almost surely to the
Bochner expectation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: mathlib proves the stronger
Banach-valued result under pairwise independence.
declarations.header: theorem hilbert_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] {μ : Measure Ω} (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : Integrable (X 0) μ) (hindep : Pairwise fun i j => X i ⟂ᵢ[μ] X j) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, X i ω) atTop (𝓝 (FunctionalData.hilbertExpectation μ (X 0))) :=
declarations.name: hilbert_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment: Scalar projection along a fixed Hilbert-space direction.
declarations.header: def scalarProjection {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (h x : H) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: scalarProjection

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: finite-dimensional marginal core of the central-limit clause of
Theorem `thm:lln-clt-mean` in
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`.

Original label: `thm:lln-clt-mean`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: every fixed scalar projection of the
normalised Hilbert-valued sum satisfies the ordinary real central limit
theorem. `DayAhead.HilbertCLTInfinite` combines these projections with
uniform tightness to construct the Gaussian limit in the whole space.
declarations.header: theorem scalarProjection_central_limit {Ω : Type u} {Ω' : Type w} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace Ω'] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (μ' : Measure Ω') [IsProbabilityMeasure μ'] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) (h : H) (Y : Ω' → ℝ) (hY : HasLaw Y (gaussianReal 0 Var[(fun ω => scalarProjection h (X 0 ω)); μ].toNNReal) μ') : TendstoInDistribution (fun (n : ℕ) ω => (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X k ω) - n * μ[fun ω => scalarProjection h (X 0 ω)])) atTop Y (fun _ => μ) μ' :=
declarations.name: scalarProjection_central_limit

declarations.docComment:
The preceding projection CLT with the identity random variable on the
canonical centred Gaussian law as its explicit limit.
declarations.header: theorem scalarProjection_central_limit_gaussianReal {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) (h : H) : TendstoInDistribution (fun (n : ℕ) ω => (Real.sqrt n)⁻¹ * (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X k ω) - n * μ[fun ω => scalarProjection h (X 0 ω)])) atTop id (fun _ => μ) (gaussianReal 0 Var[(fun ω => scalarProjection h (X 0 ω)); μ].toNNReal) :=
declarations.name: scalarProjection_central_limit_gaussianReal

declarations.docComment: Empirical raw rank-one second-moment operator.
declarations.header: noncomputable def rawSecondMomentOperator {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : H →L[ℝ] H :=
declarations.name: rawSecondMomentOperator

declarations.docComment: Biased empirical covariance of two fixed scalar projections.
declarations.header: noncomputable def scalarBiasedCovariance {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (h k : H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: scalarBiasedCovariance

declarations.docComment: Elementary centring identity for two finite scalar samples.
declarations.header: theorem sum_centered_mul_centered {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (a b : ι → ℝ) : (∑ i ∈ s, (a i - (s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j ∈ s, a j) * (b i - (s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ j ∈ s, b j)) = (∑ i ∈ s, a i * b i) - (s.card : ℝ) * ((s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ s, a i) * ((s.card : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ s, b i) :=
declarations.name: sum_centered_mul_centered

declarations.docComment: Empirical mean of the first `n` observations, using the thesis convention.
declarations.header: noncomputable def empiricalMean {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [NormedSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : H :=
declarations.name: empiricalMean

declarations.docComment: Taking a scalar projection commutes with the empirical mean.
declarations.header: theorem scalarProjection_empiricalMean {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h : H) : scalarProjection h (empiricalMean X n ω) = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X i ω) :=
declarations.name: scalarProjection_empiricalMean

declarations.docComment: Matrix coefficients of the empirical raw second-moment operator.
declarations.header: theorem inner_rawSecondMomentOperator_apply {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h k : H) : inner ℝ h (rawSecondMomentOperator X n ω k) = (n : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X i ω) * scalarProjection k (X i ω) :=
declarations.name: inner_rawSecondMomentOperator_apply

declarations.docComment:
Biased empirical covariance operator, written as raw second moment minus
the rank-one empirical-mean correction.
declarations.header: noncomputable def biasedCovarianceOperator {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : H →L[ℝ] H :=
declarations.name: biasedCovarianceOperator

declarations.docComment:
Every matrix coefficient of the biased covariance operator is the scalar
biased covariance already used in the coefficientwise proof.
declarations.header: theorem inner_biasedCovarianceOperator_apply {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h k : H) : inner ℝ h (biasedCovarianceOperator X n ω k) = scalarBiasedCovariance X h k n ω :=
declarations.name: inner_biasedCovarianceOperator_apply

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: equation `eq:covariance-operator-estimate` in
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`.

Original label: `eq:covariance-operator-estimate`.

The definition is total on natural indices, while the convergence theorem
below deliberately evaluates it only at `n = k + 2`, where the manuscript's
unbiased denominator is nonzero.
declarations.header: noncomputable def sampleCovariance {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) : H →L[ℝ] H :=
declarations.name: sampleCovariance

declarations.docComment: Pointwise action of the empirical covariance operator.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovariance_apply {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (z : H) : sampleCovariance X n ω z = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ • ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, inner ℝ (X i ω - empiricalMean X n ω) z • (X i ω - empiricalMean X n ω) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovariance_apply

declarations.docComment:
Every matrix coefficient of the empirical covariance operator is the
usual empirical cross-covariance of the corresponding scalar projections.
declarations.header: theorem inner_sampleCovariance_apply {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h k : H) : inner ℝ h (sampleCovariance X n ω k) = ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * ∑ i ∈ Finset.range n, scalarProjection h (X i ω - empiricalMean X n ω) * scalarProjection k (X i ω - empiricalMean X n ω) :=
declarations.name: inner_sampleCovariance_apply

declarations.docComment:
The unbiased operator estimator differs from the biased scalar covariance
coefficient by the usual factor `n/(n-1)`.
declarations.header: theorem inner_sampleCovariance_eq_unbiasedFactor {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (h k : H) (hn : 0 < n) : inner ℝ h (sampleCovariance X n ω k) = (n : ℝ) * ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹ * scalarBiasedCovariance X h k n ω :=
declarations.name: inner_sampleCovariance_eq_unbiasedFactor

declarations.docComment: Exact operator identity behind the scalar unbiased-correction formula.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovariance_eq_unbiasedFactor_smul_biased {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (n : ℕ) (ω : Ω) (hn : 0 < n) : sampleCovariance X n ω = ((n : ℝ) * ((n - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹) • biasedCovarianceOperator X n ω :=
declarations.name: sampleCovariance_eq_unbiasedFactor_smul_biased

declarations.docComment:
The unbiased correction factor along the safe indexing `n + 2` tends to
one.
declarations.header: theorem unbiasedFactor_tendsto_one : Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => ((n + 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) * (((n + 2 - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ)⁻¹)) atTop (𝓝 1) :=
declarations.name: unbiasedFactor_tendsto_one

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:lln-covariance`.
The current thesis asks for operator-norm convergence. This proves that
statement directly in the Banach space of bounded operators, under precisely
the second-moment assumption; no fourth moment is needed.
declarations.header: theorem sampleCovariance_operatorNorm_strong_law_ae {Ω : Type u} {H : Type v} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [MeasurableSpace H] [BorelSpace H] (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : MemLp (X 0) 2 μ) (hindep : iIndepFun X μ) (hident : ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ) : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, Tendsto (fun k => sampleCovariance X (k + 2) ω) atTop (𝓝 (FunctionalData.covarianceOperator μ (X 0))) :=
declarations.name: sampleCovariance_operatorNorm_strong_law_ae

declarations.docComment:
Extended Hilbert--Schmidt norm computed in a fixed Hilbert basis.  The
value may be `∞` for a general bounded operator.
declarations.header: noncomputable def hilbertSchmidtENorm {ι : Type*} {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (A : H →L[ℝ] H) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: hilbertSchmidtENorm

declarations.header: theorem continuous_tensorProduct : Continuous (fun p : H × H ↦ tensorProduct p.1 p.2) :=
declarations.name: continuous_tensorProduct

declarations.header: theorem integrable_tensorProduct_of_memLp_two (μ : Measure Ω) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ tensorProduct (X ω) (Y ω)) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_tensorProduct_of_memLp_two

declarations.docComment:
The tensor order agrees with the thesis: the first argument is the input
functional and the second is the output vector.
declarations.header: noncomputable def crossCovarianceOperator (μ : Measure Ω) (X Y : Ω → H) : H →L[ℝ] H :=
declarations.name: crossCovarianceOperator

declarations.header: theorem integrable_centered_tensorProduct_of_memLp_two (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : Integrable (fun ω ↦ tensorProduct (X ω - hilbertExpectation μ X) (Y ω - hilbertExpectation μ Y)) μ :=
declarations.name: integrable_centered_tensorProduct_of_memLp_two

declarations.header: theorem inner_crossCovarianceOperator_apply (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (a c : H) : inner ℝ c (crossCovarianceOperator μ X Y a) = ∫ ω, inner ℝ a (X ω - hilbertExpectation μ X) * inner ℝ c (Y ω - hilbertExpectation μ Y) ∂μ :=
declarations.name: inner_crossCovarianceOperator_apply

declarations.header: theorem crossCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (i j : ι) : crossCovarianceCoordinates μ b X Y (i, j) = inner ℝ (b i) (crossCovarianceOperator μ X Y (b j)) :=
declarations.name: crossCovarianceCoordinates_apply_eq_matrixCoefficient

declarations.docComment:
Square summability of all matrix entries is the Hilbert--Schmidt condition
in the fixed orthonormal basis.
declarations.header: def IsHilbertSchmidt (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (A : H →L[ℝ] H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: IsHilbertSchmidt

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:weak-stationarity`.
The cross-covariance operator is genuinely Hilbert--Schmidt; this is stronger
than proving finiteness of its individual scalar entries.
declarations.header: theorem crossCovarianceOperator_isHilbertSchmidt (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) : IsHilbertSchmidt b (crossCovarianceOperator μ X Y) :=
declarations.name: crossCovarianceOperator_isHilbertSchmidt

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:weak-stationarity`.
The actual process definition, including the required Hilbert--Schmidt lag
operators. Centering at each time's own expectation equals centering at the
common mean under the first conjunct.
declarations.header: def WeaklyStationaryProcess (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: WeaklyStationaryProcess

declarations.docComment:
Scalar stationarity in exactly the expectation and centered-product form
of the manuscript, with a single coordinate mean for every time.
declarations.header: def ScalarStationaryProcess (μ : Measure Ω) (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) : Prop :=
declarations.name: ScalarStationaryProcess

declarations.header: theorem score_crossCovarianceOperator (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X Y : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hY : MemLp Y 2 μ) (n m : ι) : score b m (crossCovarianceOperator μ X Y (b n)) = ∫ ω, (score b n (X ω) - ∫ η, score b n (X η) ∂μ) * (score b m (Y ω) - ∫ η, score b m (Y η) ∂μ) ∂μ :=
declarations.name: score_crossCovarianceOperator

declarations.header: theorem weaklyStationaryProcess_iff_moments (μ : Measure Ω) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : ∀ t, MemLp (X t) 2 μ) : WeaklyStationaryProcess μ b X ↔ WeaklyStationaryMoments (fun t ↦ hilbertExpectation μ (X t)) (fun t s ↦ crossCovarianceOperator μ (X t) (X s)) :=
declarations.name: weaklyStationaryProcess_iff_moments

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:weak-stationarity`.
Full stochastic version: expectations and covariance operators are constructed
from the square-integrable process, their scalar formulas are proved, and the
Hilbert--Schmidt requirement is discharged. No moment-identification assumptions
are supplied by the caller.
declarations.header: theorem weaklyStationaryProcess_iff_scalar (μ : Measure Ω) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (b : HilbertBasis ι ℝ H) (X : ℕ → Ω → H) (hX : ∀ t, MemLp (X t) 2 μ) : WeaklyStationaryProcess μ b X ↔ ScalarStationaryProcess μ b X :=
declarations.name: weaklyStationaryProcess_iff_scalar

declarations.header: def risk (predictionMinus predictionPlus : ℝ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: risk

declarations.header: theorem constant_risk (c : ℝ) : risk c c = 1 + c ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: constant_risk

declarations.header: theorem best_constant_risk (c : ℝ) : 1 ≤ risk c c :=
declarations.name: best_constant_risk

declarations.header: theorem constant_minimum_attained : risk 0 0 = 1 :=
declarations.name: constant_minimum_attained

declarations.header: theorem fully_observed_risk : risk (-1) 1 = 0 :=
declarations.name: fully_observed_risk

declarations.header: theorem information_sets_have_different_minima : risk (-1) 1 < risk 0 0 ∧ (∀ c : ℝ, risk 0 0 ≤ risk c c) :=
declarations.name: information_sets_have_different_minima

declarations.header: theorem norm_sq_eq_integral (f : Ω →₂[μ] H) : ‖f‖ ^ 2 = ∫ ω, ‖f ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: norm_sq_eq_integral

declarations.header: theorem meanSquareError_eq_norm_sq (f g : Ω →₂[μ] H) : (∫ ω, ‖f ω - g ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) = ‖f - g‖ ^ 2 :=
declarations.name: meanSquareError_eq_norm_sq

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:regression-theorem`.
Expected squared error, rather than merely distance in the abstract L² space,
is minimized by the conditional-expectation projection.
declarations.header: theorem condExpL2_meanSquareError_le (hm : m ≤ m₀) (f : Ω →₂[μ] H) (g : lpMeas H ℝ m 2 μ) : (∫ ω, ‖f ω - (condExpL2 H ℝ hm f : Ω →₂[μ] H) ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤ ∫ ω, ‖f ω - (g : Ω →₂[μ] H) ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: condExpL2_meanSquareError_le

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:regression-theorem`.
For actual random variables, the chosen conditional-expectation version
minimizes the integral of squared error against every square-integrable
predictor measurable with respect to the same information set.
declarations.header: theorem conditionalExpectation_minimizes_meanSquareError [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (hm : m ≤ m₀) (X Z : Ω → H) (hX : MemLp X 2 μ) (hZ : MemLp Z 2 μ) (hZm : AEStronglyMeasurable[m] Z μ) : (∫ ω, ‖X ω - μ[X | m] ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ) ≤ ∫ ω, ‖X ω - Z ω‖ ^ 2 ∂μ :=
declarations.name: conditionalExpectation_minimizes_meanSquareError

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`.
Normalization leaves exactly a sign choice in a one-dimensional eigenspace.
declarations.header: theorem unit_vectors_eq_or_neg_of_finrank_one (U : Submodule ℝ H) (hU : Module.finrank ℝ U = 1) {x y : U} (hx : ‖x‖ = 1) (hy : ‖y‖ = 1) : y = x ∨ y = -x :=
declarations.name: unit_vectors_eq_or_neg_of_finrank_one

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`.
Both signs are unit eigenvectors for the same eigenvalue.
declarations.header: theorem neg_unit_eigenvector (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (eigenvalue : ℝ) {x : H} (hx : A x = eigenvalue • x) (hn : ‖x‖ = 1) : A (-x) = eigenvalue • (-x) ∧ ‖-x‖ = 1 :=
declarations.name: neg_unit_eigenvector

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`.
Distinct orthonormal basis vectors can be exchanged within one eigenspace.
declarations.header: theorem orthonormalBasis_swap_ne {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (b : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ H) {i j : ι} (hij : i ≠ j) : ∃ c : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ H, c ≠ b ∧ c i = b j ∧ c j = b i :=
declarations.name: orthonormalBasis_swap_ne

declarations.docComment:
Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`.
The sum of rank-one projections depends only on the eigenspace, for any two
orthonormal bases, even with different finite index types.
declarations.header: theorem orthonormalBasis_projection_invariant {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (U : Submodule ℝ H) [U.HasOrthogonalProjection] (b : OrthonormalBasis ι ℝ U) (c : OrthonormalBasis κ ℝ U) : (∑ i, InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ (b i : H) (b i : H)) = ∑ j, InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ (c j : H) (c j : H) :=
declarations.name: orthonormalBasis_projection_invariant

declarations.docComment:
A positive countable family with finite positive superlevel sets can be
enumerated in decreasing order. Equal values are ordered using an injective
natural-number encoding; finite predecessor counts give the ordered indices.
The empty and finite cases are included.
declarations.header: theorem exists_antitone_reindex {ι : Type v} [Countable ι] (f : ι → ℝ) (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < f i) (hfinite : ∀ ε > 0, Set.Finite {i | ε ≤ f i}) : ∃ (I : Set ℕ) (r : I ≃ ι), Antitone (fun n => f (r n)) :=
declarations.name: exists_antitone_reindex

declarations.docComment:
Supporting fact: the algebraic span of an infinite orthonormal basis is proper.

The dense span of a countably infinite Hilbert basis is strictly larger than
its algebraic span: the vector with coordinates `2⁻ⁿ` has infinitely many
nonzero coordinates, whereas every finite linear combination has finite support.
declarations.header: theorem hilbertBasis_algebraic_span_ne_top (b : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ H) : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range b) ≠ ⊤ :=
declarations.name: hilbertBasis_algebraic_span_ne_top

declarations.docComment:
Operator-norm convergence of an orthonormal eigen-expansion forces only
finitely many eigenvalues to exceed any given positive magnitude.
declarations.header: theorem finite_eigenvalue_superlevels {ι : Type v} (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (e : ι → H) (eigenvalue : ι → ℝ) (he : Orthonormal ℝ e) (heigen : ∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) (hseries : Tendsto (fun s : Finset ι => ∑ i ∈ s, eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) atTop (𝓝 A)) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) : Set.Finite {i | ε ≤ |eigenvalue i|} :=
declarations.name: finite_eigenvalue_superlevels

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: the eigenvalue-ordering clause in the spectral remark.

Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`

This is an actual ordered nonzero eigenbasis and operator-norm expansion,
including empty and finite-dimensional range cases.
declarations.header: theorem compact_selfAdjoint_ordered_rankOne_expansion [CompleteSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : ∃ (I : Set ℕ) (e : I → H) (eigenvalue : I → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ e ∧ (∀ i, eigenvalue i ≠ 0) ∧ Antitone (fun i => |eigenvalue i|) ∧ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e)).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure ∧ (∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) ∧ HasSum (fun i => eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) A :=
declarations.name: compact_selfAdjoint_ordered_rankOne_expansion

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: the kernel-extension clause in the spectral remark.

Original block id: `source:2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex:105:rem:5`

An orthonormal basis of the closed range extends to a Hilbert basis of the
whole space, and the newly adjoined orthonormal vectors have closed span
exactly the kernel. Ordering is asserted for the nonzero range eigenvalues
separately; it is not imposed on a natural-number enumeration of this union.
declarations.header: theorem range_basis_extension_by_kernel [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) {ι : Type v} (e : ι → H) (he : Orthonormal ℝ e) (hspan : (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e)).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure) : ∃ (w : Set H) (b : HilbertBasis w ℝ H), Set.range e ⊆ w ∧ ⇑b = (Subtype.val : w → H) ∧ (∀ x ∈ w \ Set.range e, A x = 0) ∧ (Submodule.span ℝ (w \ Set.range e)).topologicalClosure = LinearMap.ker A.toLinearMap :=
declarations.name: range_basis_extension_by_kernel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: `2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`, spectral
completeness core of Theorem `thm:spectral-thm`.

Original label: `thm:spectral-thm`.

Informal statement: the eigenspaces of a compact self-adjoint operator span a
dense subspace of the Hilbert space (including the zero eigenspace, i.e. the
kernel).

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is Mathlib's compact self-adjoint
spectral theorem. The manuscript's basis of `closure (range A)` is obtained by
discarding the zero eigenspace; a basis of the kernel then extends it to the
whole space.
declarations.header: theorem compact_selfAdjoint_eigenspaces_complete {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : (⨆ a : ℝ, Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap a)ᗮ = ⊥ :=
declarations.name: compact_selfAdjoint_eigenspaces_complete

declarations.docComment: Every nonzero eigenspace of a compact operator has finite dimension.
declarations.header: theorem compact_nonzero_eigenspace_finiteDimensional {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (a : ℝ) (ha : a ≠ 0) : FiniteDimensional ℝ (Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap a) :=
declarations.name: compact_nonzero_eigenspace_finiteDimensional

declarations.docComment: Distinct eigenspaces of a self-adjoint operator are orthogonal.
declarations.header: theorem selfAdjoint_distinct_eigenvectors_orthogonal {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) {eigenvalue₁ eigenvalue₂ : ℝ} (hne : eigenvalue₁ ≠ eigenvalue₂) {x y : H} (hx : x ∈ Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue₁) (hy : y ∈ Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue₂) : inner ℝ x y = 0 :=
declarations.name: selfAdjoint_distinct_eigenvectors_orthogonal

declarations.docComment: A nonzero-eigenvalue eigenspace lies in the range of the operator.
declarations.header: theorem nonzero_eigenspace_le_range {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (eigenvalue : ℝ) (hne : eigenvalue ≠ 0) : Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue ≤ LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap :=
declarations.name: nonzero_eigenspace_le_range

declarations.docComment:
The closed range of a self-adjoint operator is the orthogonal complement
of its kernel.  This is the structural fact behind the manuscript's statement
that a nonzero eigenbasis spans `closure (range A)` and may be extended by a
basis of the kernel.
declarations.header: theorem selfAdjoint_closure_range_eq_orthogonal_ker {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.ker A.toLinearMap)ᗮ :=
declarations.name: selfAdjoint_closure_range_eq_orthogonal_ker

declarations.docComment: The supremum of all nonzero eigenspaces is contained in the closed range.
declarations.header: theorem iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_le_closure_range {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) : (⨆ eigenvalue : {a : ℝ // a ≠ 0}, Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue.1) ≤ (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure :=
declarations.name: iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_le_closure_range

declarations.docComment:
For a compact self-adjoint operator, the orthogonal complement of the
nonzero eigenspaces is exactly the kernel.
declarations.header: theorem orthogonal_iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_eq_ker {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : (⨆ eigenvalue : {a : ℝ // a ≠ 0}, Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue.1)ᗮ = LinearMap.ker A.toLinearMap :=
declarations.name: orthogonal_iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_eq_ker

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: subspace-completeness clause of Theorem `thm:spectral-thm` in
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`.

Original label: `thm:spectral-thm`.

The closed span of all nonzero eigenspaces is exactly the closure of the
operator range.  This verifies the subspace-completeness clause of the
manuscript's spectral theorem without invoking the external rank-one series.
declarations.header: theorem closure_iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_eq_closure_range {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : (⨆ eigenvalue : {a : ℝ // a ≠ 0}, Module.End.eigenspace A.toLinearMap eigenvalue.1).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure :=
declarations.name: closure_iSup_nonzero_eigenspaces_eq_closure_range

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source: finite-dimensional specialisation of Theorem
`thm:spectral-thm` in
`2 - day-ahead/3_functional_data_analysis.tex`.

Original label: `thm:spectral-thm`.

In finite dimension the complete rank-one eigen-expansion follows directly
from Mathlib's orthonormal eigenvector basis.  No compactness hypothesis or
external theorem is needed in this case.
declarations.header: theorem finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [FiniteDimensional ℝ H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : let e := hsymm.eigenvectorBasis
declarations.name: finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion

declarations.docComment:
The finite-subset net of the preceding finite-dimensional expansion is
eventually equal to the operator.
declarations.header: theorem finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion_tendsto {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [FiniteDimensional ℝ H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : let I := Fin (Module.finrank ℝ H)
declarations.name: finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion_tendsto

declarations.docComment:
Removing the zero-eigenvalue indices from the finite-dimensional
expansion does not change the represented operator.
declarations.header: theorem finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_nonzero_rankOne_expansion {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [FiniteDimensional ℝ H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : let eBasis := hsymm.eigenvectorBasis
declarations.name: finiteDimensional_selfAdjoint_nonzero_rankOne_expansion

declarations.docComment:
In finite dimension, the thesis's nonzero-eigenvector series package is
fully internal, including countability and convergence of the finite-subset
net.
declarations.header: theorem finiteDimensional_rankOne_expansion_data {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] [FiniteDimensional ℝ H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : ∃ (I : Type) (_hI : Countable I) (e : I → H) (eigenvalue : I → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ e ∧ (∀ i, eigenvalue i ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) ∧ Tendsto (fun s : Finset I ↦ ∑ i ∈ s, eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) atTop (𝓝 A) :=
declarations.name: finiteDimensional_rankOne_expansion_data

declarations.docComment:
Exact operator-series packaging of thesis Theorem `thm:spectral-thm`.

Original label: `thm:spectral-thm`.

Proof: choose an orthonormal basis of each finite-dimensional nonzero
eigenspace and combine them using orthogonality of distinct eigenspaces.
Separability makes the resulting family countable. Its closed span contains
the operator range, and finite orthogonal projections converge uniformly on
the compact closure of the image of the unit ball. This gives convergence in
operator norm. The historical declaration name is retained for compatibility;
it no longer introduces an axiom.

The finite-subset net avoids choosing an arbitrary enumeration. Countability
matches the separability assumption in the thesis. The closed-span conclusion
is no longer assumed here: it is derived below from the operator-norm limit.
declarations.header: theorem compact_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion_external {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) (_hInfinite : ¬ FiniteDimensional ℝ H) : ∃ (ι : Type) (_hι : Countable ι) (e : ι → H) (eigenvalue : ι → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ e ∧ (∀ i, eigenvalue i ≠ 0) ∧ (∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) ∧ Tendsto (fun s : Finset ι => ∑ i ∈ s, eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) atTop (𝓝 A) :=
declarations.name: compact_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion_external

declarations.docComment:
An operator-norm-convergent rank-one eigen-expansion necessarily has
closed eigenvector span equal to the closed operator range.
declarations.header: theorem closedSpan_eq_closure_range_of_rankOne_expansion {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) {ι : Type v} (e : ι → H) (eigenvalue : ι → ℝ) (hne : ∀ i, eigenvalue i ≠ 0) (heigen : ∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) (hseries : Tendsto (fun s : Finset ι => ∑ i ∈ s, eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) atTop (𝓝 A)) : (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e)).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure :=
declarations.name: closedSpan_eq_closure_range_of_rankOne_expansion

declarations.docComment:
Full operator-series formulation of thesis Theorem `thm:spectral-thm`.

Original label: `thm:spectral-thm`.

Both the finite- and infinite-dimensional expansions are proved internally.
The basis-of-closed-range clause follows from the operator-norm series limit
and the nonzero eigenvalue identities.
declarations.header: theorem compact_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion {H : Type u} [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℝ H] [CompleteSpace H] [SecondCountableTopology H] (A : H →L[ℝ] H) (hcompact : IsCompactOperator A) (hsymm : A.toLinearMap.IsSymmetric) : ∃ (ι : Type) (_hι : Countable ι) (e : ι → H) (eigenvalue : ι → ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ e ∧ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range e)).topologicalClosure = (LinearMap.range A.toLinearMap).topologicalClosure ∧ (∀ i, A (e i) = eigenvalue i • e i) ∧ Tendsto (fun s : Finset ι => ∑ i ∈ s, eigenvalue i • FunctionalData.tensorProduct (e i) (e i)) atTop (𝓝 A) :=
declarations.name: compact_selfAdjoint_rankOne_expansion

Informal statement: after the thesis' length-stabilization step, appending

measurable sorting rule, matching the thesis proof.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: operation set `A = {\oplus, \ominus, \circledast}` in
`defn:actions`.

Informal statement: the three primitive operation labels: tuple addition,
cancellation, and modification.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: instead of using a literal finite set of
function symbols, Lean uses an inductive type with three constructors. This is
the tag set indexing the dependent family `ActionPayload`.
declarations.header: inductive ActionKind
declarations.name: ActionKind

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: `defn:actions`, action space `\mathscr{A}(X)`.

Informal statement: an action is a disjoint-union element consisting of a
primitive operation label and a payload admissible for that operation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes a disjoint union
`\bigsqcup_{\alpha\in A} F_\alpha`. Lean represents this finite dependent
disjoint union as an inductive type with one constructor for each primitive
operation. This avoids universe bookkeeping around the heterogeneous payload
spaces while keeping the same tagged-union content.
declarations.header: inductive MarketAction (X : Type u) : Type (max u 1)
declarations.name: MarketAction

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: operation label in `defn:actions`.

Informal statement: recover the primitive operation label from a tagged
market action.
declarations.header: def kind : MarketAction X → ActionKind | add _ => ActionKind.add | cancel _ => ActionKind.cancel | modify _ => ActionKind.modify end MarketAction /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Composite Actions". Original label: application/evaluation map in `defn:actions`. Informal statement: apply one action to a tuple
declarations.name: kind

`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: application/evaluation map in `defn:actions`.

Informal statement: apply one action to a tuple by selecting the primitive
operation associated with the action tag.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes `x \lhd (o,\alpha)=\alpha(x,o)`. Lean
pattern matches on the action constructor, so the payload `o` automatically
has the right type in each branch.
declarations.header: noncomputable def applyAction (x : Tuple X) (a : MarketAction X) : Tuple X :=
declarations.name: applyAction

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: addition case of the application map in `defn:actions`.
declarations.header: theorem applyAction_add (x y : Tuple X) : applyAction x (MarketAction.add y) = concat x y :=
declarations.name: applyAction_add

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: cancellation case of the application map in `defn:actions`.

declarations.name: applyAction_cancel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the action-space extended distance is the disjoint-union
distance over the three primitive action payload spaces. Actions with the same
operation label are compared by the corresponding payload distance; actions
with different labels are at distance `∞`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes the action space as a finite disjoint union
and then applies the disjoint-union metric. Since `MarketAction` is the
Lean-native tagged union used for that finite disjoint union, the same metric
is written by pattern matching on constructors.
declarations.header: noncomputable def actionEDistance {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : MarketAction X → MarketAction X → ENNReal | MarketAction.add x, MarketAction.add y => edist x y | MarketAction.cancel eta, MarketAction.cancel theta => edist eta theta | MarketAction.modify xi, MarketAction.modify zeta => edist xi zeta | _, _ => ⊤ /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`. Informal statement: two addition actions are compared
declarations.name: actionEDistance

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: two addition actions are compared by the tuple Hausdorff
distance of their payload tuples.
declarations.header: theorem actionEDistance_add_add {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : actionEDistance (MarketAction.add x) (MarketAction.add y) = edist x y :=
declarations.name: actionEDistance_add_add

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: two cancellation actions are compared by the finite-set
Hausdorff distance of their index sets.
declarations.header: theorem actionEDistance_cancel_cancel {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (eta theta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : actionEDistance (MarketAction.cancel (X := X) eta)
declarations.name: actionEDistance_cancel_cancel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: two modification actions are compared by the distinct
finite-set Hausdorff distance of their replacement graphs.
declarations.header: theorem actionEDistance_modify_modify {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (xi zeta : DistinctFiniteSubsets X) : actionEDistance (MarketAction.modify xi) (MarketAction.modify zeta) = edist xi zeta :=
declarations.name: actionEDistance_modify_modify

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: different action labels lie in different disjoint-union
components, so their action distance is `∞`.
declarations.header: theorem actionEDistance_eq_top_of_kind_ne {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a b : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind ≠ b.kind) : actionEDistance a b = ⊤ :=
declarations.name: actionEDistance_eq_top_of_kind_ne

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: finite action distance forces the two actions to have the
same operation label.
declarations.header: theorem kind_eq_of_actionEDistance_lt_top {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a b : MarketAction X} (h : actionEDistance a b < ⊤) : a.kind = b.kind :=
declarations.name: kind_eq_of_actionEDistance_lt_top

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`, component family `F_α`.

Informal statement: the three payload spaces `F_⊕ = T(X)`, `F_⊖ = F(ℕ)` and
`F_⊛ = L(X)`, indexed by the operation labels and lifted to a common universe so
that they form a Lean `Sigma` family: the thesis disjoint union
`⨆_{α ∈ A} F_α`.
declarations.header: def ActionFamily (X : Type u) : ActionKind → Type (max u 1) | .add => ULift.{max u 1} (Tuple X) | .cancel => ULift.{max u 1} (FiniteSubsets ℕ) | .modify => ULift.{max u 1} (DistinctFiniteSubsets X) /-- Each component `F_α` carries its thesis metric `d_α` (universe lifting is isometric). -/ @[reducible] noncomputable instance actionFamilyEMetricSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (k : ActionKind) : EMetricSpace (ActionFamily X k) :=
declarations.name: ActionFamily

declarations.docComment:
Each component `F_α` carries its thesis metric `d_α` (universe lifting is
isometric).
declarations.header: @[reducible] noncomputable instance actionFamilyEMetricSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (k : ActionKind) : EMetricSpace (ActionFamily X k) :=
declarations.name: actionFamilyEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`, `𝒜(X) = ⨆_{α ∈ A} F_α`.

Informal statement: the tagged union `MarketAction X` is (in bijection with)
the thesis disjoint union of the payload spaces.
declarations.header: def actionSigmaEquiv (X : Type u) : MarketAction X ≃ Sigma (ActionFamily X)
declarations.name: actionSigmaEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`, definition of `Δ`.

Informal statement: under the identification `𝒜(X) = ⨆_α F_α`, the action
distance `Δ` is literally the disjoint-union distance of
`defn:disjoint-union-metrisation`.
declarations.header: theorem disjointEdist_actionSigmaEquiv {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (a b : MarketAction X) : DisjointUnionTopology.disjointEdist (actionSigmaEquiv X a) (actionSigmaEquiv X b) = actionEDistance a b :=
declarations.name: disjointEdist_actionSigmaEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: register the thesis action distance as the Lean extended
distance on the action space.
declarations.header: noncomputable instance instEDist {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : EDist (MarketAction X)
declarations.name: instEDist

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the action-space distance satisfies the extended
pseudometric laws.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: exactly the thesis citation of
`prop:disjoint-union-metrisation`: by `disjointEdist_actionSigmaEquiv`, `Δ` is
the disjoint-union distance on `⨆_α F_α`, so the pseudometric laws are those of
`DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace`.
declarations.header: noncomputable instance instPseudoEMetricSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : PseudoEMetricSpace (MarketAction X)
declarations.name: instPseudoEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the action-space pseudometric separates points, hence is
an extended metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: as in the thesis, this is the separation
clause of `prop:disjoint-union-metrisation` for `⨆_α F_α`, transported along
the identification `actionSigmaEquiv`.
declarations.header: noncomputable instance instEMetricSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : EMetricSpace (MarketAction X) :=
declarations.name: instEMetricSpace

declarations.header: theorem edist_add_add {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : edist (MarketAction.add x) (MarketAction.add y) = edist x y :=
declarations.name: edist_add_add

declarations.header: theorem edist_cancel_cancel {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (eta theta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : edist (MarketAction.cancel (X := X) eta) (MarketAction.cancel theta) =
declarations.name: edist_cancel_cancel

declarations.header: theorem edist_modify_modify {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (xi zeta : DistinctFiniteSubsets X) : edist (MarketAction.modify xi) (MarketAction.modify zeta) = edist xi zeta :=
declarations.name: edist_modify_modify

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: `(𝒜(X), Δ)` is isometric to the disjoint union
`⨆_{α ∈ A} F_α` carrying the metric of `prop:disjoint-union-metrisation`. This
is the identification through which the thesis cites the disjoint-union
propositions for the metric, completeness and separability of `𝒜(X)`.
declarations.header: def actionSigmaIsometry (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : letI : EMetricSpace (Sigma (ActionFamily X)) :=
declarations.name: actionSigmaIsometry

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Original label: `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: topologically, the action space is the coproduct
`⨆_{α ∈ A} F_α` (every component is open). This follows from the isometry above
and the thesis topology bridge `metricTopology_eq_sigma`; it is the canonical
identification used by the pasting arguments below.
declarations.header: def actionSigmaHomeomorph (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : MarketAction X ≃ₜ Sigma (ActionFamily X) :=
declarations.name: actionSigmaHomeomorph

declarations.header: @[simp] theorem actionSigmaHomeomorph_apply {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (a : MarketAction X) : actionSigmaHomeomorph X a = actionSigmaEquiv X a := rfl
declarations.name: actionSigmaHomeomorph_apply

declarations.header: @[simp] theorem actionSigmaHomeomorph_symm_apply {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (a : Sigma (ActionFamily X)) : (actionSigmaHomeomorph X).symm a = (actionSigmaEquiv X).symm a := rfl
declarations.name: actionSigmaHomeomorph_symm_apply

declarations.docComment:
Universe lifting is an isometric equivalence, so each lifted component of
`ActionFamily` has exactly the metric properties of its payload space.
declarations.header: def uliftIsometryEquiv (α : Type*) [PseudoEMetricSpace α] : ULift.{max u 1} α ≃ᵢ α :=
declarations.name: uliftIsometryEquiv

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: in the registered metric, actions in different operation
components have distance `∞`.
declarations.header: theorem edist_eq_top_of_kind_ne {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a b : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind ≠ b.kind) : edist a b = ⊤ :=
declarations.name: edist_eq_top_of_kind_ne

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: finite registered action distance forces a shared
operation label.
declarations.header: theorem kind_eq_of_edist_lt_top {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a b : MarketAction X} (h : edist a b < ⊤) : a.kind = b.kind :=
declarations.name: kind_eq_of_edist_lt_top

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: a Cauchy sequence of actions is eventually contained in
one operation component.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: an auxiliary consequence of the
disjoint-union metric (distance `< ∞` forces equal tags, and a Cauchy sequence
is eventually at distance `< 1`); it is the action-space instance of
`DisjointUnionTopology.cauchySeq_eventually_constant_tag`. It is not used by
the mapped completeness proof `completeSpace`, which transfers
`prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties` along `actionSigmaIsometry`.
declarations.header: theorem cauchySeq_eventually_constant_kind {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {u : ℕ → MarketAction X} (hu : CauchySeq u) : ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n, N ≤ n → (u n).kind = (u N).kind :=
declarations.name: cauchySeq_eventually_constant_kind

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: extract an addition payload, using a default value away
from the addition component.
declarations.header: def addPayloadD (default : Tuple X) : MarketAction X → Tuple X | MarketAction.add y => y | _ => default /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`. Informal statement: extract a cancellation payload, using a default value away from the cancellation component. -/ def cancelPayloadD (default : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : MarketAction X → FiniteSubsets ℕ | MarketAction.cancel eta => eta | _ => default /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`. Informal statement: extract a modification payload, using a default value away from the modification component. -/ def modifyPayloadD (default : DistinctFiniteSubsets X) : MarketAction X → DistinctFiniteSubsets X | MarketAction.modify xi => xi | _ => default theorem add_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : Tuple X} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.add) : MarketAction.add (addPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: addPayloadD

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: extract a cancellation payload, using a default value
away from the cancellation component.
declarations.header: def cancelPayloadD (default : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : MarketAction X → FiniteSubsets ℕ | MarketAction.cancel eta => eta | _ => default /-- Thesis source: `1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, `cor:action-metrisation`. Informal statement: extract a modification payload, using a default value away from the modification component. -/ def modifyPayloadD (default : DistinctFiniteSubsets X) : MarketAction X → DistinctFiniteSubsets X | MarketAction.modify xi => xi | _ => default theorem add_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : Tuple X} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.add) : MarketAction.add (addPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: cancelPayloadD

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: extract a modification payload, using a default value away
from the modification component.
declarations.header: def modifyPayloadD (default : DistinctFiniteSubsets X) : MarketAction X → DistinctFiniteSubsets X | MarketAction.modify xi => xi | _ => default theorem add_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : Tuple X} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.add) : MarketAction.add (addPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: modifyPayloadD

declarations.header: theorem add_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : Tuple X} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.add) : MarketAction.add (addPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: add_payload_mk_of_kind

declarations.header: theorem cancel_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : FiniteSubsets ℕ} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.cancel) : MarketAction.cancel (X := X) (cancelPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: cancel_payload_mk_of_kind

declarations.header: theorem modify_payload_mk_of_kind {X : Type u} {default : DistinctFiniteSubsets X} {a : MarketAction X} (h : a.kind = ActionKind.modify) : MarketAction.modify (modifyPayloadD default a) = a :=
declarations.name: modify_payload_mk_of_kind

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: if `X` is complete, then the action space
`\mathscr{A}(X)` is complete.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. The components
are complete (`thm:tuple-space-properties` for `T(X)`,
`thm:labelled-properties` for `L(X)`, uniform discreteness for `F(ℕ)`), so the
disjoint union `⨆_α F_α` is complete by `prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties`
(`DisjointUnionTopology.completeSpace`), and `𝒜(X)` is isometric to it
(`actionSigmaIsometry`).
declarations.header: theorem completeSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] : CompleteSpace (MarketAction X) :=
declarations.name: completeSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`cor:action-metrisation`.

Informal statement: if `X` is separable, then the action space
`\mathscr{A}(X)` is separable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. The components
are separable (`thm:tuple-space-properties`, `thm:labelled-properties`,
`prop:finite-separable`), so the finite disjoint union `⨆_α F_α` is separable
by `prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties`
(`DisjointUnionTopology.separableSpace_sigma_of_countable`), and `𝒜(X)` is
homeomorphic to it (`actionSigmaHomeomorph`, built from the isometry).
declarations.header: theorem separableSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (MarketAction X) :=
declarations.name: separableSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`prop:application-continuous`.

Informal statement: if an action is finitely close to an addition action,
then it is itself an addition action and its tuple payload is close.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: an auxiliary local consequence of the
disjoint-union metric (different components have distance `∞`, so any
finite-radius neighborhood of an addition action stays in the addition
component). It is not used by the mapped continuity proof below, which follows
the thesis pasting argument.
declarations.header: theorem exists_add_payload_of_edist_lt {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a : MarketAction X} {y₀ : Tuple X} {δ : ENNReal} (h : edist a (MarketAction.add y₀) < δ) : ∃ y : Tuple X, a = MarketAction.add y ∧ edist y y₀ < δ :=
declarations.name: exists_add_payload_of_edist_lt

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`prop:application-continuous`.

Informal statement: finite closeness to a cancellation action forces the
nearby action to be cancellation, with close finite-index payload.
declarations.header: theorem exists_cancel_payload_of_edist_lt {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a : MarketAction X} {eta₀ : FiniteSubsets ℕ} {δ : ENNReal} (h : edist a (MarketAction.cancel (X := X) eta₀) < δ) :
declarations.name: exists_cancel_payload_of_edist_lt

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`prop:application-continuous`.

Informal statement: finite closeness to a modification action forces the
nearby action to be modification, with close distinct finite-set payload.
declarations.header: theorem exists_modify_payload_of_edist_lt {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {a : MarketAction X} {xi₀ : DistinctFiniteSubsets X} {δ : ENNReal} (h : edist a (MarketAction.modify xi₀) < δ) : ∃ xi : DistinctFiniteSubsets X, a = MarketAction.modify xi ∧ edist xi xi₀ < δ :=
declarations.name: exists_modify_payload_of_edist_lt

declarations.docComment:
Product distributes over the open coproduct: a map out of `P × ⨆_a F a` is
continuous iff each restriction to `P × F a` is. This is the canonical
homeomorphism `P × ⨆_a F_a ≅ ⨆_a (P × F_a)` (every component is open) followed
by the pasting lemma for disjoint unions.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_prod_sigma_iff {A : Type*} {F : A → Type*} {P Z : Type*} [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (F a)] [TopologicalSpace P] [TopologicalSpace Z] (f : P × Sigma F → Z) : Continuous f ↔ ∀ a, Continuous (fun p : P × F a => f (p.1, ⟨a, p.2⟩)) :=
declarations.name: continuous_prod_sigma_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`prop:application-continuous`.

Informal statement: the action application map
`\mathscr{T}(X) × \mathscr{A}(X) → \mathscr{T}(X)` is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. The canonical
identification `T(X) × ⨆_α F_α ≅ ⨆_α (T(X) × F_α)` is a homeomorphism
(`actionSigmaHomeomorph` followed by `continuous_prod_sigma_iff`); the
restriction of `◁` to each component is exactly the corresponding primitive
operation, which is continuous by `thm:analytic-properties-actions`; and the
pasting lemma for disjoint unions gives continuity of `◁`. No epsilon-delta
argument is used.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_applyAction_emetricTopology {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : @Continuous (Tuple X × MarketAction X) (Tuple X) PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace (fun p : Tuple X × MarketAction X => applyAction p.1 p.2) :=
declarations.name: continuous_applyAction_emetricTopology

declarations.name: continuousAt_applyAction_emetricTopology

Definition "Composite Actions".

Informal statement: apply a composite action by applying each single action in
tuple order, returning the original tuple for the empty composite action.

recursion as a left fold over the ordered list of action entries.

Thesis source:

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section
"Composite Actions".

Original label: recursive application equation

Informal statement: for a composite action represented by `Fin n → A(X)`,
application is left-folded application of the entries in index order.
declarations.header: theorem applyCompositeAction_mk (x : Tuple X) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → MarketAction X) : applyCompositeAction x (Sigma.mk n c : CompositeAction X) = (List.ofFn c).foldl applyAction x :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`thm:composite-application-continuous`.

Informal statement: on a fixed composite-action length layer
`\mathscr{C}_n(X) ≃ \mathscr{A}(X)^n`, recursive application is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis recursion
`Φ_0(x) = x` and `Φ_n(x, a_1, …, a_n) = Φ_{n-1}(x, a_1, …, a_{n-1}) ◁ a_n`.
Lean uses zero-based `Fin` indices and `List.ofFn`; the proof is induction on
the composite length, peeling off the last action (`List.ofFn_succ'`) and using
the continuity of the one-step application map
(`prop:application-continuous`).
declarations.header: theorem continuous_fixedCompositeApply_emetricTopology {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (n : ℕ) : @Continuous (Tuple X × (Fin n → MarketAction X)) (Tuple X) PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace (fun p : Tuple X × (Fin n → MarketAction X) => (List.ofFn p.2).foldl applyAction p.1) :=
declarations.name: continuous_fixedCompositeApply_emetricTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`,
`thm:composite-application-continuous`.

Informal statement: the extended application map
`\mathscr{T}(X) × \mathscr{C}(X) → \mathscr{T}(X)` is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. The fixed-length
maps `Φ_n` are continuous by induction
(`continuous_fixedCompositeApply_emetricTopology`); the standard machinery
identifies the composite tuple topology with the coproduct of its length layers
`𝒞(X) = ⨆ₙ 𝒞ₙ(X)` (`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma`); the product with
`T(X)` distributes over this coproduct (`continuous_prod_sigma_iff`), and the
pasting lemma for disjoint unions gives global continuity.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_applyCompositeAction_emetricTopology {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : @Continuous (Tuple X × CompositeAction X) (Tuple X) PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace (fun p : Tuple X × CompositeAction X => applyCompositeAction p.1 p.2) :=
declarations.name: continuous_applyCompositeAction_emetricTopology

declarations.name: identifier_edist

declarations.name: identifier_separation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `exmp:identifier-coordinates`.
The product metric is exactly the maximum specified by the manuscript.
declarations.header: theorem identifier_product_edist {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} (x y : Y × Identifier I) : edist x y = max (edist x.1 y.1) (if x.2 = y.2 then 0 else 1) :=

declarations.docComment: Original label: `exmp:identifier-coordinates`.

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:identifier-cancel`.
Resolve identifiers against the current input tuple, then remove the
matching entries in their original order.
declarations.header: def cancelByIdentifier {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} (x : Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) (J : FiniteSubsets (Identifier I)) : Tuple (Y × Identifier I) := cancelIdentifiers Prod.snd (J : Set (Identifier I)) x
declarations.name: cancelByIdentifier

declarations.header: theorem identifier_sets_eq_of_near {I : Type u} {J K : FiniteSubsets (Identifier I)} (h : edist J K < 1) : J = K :=
declarations.name: identifier_sets_eq_of_near

declarations.header: theorem identifierIndices_eq_of_near {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} {n : ℕ} {x y : Fin n → Y × Identifier I} (J : Set (Identifier I)) (h : edist (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) (Sigma.mk n y) < 1) : identifierIndices Prod.snd J (Sigma.mk n x) = identifierIndices Prod.snd J (Sigma.mk n y) :=
declarations.name: identifierIndices_eq_of_near

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (i).
No distinctness restriction on the identifiers is required.

declarations.name: continuous_cancelByIdentifier

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking`.
The key order remains partial when different payloads have the same key.
