declarations.name: priorityOrder

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking`, clause (i).
declarations.header: theorem priorityOrder_total_on_distinct_identifiers {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} {K : Type w} [LinearOrder I] [LinearOrder K] (h : Y → K) {x y : Y × I} (hid : x.2 ≠ y.2) : @LE.le _ (priorityOrder h).toLE x y ∨ @LE.le _ (priorityOrder h).toLE y x :=
declarations.name: priorityOrder_total_on_distinct_identifiers

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking`.
On a tuple with distinct identifiers, the sorting key is injective even if
the primary attribute map is not.
declarations.header: theorem key_injective_on_tuple {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} {K : Type w} (h : Y → K) (x : Tuple (Y × I)) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => (x.entry i).2)) : Function.Injective (fun i => (h (x.entry i).1, (x.entry i).2)) :=
declarations.name: key_injective_on_tuple

declarations.docComment:
The order-preserving inclusion of the reindexed domain in the original
domain. The entries themselves are never altered.
declarations.header: def keptIndex {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) (i : Fin (reindex x η).length) : Fin x.length :=
declarations.name: keptIndex

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:reindex-bracket-notation`, order-preservation clause.
The kept indices are enumerated in increasing order, so `reindex` preserves the
relative order of the surviving entries.
declarations.header: theorem keptIndex_strictMono {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : StrictMono (keptIndex x η) :=
declarations.name: keptIndex_strictMono

declarations.header: theorem keptIndex_mem {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) (k : Fin x.length) : (∃ i, keptIndex x η i = k) ↔ k.val ∈ (η : Set ℕ) :=
declarations.name: keptIndex_mem

declarations.header: theorem keptIndex_list {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : List.ofFn (keptIndex x η) = (List.finRange x.length).filter (fun i => decide (i.val ∈ (η : Set ℕ))) :=
declarations.name: keptIndex_list

declarations.header: theorem tupleList_reindex {X : Type u} (x : Tuple X) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : tupleList (reindex x η) = ((List.finRange x.length).filter (fun i => decide (i.val ∈ (η : Set ℕ)))).map x.entry :=
declarations.name: tupleList_reindex

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:identifier-coordinates`.
The list characterization proves that every matching identifier is deleted
and that the relative order and multiplicities of all survivors are kept.
declarations.header: theorem tupleList_cancelIdentifiers {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (J : Set I) (x : Tuple X) : tupleList (cancelIdentifiers id J x) = (tupleList x).filter (fun z => decide (id z ∉ J)) :=
declarations.name: tupleList_cancelIdentifiers

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:identifier-coordinates`.
Unlike position-based cancellation, requests by stable identifiers combine
by set union, including repeated requests and repeated identifiers.
declarations.header: theorem cancelIdentifiers_union {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (J K : Set I) (x : Tuple X) : cancelIdentifiers id K (cancelIdentifiers id J x) = cancelIdentifiers id (J ∪ K) x :=
declarations.name: cancelIdentifiers_union

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
Deletion preserves injectivity because its reindexing is strictly increasing.
declarations.header: theorem injective_identifiers_reindex {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (x : Tuple X) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => id (x.entry i))) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : Function.Injective (fun i => id ((reindex x η).entry i)) :=
declarations.name: injective_identifiers_reindex

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem injective_identifiers_cancel {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (x : Tuple X) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => id (x.entry i))) (η : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : Function.Injective (fun i => id ((cancel x η).entry i)) :=
declarations.name: injective_identifiers_cancel

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem injective_identifiers_cancelIdentifiers {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (x : Tuple X) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => id (x.entry i))) (J : Set I) : Function.Injective (fun i => id ((cancelIdentifiers id J x).entry i)) :=
declarations.name: injective_identifiers_cancelIdentifiers

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem injective_identifiers_sort {X : Type u} [Preorder X] {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (σ : SortingRule X) (x : Tuple X) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => id (x.entry i))) : Function.Injective (fun i => id ((σ.sort x).entry i)) :=
declarations.name: injective_identifiers_sort

declarations.header: theorem priorityOrder_lt_iff {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} {K : Type w} [LinearOrder I] [LinearOrder K] (h : Y → K) (x y : Y × I) : @LT.lt _ (priorityOrder h).toLT x y ↔ toLex (h x.1, x.2) < toLex (h y.1, y.2) :=
declarations.name: priorityOrder_lt_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking`, clause (ii).
Distinct identifiers determine not only the sorted rearrangement but also
its sorting permutation uniquely.
declarations.header: theorem tie_break_sortingPermutation_unique {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} {K : Type w} [LinearOrder I] [LinearOrder K] (h : Y → K) (x : Tuple (Y × I)) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => (x.entry i).2)) : letI : PartialOrder (Y × I) := priorityOrder h
declarations.name: tie_break_sortingPermutation_unique

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem tie_break_sortingRules_agree {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} {K : Type w} [LinearOrder I] [LinearOrder K] (h : Y → K) (x : Tuple (Y × I)) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => (x.entry i).2)) : letI : PartialOrder (Y × I) := priorityOrder h
declarations.name: tie_break_sortingRules_agree

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-tie-breaking-borel`.
The source's Borel graph is taken in the topology of the full product.
No separability of the payload space is imposed.
declarations.header: theorem priorityOrder_borel {Y : Type u} [TopologicalSpace Y] [T2Space Y] {I : Type v} [TopologicalSpace I] [DiscreteTopology I] [LinearOrder I] {K : Type w} [TopologicalSpace K] [SecondCountableTopology K] [T2Space K] [LinearOrder K] (h : Y → K) (hh : @Measurable Y K (borel Y) (borel K) h) (hlt : @MeasurableSet (K × K) (borel (K × K)) {p | p.1 < p.2}) : @MeasurableSet ((Y × I) × (Y × I)) (borel ((Y × I) × (Y × I))) {p | @LE.le _ (priorityOrder h).toLE p.1 p.2} :=
declarations.name: priorityOrder_borel

declarations.docComment: Original label: `exmp:identifier-coordinates`.
declarations.header: def HasDistinctIdentifiers {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} (x : Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) : Prop :=
declarations.name: HasDistinctIdentifiers

declarations.header: theorem hasDistinctIdentifiers_iff_of_near {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} {x y : Tuple (Y × Identifier I)} (h : edist x y < 1) : HasDistinctIdentifiers x ↔ HasDistinctIdentifiers y :=
declarations.name: hasDistinctIdentifiers_iff_of_near

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
On a fixed length layer `Xⁿ`, the distinct-identifier set is the finite
intersection `⋂_{k ≠ l} {x ∈ Xⁿ | id(x(k)) ≠ id(x(l))}`; each comparison set is
clopen because `id` takes values in the discrete identifier space.
declarations.header: theorem distinctIdentifiers_fixedLayer_clopen {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} (n : ℕ) : IsClopen {x : Fin n → Y × Identifier I | Function.Injective (fun i => (x i).2)} :=
declarations.name: distinctIdentifiers_fixedLayer_clopen

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
As in the thesis: `T(X) = ⨆ₙ Xⁿ` by the standard machinery
(`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma`), and on every layer `T≠(X) ∩ Xⁿ` is
clopen by the finite coordinate comparison
`distinctIdentifiers_fixedLayer_clopen`.
declarations.header: theorem distinctIdentifiers_clopen {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} : @IsClopen (Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) (emetricTopology _) {x | HasDistinctIdentifiers x} :=
declarations.name: distinctIdentifiers_clopen

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
declarations.header: theorem distinctIdentifiers_polish {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] [PolishSpace Y] {I : Type v} [Countable I] : letI : TopologicalSpace (Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) := emetricTopology _
declarations.name: distinctIdentifiers_polish

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
Concatenation preserves identifier uniqueness precisely when there are no
cross-tuple collisions, assuming uniqueness within each input.
declarations.header: theorem injective_identifiers_concat {X : Type u} {I : Type v} (id : X → I) (x y : Tuple X) (hx : Function.Injective (fun i => id (x.entry i))) (hy : Function.Injective (fun i => id (y.entry i))) (hdisj : ∀ i j, id (x.entry i) ≠ id (y.entry j)) : Function.Injective (fun i => id ((concat x y).entry i)) :=
declarations.name: injective_identifiers_concat

declarations.docComment:
Product distributes over the open coproduct: a map out of `P × ⨆_a F a` is
continuous iff each restriction to `P × F a` is (used to paste over the
product length layers `Xⁿ × Xᵐ`).
declarations.header: private theorem continuous_prod_sigma_iff {A : Type*} {F : A → Type*} {P Z : Type*} [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (F a)] [TopologicalSpace P] [TopologicalSpace Z] (f : P × Sigma F → Z) : Continuous f ↔ ∀ a, Continuous (fun p : P × F a => f (p.1, ⟨a, p.2⟩)) :=
declarations.name: continuous_prod_sigma_iff

declarations.header: private theorem continuous_sigma_prod_iff {A : Type*} {F : A → Type*} {P Z : Type*} [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (F a)] [TopologicalSpace P] [TopologicalSpace Z] (f : Sigma F × P → Z) : Continuous f ↔ ∀ a, Continuous (fun p : F a × P => f (⟨a, p.1⟩, p.2)) :=
declarations.name: continuous_sigma_prod_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
On a product layer `Xⁿ × Xᵐ`, cross-identifier disjointness is the finite
intersection `⋂_{k,l} {(x, y) | id(x(k)) ≠ id(y(l))}` of clopen comparison
sets.
declarations.header: theorem disjointIdentifiers_fixedLayers_clopen {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} (n m : ℕ) : IsClopen {p : (Fin n → Y × Identifier I) × (Fin m → Y × Identifier I) | ∀ i j, (p.1 i).2 ≠ (p.2 j).2} :=
declarations.name: disjointIdentifiers_fixedLayers_clopen

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
Cross-identifier disjointness is clopen in `T(X) × T(X)`: decompose both
factors into their clopen length layers (`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma`),
distribute the product over the coproducts, and use the finite comparison
`disjointIdentifiers_fixedLayers_clopen` on each product layer `Xⁿ × Xᵐ`.
declarations.header: theorem disjointIdentifiers_clopen_tuples {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} : letI : TopologicalSpace (Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) := emetricTopology _
declarations.name: disjointIdentifiers_clopen_tuples

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (ii).
Cross-identifier-disjointness is clopen in the product of the distinct-ID
tuple spaces, with the subspace topology required by the manuscript: the
product-layer finite-intersection result `disjointIdentifiers_clopen_tuples`
restricted to `T≠(X)²`.
declarations.header: theorem disjointIdentifiers_clopen {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} : letI : TopologicalSpace (Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) := emetricTopology _
declarations.name: disjointIdentifiers_clopen

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (iv).
declarations.header: def forgetIdentifiers {Y : Type u} {I : Type v} (x : Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) : Tuple Y :=
declarations.name: forgetIdentifiers

declarations.docComment: Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (iv).
declarations.header: theorem continuous_forgetIdentifiers {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] {I : Type v} : @Continuous (Tuple (Y × Identifier I)) (Tuple Y) (emetricTopology _) (emetricTopology _) forgetIdentifiers :=
declarations.name: continuous_forgetIdentifiers

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:identifier-cancel-continuous`, clause (iii).
The input sigma algebra is the product of the Borel sigma algebras of the
two factors, exactly as required by the manuscript.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_sortedCancelByIdentifier {Y : Type u} [EMetricSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace Y] {I : Type v} [Countable I] [Preorder (Y × Identifier I)] (σ : SortingRule (Y × Identifier I)) (hσ : IsMeasurableSortingRule σ) : @Measurable (Tuple (Y × Identifier I) × FiniteSubsets (Identifier I)) (SortedTuple (Y × Identifier I)) (@Prod.instMeasurableSpace _ _ (emetricBorel (Tuple (Y × Identifier I))) (emetricBorel (FiniteSubsets (Identifier I)))) (emetricBorel (SortedTuple (Y × Identifier I))) (fun p => σ.toSortedTuple (cancelByIdentifier p.1 p.2)) :=
declarations.name: measurable_sortedCancelByIdentifier

Original label: `defn:pairing`.

Informal statement: a finite set in a totally ordered space can be enumerated
as an increasing tuple.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis defines the pairing recursively by repeated minima.
Lean uses mathlib's `Finset.orderEmbOfFin`, which is exactly the increasing
enumeration of a finite set in a linear order.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: the range theorem `pairing_range_eq` below records the
surjectivity half of the enumeration, making explicit that the pairing lists
every element of the finite set, not just elements drawn from it.

declarations.name: pairing

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: cardinality/domain assertion in `defn:pairing`.

Informal statement: the pairing of a finite set has length equal to the set's
cardinality.
declarations.header: theorem pairing_length [LinearOrder X] (xi : FiniteSubsets X) : (pairing xi).length = (FiniteSubsets.toFinset xi).card :=
declarations.name: pairing_length

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `cor:pairing-finite-set-is-sorted-tuple`.

Informal statement: the pairing tuple is sorted.
declarations.header: theorem pairing_isSorted [LinearOrder X] (xi : FiniteSubsets X) : IsSorted (pairing xi) :=
declarations.name: pairing_isSorted

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: range property implicit in `defn:pairing`.

Informal statement: every entry of the pairing belongs to the finite set being
enumerated.
declarations.header: theorem pairing_entry_mem [LinearOrder X] (xi : FiniteSubsets X) (i : Fin (pairing xi).length) : Tuple.entry (pairing xi) i ∈ (xi : Set X) :=
declarations.name: pairing_entry_mem

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: full enumeration property implicit in `defn:pairing`.

Informal statement: the entries of the pairing tuple are exactly the finite set
being paired.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the range statement for mathlib's increasing
enumeration `Finset.orderEmbOfFin`, translated back from the representative
`Finset` to the thesis finite-subset type.
declarations.header: theorem pairing_range_eq [LinearOrder X] (xi : FiniteSubsets X) : Set.range (fun i : Fin (pairing xi).length => Tuple.entry (pairing xi) i) = (xi : Set X) :=
declarations.name: pairing_range_eq

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: existence direction implicit in `defn:pairing`.

Informal statement: every element of the finite set appears at some index of
its pairing tuple.
declarations.header: theorem exists_pairing_entry_eq_of_mem [LinearOrder X] (xi : FiniteSubsets X) {x : X} (hx : x ∈ (xi : Set X)) : ∃ i : Fin (pairing xi).length, Tuple.entry (pairing xi) i = x :=
declarations.name: exists_pairing_entry_eq_of_mem

Informal statement: the natural-number domain of a tuple is the finite set of
indices below its length.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis uses `{1, ..., l(x)}`; Lean uses zero-based
`{n | n < x.length}`.
declarations.header: def tupleDomain (x : Tuple X) : FiniteSubsets ℕ :=
declarations.name: tupleDomain

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: domain membership used in `defn:reindex`.

Informal statement: a natural number belongs to the tuple domain iff it is
below the tuple length.
declarations.header: theorem mem_tupleDomain (x : Tuple X) {n : ℕ} : n ∈ (tupleDomain x : Set ℕ) ↔ n < x.length :=
declarations.name: mem_tupleDomain

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: finite-set intersection used in `defn:reindex`.

Informal statement: intersection of finite index sets is finite.
declarations.header: def finiteSubsetInter {A : Type u} (s t : FiniteSubsets A) : FiniteSubsets A :=
declarations.name: finiteSubsetInter

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Informal statement: difference of finite index sets is finite.
declarations.header: def finiteSubsetDiff {A : Type u} (s t : FiniteSubsets A) : FiniteSubsets A :=
declarations.name: finiteSubsetDiff

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `defn:reindex`.

Informal statement: restrict a tuple to a finite set of surviving natural
indices, intersect with the tuple's domain, then compress the surviving
indices back to an initial finite domain.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: compression is implemented by applying the pairing map to the
finite subset of surviving indices. Since the paired indices lie in
`tupleDomain x`, Lean can construct the required `Fin x.length` index.
declarations.header: noncomputable def reindex (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : Tuple X :=
declarations.name: reindex

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `defn:reindex`.

Informal statement: the length of a reindexed tuple is the number of surviving
indices after intersecting with the original tuple domain.
declarations.header: theorem reindex_length (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : (reindex x eta).length = (FiniteSubsets.toFinset (finiteSubsetInter eta (tupleDomain x))).card :=
declarations.name: reindex_length

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: subsequence step behind `cor:cancel-closure-sorted`.

Informal statement: reindexing a sorted tuple along any finite index set keeps
the remaining entries sorted, because the surviving indices are paired in
increasing order.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: as in the thesis sentence preceding
`cor:cancel-closure-sorted`, this holds for every preorder (hence every
partial order): sortedness is the pairwise condition that no later entry is
strictly below an earlier one, and a subsequence inherits it. Only the index
pairing uses the linear order on `ℕ`.
declarations.header: theorem reindex_isSorted [Preorder X] {x : Tuple X} (hx : IsSorted x) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : IsSorted (reindex x eta) :=
declarations.name: reindex_isSorted

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `defn:cancel`.

Informal statement: cancellation removes the requested finite set of indices
from the tuple domain and then reindexes the survivors.
declarations.header: noncomputable def cancel (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : Tuple X :=
declarations.name: cancel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: length consequence of `defn:cancel`.

Informal statement: cancellation has the length of the surviving finite index
set.
declarations.header: theorem cancel_length (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : (cancel x eta).length = (FiniteSubsets.toFinset (finiteSubsetInter (finiteSubsetDiff (tupleDomain x) eta) (tupleDomain x))).card :=
declarations.name: cancel_length

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: closure step behind `cor:cancel-closure-sorted`.

Informal statement: cancelling indices from a sorted tuple leaves a sorted
tuple (for every preorder, as the thesis states).
declarations.header: theorem cancel_isSorted [Preorder X] {x : Tuple X} (hx : IsSorted x) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : IsSorted (cancel x eta) :=
declarations.name: cancel_isSorted

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `defn:sorted-cancel`.

Informal statement: sorted cancellation is cancellation followed by the fixed
sorting rule.
declarations.header: noncomputable def sortedCancel [Preorder X] (varsigma : SortingRule X) (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : SortedTuple X :=
declarations.name: sortedCancel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: codomain assertion in `defn:sorted-cancel`.

Informal statement: sorted cancellation produces a sorted tuple.
declarations.header: theorem sortedCancel_isSorted [Preorder X] (varsigma : SortingRule X) (x : Tuple X) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : IsSorted (sortedCancel varsigma x eta).1 :=
declarations.name: sortedCancel_isSorted

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `cor:cancel-closure-sorted`.

Informal statement: for a sorted tuple in a total order, sorted cancellation
has the same underlying tuple as ordinary cancellation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this follows the thesis proof in its two
steps. Step (a): deleting entries from a sorted tuple leaves a sorted tuple, so
`cancel x eta` is sorted (`cancel_isSorted`, valid for every preorder). Step
(b): since the order is total, `cor:unique-sorting-map-total-order` (cited via
`sortingRule_fixes_sorted`) says the sorting rule fixes every sorted tuple,
whence `x - eta = varsigma (x ⊖ eta) = x ⊖ eta`. The first equality is the
definition of sorted cancellation (`sortedCancel`, `defn:sorted-cancel`).
declarations.header: theorem sortedCancel_eq_cancel [LinearOrder X] (varsigma : SortingRule X) {x : Tuple X} (hx : IsSorted x) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : (sortedCancel varsigma x eta).1 = cancel x eta :=
declarations.name: sortedCancel_eq_cancel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: `cor:cancel-closure-sorted`.

Informal statement: as an equality in the sorted-tuple subtype, sorted
cancellation is ordinary cancellation equipped with its sortedness proof.
declarations.header: theorem sortedCancel_eq_cancelSubtype [LinearOrder X] (varsigma : SortingRule X) {x : Tuple X} (hx : IsSorted x) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : sortedCancel varsigma x eta = ⟨cancel x eta, cancel_isSorted hx eta⟩ :=
declarations.name: sortedCancel_eq_cancelSubtype

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/3_market_actions.tex`, section "Primitive
Actions".

Original label: auxiliary value choice for `defn:modification`.

Informal statement: if the distinct finite modification set contains a
replacement at index `n`, use it; otherwise keep the default value.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: uniqueness of the replacement value is supplied by the
`DistinctFiniteSubsets` invariant.

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:executable-volume-usc`, the thesis `g_k`.
For a fixed limit point `s = ((Q, p), (Q', p'))`, the maximum of
`min(Q_t(i), Q'_t(j))` over the limit's feasible index set `I(p, p')`,
evaluated at a variable point `t`; along a sequence `z_k → s` this is the
thesis `g_k = fixedIndexVolume s (z k)` (with the value `0` when
`I(p, p') = ∅`).
declarations.header: def fixedIndexVolume (s t : ClearingInput) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: fixedIndexVolume

declarations.header: @[simp] theorem fixedIndexVolume_self (s : ClearingInput) : fixedIndexVolume s s = equilibriumQuantity s := rfl
declarations.name: fixedIndexVolume_self

declarations.docComment:
Thesis step: "the maximum and minimum over a fixed finite index set are
continuous", so `g_k → Q(z)`.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_fixedIndexVolume (s : ClearingInput) : Continuous (fixedIndexVolume s) :=
declarations.name: continuous_fixedIndexVolume

declarations.docComment:
Thesis step: once the lengths have stabilized, every pair `(i, j)` that is
infeasible at the limit (`p(i) > p'(j)`) stays infeasible nearby, and since
there are finitely many pairs, `I(p_k, p'_k) ⊆ I(p, p')` for all large `k`.
The eventual filter is the thesis' common threshold `K`.
declarations.header: theorem eventually_feasible_subset (s : ClearingInput) : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 s, (feasibleEquilibriumIndexSet t.1.2 t.2.2 : Set (ℕ × ℕ)) ⊆ (feasibleEquilibriumIndexSet s.1.2 s.2.2 : Set (ℕ × ℕ)) :=
declarations.name: eventually_feasible_subset

declarations.docComment:
Thesis step: "since all cumulative quantities are non-negative, the
inclusion `I(p_k, p'_k) ⊆ I(p, p')` implies `Q(z_k) ≤ g_k`" (including the
case `I(p, p') = ∅`, where both sides are `0`).
declarations.header: theorem eventually_le_fixedIndexVolume (s : ClearingInput) : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 s, equilibriumQuantity t ≤ fixedIndexVolume s t :=
declarations.name: eventually_le_fixedIndexVolume

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:executable-volume-usc`, the displayed inequality of
the proof of (i): for every sequence `z_k → z`,
`limsup_k Q(z_k) ≤ lim_k g_k = Q(z)`.
declarations.header: theorem sequence_limsup_le {z : ℕ → ClearingInput} {s : ClearingInput} (hz : Tendsto z atTop (𝓝 s)) : limsup (fun k => equilibriumQuantity (z k)) atTop ≤ equilibriumQuantity s :=
declarations.name: sequence_limsup_le

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:executable-volume-usc`.
Clause (i), by the thesis argument: near the limit point `s` the lengths
stabilize and the infeasible pairs stay infeasible, so the feasible index set
is contained in that of `s` (`eventually_feasible_subset`); nonnegativity of
the cumulative quantities then dominates `Q` by the fixed-index maximum `g`
(`eventually_le_fixedIndexVolume`), and `g` is continuous with `g(s) = Q(s)`
(`continuous_fixedIndexVolume`). This is the neighbourhood form of
`limsup Q(z_k) ≤ lim g_k = Q(z)`; the literal sequential inequality is
`sequence_limsup_le`. The closed-superlevel-set facts for the fixed layers
above are not used here. Restricting to the thesis' sorted matching-length
subspace preserves upper semicontinuity.
declarations.header: theorem upperSemicontinuous_equilibriumQuantity : UpperSemicontinuous equilibriumQuantity :=
declarations.name: upperSemicontinuous_equilibriumQuantity

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:executable-volume-usc`, clause (iii) on the thesis
domain `\mathfrak{C}(\leq) \times \mathfrak{C}(\geq)`.
The thesis witnesses `z_k = ((Q, p_k), (Q', p'))` with `p_k(1) = 1/k` lie in

`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 5.

Original label: `thm:index-measurable`.

Informal statement: the feasible equilibrium index map is Borel measurable
on the product of sell-price and buy-price tuple spaces.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis proves this by decomposing the tuple spaces into
the countable family of fixed-dimensional layers
`\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m`, proving measurability on each layer, and
pasting. Lean follows that strategy by writing each singleton fiber as a
countable union over `(n,m)` of fixed-layer fibers.

Domain note: the thesis states the theorem on the sorted domain
`\mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R},\leq) \times \mathscr{S}(\mathbb{R},\geq)` and
therefore first shows that the sorted layers `I_n`, `D_m` are Borel
(`lem:increasing-decreasing-measurable`:
`measurableSet_increasingRealFixedSet`, `measurableSet_decreasingRealFixedSet`)
and that the comparison cells `L^{i,j}_{n,m} ⊆ I_n × D_m` and
`G^{i,j}_{n,m} ⊆ I_n × D_m` are Borel (`lem:bounded-sets-measurable`:
`measurableSet_feasibleComparisonCell`, `measurableSet_infeasibleComparisonCell`).
Lean proves the fiber identity on the whole layer
`\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}^m` (`measurableSet_fixedLength_feasibleEquilibriumIndexSet_fiber`)
using the unrestricted half-spaces `{p^s_i ≤ p^b_j}` and `{p^s_i > p^b_j}`,
whose traces on `I_n × D_m` are exactly `L^{i,j}_{n,m}` and `G^{i,j}_{n,m}`.
The sortedness constraint is thus not needed for measurability: the ambient
theorem subsumes the thesis statement, and the two lemmas are not on its
proof path. The thesis domain is recovered by restriction in
`measurable_feasibleEquilibriumIndexSet_restricted`.

declarations.name: measurable_feasibleEquilibriumIndexSet

The cumulative and price coordinates use the same permutation and have the
same length, so a reaching quantity index selects a genuine price.
declarations.header: theorem cumulativeSell_length_eq_price_length (m : MarketTuple) : (cumulativeSellQuantityTuple m).length = (sortedSellPriceTuple m).length :=
declarations.name: cumulativeSell_length_eq_price_length

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `cor:state-midpoint-price-measurable`.
For positive volume, both least reaching indices exist in the actual cumulative
tuples and the midpoint uses precisely their selected prices.
declarations.header: theorem marketMidpointPrice_positive_formula (m : MarketTuple) (hq : 0 < marketEquilibriumQuantity m) : ∃ i j : ℕ, ReachesFirst ((cumulativeSellQuantityTuple m, sortedSellPriceTuple m), marketEquilibriumQuantity m) i ∧ ReachesFirst ((cumulativeBuyQuantityTuple m, sortedBuyPriceTuple m), marketEquilibriumQuantity m) j ∧ i < (cumulativeSellQuantityTuple m).length ∧ j < (cumulativeBuyQuantityTuple m).length ∧ i < (sortedSellPriceTuple m).length ∧ j < (sortedBuyPriceTuple m).length ∧ marketMidpointPrice m = (tuplePriceEval i (sortedSellPriceTuple m) + tuplePriceEval j (sortedBuyPriceTuple m)) / 2 :=
declarations.name: marketMidpointPrice_positive_formula

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `cor:state-midpoint-price-measurable`.
This is the thesis proof by the measurable-partition theorem. The state space
is covered by the countable family of measurable cells
`A_0 = {\mathscr{Q}_{state} = 0}` and
`B^{i,j} = {\mathscr{Q}_{state} > 0, ι^s = i, ι^b = j}` (the cells
`B^{i,j}_{n_s,n_b}` of the thesis; the length indices `(n_s, n_b)` are absorbed
because the coordinate evaluations `ev_i = tuplePriceEval i` are defined on
all of tuple space and vanish out of range). On `A_0` the midpoint price is
`0`; on `B^{i,j}` it coincides with the fixed measurable combination
`(ev_i(\hat p^s) + ev_j(\hat p^b)) / 2`
(`marginalPrice_eq`). The cells are measurable because the state maps
(sorting, cumulative sums, compatible volume) are, and they cover the space by
`positive_equilibrium_has_marginals`;
`measurable_of_measurable_restrict_countable_cover` pastes the restrictions.
The marginal-index cells are described by `ReachesFirst`, i.e.
`ev_{i-1}(\hat Q) < \mathscr{Q}_{state} ≤ ev_i(\hat Q)` in the thesis'
notation.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_marketMidpointPrice : letI : EMetricSpace MarketOrder :=
declarations.name: measurable_marketMidpointPrice

argument, using the Chapter 3 fixed-index nonexpansive estimate for `reindex`.

Filters, and Market Segregation".

Original label: `prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Informal statement: given coordinatewise characteristic functions
`\chi_i : X -> {0,1}`, collect exactly the tuple indices at which the
corresponding characteristic function is true.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean uses `Bool` for the two-point set `{0,1}` and zero-based
indices `n < x.length` for the thesis domain `{1,\dots,\ell(\bm{x})}`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def characteristicIndexSet {X : Type u} (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (x : Tuple X) : FiniteSubsets ℕ :=
declarations.name: characteristicIndexSet

declarations.header: theorem mem_characteristicIndexSet {X : Type u} (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (x : Tuple X) {n : ℕ} : n ∈ (characteristicIndexSet χ x : Set ℕ) ↔ ∃ h : n < x.length, χ n (Tuple.entry x ⟨n, h⟩) = true :=
declarations.name: mem_characteristicIndexSet

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Original label: support observation in `prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Informal statement: the characteristic selector only returns indices inside
the tuple domain.
declarations.header: theorem characteristicIndexSet_subset_domain {X : Type u} (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (x : Tuple X) : (characteristicIndexSet χ x : Set ℕ) ⊆ (tupleDomain x : Set ℕ) :=
declarations.name: characteristicIndexSet_subset_domain

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Original label: fixed-length fiber step in
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Informal statement: on a fixed tuple-length layer, the fiber of the
characteristic index selector over a finite index set is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis' finite-coordinate argument. For length
`n`, membership of the output index set is decided by the finitely many
Boolean tests `χ_i(x_i)`, `i < n`; if the proposed output contains an index
outside `{0, ..., n-1}`, the fiber is empty.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixedLength_characteristicIndexSet_fiber {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (hχ : ∀ i : ℕ, @Measurable X Bool (emetricBorel X) inferInstance (χ i)) (n : ℕ) (eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) {x : Fin n → X | characteristicIndexSet χ (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) = eta} :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixedLength_characteristicIndexSet_fiber

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Original label: fixed-length step in
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Informal statement: on every fixed-length layer, the characteristic index
selector is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean proves this from measurable fibers into the countable
finite-subset space of `ℕ`. This is the fixed-length version of the thesis'
measurable-set construction.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_fixedLength_characteristicIndexSet {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (hχ : ∀ i : ℕ, @Measurable X Bool (emetricBorel X) inferInstance (χ i)) (n : ℕ) : @Measurable (Fin n → X) (FiniteSubsets ℕ) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) (emetricBorel (FiniteSubsets ℕ)) (fun x : Fin n → X => characteristicIndexSet χ (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) :=
declarations.name: measurable_fixedLength_characteristicIndexSet

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Original label: `prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.

Informal statement: if the coordinate characteristic functions
`\chi_i : X -> {0,1}` are Borel measurable, then the tuple-index selector
`\bm{x} \mapsto \{i : \chi_i(x_i)=1\}` is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis phrases the proof as measurable pasting across the
tuple layers. Lean uses the Chapter 2 theorem
`measurable_tupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength`, which formalizes exactly that
countable disjoint-union pasting step for the tuple Hausdorff topology.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_characteristicIndexSet_emetricBorel {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (χ : ℕ → X → Bool) (hχ : ∀ i : ℕ, @Measurable X Bool (emetricBorel X) inferInstance (χ i)) : @Measurable (Tuple X) (FiniteSubsets ℕ) (emetricBorel (Tuple X)) (emetricBorel (FiniteSubsets ℕ)) (characteristicIndexSet χ) :=
declarations.name: measurable_characteristicIndexSet_emetricBorel

`cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Original label: `cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Informal statement: the Boolean characteristic function of a set.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: arbitrary set membership is classically decidable in the
manuscript. Lean makes this explicit by defining the characteristic function
noncomputably under classical choice.
declarations.header: noncomputable def setCharacteristicBool {X : Type u} (B : Set X) (x : X) : Bool :=

declarations.header: theorem setCharacteristicBool_eq_true {X : Type u} (B : Set X) (x : X) : setCharacteristicBool B x = true ↔ x ∈ B :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Original label: `cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Informal statement: the index selector associated with a countable Borel
family `(B_i)` keeps exactly those tuple indices whose entry lies in `B_i`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes this directly as a set comprehension. Lean
implements it by turning membership in `B_i` into the Boolean characteristic
function used in `prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def borelIndexSet {X : Type u} (B : ℕ → Set X) (x : Tuple X) : FiniteSubsets ℕ :=

declarations.header: theorem mem_borelIndexSet {X : Type u} (B : ℕ → Set X) (x : Tuple X) {n : ℕ} : n ∈ (borelIndexSet B x : Set ℕ) ↔ ∃ h : n < x.length, Tuple.entry x ⟨n, h⟩ ∈ B n :=
declarations.name: mem_borelIndexSet

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Original label: `cor:measurable-index-filter-for-countable-borel-family`.

Informal statement: if `(B_i)` is a countable family of Borel subsets of

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is exactly the thesis corollary from
`prop:characteristic-functions-tuple`; the only Lean-specific step is spelling
the characteristic functions as `if y ∈ B_i then true else false`.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_borelIndexSet_emetricBorel {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (B : ℕ → Set X) (hB : ∀ i : ℕ, @MeasurableSet X (emetricBorel X) (B i)) : @Measurable (Tuple X) (FiniteSubsets ℕ) (emetricBorel (Tuple X)) (emetricBorel (FiniteSubsets ℕ)) (borelIndexSet B) :=
declarations.name: measurable_borelIndexSet_emetricBorel

Alternative route for `prop:tuple-projection-continuous` (not the mapped

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Original label: Hausdorff-distance step of `prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Informal statement: a distance-decreasing map does not increase the Hausdorff
distance between images; this includes empty sets and infinite distances.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis proof uses that the graph map
`(i, x) ↦ (i, P_α x)` is `1`-Lipschitz and concludes
`d_{H,α}(P_α x, P_α x₀) ≤ d_H(x, x₀)`. This lemma is the general statement
behind that step, for the extended Hausdorff distance on arbitrary subsets.
declarations.header: theorem hausdorffEDist_image_le_of_edist_le {B : Type u} {C : Type v} [PseudoEMetricSpace B] [PseudoEMetricSpace C] (f : B → C) (hf : ∀ x y, edist (f x) (f y) ≤ edist x y) (s t : Set B) : Metric.hausdorffEDist (f '' s) (f '' t) ≤ Metric.hausdorffEDist s t :=
declarations.name: hausdorffEDist_image_le_of_edist_le

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Original label: `prop:tuple-projection-continuous`, the `1`-Lipschitz
estimate `d_{H,α}(P_α x, P_α x₀) ≤ d_H(x, x₀)`.

Informal statement: the tuple projection `\bm{P}_α` does not increase the
tuple Hausdorff distance when `\prod_α X_α` carries the maximum product
metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: exactly the thesis inequality. The graph
of `\bm{P}_α x` is the image of the graph of `x` under the graph map
`(i, x) ↦ (i, P_α x)`, which is `1`-Lipschitz because the index distance is
unchanged and `edist (x a) (y a) ≤ edist x y` for the maximum product metric
(`edist_le_pi_edist`). The Hausdorff estimate above finishes the proof.
declarations.header: theorem tupleProjection_edist_le {A : Type v} [Fintype A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) (x y : Tuple ((b : A) → X b)) : edist (tupleProjection a x) (tupleProjection a y) ≤ edist x y :=
declarations.name: tupleProjection_edist_le

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Original label: `prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Informal statement: each tuple projection
`\bm{P}_α : \mathscr{T}(\prod_α X_α) → \mathscr{T}(X_α)` is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis epsilon-delta proof.
Since the graph map `(i, x) ↦ (i, P_α x)` is `1`-Lipschitz for the maximum
product metric, `d_{H,α}(P_α x, P_α x₀) ≤ d_H(x, x₀)`
(`tupleProjection_edist_le`), so for every `ε > 0` the choice `δ = ε` works
at every `x₀`.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_tupleProjection_tupleHausdorff {A : Type v} {X : A → Type u} [Fintype A] [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) : @Continuous (Tuple ((b : A) → X b)) (Tuple (X a)) (tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := ((b : A) → X b)))
declarations.name: continuous_tupleProjection_tupleHausdorff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Original label: `prop:tuple-projection-continuous`.

Informal statement: the tuple decomposition
`\bm{P} : \mathscr{T}(\prod_α X_α) → \prod_α \mathscr{T}(X_α)` is continuous
for the product topology.

coordinate projections is pointwise equality in the dependent product.

Filters, and Market Segregation".

`defn:separation-operators`.

Informal statement: once a disjoint-union element is known to have tag `a`,
return its value as an element of `X_a`.

necessary in Lean's dependent Sigma type.

`defn:separation-operators`.

Original label: index set in `defn:separation-operators`.

Informal statement: the finite index set
`{i ∈ domain(x) : x(i) ∈ X_a × {a}}`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def separationIndexSet {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} (a : A) (x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) : FiniteSubsets ℕ :=

`defn:separation-operators`.

Informal statement: project a tuple along a finite set of indices already
known to point into the `a`-component.

Thesis source:

Informal statement: the `a`-separation operator filters a tuple in the
disjoint union to the entries tagged by `a`, then forgets the tag.

finite-set pairing used in Chapter 3's reindexing operator. This is the Lean
version of the thesis formula
`\Pi_a x = P_element (x[{i : x(i) ∈ X_a × {a}}])`.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: radius-`1` tag-stability step in
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: in the disjoint-union metric, points at distance below
`1` must lie in the same component.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the formal version of the thesis observation that
cross-component distances are infinite.
declarations.header: theorem tag_eq_of_disjoint_edist_lt_one {A : Type v} {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {z w : DisjointUnion X} (h : @edist (DisjointUnion X) (DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)).toEDist z w < (1 : ENNReal)) : z.1 = w.1 :=
declarations.name: tag_eq_of_disjoint_edist_lt_one

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: element-projection distance step in
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: when two disjoint-union points have the same tag `a`,
their disjoint-union distance is exactly the component distance between their
projected values.
declarations.header: theorem valueAtTag_edist_eq {A : Type v} {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {a : A} {z w : DisjointUnion X} (hz : z.1 = a) (hw : w.1 = a) : edist (valueAtTag a z hz) (valueAtTag a w hw) = @edist (DisjointUnion X) (DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)).toEDist z w :=
declarations.name: valueAtTag_edist_eq

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: selected-index stability in `prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: below tuple Hausdorff distance `1`, fixed-length tuples
over the disjoint union have the same indices in the `a`-component.
declarations.header: theorem separationIndexSet_eq_of_fixed_edist_lt_one {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {n : ℕ} {x y : Fin n → DisjointUnion X} (a : A) (h : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X) edist (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) < (1 : ENNReal)) : separationIndexSet a (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) = separationIndexSet a (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) :=
declarations.name: separationIndexSet_eq_of_fixed_edist_lt_one

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, proof of
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: fixed-index estimate in `prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: if two fixed-length disjoint-union tuples are close and a
common finite index set selects entries in component `a` for both, then the
projected component tuples are close by the same radius.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the proof's quantitative core. It uses the thesis'
same-index comparison after the radius-`1` stabilization step.
declarations.header: theorem componentFromIndices_edist_lt_of_fixed_near {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {n : ℕ} {x y : Fin n → DisjointUnion X} {eta : FiniteSubsets ℕ} {δ : ENNReal} (a : A) (hδle : δ ≤ (1 : ENNReal)) (hxyδ : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X) edist (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) < δ) (hηx : (eta : Set ℕ) ⊆ (separationIndexSet a (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) : Set ℕ)) (hηy : (eta : Set ℕ) ⊆ (separationIndexSet a (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) : Set ℕ)) : edist (componentFromIndices a (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) eta hηx) (componentFromIndices a (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) eta hηy) < δ :=
declarations.name: componentFromIndices_edist_lt_of_fixed_near

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: component part of `prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: the `a`-separation operator is continuous at every tuple
when the disjoint union is endowed with the thesis disjoint-union metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof verbatim in radius form. Below radius
`1`, tuple length and component tags stabilize; the selected index set is
therefore unchanged, and the projected component tuple is controlled by the
same coordinatewise distance estimate.
declarations.header: theorem continuousAt_separationComponent_disjointTopology {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) (x₀Tuple : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: continuousAt_separationComponent_disjointTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original labels: `prop:separation-continuous`, `prop:separation-1`.

Informal statement: each component separation operator
`\Pi_a : \mathscr{T}(\bigsqcup_a X_a) -> \mathscr{T}(X_a)` is continuous.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_separationComponent_disjointTopology {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: continuous_separationComponent_disjointTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: product part of `prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: the full separation operator
`\Pi x = (\Pi_a x)_a` is continuous into the product of component tuple
spaces.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this theorem uses the ordinary product
topology on `\prod_a \mathscr{T}(X_a)`. For infinite families that topology
can differ from the unweighted supremum-metric topology in the manuscript.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: this is the topology-first product statement. The finite
wrapper `continuous_separationOperator_finitePiEMetric` restates the same
result for Lean's finite `Pi` extended-metric topology, which is the formal
counterpart of the thesis' maximum product metric on finite products. The
thesis statement (ii), continuity into the sup product metric for an
arbitrary (in particular countable) index family, is
`continuous_separationOperator_supMetric` below, which is the mapped proof.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_separationOperator_disjointTopology {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: continuous_separationOperator_disjointTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Alternative route for `prop:separation-continuous` (not the mapped proof):
finite-family variant with Lean's `Pi` extended-metric topology.

Informal statement: when the component family is finite, the full separation
operator is continuous into the finite product equipped with Lean's product
extended-metric topology.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: for finite products, Lean's `Pi` extended-metric topology is
the maximum/sup product topology used in the thesis. The proof is therefore
the product-topology theorem above with the finite `Pi` metric topology made
explicit in the codomain. The thesis statement (ii) for a countable (indeed
arbitrary) family and the sup product metric is
`continuous_separationOperator_supMetric` below.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_separationOperator_finitePiEMetric {A : Type v} [Fintype A] [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: continuous_separationOperator_finitePiEMetric

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: sup product metric `D` in `prop:separation-continuous`.

Informal statement: the unweighted supremum extended metric
`D((y_α)_α, (z_α)_α) = sup_α d_{H,α}(y_α, z_α)` on `\prod_α \mathscr{T}(X_α)`,
for an arbitrary index family.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is deliberately not a global
instance. For infinite families its topology need not be the product
topology, which is why the thesis states (ii) for this metric explicitly.
declarations.header: @[reducible] noncomputable def supProductEMetricSpace {A : Type v} (Y : A → Type u) [∀ a, EMetricSpace (Y a)] : EMetricSpace ((a : A) → Y a)
declarations.name: supProductEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original label: `prop:separation-continuous`, uniform component estimate.

Informal statement: for a radius `δ ≤ 1`, `d_H(x, x₀) < δ` implies
`d_{H,α}(\Pi_α x, \Pi_α x₀) < δ` for every tag `α`, with no dependence on
`α`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis estimate in the
proof of (ii): below radius `1` the length and the tag pattern stabilize, so
the selected index set is the same, and the component tuple is controlled by
the coordinatewise distance estimate already used for (i).
declarations.header: theorem separationComponent_edist_lt_of_near {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) (x y : Tuple (DisjointUnion X)) {δ : ENNReal} (hδ : δ ≤ 1) (hxy : letI := DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X) edist x y < δ) : edist (separationComponent a x) (separationComponent a y) < δ :=
declarations.name: separationComponent_edist_lt_of_near

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`,
`prop:separation-continuous`.

Original labels: `prop:separation-continuous`, `prop:separation-2`.

Informal statement: the separation operator
`\Pi : \mathscr{T}(\bigsqcup_α X_α) → \prod_α \mathscr{T}(X_α)` is continuous
when the product carries the sup product metric
`D((y_α)_α, (z_α)_α) = sup_α d_{H,α}(y_α, z_α)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof of (ii). For
`x₀` and `ε > 0` choose `0 < δ < min(1, ε)`; then for `d_H(x, x₀) < δ` every
component satisfies `d_{H,α}(\Pi_α x, \Pi_α x₀) < δ` by the uniform estimate
above, hence `D(\Pi x, \Pi x₀) ≤ δ < ε`. The thesis assumes a countable
family; the argument needs no countability, so the statement is proved for an
arbitrary index family.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_separationOperator_supMetric {A : Type v} [DecidableEq A] {X : A → Type u} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : letI := DisjointUnionTopology.disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: continuous_separationOperator_supMetric

Thesis source:

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2`, single-factor restriction
criterion.

Informal statement: a subset of real tuple space is Borel iff all of its
fixed-length restrictions are Borel subsets of the corresponding Euclidean
finite product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the Chapter 2 Sigma/fixed-length
Borel bridge specialized to `X = ℝ`, i.e. the `k = 1` restriction criterion.
The thesis lemma itself, for `k` simultaneous layers
`L = ℝ^{n_1} × ⋯ × ℝ^{n_k} ⊆ \mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k`, is `fixedLayers_Borel` below,
proved along the thesis route.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_realTupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength {s : Set (Tuple ℝ)} : @MeasurableSet (Tuple ℝ) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := ℝ)) s ↔
declarations.name: measurableSet_realTupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2`, the layer
`L = ℝ^{n_1} × ⋯ × ℝ^{n_k}`.

Informal statement: the simultaneous fixed-length layer of `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k`
with prescribed lengths `n_1, …, n_k` (with `ℝ^0 = {e}`), as the image of the
Euclidean product under the coordinatewise layer embeddings.
declarations.header: def fixedLayers {k : ℕ} (n : Fin k → ℕ) (x : (i : Fin k) → Fin (n i) → ℝ) : Fin k → Tuple ℝ :=
declarations.name: fixedLayers

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2`, topological step.

Informal statement: `L` is open in `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k` and its subspace
topology is the usual topology of `ℝ^{n_1} × ⋯ × ℝ^{n_k}`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the standard-machinery step of
the thesis proof. Each fixed-length layer of `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)` is clopen and
homeomorphic to `ℝ^n` (the tuple topology is the Sigma topology,
`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma`, so `Sigma.mk n` is an open
embedding); taking the product over the `k` factors gives the open embedding
of `L`.
declarations.header: theorem fixedLayers_isOpenEmbedding {k : ℕ} (n : Fin k → ℕ) : letI : TopologicalSpace (Tuple ℝ) := tupleHausdorffMetricTopology
declarations.name: fixedLayers_isOpenEmbedding

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2`.

Informal statement: for `k ∈ ℕ` and lengths `n_1, …, n_k ∈ ℕ_0`, every Borel
subset of `L = ℝ^{n_1} × ⋯ × ℝ^{n_k}` is Borel in `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k` (with the
product of the tuple Hausdorff topologies), and conversely the trace on `L`
of a Borel subset of `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k` is Borel in `L`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. Since `L`
embeds openly (hence Borel-measurably, with Borel image) by
`fixedLayers_isOpenEmbedding`, the Borel σ-algebra of `L` is the trace of the
Borel σ-algebra of `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)^k`, which gives both assertions; the second
one is the preimage statement under the embedding.
declarations.header: theorem fixedLayers_Borel {k : ℕ} (n : Fin k → ℕ) : letI : TopologicalSpace (Tuple ℝ) := tupleHausdorffMetricTopology
declarations.name: fixedLayers_Borel

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2`, case `k = 1`, as used in the
proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: a Borel subset of `ℝ^n` is Borel in `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)` for
the tuple Hausdorff Borel σ-algebra, via the length-`n` layer embedding.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: same open-embedding argument as
`fixedLayers_Borel`, stated for one factor and the project's
`tupleHausdorffBorel` on `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)` so that fixed-length Borel fibres
can be transported to tuple space directly.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixedLayer_image {n : ℕ} {A : Set (Fin n → ℝ)} (hA : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → ℝ) (@borel (Fin n → ℝ) inferInstance) A) : @MeasurableSet (Tuple ℝ) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := ℝ))
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixedLayer_image

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: the set `A^\pi_k` in the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: `A^\pi_k = ⋂_{j ∈ D^\pi_{k-1}} \{x ∈ ℝ^n \mid x(\pi(k)) ⪯ x(j)\}`
with `D^\pi_{k-1} = \{\pi(j) \mid j ≥ k\}`: the tuples for which `\pi(k)` attains the
`k`-th selected minimum.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `D^\pi_{k-1}` is enumerated as
`\{\pi(j) \mid k ≤ j\}`, so the intersection over `j ∈ D^\pi_{k-1}` becomes a
universal quantifier over `j ≥ k`. The cell is stated for any preorder `X`;
the thesis uses `X = ℝ` with `⪯ ∈ \{≤, ≥\}`.
declarations.header: def minimalSelectionCell [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) (k : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → X) :=
declarations.name: minimalSelectionCell

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: the set `B^\pi_k` in the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: `B^\pi_k = ⋂_{j ∈ D^\pi_{k-1}, j < \pi(k)} \{x \mid x(\pi(k)) ≠ x(j)\}`,
the tie-breaking rule preferring the smallest original index. As in the thesis,
`j ∈ D^\pi_{k-1}` with `j < \pi(k)` is written `j = \pi(m)` with `m > k`, so
`B^\pi_k = ⋂_{m > k, \pi(m) < \pi(k)} \{x \mid x(\pi(k)) ≠ x(\pi(m))\}`.
declarations.header: def minimalTieBreakCell [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) (k : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → X) :=
declarations.name: minimalTieBreakCell

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: the finite intersection `⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` in the
proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the candidate description of the fibre
`𝒲_\pi = \{x ∈ ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)} \mid \pi^⪯(x) = \pi\}` as a finite intersection of the
selection cells `A^\pi_k` and tie-break cells `B^\pi_k`. The identity with the
fibre is `minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_mem_cell` below.
declarations.header: def minimalPermutationCell [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) : Set (Fin n → X) :=
declarations.name: minimalPermutationCell

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: pointwise reading of `⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` in the proof
of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: `x ∈ ⋂_k (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` iff for all positions `k < m`,
`x(\pi(k)) ⪯ x(\pi(m))`, and `x(\pi(k)) ≠ x(\pi(m))` whenever `\pi(m) < \pi(k)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the `j = k` instance of `A^\pi_k` is
trivial (`x(\pi(k)) ⪯ x(\pi(k))`), so only `k < m` remains; this is the form
in which the greedy recursion is compared with the cells.
declarations.header: theorem mem_minimalPermutationCell_iff [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) (x : Fin n → X) : x ∈ minimalPermutationCell (X := X) π ↔
declarations.name: mem_minimalPermutationCell_iff

`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: Lean bookkeeping for the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the relation between two graph points `p` (selected
earlier) and `q` (selected later) expressed by the cells: `p` has value `⪯`
the value of `q`, and if `q` has the smaller original index then the values
differ. A graph-point list is pairwise in this relation exactly when it lists
the cells' conditions position by position.

declarations.name: GreedyPairwiseStep

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: membership in `M^{(n)}`, the value-minimal remainder points of
`defn:sorting-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: a graph point is value-minimal in a finite remainder iff it
belongs to the remainder and no remainder point has strictly smaller value.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this unfolds the Chapter 2 definition with
the decidability instance used there (`classical`), so the lemma can be used
in a linear-order context without instance mismatch.
declarations.header: theorem mem_valueMinimalElements_iff [Preorder X] (s : Finset (IndexAugmented X)) (p : IndexAugmented X) : p ∈ valueMinimalElements (X := X) s ↔
declarations.name: mem_valueMinimalElements_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: the recursive argument for
`𝒲_\pi = ⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` in the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: for a graph-point list `l` with pairwise distinct original
indices, the recursive least-index value-minimal selector of
`defn:minimal-sort` (Chapter 2's `\varsigma^\ast`) run on the finite set of
points of `l` returns exactly `l` iff `l` satisfies the cells' conditions
position by position.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis argument, by
induction along the greedy recursion `D_0 ⊇ D_1 ⊇ ⋯`. "⊆": the head is the
least-index value-minimal point, so its value is `⪯` every later value, and
a later point with equal value must have a larger index. "⊇": if the list
satisfies the cell conditions then its head is value-minimal, has the least
index among value-minimal points (otherwise, in the words of the thesis,
`\pi^⪯` would have selected `\pi(m)` before `\pi(k)`), and is the unique
point with its index; hence the selector picks the head, removes it, and the
induction hypothesis handles the tail `D_k`.
declarations.header: theorem distinctFiniteSetSortListAux_eq_iff_pairwise_greedy [LinearOrder X] (l : List (IndexAugmented X)) (hidx : (l.map IndexAugmented.index).Nodup) : distinctFiniteSetSortListAux (X := X) (graphPointListToFinset (X := X) l) = l ↔
declarations.name: distinctFiniteSetSortListAux_eq_iff_pairwise_greedy

Informal statement: the graph points of `x ∈ X^n` listed in the order
`\pi(1), …, \pi(n)`; `\pi^⪯(x) = \pi` means precisely that the greedy recursion
produces this list.
declarations.header: def permutationGraphList {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : List (IndexAugmented X) :=
declarations.name: permutationGraphList

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: injectivity of `\pi` in the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the original indices `\pi(1), …, \pi(n)` are pairwise
distinct.
declarations.header: theorem nodup_map_index_permutationGraphList {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : ((permutationGraphList x π).map IndexAugmented.index).Nodup :=
declarations.name: nodup_map_index_permutationGraphList

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: reading `⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` along the enumeration
`(\pi(k), x(\pi(k)))_k` in the proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the graph list in `\pi`-order satisfies the cell conditions

`defn:minimal-sort`.

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `D_0 = \mathrm{domain}(x)` in `defn:minimal-sort`, in graph
form.

Informal statement: for a totally ordered tuple of length `n`, the (unique)
segment graph is the whole graph of `x`, which is the set of points of the
`\pi`-ordered enumeration `(\pi(k), x(\pi(k)))_{k=1}^n` for any permutation `\pi`.
declarations.header: theorem toFinset_segmentDistinctFiniteSet_eq_permutationGraphList [LinearOrder X] {n : ℕ} (y : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) (K : ConnectedSegment (⟨n, y⟩ : Tuple X)) : toFinset (segmentDistinctFiniteSet (⟨n, y⟩ : Tuple X) K).1 = graphPointListToFinset (X := X) (permutationGraphList y π) :=
declarations.name: toFinset_segmentDistinctFiniteSet_eq_permutationGraphList

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `\pi^⪯(x)(k) = \pi_k` in `defn:minimal-sort`.

Informal statement: the `k`-th value of the minimal permutation is the original
index of the `k`-th selected graph point.
declarations.header: theorem minimumSortPermutation_val_eq_index_graphList [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (y : Fin n → X) (k : Fin n) : (minimumSortPermutation (X := X) (⟨n, y⟩ : Tuple X) k).1 =
declarations.name: minimumSortPermutation_val_eq_index_graphList

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `\pi^⪯(x) = \pi` as a statement about the selected graph points,
in the proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: `\pi^⪯(x) = \pi` iff the greedy recursion selects the graph
points of `x` in the order `\pi(1), …, \pi(n)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: both directions compare the two lists
position by position; the selected point at position `k` has index
`\pi^⪯(x)(k)` and value `x(\pi^⪯(x)(k))`.
declarations.header: theorem minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_graphList_eq [LinearOrder X] {n : ℕ} (y : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : minimumSortPermutation (X := X) (⟨n, y⟩ : Tuple X) = π ↔
declarations.name: minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_graphList_eq

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`, fibre identity
`𝒲_\pi = ⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)`.

Informal statement: for a tuple `x ∈ X^n` over a totally ordered set and a
permutation `\pi` of length `n`, `\pi^⪯(x) = \pi` iff
`x ∈ ⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)`: `\pi(k)` attains the `k`-th selected minimum
(`A^\pi_k`) and, among equal values, has the smallest original index (`B^\pi_k`).

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis argument. Over a
totally ordered set all entries lie in one comparability component
(`minimumSortGraphList_eq_of_linearOrder`), so the Chapter 2 rule is the
greedy recursion of `defn:minimal-sort` on the whole graph `D_0`;
`\pi^⪯(x) = \pi` means the recursion lists the graph in `\pi`-order
(`minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_graphList_eq`), which by induction along the
recursion is equivalent to the cell conditions
(`distinctFiniteSetSortListAux_eq_iff_pairwise_greedy`,
`pairwise_greedy_permutationGraphList_iff`). The empty tuple is the trivial
case `n = 0`.
declarations.header: theorem minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_mem_cell [LinearOrder X] {n : ℕ} (y : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : minimumSortPermutation (X := X) (⟨n, y⟩ : Tuple X) = π ↔
declarations.name: minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_mem_cell

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: Borel measurability of `A^\pi_k` and `B^\pi_k` in the proof of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: `⋂_{k=1}^n (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` is a Borel subset of `X^n`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis argument. Each
`\{x \mid x(\pi(k)) ⪯ x(j)\}` is closed because the order is closed
(`isClosed_le`, the thesis' closed set `\{(x,y) \mid x ≤ y\}`), and each
`\{x \mid x(\pi(k)) ≠ x(\pi(m))\}` is open because the diagonal is closed
(`isOpen_ne_fun`); `A^\pi_k`, `B^\pi_k` and `⋂_k (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` are finite
intersections of these, hence Borel. Stated for the Borel σ-algebra of the
product topology on `X^n`, which for `X = ℝ` is the usual Borel σ-algebra of
`ℝ^n`.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_minimalPermutationCell {X : Type u} [LinearOrder X] [TopologicalSpace X] [OrderClosedTopology X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) (minimalPermutationCell (X := X) π) :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_minimalPermutationCell

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `𝒲_\pi = \{x ∈ ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)} \mid \pi^⪯(x) = \pi\} ⊆ ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` in the
proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`, order `\leq`.

Informal statement: the fibre `(\pi^\le)^{-1}(\{\pi\})` consists of tuples of
length `ℓ(\pi)` only, and inside `ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` it is the finite intersection
`⋂_{k=1}^{ℓ(\pi)} (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)`.
declarations.header: theorem realMinimalPermutationLE_preimage_singleton {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) : realMinimalPermutationLE ⁻¹' {(⟨n, π⟩ : FinitePermutations)} = (fun x : Fin n → ℝ => (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple ℝ)) '' minimalPermutationCell (X := ℝ) π :=
declarations.name: realMinimalPermutationLE_preimage_singleton

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `𝒲_\pi = \{x ∈ ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)} \mid \pi^⪯(x) = \pi\} ⊆ ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` in the
proof of `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`, order `\geq`.

Informal statement: the fibre `(\pi^\ge)^{-1}(\{\pi\})` consists of tuples of
length `ℓ(\pi)` only, and inside `ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` it is the finite intersection
`⋂_{k=1}^{ℓ(\pi)} (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` for `⪯ = ≥`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `⪯ = ≥` is the order `≤` of `OrderDual ℝ`,
so the cells are those of `OrderDual ℝ`, pulled back along the coordinatewise
identification `x ↦ (\mathrm{toDual}(x(i)))_i` of `ℝ^n` with `(ℝ^{op})^n`.
declarations.header: theorem realMinimalPermutationGE_preimage_singleton {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) : realMinimalPermutationGE ⁻¹' {(⟨n, π⟩ : FinitePermutations)} = (fun x : Fin n → ℝ => (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple ℝ)) '' ((fun x : Fin n → ℝ => fun i => OrderDual.toDual (x i)) ⁻¹' minimalPermutationCell (X := OrderDual ℝ) π) :=
declarations.name: realMinimalPermutationGE_preimage_singleton

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`, order `\leq`.

Informal statement: the increasing real-valued minimal price sorting
permutation map is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. Since
`\mathscr{P}` is countable (`prop:permutations-countable`,
`finitePermutations_countable`), every `B ⊆ \mathscr{P}` is the countable union
`⋃_{\pi ∈ B} \{\pi\}` of its singletons (so `\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{P})` is the
power set and no measurability hypothesis on `B` is needed), and it suffices
that each fibre `𝒲_\pi = (\pi^\le)^{-1}(\{\pi\})` is Borel. The fibre lies in
the layer `ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}`, where it equals `⋂_{k=1}^{ℓ(\pi)} (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)`
(`realMinimalPermutationLE_preimage_singleton`, built on the fibre identity
`minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_mem_cell`); this finite intersection of closed
and open sets is Borel in `ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` (`measurableSet_minimalPermutationCell`)
and hence, by `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2` (`measurableSet_fixedLayer_image`),
Borel in `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)`.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_realMinimalPermutationLE : letI : TopologicalSpace FinitePermutations := finitePermutationMetricTopology
declarations.name: measurable_realMinimalPermutationLE

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: tuple-valued consequence of
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the real increasing minimum-sort map is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proposition in the thesis is stated
for the permutation-valued map `\pi^\preceq`. The tuple-valued map is
`x ↦ x[\pi^\le(x)]` (`realMinimumSortLE_eq_permutationMap`), which is Borel
measurable because `\pi^\le` is (`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`) and
`(x,\pi) ↦ x[\pi]` is continuous (`prop:permuting-continuous`,
`measurable_permutationMap_comp`), exactly as in the thesis paragraph after
`prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_minimumSort_real_LE : @Measurable (Tuple ℝ) (Tuple ℝ) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := ℝ)) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := ℝ))
declarations.name: measurable_minimumSort_real_LE

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: `prop:minimal-sorting-measurable`, order `\geq`.

Informal statement: the decreasing real-valued minimal price sorting
permutation map is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof for `⪯ = ≥`,
with the same structure as the `\leq` case. Since `\mathscr{P}` is countable
(`prop:permutations-countable`), every `B ⊆ \mathscr{P}` is the countable union
of its singletons and it suffices that each fibre `(\pi^\ge)^{-1}(\{\pi\})` is
Borel. The fibre lies in `ℝ^{ℓ(\pi)}` and equals
`⋂_{k=1}^{ℓ(\pi)} (A^\pi_k ∩ B^\pi_k)` for `⪯ = ≥`
(`realMinimalPermutationGE_preimage_singleton`, via the fibre identity
`minimumSortPermutation_eq_iff_mem_cell` over `OrderDual ℝ`). The cells for
`≥` are the `OrderDual ℝ` cells pulled back along the continuous coordinatewise
identification `ℝ^n ≅ (ℝ^{op})^n`; they are Borel by
`measurableSet_minimalPermutationCell` (closed order relation, closed diagonal),
and `lem:tuple-space-measurable-2` (`measurableSet_fixedLayer_image`) transports
the fibre to `\mathscr{T}(ℝ)`.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_realMinimalPermutationGE : letI : TopologicalSpace FinitePermutations := finitePermutationMetricTopology
declarations.name: measurable_realMinimalPermutationGE
