declarations.header: def prefixQuantity {n : ℕ} (q : Fin n → Quantity) (i : Fin n) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: prefixQuantity

declarations.header: def below {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (r : ℝ) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: below

declarations.header: def above {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (r : ℝ) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: above

declarations.header: theorem prefix_le_below {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Monotone p) (i : Fin n) : prefixQuantity q i ≤ below p q (p i) :=
declarations.name: prefix_le_below

declarations.header: theorem prefix_le_above {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Antitone p) (i : Fin n) : prefixQuantity q i ≤ above p q (p i) :=
declarations.name: prefix_le_above

declarations.header: theorem exists_prefix_below {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Monotone p) (i : Fin n) : ∃ k, p k = p i ∧ prefixQuantity q k = below p q (p i) :=
declarations.name: exists_prefix_below

declarations.header: theorem exists_prefix_above {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Antitone p) (i : Fin n) : ∃ k, p k = p i ∧ prefixQuantity q k = above p q (p i) :=
declarations.name: exists_prefix_above

declarations.header: def cumulativeVolume {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: cumulativeVolume

declarations.header: def thresholdVolume {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) : Quantity :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume

declarations.header: theorem cumulativeVolume_eq_thresholdVolume {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (hs : Monotone ps) (hb : Antitone pb) : cumulativeVolume ps qs pb qb = thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: cumulativeVolume_eq_thresholdVolume

declarations.header: theorem eval_cumulative {n : ℕ} (q : Fin n → Quantity) (i : Fin n) : tupleQuantityEval i.val (cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, q⟩) = prefixQuantity q i :=
declarations.name: eval_cumulative

declarations.header: theorem equilibrium_eq_cumulativeVolume {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) : equilibriumQuantity ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, qs⟩, ⟨n, ps⟩), (cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨m, qb⟩, ⟨m, pb⟩)) = cumulativeVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: equilibrium_eq_cumulativeVolume

declarations.header: theorem equilibrium_eq_thresholdVolume {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (hs : Monotone ps) (hb : Antitone pb) : equilibriumQuantity ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, qs⟩, ⟨n, ps⟩), (cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨m, qb⟩, ⟨m, pb⟩)) = thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: equilibrium_eq_thresholdVolume

declarations.header: theorem below_permutation {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (π : FinitePermutation n) (r : ℝ) : below (fun i => p (π i)) (fun i => q (π i)) r = below p q r :=
declarations.name: below_permutation

declarations.header: theorem above_permutation {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (π : FinitePermutation n) (r : ℝ) : above (fun i => p (π i)) (fun i => q (π i)) r = above p q r :=
declarations.name: above_permutation

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_permutation_le {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (π : FinitePermutation n) (ρ : FinitePermutation m) : thresholdVolume (fun i => ps (π i)) (fun i => qs (π i)) (fun j => pb (ρ j)) (fun j => qb (ρ j)) ≤ thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_permutation_le

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_permutation {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (π : FinitePermutation n) (ρ : FinitePermutation m) : thresholdVolume (fun i => ps (π i)) (fun i => qs (π i)) (fun j => pb (ρ j)) (fun j => qb (ρ j)) = thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_permutation

declarations.docComment:
A price cut need not occur among the order prices. Its feasible quantity
is still bounded by the existing finite candidate maximum.
declarations.header: theorem arbitrary_threshold_le {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (r t : ℝ) (hrt : r ≤ t) : min (below ps qs r) (above pb qb t) ≤ thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: arbitrary_threshold_le

declarations.header: theorem below_prepend {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (p₀ r : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : below (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) p) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) q) r = (if p₀ ≤ r then q₀ else 0) + below p q r :=
declarations.name: below_prepend

declarations.header: theorem above_prepend {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (p₀ r : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : above (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) p) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) q) r = (if r ≤ p₀ then q₀ else 0) + above p q r :=
declarations.name: above_prepend

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_le_prepend_buy {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb ≤ thresholdVolume ps qs (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) pb) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) qb) :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_le_prepend_buy

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_prepend_zero_buy {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) : thresholdVolume ps qs (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) pb) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => 0) qb) = thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_prepend_zero_buy

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_le_prepend_sell {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb ≤ thresholdVolume (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) ps) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) qs) pb qb :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_le_prepend_sell

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_prepend_zero_sell {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) : thresholdVolume (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) ps) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => 0) qs) pb qb = thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_prepend_zero_sell

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_prepend_buy_le {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : thresholdVolume ps qs (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) pb) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) qb) ≤ thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb + q₀ :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_prepend_buy_le

declarations.header: theorem thresholdVolume_prepend_sell_le {n m : ℕ} (ps : Fin n → ℝ) (qs : Fin n → Quantity) (pb : Fin m → ℝ) (qb : Fin m → Quantity) (p₀ : ℝ) (q₀ : Quantity) : thresholdVolume (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => p₀) ps) (Fin.append (fun _ : Fin 1 => q₀) qs) pb qb ≤ thresholdVolume ps qs pb qb + q₀ :=
declarations.name: thresholdVolume_prepend_sell_le

declarations.header: theorem below_reaches_index {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (r : ℝ) (v : Quantity) (hv : 0 < v) (hvr : v ≤ below p q r) : ∃ k, p k ≤ r ∧ v ≤ prefixQuantity q k :=
declarations.name: below_reaches_index

declarations.header: theorem above_reaches_index {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (r : ℝ) (v : Quantity) (hv : 0 < v) (hvr : v ≤ above p q r) : ∃ k, r ≤ p k ∧ v ≤ prefixQuantity q k :=
declarations.name: above_reaches_index

declarations.header: theorem marginal_le_iff_below {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Monotone p) (v : Quantity) {i : ℕ} (hi : ReachesFirst ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, q⟩, ⟨n, p⟩), v) i) (r : ℝ) : marginalPrice ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, q⟩, ⟨n, p⟩), v) ≤ r ↔ v ≤ below p q r :=
declarations.name: marginal_le_iff_below

declarations.header: theorem le_marginal_iff_above {n : ℕ} (p : Fin n → ℝ) (q : Fin n → Quantity) (hp : Antitone p) (v : Quantity) {i : ℕ} (hi : ReachesFirst ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, q⟩, ⟨n, p⟩), v) i) (r : ℝ) : r ≤ marginalPrice ((cumulativeQuantityTuple ⟨n, q⟩, ⟨n, p⟩), v) ↔ v ≤ above p q r :=
declarations.name: le_marginal_iff_above

declarations.docComment: The concrete carrier for the nonseparable discrete example.
declarations.header: abbrev LargeDiscrete := Set (ℕ → Bool)
declarations.name: LargeDiscrete

declarations.docComment:
Original block id:
`source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1840:rem:91`.
The diagonal can fail to belong to the tensor product even though both
coordinate sigma algebras contain every subset. Cantor's theorem rules out
the injection forced by a tensor-measurable diagonal.
declarations.header: theorem large_diagonal_not_tensor : ¬ @MeasurableSet (LargeDiscrete × LargeDiscrete) ((⊤ : MeasurableSpace LargeDiscrete).prod ⊤) (Set.diagonal LargeDiscrete) :=
declarations.name: large_diagonal_not_tensor

declarations.docComment:
For the discrete topology the diagonal is closed, hence product-Borel,
while the preceding theorem shows it is not tensor measurable.
declarations.header: theorem large_diagonal_borel_not_tensor : @MeasurableSet (LargeDiscrete × LargeDiscrete) (@borel _ (@instTopologicalSpaceProd LargeDiscrete LargeDiscrete ⊥ ⊥)) (Set.diagonal LargeDiscrete) ∧ ¬ @MeasurableSet (LargeDiscrete × LargeDiscrete) ((@borel LargeDiscrete ⊥).prod (@borel LargeDiscrete ⊥)) (Set.diagonal LargeDiscrete) :=
declarations.name: large_diagonal_borel_not_tensor

declarations.docComment:
The discrete counterexample carries a literal finite-valued extended

declarations.header: theorem largeDiscrete_metric_topology : largeDiscreteEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace = ⊥ :=
declarations.name: largeDiscrete_metric_topology

declarations.docComment:
The example really is nonseparable. Discrete separability would make
its carrier countable; singleton coding of naturals into binary sequences
would then contradict Cantor's theorem again.
declarations.header: theorem largeDiscrete_nonseparable : ¬ @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace LargeDiscrete largeDiscreteEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace :=
declarations.name: largeDiscrete_nonseparable

declarations.docComment:
Original block id:
`source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:1840:rem:91`.
Componentwise Borel random elements always give a tensor-measurable pair;
comparison events follow if the order set belongs to that tensor sigma algebra.
declarations.header: theorem comparison_event_of_tensor_order {Ω X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace X] (ξ η : Ω → X) (hξ : @Measurable Ω X inferInstance (borel X) ξ) (hη : @Measurable Ω X inferInstance (borel X) η) (r : X → X → Prop) (hr : @MeasurableSet (X × X) ((borel X).prod (borel X)) {p | r p.1 p.2}) : MeasurableSet {ω | r (ξ ω) (η ω)} :=
declarations.name: comparison_event_of_tensor_order

declarations.docComment:
Original block id:
`source:1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex:350:rem:18`.
Different submitting agents have the same visible order and the same kernel
class. Pulling back a reflexive quotient order is therefore not antisymmetric
on the original labelled submissions.
declarations.header: theorem equal_view_distinct_agents {A : Type u} (o : OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) (a b : A) (hab : a ≠ b) (r : (OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) → (OrderSide × (ℝ × Quantity)) → Prop) (hr : ∀ o, r o o) : marketView (o, a) = marketView (o, b) ∧ (o, a) ≠ (o, b) ∧ r (marketView (o, a)) (marketView (o, b)) ∧ r (marketView (o, b)) (marketView (o, a)) :=
declarations.name: equal_view_distinct_agents

declarations.docComment:
Equal visible submissions with distinct agents collapse to a single
visible set element; the original two-element set still has cardinality two.

declarations.name: quotient_forgets_multiplicity

declarations.docComment:
Ordered configurations contain distinct points; the kernel of range
forgets exactly their enumeration, and hence multiplicity is not introduced.
declarations.header: def OrderedConfiguration (X : Type u) (n : ℕ) := {f : Fin n → X // Function.Injective f}
declarations.name: OrderedConfiguration

declarations.header: def configurationRange {X : Type u} {n : ℕ} (f : OrderedConfiguration X n) : FiniteSubsets X := ⟨Set.range f.val, Set.finite_range _⟩
declarations.name: configurationRange

declarations.header: def UnorderedConfiguration (X : Type u) (n : ℕ) :=
declarations.name: UnorderedConfiguration

declarations.docComment:
Equality of unordered ranges of distinct configurations is exactly
equality up to a finite permutation, so this is the usual configuration
quotient, rather than a new quotient relation.
declarations.header: theorem configuration_same_range_iff_permutation {X : Type u} {n : ℕ} (f g : OrderedConfiguration X n) : configurationRange f = configurationRange g ↔ ∃ π : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), ∀ i, g.val (π i) = f.val i :=
declarations.name: configuration_same_range_iff_permutation

declarations.name: configurationToFinite

declarations.name: configurationToFinite_bijective

The ordinary set-of-pairs representation of the disjoint union
`\bigcup a, S a × {a}`. In Lean this is the subset of `β × A` whose value
belongs to the component selected by its tag.

The product representation `(\bigcup a, S a) × A`, written as a subset of

The set-of-pairs disjoint union is contained in the product of the ordinary

Thesis `prop:disjoint-product`.

The set-of-pairs disjoint union equals the product representation exactly when
all component sets are equal.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis' equality/iff clause expressed as equality
of subsets of the common ambient product `β × A`, while the typed object
`SetDisjointUnion S = Σ a, S a` remains Lean's safer internal representation.

If the components are pairwise disjoint, the ordinary union and the disjoint

The tagged product map is injective: keeping both the ordinary-union element

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-partial-order`.

The order on a disjoint union compares only elements with the same tag, using
the order from that component.

Instance note: `DisjointUnion X` is an `abbrev` for `Σ a, X a`, so this is a
global `LE` instance on every sigma type with ordered fibres. Mathlib's
`Mathlib.Data.Sigma.Order` declares a global disjoint-sum instance on the same
type (`Sigma.LE`, an inductive relation) that is logically equivalent
(`Sigma.le_def`) but not definitionally equal to this one. No project module
currently imports `Mathlib.Data.Sigma.Order` (checked over the import closure
of every module), so the two never coexist. If that import is ever added, make
`instLE`/`instPartialOrder` `scoped` and `open scoped` them where the
disjoint-union order is used.
declarations.header: instance instLE [∀ a, LE (X a)] : LE (DisjointUnion X)
declarations.name: instLE

declarations.header: theorem mk_le_mk_same [∀ a, LE (X a)] {a : A} {x y : X a} : (Sigma.mk a x : DisjointUnion X) ≤ Sigma.mk a y ↔ x ≤ y :=
declarations.name: mk_le_mk_same

declarations.header: theorem not_le_of_ne [∀ a, LE (X a)] {a b : A} (h : a ≠ b) (x : X a) (y : X b) : ¬ (Sigma.mk a x : DisjointUnion X) ≤ Sigma.mk b y :=
declarations.name: not_le_of_ne

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-partial-order`.

Partial orders on each component induce a partial order on the disjoint union.

Instance note: see `instLE`; Mathlib's `Mathlib.Data.Sigma.Order` carries a
non-definitionally-equal global `PartialOrder (Σ i, α i)` on the same type,
which no project module imports.
declarations.header: instance instPartialOrder [∀ a, PartialOrder (X a)] : PartialOrder (DisjointUnion X)
declarations.name: instPartialOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-total-order`.

The lexicographic non-strict order on a disjoint union. This is kept as a
named relation rather than a global `≤` instance because the thesis also uses
the same-tag-only partial order on the same underlying disjoint union.
declarations.header: def LexLE [LT A] [∀ a, LE (X a)] (z w : DisjointUnion X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: LexLE

declarations.header: theorem lexLE_refl [Preorder A] [∀ a, Preorder (X a)] (z : DisjointUnion X) : LexLE z z :=
declarations.name: lexLE_refl

declarations.header: theorem lexLE_trans [Preorder A] [∀ a, Preorder (X a)] {x y z : DisjointUnion X} : LexLE x y → LexLE y z → LexLE x z :=
declarations.name: lexLE_trans

declarations.header: theorem lexLE_antisymm [PartialOrder A] [∀ a, PartialOrder (X a)] {x y : DisjointUnion X} : LexLE x y → LexLE y x → x = y :=
declarations.name: lexLE_antisymm

declarations.header: theorem lexLE_total [LinearOrder A] [∀ a, LinearOrder (X a)] (x y : DisjointUnion X) : LexLE x y ∨ LexLE y x :=
declarations.name: lexLE_total

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-total-order`.

The lexicographic relation is a partial order when the index and component
relations are linear orders.
declarations.header: theorem lexLE_isPartialOrder [LinearOrder A] [∀ a, LinearOrder (X a)] : IsPartialOrder (DisjointUnion X) LexLE
declarations.name: lexLE_isPartialOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-total-order`.

The lexicographic relation is total when the index and component relations are
linear orders.
declarations.header: theorem lexLE_isTotal [LinearOrder A] [∀ a, LinearOrder (X a)] : Std.Total (LexLE (X := X))
declarations.name: lexLE_isTotal

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `cor:strict-disjoint-total-order`.

The strict lexicographic order on a disjoint union.
declarations.header: def LexLT [LT A] [∀ a, LT (X a)] (z w : DisjointUnion X) : Prop :=
declarations.name: LexLT

declarations.header: theorem lexLT_irrefl [Preorder A] [∀ a, Preorder (X a)] (z : DisjointUnion X) : ¬ LexLT z z :=

declarations.header: theorem lexLT_trans [Preorder A] [∀ a, Preorder (X a)] {x y z : DisjointUnion X} : LexLT x y → LexLT y z → LexLT x z :=

declarations.header: theorem lexLT_trichotomous [LinearOrder A] [∀ a, LinearOrder (X a)] : Std.Trichotomous (LexLT (X := X))
declarations.name: lexLT_trichotomous

Thesis `cor:strict-disjoint-total-order`.

The strict lexicographic relation is a strict total order.
declarations.header: theorem lexLT_isStrictTotalOrder [LinearOrder A] [∀ a, LinearOrder (X a)] : IsStrictTotalOrder (DisjointUnion X) LexLT
declarations.name: lexLT_isStrictTotalOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `defn:disjoint-union-metrisation`.

The extended distance on a disjoint union: use the component distance for
points with the same tag, and `∞` for points from different components.
declarations.header: noncomputable def disjointEdist {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EDist (X a)] (z w : DisjointUnion X) : ENNReal :=
declarations.name: disjointEdist

declarations.header: theorem disjointEdist_mk_mk_same {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EDist (X a)] {a : A} (x y : X a) : disjointEdist (Sigma.mk a x : DisjointUnion X) (Sigma.mk a y) = edist x y :=
declarations.name: disjointEdist_mk_mk_same

declarations.header: theorem disjointEdist_mk_mk_ne {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EDist (X a)] {a b : A} (h : a ≠ b) (x : X a) (y : X b) : disjointEdist (Sigma.mk a x : DisjointUnion X) (Sigma.mk b y) = ⊤ :=
declarations.name: disjointEdist_mk_mk_ne

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-union-metrisation`.

The extended disjoint-union distance is an `EMetricSpace`. This is intentionally
not registered as a global instance: mathlib already provides a Sigma topology,
and we prove below that the topology induced by this explicit metric agrees
with mathlib's topology.
declarations.header: noncomputable def disjointUnionEMetricSpace {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X)
declarations.name: disjointUnionEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment: The topology induced by the thesis extended disjoint-union metric.
declarations.header: noncomputable def disjointUnionMetricTopology {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : TopologicalSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: disjointUnionMetricTopology

declarations.header: theorem sigma_mk_cast_eq {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {a b : A} (h : b = a) (x : X b) : Sigma.mk a (h ▸ x) = (Sigma.mk b x : DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: sigma_mk_cast_eq

declarations.docComment: Thesis `defn:disjoint-union-metrisation`, different-component clause.
declarations.header: theorem edist_eq_top_of_tag_ne {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {z w : DisjointUnion X} (h : z.1 ≠ w.1) : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: edist_eq_top_of_tag_ne

declarations.docComment: Finite extended distance forces points to lie in the same component.
declarations.header: theorem tag_eq_of_edist_lt_top {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {z w : DisjointUnion X} : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: tag_eq_of_edist_lt_top

declarations.docComment:
Thesis topology bridge for `defn:disjoint-union-metrisation`.

A set is open in the topology induced by the thesis extended metric iff each
component restriction is open. This is the componentwise Sigma-topology
characterization.
declarations.header: theorem metricTopology_isOpen_iff {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {s : Set (DisjointUnion X)} : @IsOpen (DisjointUnion X) (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X)) s ↔
declarations.name: metricTopology_isOpen_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis topology bridge for `defn:disjoint-union-metrisation`.

The topology induced by the thesis extended metric is exactly mathlib's native
Sigma coproduct topology. This theorem resolves the Lean instance mismatch:
metric arguments can be rewritten to componentwise Sigma arguments, and
componentwise topological arguments can be rewritten back to metric arguments.
declarations.header: theorem metricTopology_eq_sigma {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X) = instTopologicalSpaceSigma :=
declarations.name: metricTopology_eq_sigma

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `thm:pasting-lemma` (not the mapped proof).

Sigma-topology version for arbitrary topological components: a function out of
a disjoint union is continuous exactly when its restriction to every component
is continuous. This is mathlib's Sigma-topology pasting lemma
`continuous_sigma_iff`, restated with thesis terminology. The thesis's own
metric argument is `continuous_metricTopology_pasting_iff` below.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_pasting_iff {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {Y : Type w} [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (X a)] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : DisjointUnion X → Y} : Continuous f ↔ ∀ a, Continuous (fun x => f (Sigma.mk a x)) :=
declarations.name: continuous_pasting_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma`.

A function `f` out of the disjoint-union metric space is continuous exactly
when every restriction `f ∘ ι_α : x ↦ f (x, α)` is continuous.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof is the thesis's function-level
`ε`-`δ` argument, not the Sigma-topology shortcut. Forward direction: fix `α`,
`x₀ ∈ X_α` and a neighbourhood of `f (x₀, α)`; continuity of `f` at `(x₀, α)`
gives a radius `δ`, and `d((x, α), (x₀, α)) = d_α(x, x₀)`
(`disjointEdist_mk_mk_same`) turns it into a radius for `f ∘ ι_α` at `x₀`.
Converse: fix `(x₀, α₀)`; continuity of `f ∘ ι_{α₀}` at `x₀` gives `δ₀`; with
`δ = min(δ₀, 1/2)` every point within `δ` of `(x₀, α₀)` has tag `α₀`
(`tag_eq_of_edist_lt_top`), so the component estimate applies. The target `Y`
is only assumed topological, so the thesis's `ε`-ball in `Y` is an arbitrary
neighbourhood of `f (x₀, α₀)`; the thesis statement (metric `Y`) is the special
case.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_metricTopology_pasting_iff {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {Y : Type w} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] [TopologicalSpace Y] {f : DisjointUnion X → Y} : @Continuous (DisjointUnion X) Y (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X))
declarations.name: continuous_metricTopology_pasting_iff

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable` (not the mapped proof).

Abstract direct-sum version: for arbitrary measurable spaces on the components
and mathlib's Sigma measurable structure on the disjoint union (the "direct sum
of measurable spaces" of the remark following the thesis theorem), a function
out of the disjoint union is measurable exactly when its restriction to every
component is measurable. No countability is needed here, and the proof is
sigma-algebra lattice algebra. The thesis's own Borel argument for a countable
family of metric spaces is `measurable_metricTopology_pasting_iff` below.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_pasting_iff {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {Y : Type w} [∀ a, MeasurableSpace (X a)] [MeasurableSpace Y] {f : DisjointUnion X → Y} : Measurable f ↔ ∀ a, Measurable (fun x => f (Sigma.mk a x)) :=
declarations.name: measurable_pasting_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`, measurable-structure bridge.

For a countable disjoint union, the Borel sigma-algebra of mathlib's Sigma
coproduct topology is exactly the Sigma measurable structure generated by the
Borel sigma-algebras on the components.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the measurable analogue of `metricTopology_eq_sigma`.
The countability hypothesis is used in the reverse inclusion, where a set in
the Sigma measurable structure is reconstructed as a countable union of its
componentwise images.
declarations.header: theorem borel_sigma_eq {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [Countable A] [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (X a)] : @borel (DisjointUnion X) instTopologicalSpaceSigma = @Sigma.instMeasurableSpace A X (fun a => @borel (X a) inferInstance) :=
declarations.name: borel_sigma_eq

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`, measurable-structure bridge.

For a countable disjoint union equipped with the thesis extended metric, its
Borel sigma-algebra is the Sigma measurable structure generated by the Borel
sigma-algebras on the metric components.
declarations.header: theorem borel_metricTopology_eq_sigma {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [Countable A] [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] : @borel (DisjointUnion X) (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X)) =
declarations.name: borel_metricTopology_eq_sigma

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`, first step.

The canonical injection `ι_α : X_α → X`, `x ↦ (x, α)`, is an isometry for the
thesis disjoint-union metric, since `d((x, α), (x', α)) = d_α(x, x')`.
declarations.header: theorem isometry_sigmaMk {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: isometry_sigmaMk

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`, first step.

Each component `X_α × {α} = ι_α(X_α)` is open in the disjoint-union metric
space: the ball of radius `1/2` around `(x, α)` stays inside the component,
because points at finite distance share the tag.
declarations.header: theorem isOpen_range_sigmaMk_metricTopology {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) : @IsOpen (DisjointUnion X) (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X))
declarations.name: isOpen_range_sigmaMk_metricTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`, first step.

The canonical injection `ι_α` is a homeomorphism onto the open component
`X_α × {α}`, i.e. an open embedding for the disjoint-union metric topology.
declarations.header: theorem isOpenEmbedding_sigmaMk_metricTopology {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] (a : A) : @Topology.IsOpenEmbedding (X a) (DisjointUnion X) inferInstance (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X)) (Sigma.mk a) :=
declarations.name: isOpenEmbedding_sigmaMk_metricTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `thm:pasting-lemma-measurable`.

For a countable family of metric spaces, a function `f` from the disjoint-union
metric space (with its Borel sigma-algebra) to a measurable space is measurable
exactly when every restriction `f ∘ ι_α : x ↦ f (x, α)` is Borel measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof follows the thesis's two
directions rather than the Sigma-structure bridge. First, `ι_α` is an isometry
onto the open component `X_α × {α}` (`isometry_sigmaMk`,
`isOpen_range_sigmaMk_metricTopology`), hence a homeomorphism onto a Borel set
(`isOpenEmbedding_sigmaMk_metricTopology`). Forward direction:
`(f ∘ ι_α)⁻¹(B) = ι_α⁻¹(f⁻¹(B))` is Borel because `ι_α` is continuous.
Converse: `f⁻¹(B) = ⋃_α ι_α((f ∘ ι_α)⁻¹(B))`; each image is Borel because
`ι_α` is a measurable embedding onto a Borel set, and the union is countable.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_metricTopology_pasting_iff {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} {Y : Type w} [Countable A] [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] [MeasurableSpace Y] {f : DisjointUnion X → Y} : @Measurable (DisjointUnion X) Y (@borel (DisjointUnion X) (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X)))
declarations.name: measurable_metricTopology_pasting_iff

declarations.docComment: Cauchy sequences for the thesis metric eventually remain in one component.
declarations.header: theorem cauchySeq_eventually_constant_tag {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] {u : ℕ → DisjointUnion X} : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: cauchySeq_eventually_constant_tag

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties`, completeness transfer.

If every component is complete, then the thesis extended metric on the disjoint
union is complete.
declarations.header: theorem completeSpace {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] [∀ a, CompleteSpace (X a)] : letI : EMetricSpace (DisjointUnion X) := disjointUnionEMetricSpace (X := X)
declarations.name: completeSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties`, separability transfer.

A countable Sigma coproduct of separable components is separable.
declarations.header: theorem separableSpace_sigma_of_countable {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [Countable A] [∀ a, TopologicalSpace (X a)] [∀ a, TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (X a)] : TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (DisjointUnion X) :=
declarations.name: separableSpace_sigma_of_countable

declarations.docComment:
Thesis `prop:disjoint-union-metric-properties`, separability transfer.

Using `metricTopology_eq_sigma`, the same countable-index separability result
holds for the topology induced by the thesis extended metric.
declarations.header: theorem separableSpace_metricTopology_of_countable {A : Type u} {X : A → Type v} [Countable A] [∀ a, EMetricSpace (X a)] [∀ a, TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (X a)] : @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (DisjointUnion X) (disjointUnionMetricTopology (X := X)) :=
declarations.name: separableSpace_metricTopology_of_countable

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:reflexive-transitive-closure`.
Relation powers with the manuscript's left-to-right composition convention.
The zeroth power supplies the separately displayed diagonal.
declarations.header: def relationPower (R : X → X → Prop) : ℕ → X → X → Prop | 0 => Eq | n + 1 => fun x z => ∃ y, relationPower R n x y ∧ R y z /-- Original label: `defn:reflexive-transitive-closure`. -/ @[simp] theorem relationPower_one (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : X) : relationPower R 1 x y ↔ R x y :=
declarations.name: relationPower

declarations.docComment: Original label: `defn:reflexive-transitive-closure`.
declarations.header: @[simp] theorem relationPower_one (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : X) : relationPower R 1 x y ↔ R x y :=
declarations.name: relationPower_one

declarations.header: theorem relationPower_head {R : X → X → Prop} {x y z : X} {n : ℕ} (hxy : R x y) (hyz : relationPower R n y z) : relationPower R (n + 1) x z :=
declarations.name: relationPower_head

declarations.header: theorem relationPower_to_closure {R : X → X → Prop} {n : ℕ} {x y : X} (h : relationPower R n x y) : Relation.ReflTransGen R x y :=
declarations.name: relationPower_to_closure

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:reflexive-transitive-closure`.
The inductive closure used by tuple connectivity equals the literal union
of relation powers (including the diagonal at power zero).
declarations.header: theorem closure_iff_exists_power (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : X) : Relation.ReflTransGen R x y ↔ ∃ n, relationPower R n x y :=
declarations.name: closure_iff_exists_power

declarations.docComment:
Deleting cycles gives a chain with no repeated vertices. This construction
uses only forward edges, so it also applies to directed relations.
declarations.header: theorem closure_exists_nodup_chain {R : X → X → Prop} {x y : X} (h : Relation.ReflTransGen R x y) : ∃ l : List X, (x :: l).IsChain R ∧ (x :: l).Nodup ∧ (x :: l).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil _ _) = y :=
declarations.name: closure_exists_nodup_chain

declarations.header: theorem chain_relationPower {R : X → X → Prop} {x : X} {l : List X} (h : (x :: l).IsChain R) : relationPower R l.length x ((x :: l).getLast (List.cons_ne_nil _ _)) :=
declarations.name: chain_relationPower

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:transitive-closure-finite`.
For every relation on a finite carrier, every reachable pair has a witness
with fewer edges than the number of vertices. No symmetry is needed.
declarations.header: theorem closure_iff_exists_bounded_power [Fintype X] (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : X) : Relation.ReflTransGen R x y ↔ ∃ n < Fintype.card X, relationPower R n x y :=
declarations.name: closure_iff_exists_bounded_power

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:transitive-closure-finite`.
The exact displayed formula: diagonal union the powers from one to |X|-1.
It also holds for an empty carrier, where there are no pairs to check.
declarations.header: theorem finite_closure_formula [Fintype X] (R : X → X → Prop) (x y : X) : Relation.ReflTransGen R x y ↔ x = y ∨ ∃ n, 1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ Fintype.card X - 1 ∧ relationPower R n x y :=
declarations.name: finite_closure_formula

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:reflexive-transitive-closure`.
Literal equality of subsets of X × X, with the diagonal displayed separately.
declarations.header: theorem closure_eq_diagonal_union_powers (R : X → X → Prop) : {p : X × X | Relation.ReflTransGen R p.1 p.2} = {p : X × X | p.1 = p.2} ∪ ⋃ n ∈ Set.Ici 1, {p : X × X | relationPower R n p.1 p.2} :=
declarations.name: closure_eq_diagonal_union_powers

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:transitive-closure-finite`.
The finite closure formula as literal equality of relations viewed as sets.
declarations.header: theorem finite_closure_eq_diagonal_union_powers [Fintype X] (R : X → X → Prop) : {p : X × X | Relation.ReflTransGen R p.1 p.2} = {p : X × X | p.1 = p.2} ∪ ⋃ n ∈ Set.Icc 1 (Fintype.card X - 1), {p : X × X | relationPower R n p.1 p.2} :=
declarations.name: finite_closure_eq_diagonal_union_powers

declarations.docComment:
On a discrete metric space compact subsets are exactly finite subsets.
Both hyperspaces use the actual Hausdorff extended distance, including empty sets.
declarations.header: def finiteSubsetsEquivCompacts {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] : FiniteSubsets X ≃ᵢ Compacts X
declarations.name: finiteSubsetsEquivCompacts

declarations.docComment:
Completeness follows from compact-hyperspace completeness, without any
uniform lower bound on distances between distinct base points.
declarations.header: theorem finiteSubsets_complete_of_complete_discrete {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] [DiscreteTopology X] : CompleteSpace (FiniteSubsets X) :=
declarations.name: finiteSubsets_complete_of_complete_discrete

declarations.docComment: The `n`th component has two real points separated by `1/(n+1)`.
declarations.header: def Pair (n : ℕ) := {x : ℝ // x ∈ ({0, (n + 1 : ℝ)⁻¹} : Set ℝ)}
declarations.name: Pair

declarations.docComment: A countable union of shrinking pairs, with distinct components separated.
declarations.header: def Space := Σ n, Pair n
declarations.name: Space

declarations.header: def leftPoint (n : ℕ) : Space := ⟨n, ⟨0,
declarations.name: leftPoint

declarations.header: def rightPoint (n : ℕ) : Space := ⟨n, ⟨(n + 1 : ℝ)⁻¹,
declarations.name: rightPoint

declarations.header: theorem leftPoint_ne_rightPoint (n : ℕ) : leftPoint n ≠ rightPoint n :=
declarations.name: leftPoint_ne_rightPoint

declarations.header: theorem dist_leftPoint_rightPoint (n : ℕ) : dist (leftPoint n) (rightPoint n) = 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ) :=
declarations.name: dist_leftPoint_rightPoint

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-hausdorff-uniformly-discrete-iff`.
Evidence for the following informal non-necessity claim: no uniform bound
works for this complete, discrete metric space.
declarations.header: theorem not_isolative : ¬ Isolative Space :=
declarations.name: not_isolative

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-hausdorff-uniformly-discrete-iff`.
The complete finite-subset Hausdorff space in the source's informal claim,
with an ordinary finite-valued metric on its non-isolative base.
declarations.header: theorem finiteSubsets_complete_without_isolation : CompleteSpace (FiniteSubsets Space) ∧ ¬ Isolative Space :=
declarations.name: finiteSubsets_complete_without_isolation

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:uniformly-discrete`.
Allowing an extended-real isolation bound is equivalent to a finite positive
real bound, as used in the manuscript.
declarations.header: theorem isolative_iff_real_bound {α : Type u} [EDist α] : Isolative α ↔ ∃ B : ℝ, 0 < B ∧ ∀ x y : α, x ≠ y → ENNReal.ofReal B ≤ edist x y :=
declarations.name: isolative_iff_real_bound

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-hausdorff-uniformly-discrete`.
The exact supplied bound is retained, not just existence of some new bound.
declarations.header: theorem finiteSubsets_same_isolation_bound {α : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] {B : ENNReal} (hB : ∀ x y : α, x ≠ y → B ≤ edist x y) (s t : FiniteSubsets α) (hne : s ≠ t) : B ≤ edist s t :=
declarations.name: finiteSubsets_same_isolation_bound

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `rem:hausdorff-infinite-values`.
On nonempty finite subsets of a finite-valued metric space, the Hausdorff
distance gives an ordinary metric with the same topology and uniformity.
declarations.header: def nonemptyFiniteSubsetsMetricSpace (α : Type u) [MetricSpace α] : MetricSpace {s : FiniteSubsets α // (s : Set α).Nonempty} :=
declarations.name: nonemptyFiniteSubsetsMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-sets-over-finite-set`.
Literal equality of families in the finite-base proposition.
declarations.header: theorem finite_subsets_eq_powerset {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Finite) : {t : Set α | t ⊆ s ∧ t.Finite} = 𝒫 s :=
declarations.name: finite_subsets_eq_powerset

declarations.docComment:
A point occurring in every sufficiently late prefix belongs to any finite
Hausdorff limit.
declarations.header: theorem range_subset_of_finitePrefix_tendsto {α : Type u} [EMetricSpace α] (x : ℕ → α) (s : FiniteSubsets α) (hs : Tendsto (finitePrefix x) atTop (𝓝 s)) : range x ⊆ (s : Set α) :=
declarations.name: range_subset_of_finitePrefix_tendsto

declarations.header: theorem injective_finitePrefix_has_no_limit {α : Type u} [EMetricSpace α] (x : ℕ → α) (hx : Function.Injective x) : ¬ ∃ s : FiniteSubsets α, Tendsto (finitePrefix x) atTop (𝓝 s) :=
declarations.name: injective_finitePrefix_has_no_limit

declarations.header: def reciprocalSequence (n : ℕ) : ℝ := 1 / (n + 1 : ℝ)
declarations.name: reciprocalSequence

declarations.header: theorem reciprocalSequence_injective : Function.Injective reciprocalSequence :=
declarations.name: reciprocalSequence_injective

declarations.docComment: The manuscript's reciprocal-prefix example is Cauchy but has no finite-set limit.
declarations.header: theorem reciprocalPrefixes_cauchy_without_limit : CauchySeq (finitePrefix reciprocalSequence) ∧ ¬ ∃ s : FiniteSubsets ℝ, Tendsto (finitePrefix reciprocalSequence) atTop (𝓝 s) :=
declarations.name: reciprocalPrefixes_cauchy_without_limit

declarations.header: theorem real_finiteSubsets_not_complete : ¬ CompleteSpace (FiniteSubsets ℝ) :=
declarations.name: real_finiteSubsets_not_complete

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: auxiliary bridge for finite subsets.

Informal statement: the `Finset` associated to a finite subset has exactly the
same elements as the original subset.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: auxiliary bridge for finite subsets.

Informal statement: membership in the finite subset is equivalent to
membership in its associated `Finset`.

declarations.name: mem_toFinset

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: auxiliary bridge for `prop:countable-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: the representation map from proof-carrying finite subsets
to mathlib `Finset`s is injective.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the target is `Finset α`, mathlib's finite-set structure. The
result says no set-theoretic information is lost by passing through this
representation. The thesis proposition `prop:injection-into-finite-sets`
itself is the singleton injection formalized below as `singleton_injective`.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

finite subset.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: `prop:injection-into-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: the singleton map into finite subsets is injective.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,

Informal statement: `Of s` is the type of finite subsets contained in `s`.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: auxiliary map for `prop:finite-sets-over-finite-set`.

Informal statement: finite subsets of a finite base inject into the powerset
of the base `Finset`.

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: `prop:finite-sets-over-finite-set`.

Informal statement: if the base set `s` is finite, then finite subsets
contained in `s` are equivalent to arbitrary subsets of `s`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis equality `𝓕(X) = 𝒫(X)` for finite `X`,
stated as an equivalence between the subtype of finite subsets contained in
`s` and the ambient powerset subtype `{u : Set α // u ⊆ s}`. The inverse
uses the finite-base hypothesis to prove every subset of `s` is finite.
declarations.header: noncomputable def ofFiniteSetEquivPowerset {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Finite) : Of s ≃ {u : Set α // u ⊆ s}
declarations.name: ofFiniteSetEquivPowerset

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: consequence of `prop:finite-sets-over-finite-set`.

Informal statement: finite subsets contained in a finite base set form a
finite type.
declarations.header: theorem finite_of_finite_set {α : Type u} {s : Set α} (hs : s.Finite) : Finite (Of s) :=
declarations.name: finite_of_finite_set

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

space is finite.

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: `defn:separable`.

Informal statement: a topological space is separable if it has a countable
dense subset.

`TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace`; this definition keeps the thesis spelling
available as an explicit proposition.

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

The thesis uses the `[0,∞]`-valued convention. This real-valued wrapper is kept
only as a compatibility bridge to mathlib's ordinary `hausdorffDist`; it is not

Thesis source:
`A - appendices/analysis.tex`,
Proposition `prop:hausdorff-distance`, used in
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`.

Informal statement: the extended Hausdorff distance on the full powerset
`𝒫(X)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis states the background pseudometric theorem on
`𝒫(X)` before specializing to finite subsets. Mathlib defines
`Metric.hausdorffEDist` for arbitrary subsets; this wrapper keeps the
full-powerset theorem visible in the thesis namespace.

Proposition `prop:hausdorff-distance`.

Thesis source:
`A - appendices/analysis.tex`,
Proposition `prop:hausdorff-distance`.

Proposition `prop:hausdorff-distance`.

Original label: `prop:hausdorff-distance`.

Informal statement: the full powerset `𝒫(X)`, equipped with the Hausdorff
extended distance, is an extended pseudometric space.

than a global instance on `Set α`, so it does not change mathlib's default
topology or measurable structure for sets. The finite-subset instance below is
the downstream specialization used in Chapter 2.

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: `defn:Hausdorff-distance`.

Informal statement: the extended Hausdorff distance between finite subsets is
the extended Hausdorff distance between their underlying sets.

(`ENNReal`), matching the thesis codomain `[0,\infty]` and preserving the

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: basic property for `defn:Hausdorff-distance`.

Informal statement: the extended Hausdorff distance is symmetric.
declarations.header: theorem hausdorffEDistance_comm {α : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] (s t : FiniteSubsets α) : hausdorffEDistance s t = hausdorffEDistance t s :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: pseudometric part of `thm:Hausdorff-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: by the background Hausdorff-distance theorem, the extended
Hausdorff distance on finite subsets is a pseudometric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis cites the background result
`prop:hausdorff-distance`; in Lean this is provided by mathlib's Hausdorff
edistance lemmas.

declarations.name: instPseudoEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: auxiliary closedness fact for finite subsets.

Informal statement: finite subsets of a T1 topological space are closed.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this fact is not used in the separation
step of `thm:Hausdorff-finite-sets` (which follows the thesis's attained-minimum
argument in `hausdorffEDistance_eq_zero` below); it is kept for downstream
examples that identify points at infimal distance zero from a finite set.
declarations.header: theorem isClosed_coe {α : Type u} [TopologicalSpace α] [T1Space α] (s : FiniteSubsets α) : IsClosed (s : Set α) :=
declarations.name: isClosed_coe

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: finite-minimum step in `thm:Hausdorff-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: for a nonempty finite set `η` and a point `x`, the infimum
`inf_{x' ∈ η} d(x, x')` is a minimum: it is attained at some `x' ∈ η`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis sentence "since the
sets are finite, the infimum coincides with the minimum", proved by
`Set.exists_min_image` on the finite set; no closure argument is involved.
declarations.header: theorem infEDist_attained {α : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] (s : FiniteSubsets α) (hs : (s : Set α).Nonempty) (x : α) : ∃ y ∈ (s : Set α), Metric.infEDist x (s : Set α) = edist x y :=
declarations.name: infEDist_attained

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: separation step in `thm:Hausdorff-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: if two finite subsets are at extended Hausdorff distance
zero, then they are equal, and conversely.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof's final
pseudometric-to-metric step, following the thesis route. For `x ∈ ξ`, the
inner infimum `inf_{x' ∈ η} d(x, x')` is at most `d_H(ξ, η) = 0`. If `η` is
empty the infimum is `∞`, contradicting zero (the empty case of the thesis,
handled by the extended convention). Otherwise the infimum is a minimum on the
finite set `η` (`infEDist_attained`), attained at some `x' ∈ η` with
`d(x, x') = 0`, so `x = x' ∈ η`; hence `ξ ⊆ η`. By symmetry of `d_H`, also
`η ⊆ ξ`, so `ξ = η`. In the ambient space a point at distance zero from `x`
equals `x` because the space is T1 (the thesis's metric axiom).
declarations.header: theorem hausdorffEDistance_eq_zero {α : Type u} [PseudoEMetricSpace α] [T1Space α] (s t : FiniteSubsets α) : hausdorffEDistance s t = 0 ↔ s = t :=
declarations.name: hausdorffEDistance_eq_zero

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
section "Finite Sets and the Hausdorff Distance".

Original label: `thm:Hausdorff-finite-sets`.

Informal statement: if the ambient space is an extended metric space, then the
finite-subset space equipped with the thesis Hausdorff distance is an extended
metric space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis calls this a metric because its metrics take values
in `[0,\infty]`. Lean's matching structure is `EMetricSpace`, whose distance
takes values in `ℝ≥0∞`. As in the thesis, the pseudometric part is
`instPseudoEMetricSpace` and the only remaining axiom, `d_H(ξ, η) = 0 ⇒ ξ = η`,
is `hausdorffEDistance_eq_zero`, proved by attained finite minima.
declarations.header: noncomputable instance instEMetricSpace {α : Type u} [EMetricSpace α] : EMetricSpace (FiniteSubsets α) :=
declarations.name: instEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:

Original label: `property:labelled-finite-separable` in
`thm:labelled-properties`.

Informal statement: if `X` is separable, then the distinct finite-set
Hausdorff space over `X` is separable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof follows the thesis paragraph
verbatim. `ℕ × X` is separable as a product of two separable spaces
(`IndexAugmented.separableSpace`); by `prop:finite-separable`
(`finiteSubsets_separableSpace`) the finite-subset space
`\mathscr{F}(\mathbb{N} × X)` is separable; and `\mathscr{L}(X)` is a subspace
of it, so it is separable because every subspace of a separable metric space is
separable. That last fact is used in its standard form: a separable
(pseudo-e)metric space is second countable
(`UniformSpace.secondCountable_of_separable`), second countability passes to
subspaces, and second countable spaces are separable.

declarations.name: separableSpace

Original label: finite-list bookkeeping for remaining tails.

Informal statement: an element belongs to the dropped tail `l.drop r`

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the list-index version of the thesis notation
`C^{(r)}` for a finite remainder after earlier selections have been removed.
declarations.header: theorem list_mem_drop_iff_exists_get_ge {α : Type u} (l : List α) (r : ℕ) (a : α) : a ∈ l.drop r ↔ ∃ s : Fin l.length, r ≤ s.1 ∧ l.get s = a :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: `thm:measurable-partition`.

Informal statement: if `(S n)` is a countable measurable partition of `α`,
then a function `f : α → β` is measurable iff every restriction
`f|_{S n}` is measurable for the trace sigma-algebra.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: Lean represents the trace sigma-algebra on `S n` by the
subtype measurable space. The proof follows the thesis proof: reconstruct
`f ⁻¹' B` as a countable union of the measurable images of the restricted
preimages on each partition cell. The disjointness assumption is included to
match the thesis statement, although the measurability argument only needs a
countable measurable cover.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_iff_measurable_restrict_partition {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β] {S : ℕ → Set α} (hS : ∀ n, MeasurableSet (S n)) (_hdisjoint : Pairwise fun n m => Disjoint (S n) (S m)) (hcover : ⋃ n, S n = Set.univ) {f : α → β} : Measurable f ↔ ∀ n : ℕ, Measurable (fun x : S n => f x) :=
declarations.name: measurable_iff_measurable_restrict_partition

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: measurable-pasting lemma used in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: a function is measurable if it is measurable on each set
of a countable measurable cover.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis states this for partitions. The proof only needs a
cover; disjointness is relevant for uniqueness of the branch description, not
for measurability of the pasted map.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_of_measurable_restrict_countable_cover {α : Type u} {β : Type v} {ι : Type w} [MeasurableSpace α] [MeasurableSpace β] [Countable ι] {S : ι → Set α} (hS : ∀ i, MeasurableSet (S i)) (hcover : ⋃ i, S i = Set.univ) {f : α → β} (hrestr : ∀ i : ι, Measurable (fun x : S i => f x)) : Measurable f :=
declarations.name: measurable_of_measurable_restrict_countable_cover

Original label: `defn:permutation-map`.

Informal statement: the permutation map sends `(x, π)` to `x ∘ π` when the

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `FinitePermutations` is the Sigma type

declarations.header: def permutationMap (x : Tuple X) (π : FinitePermutations) : Tuple X :=

declarations.header: theorem permutationMap_same_length {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : permutationMap (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n π) = permute (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) π :=
declarations.name: permutationMap_same_length

declarations.header: theorem permutationMap_ne_length {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≠ n) (x : Fin m → X) (π : FinitePermutation n) : permutationMap (Sigma.mk m x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n π) = Tuple.empty X :=
declarations.name: permutationMap_ne_length

`< 1`, then they are equal.

`\mathscr{P}` is isolative under the tuple Hausdorff metric inherited from
`\mathscr{T}(\mathbb{N})`.
declarations.header: theorem finitePermutation_eq_of_edist_lt_one {π ρ : FinitePermutations} (h : edist π ρ < (1 : ENNReal)) : π = ρ :=
declarations.name: finitePermutation_eq_of_edist_lt_one

declarations.docComment:

Informal statement: singleton permutation sets are open in the induced

declarations.name: isOpen_singleton_finitePermutation

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: product-topology convention in `prop:permuting-continuous`.

Informal statement: the product topology on tuple space and permutation
space, using their thesis metric topologies.
declarations.header: noncomputable def permutationProductTopology {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : TopologicalSpace (Tuple X × FinitePermutations) :=
declarations.name: permutationProductTopology

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: fixed-permutation metric identity in
`prop:permuting-continuous`.

Informal statement: reindexing two fixed-length tuples by the same finite
permutation does not change their maximum coordinate distance.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis equality
`d_H(x[π₀], x₀[π₀]) = d_H(x, x₀)` on a fixed-length layer: the finite maximum
over `i` of `d(x(π₀ i), x₀(π₀ i))` is a reindexing of the maximum over `i` of
`d(x(i), x₀(i))`.
declarations.header: theorem coordinateEDistSup_permutation {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (π : FinitePermutation n) (x y : Fin n → X) : coordinateEDistSup (fun i => x (π i)) (fun i => y (π i)) = coordinateEDistSup x y :=
declarations.name: coordinateEDistSup_permutation

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: local estimate in `prop:permuting-continuous`.

Informal statement: below tuple Hausdorff distance `1`, applying a fixed
finite permutation to both tuples does not increase their distance.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis case analysis after
the length and permutation have been frozen by the bound `1`. If the common
tuple length differs from the permutation length both images are the empty
tuple; otherwise `d_H(x[π], x₀[π]) ≤ max_i d(x(π i), x₀(π i)) = max_i d(x(i),
x₀(i)) = d_H(x, x₀)` by `thm:tuple-space-properties` (ii).
declarations.header: theorem permutationMap_edist_le_of_edist_lt_one {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (π : FinitePermutations) {x y : Tuple X} (h : edist x y < (1 : ENNReal)) : edist (permutationMap x π) (permutationMap y π) ≤ edist x y :=
declarations.name: permutationMap_edist_le_of_edist_lt_one

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: `prop:permuting-continuous`.

Informal statement: the two-variable permutation map
`(x, π) ↦ x[π]` is continuous for the product topology on
`\mathscr{T}(X) × \mathscr{P}`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis ε-δ proof. Given
`(x₀, π₀)` and `ε > 0`, take `δ = min(ε, 1)`. Within the product distance `δ`
(the maximum of the two coordinate distances), the permutation is frozen,
`π = π₀`, because `\mathscr{P}` is uniformly discrete with bound `1`
(`finitePermutation_eq_of_edist_lt_one`), and the tuple length is frozen by
`thm:tuple-space-properties` (i); the fixed-permutation estimate
`permutationMap_edist_le_of_edist_lt_one` then gives
`d_H(x[π], x₀[π₀]) ≤ d_H(x, x₀) < δ ≤ ε`.
declarations.header: theorem continuous_permutationMap {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : @Continuous (Tuple X × FinitePermutations) (Tuple X) (permutationProductTopology (X := X))
declarations.name: continuous_permutationMap

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties"; used again in
`1 - theoretical foundations/4_market_clearing.tex`, Step 3.

Original label: measurable consequence of `prop:permuting-continuous`.

Informal statement: if a tuple-valued map and a finite-permutation-valued map
are Borel measurable, then applying the permutation to the tuple is Borel
measurable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the formal composition step behind the thesis phrase
"done in a measurable way": the continuous two-variable map
`(x,\pi) \mapsto x[\pi]` is composed with the measurable graph
`a \mapsto (x(a),\pi(a))`.
declarations.header: theorem measurable_permutationMap_comp {α X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace α] [EMetricSpace X] {f : α → Tuple X} {π : α → FinitePermutations} (hf : @Measurable α (Tuple X) inferInstance (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := X)) f)
declarations.name: measurable_permutationMap_comp

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: `prop:permutations-countable`.

Informal statement: the set of all finite permutations is countable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof. Each
`ℕⁿ = (Fin n → ℕ)` is countable as a finite product of countable sets, so
`T(ℕ) = ⋃ₙ ℕⁿ` (the Sigma type `Tuple ℕ`) is countable as a countable union of
countable sets; `\mathscr{P}` injects into `T(ℕ)` via the index-value tuple
`finitePermutationTuple`, hence is countable as a subset of a countable set.
declarations.header: theorem finitePermutations_countable : Countable FinitePermutations :=
declarations.name: finitePermutations_countable

declarations.name: continuous_sortingValidMap

declarations.docComment:

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: `lem:permutations-inherit-order`.

Informal statement: the pullback order along a bijection
`φ : \mathscr{P} → ℕ` is total.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: rather than registering a global `LinearOrder` instance
depending on `φ`, Lean records the four order laws needed downstream.
declarations.header: theorem permutationInheritedLE_total_order (φ : FinitePermutations ≃ ℕ) : (∀ π, permutationInheritedLE φ π π) ∧ (∀ π ρ τ, permutationInheritedLE φ π ρ → permutationInheritedLE φ ρ τ → permutationInheritedLE φ π τ) ∧ (∀ π ρ, permutationInheritedLE φ π ρ → permutationInheritedLE φ ρ π → π = ρ) ∧ (∀ π ρ, permutationInheritedLE φ π ρ ∨ permutationInheritedLE φ ρ π) :=
declarations.name: permutationInheritedLE_total_order

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, set-valued form used inside
`prop:measurable-partition-sorting`.

Informal statement: a subset of tuple space is Borel for the tuple Hausdorff
topology iff all of its fixed-length restrictions are Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis invokes this as the product-layer reduction
`\mathscr{T}(X)=\bigsqcup_n X^n`. Lean derives the set statement by applying
the existing function-valued bridge to the characteristic predicate
`x ↦ x ∈ s`.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: this lemma is only the set-level fixed-layer bridge used
inside measurable sorting. The full five-part `thm:the-standard-machinery`
is formalized in `TuplesMetricTopology.lean` through the identity
homeomorphism, continuity equivalences, and measurability equivalences.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_tupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {s : Set (Tuple X)} : @MeasurableSet (Tuple X) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := X)) s ↔
declarations.name: measurableSet_tupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: fixed-product step in
`prop:measurable-partition-sorting`.

Informal statement: on a fixed product layer `X^n`, the set of tuples sorted
by a fixed permutation is Borel when the strict order relation is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is exactly the thesis' finite-intersection argument. For
each pair `i ≤ j`, the forbidden set
`{x | x (π j) < x (π i)}` is the preimage of the Borel strict-order relation
under a continuous coordinate-pair map, and sortedness is the finite
intersection of its complements.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixed_sortingValid_of_strictOrder {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [Preorder X] (hstrict : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 < p.2}) (n : ℕ) (π : FinitePermutation n) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) {x | IsSorted (permutationMap (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n π))} :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixed_sortingValid_of_strictOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: Borel-valid-set step in
`prop:measurable-partition-sorting`.

Informal statement: every sorting-valid set `\mathscr{V}_π` is Borel when
the strict order relation is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis first fixes `N = \ell(π)` and proves measurability
inside `X^N`; Lean then pastes the fixed-length restrictions back into the
Sigma tuple space using `measurableSet_tupleHausdorff_iff_fixedLength`.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_sortingValidSet_of_strictOrder {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [Preorder X] (hstrict : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 < p.2}) : ∀ π : FinitePermutations, @MeasurableSet (Tuple X) (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := X))
declarations.name: measurableSet_sortingValidSet_of_strictOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: Borel strict-order step in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: if the partial-order relation `≤` is Borel, then the
strict-order relation `<` is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes `\prec = \preceq \setminus \Delta`. Lean's
strict order on a partial order is definitionally `a ≤ b ∧ ¬ b ≤ a`, so the
proof uses the Borel order relation and its pullback along the continuous
coordinate swap.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_strictOrder_of_measurableSet_le {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [PartialOrder X] (hle : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 ≤ p.2}) : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 < p.2} :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_strictOrder_of_measurableSet_le

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: first fixed-length component of
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: on a fixed layer `X^n`, `C_{i,j}` is the set of tuples
for which indices `i` and `j` are immediately comparable.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes indices as elements of `{1,\dots,n}`.
Lean uses `Fin n`; the set is otherwise the same
`x i ≤ x j ∨ x j ≤ x i`.
declarations.header: def fixedIndexComparableSet [Preorder X] (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → X) :=
declarations.name: fixedIndexComparableSet

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: measurability of the sets `C_{i,j}` in the proof of
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: if the ambient order relation is Borel, then each
fixed-length immediate-comparability set `C_{i,j}` is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis coordinate-pullback argument: coordinate
evaluation maps on `X^n` are continuous, and `C_{i,j}` is the union of the
order relation pulled back by `(x i, x j)` and by `(x j, x i)`.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixedIndexComparableSet_of_borelOrder {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [Preorder X] (hle : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 ≤ p.2}) (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) (fixedIndexComparableSet (X := X) n i j) :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixedIndexComparableSet_of_borelOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: strict-order set `A_{i,j}` in the proof of
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: on a fixed layer `X^n`, `A_{i,j}` is the set of tuples
for which coordinate `j` is strictly smaller than coordinate `i`.
declarations.header: def fixedStrictLowerSet [LT X] (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) : Set (Fin n → X) :=
declarations.name: fixedStrictLowerSet

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: measurability of `A_{i,j}` in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: if the partial order is Borel, then every fixed-length
strict-lower set `A_{i,j}` is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes `≺ = \preceq \setminus Δ`. Lean uses the
previous theorem `measurableSet_strictOrder_of_measurableSet_le` and pulls it
back along the continuous coordinate map `(x j, x i)`.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixedStrictLowerSet_of_borelOrder {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [PartialOrder X] (hle : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 ≤ p.2}) (n : ℕ) (i j : Fin n) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) (fixedStrictLowerSet (X := X) n i j) :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixedStrictLowerSet_of_borelOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: finite path expansion in the proof of
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: a fixed finite path of indices is comparable along every
successive edge.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis indexes paths as `(i_0,\dots,i_k)`. Lean represents
such a path by a function `Fin (k+1) → Fin n`; the edge from `r` to `r+1` is
expressed using `Fin.castSucc r` and `Fin.succ r`.
declarations.header: def fixedPathComparable [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) {k : ℕ} (p : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n) : Prop :=
declarations.name: fixedPathComparable

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: finite path expansion in the proof of
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the set of fixed-length tuples for which a specified
index path is comparable along each edge is Borel.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the finite-intersection step in the thesis proof.
declarations.header: theorem measurableSet_fixedPathComparable_of_borelOrder {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [Preorder X] (hle : @MeasurableSet (X × X) (@borel (X × X) inferInstance) {p | p.1 ≤ p.2}) {n k : ℕ} (p : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n) : @MeasurableSet (Fin n → X) (@borel (Fin n → X) inferInstance) {x | fixedPathComparable (X := X) x p} :=
declarations.name: measurableSet_fixedPathComparable_of_borelOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: path interpretation of connectivity in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: a concrete comparable path induces membership in the
reflexive-transitive connectivity relation.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the forward direction of the thesis' path expansion of
the transitive closure.
declarations.header: theorem fixedPathComparable_indexConnected [Preorder X] {n k : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) (p : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n) (hpath : fixedPathComparable (X := X) x p) :
declarations.name: fixedPathComparable_indexConnected

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: path interpretation of connectivity in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: every connected pair of fixed-length indices is witnessed
by some finite comparable path.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: mathlib's `Relation.ReflTransGen` is inductive, so the proof
constructs the thesis path by induction on the closure proof.
declarations.header: theorem indexConnected_exists_fixedPathComparable [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) {i j : Fin n} (hconn : IndexConnected (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) i j) : ∃ k : ℕ, ∃ p : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n, p 0 = i ∧ p (Fin.last k) = j ∧ fixedPathComparable (X := X) x p :=
declarations.name: indexConnected_exists_fixedPathComparable

declarations.docComment:

only). The mapped proof of the proposition is the thesis cycle-excision

`indexConnected_exists_bounded_fixedPathComparable` below consumes directly.
declarations.header: noncomputable def indexComparableSimpleGraph [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) :=
declarations.name: indexComparableSimpleGraph

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Alternative route for `prop:transitive-closure-finite` (not the mapped
proof).

Informal statement: reachability in the finite simple graph generated by
immediate comparability is exactly the tuple connectivity relation.
declarations.header: theorem indexComparableSimpleGraph_reachable_iff_indexConnected [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) (i j : Fin n) : (indexComparableSimpleGraph (X := X) x).Reachable i j ↔
declarations.name: indexComparableSimpleGraph_reachable_iff_indexConnected

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: chain characterisation of `R^n` stated before
`prop:transitive-closure-finite`.

Informal statement: a pair of indices in the `k`-th power of the immediate
comparability relation is joined by a comparable index path with exactly `k`
edges.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis sentence "induction
on `n` shows that `(x,z) ∈ Rⁿ` iff there is a chain `x = x₁, …, x_{n+1} = z`
with `(x_r, x_{r+1}) ∈ R`", in the direction needed below, with
`FiniteRelationClosure.relationPower` as `Rⁿ` and the chain represented as a
function `Fin (k+1) → Fin n`.
declarations.header: theorem relationPower_indexComparable_exists_fixedPathComparable [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) {k : ℕ} {i j : Fin n} (h : FiniteRelationClosure.relationPower (X := Fin n) (IndexComparable (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) k i j) : ∃ p : Fin (k + 1) → Fin n, p 0 = i ∧ p (Fin.last k) = j ∧ fixedPathComparable (X := X) x p :=
declarations.name: relationPower_indexComparable_exists_fixedPathComparable

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: `prop:transitive-closure-finite`.

Informal statement: if `i` and `j` are connected in a tuple of length `n`,
then some comparable path from `i` to `j` has edge count `k < n`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `k : Fin n` is Lean's zero-based version of the thesis bound
`k ≤ n-1`. The path itself is still represented as
`Fin (k+1) → Fin n`, matching the thesis sequence
`(i_0,\dots,i_k)`.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: this is the tuple instance of the
thesis proposition, derived from the general statement for an arbitrary
relation on a finite set, `FiniteRelationClosure.finite_closure_formula`
(`\overline{R} = Δ ∪ ⋃_{m=1}^{|X|-1} R^m`, proved by the thesis cycle-excision
argument, without any symmetry hypothesis). The diagonal case gives the
trivial path of length `0`; a power `R^m` with `1 ≤ m ≤ n-1` unfolds into a
comparable chain by the chain characterisation
`relationPower_indexComparable_exists_fixedPathComparable`. This is the route
that `thm:minimal-sorting-measurable` consumes below.
declarations.header: theorem indexConnected_exists_bounded_fixedPathComparable [Preorder X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) {i j : Fin n} (hconn : IndexConnected (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) i j) : ∃ k : Fin n, ∃ p : Fin (k.1 + 1) → Fin n, p 0 = i ∧ p (Fin.last k.1) = j ∧ fixedPathComparable (X := X) x p :=
declarations.name: indexConnected_exists_bounded_fixedPathComparable

by proving equality of membership in the underlying sets.

enumeration reads the index coordinate of the sorted graph-point list.

subsection "Sorting Properties".

Original label: nonempty blocks `C_k` in
`thm:minimal-sorting-measurable`.

Informal statement: the block obtained from a connected segment is nonempty.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis treats connected components as nonempty partition

stabilizes. Then each coordinate sequence in the fixed finite layer is Cauchy
in `X`, hence converges. The limiting tuple is formed coordinatewise.

Original label: separability transfer in `thm:tuple-space-properties`.

Informal statement: if `X` is separable, then the tuple Hausdorff space

the distinct finite-set space through the graph map.

to tuple space.

Original label: separability transfer in `thm:tuple-space-properties`.

Informal statement: if `X` is separable, then the tuple Hausdorff space
`\mathscr{T}(X)` is separable.

Lean strategy / thesis strategy note: the headline theorem now follows the thesis graph-image
argument. The earlier direct dense-support construction remains available as
the auxiliary lemmas `tupleSupportedOn_countable` and `tupleSupportedOn_dense`.
declarations.header: theorem separableSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (Tuple X) PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace :=
declarations.name: separableSpace

subsection "The Tuple Hausdorff Metric".

Original label: sorted tuple separability in `thm:tuple-space-properties`,
item `eq:sorted-tuple-separable`.

Informal statement: if `(X, d)` is separable and `\preceq` is any partial
order on `X`, then the sorted tuple space is separable as a metric subspace of
the tuple Hausdorff space.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis invokes the standard metric-space fact that every
subspace of a separable metric space is separable. Lean states this through
`TopologicalSpace.IsSeparable.separableSpace`; the theorem is explicit about
the tuple Hausdorff metric topology to avoid the native Sigma topology on
`Tuple X`. As in the thesis statement, only a partial order is assumed:
totality plays no role in the subspace argument.
declarations.header: theorem sortedTuple_separableSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] [PartialOrder X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (SortedTuple X) PseudoEMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace :=
declarations.name: sortedTuple_separableSpace
