Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the `d∞` metric on tuple space is the disjoint-union
metric over the fixed-length product layers `Fin n → X`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: `Tuple X` is definitionally the dependent sum
`Σ n, Fin n → X`, so the thesis' disjoint union
`\bigsqcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}_0} X^n` is already the Lean representation. This
definition deliberately does not become the global `EMetricSpace` instance,
because the file's default tuple metric is the tuple Hausdorff distance.
declarations.header: noncomputable def tupleSupEMetricSpace {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : EMetricSpace (Tuple X) :=
declarations.name: tupleSupEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: distance function in `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the `d∞` distance function itself, kept as a named
function so it can coexist with the global tuple Hausdorff `edist`.
declarations.header: noncomputable def tupleSupEDistance {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : ENNReal :=
declarations.name: tupleSupEDistance

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: same-length case in `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: on a fixed-length layer, `d∞` is the maximum coordinate
edistance.
declarations.header: theorem tupleSup_edist_same {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : tupleSupEDistance (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n y) = coordinateEDistSup x y :=
declarations.name: tupleSup_edist_same

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: different-length case in `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: tuples of different lengths have `d∞` distance `∞`.
declarations.header: theorem tupleSup_edist_ne_length {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≠ n) (x : Fin m → X) (y : Fin n → X) : tupleSupEDistance (Sigma.mk m x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n y) = ⊤ :=
declarations.name: tupleSup_edist_ne_length

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: proposition following `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: after truncating at radius `1`, the tuple Hausdorff
distance and the thesis `d∞` distance agree.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis says that replacing a metric by `min(d,1)`
preserves the induced topology. The formal bridge recorded here is the
pointwise identity needed for tuple space: below radius `1`, the tuple
Hausdorff metric collapses to the fixed-layer maximum metric; across different
lengths, both truncated distances are exactly `1`.
declarations.header: theorem tupleHausdorff_min_one_eq_tupleSup_min_one {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : min (edist x y) (1 : ENNReal) = min (tupleSupEDistance x y) (1 : ENNReal) :=
declarations.name: tupleHausdorff_min_one_eq_tupleSup_min_one

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: proposition following `cor:tuple-metrisation`.

Informal statement: the Hausdorff and `d∞` tuple distances have the same
open balls below radius `1`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the local form of the thesis truncation argument:
small neighborhoods are fixed-length neighborhoods, and on each fixed-length
layer the two distances coincide with the same coordinate supremum metric.
declarations.header: theorem tupleHausdorff_lt_one_iff_tupleSup_lt_one {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : edist x y < (1 : ENNReal) ↔ tupleSupEDistance x y < (1 : ENNReal) :=
declarations.name: tupleHausdorff_lt_one_iff_tupleSup_lt_one

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, topology component.

Informal statement: a set is open for the tuple Hausdorff metric iff its
restriction to every fixed-length tuple layer is open.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the tuple analogue of the disjoint-union topology
pasting criterion. The proof follows the thesis: below radius `1`, tuple
Hausdorff neighborhoods cannot change length; inside a fixed-length layer,
they are exactly product-sup neighborhoods.
declarations.header: theorem tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_isOpen_iff {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {s : Set (Tuple X)} : @IsOpen (Tuple X) (tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := X)) s ↔
declarations.name: tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_isOpen_iff

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Extended-metric form of `prop:truncated-metric-equivalent-topology` (the
mapped `MetricSpace` statement is `exists_truncatedMetricSpace_same_topology`
above): two extended metrics on the same carrier whose truncations `min(d, 1)`
agree pointwise induce the same topology.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the step invoked in the thesis
proof of `thm:the-standard-machinery` (i). The argument is the pointwise one:
an open ball of radius `min(ε, 1)` for one metric lies inside the ball of
radius `ε` for the other, because below radius `1` the two distances agree.
declarations.header: theorem topologies_eq_of_equal_truncations {X : Type u} (m₁ m₂ : EMetricSpace X) (h : ∀ x y, min (@edist X m₁.toEDist x y) 1 = min (@edist X m₂.toEDist x y) 1) : m₁.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace = m₂.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace :=
declarations.name: topologies_eq_of_equal_truncations

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, topology component.

Informal statement: the tuple Hausdorff topology and the thesis `d∞`
disjoint-union topology coincide.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis proof of
`thm:the-standard-machinery` (i): `min(d_H, 1) = min(d_∞, 1)` pointwise
(`tupleHausdorff_min_one_eq_tupleSup_min_one`), hence the two metrics induce
the same topology by `prop:truncated-metric-equivalent-topology`
(`topologies_eq_of_equal_truncations`).
declarations.header: theorem tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_tupleSup {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := X) =
declarations.name: tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_tupleSup

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, topology component.

Informal statement: the tuple Hausdorff metric topology is the usual
topological disjoint union of the fixed-length product layers.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: as in the thesis, this is obtained from
the identity homeomorphism `(T(X), d_H) ≅ (T(X), d_∞)` of clause (i)
(`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_tupleSup`) together with the identification
of `(T(X), d_∞)` with the disjoint-union metric space `⨆ₙ Xⁿ`
(`DisjointUnionTopology.metricTopology_eq_sigma`). The direct open-set
criterion `tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_isOpen_iff` provides an independent
proof of the same identity.
declarations.header: theorem tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := X) = instTopologicalSpaceSigma :=
declarations.name: tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_sigma

declarations.docComment:

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, clause (vi): each layer is open.

Informal statement: each fixed-length layer `Xⁿ = {x ∈ T(X) | ℓ(x) = n}` is
open in `(T(X), d_H)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: exactly the thesis argument: the layer is
the union of the open balls of radius `1` about its elements, since distance
below `1` forces equal length (`thm:tuple-space-properties` (i),
`length_eq_of_edist_lt_one`).
declarations.header: theorem isOpen_fixedLength_layer {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (n : ℕ) : @IsOpen (Tuple X) (tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := X))
declarations.name: isOpen_fixedLength_layer

declarations.docComment:

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, clause (vi): each layer is
closed.

Informal statement: each fixed-length layer `Xⁿ` is closed in `(T(X), d_H)`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: as in the thesis, the complement of `Xⁿ`
is the union of the other layers `Xᵐ`, `m ≠ n`, each of which is open.
declarations.header: theorem isClosed_fixedLength_layer {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (n : ℕ) : @IsClosed (Tuple X) (tupleHausdorffMetricTopology (X := X))
declarations.name: isClosed_fixedLength_layer

declarations.docComment:

declarations.name: isClopen_fixedLength_layer

`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "The Tuple Topology".

Original label: `thm:the-standard-machinery`, identity homeomorphism.

Informal statement: the identity map is a homeomorphism between tuple space
with the tuple Hausdorff topology and tuple space with the thesis `d∞`

equal (`tupleHausdorffMetricTopology_eq_tupleSup`), and the identity
equivalence is continuous in both directions.

declarations.name: tupleHausdorffTupleSupHomeomorph

declarations.docComment:

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: first-differing-index contradiction in the proof of
`cor:unique-sorting-map-total-order`.

Informal statement: let `g` and `g'` be two rearrangements of the same
fixed-length tuple (`g' = g ∘ τ` for a permutation `τ`), let `g'` be sorted,
and let `k` be an index at which they first differ with `g k ≺ g' k`. Then a
contradiction follows.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the thesis argument verbatim.
Since `g'` is sorted and `g' k ≻ g k`, every index `m` with `g' m ⪯ g k`
satisfies `m < k`, where `g'` agrees with `g`; so the indices with
`g' m ⪯ g k` form a subset of those with `g m ⪯ g k` which misses `k`. But
the two index sets correspond under `τ` (the entries agree with multiplicity),
so their cardinalities are equal, a contradiction.
declarations.header: theorem no_first_difference_of_sorted [LinearOrder X] {n : ℕ} (g g' : Fin n → X) (hg' : ∀ i j : Fin n, i ≤ j → ¬ g' j < g' i) (τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (hτ : ∀ m, g' m = g (τ m)) (k : Fin n) (hbelow : ∀ m, m < k → g m = g' m) (hlt : g k < g' k) : False :=
declarations.name: no_first_difference_of_sorted

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: uniqueness part of `cor:unique-sorting-map-total-order`.

Informal statement: over a total order, any two sorting permutations of the
same tuple produce the same sorted tuple.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this follows the thesis proof. Suppose
the two sorted rearrangements `y = x ∘ π` and `y' = x ∘ ρ` differ, take the
smallest index `k` with `y k ≠ y' k`, and use totality to assume (up to
swapping the roles) `y k ≺ y' k`; the first-differing-index contradiction
`no_first_difference_of_sorted` then applies, with `τ = π⁻¹ ∘ ρ` witnessing
that the two rearrangements have the same entries with multiplicity.
declarations.header: theorem sortedPermutations_eq_of_linearOrder [LinearOrder X] (x : Tuple X) (π ρ : SortingPermutations x) : permute x π.1 = permute x ρ.1 :=
declarations.name: sortedPermutations_eq_of_linearOrder

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:

Original label: `cor:unique-sorting-map-total-order`.

Informal statement: every sorting rule on a linear order fixes every sorted
input, including inputs not initially presented as outputs of that rule.

declarations.name: sortingRule_fixes_sorted

`prop:components-partition-incomp`. The source prose above is inside this doc
comment; if an audit copy shows it as raw text, the issue is in archive

declarations.header: theorem indexConnected_of_mem_segmentDistinctFiniteSet [Preorder X] (x : Tuple X) {K : ConnectedSegment x} {p q : IndexAugmented X} (hp : p ∈ ((segmentDistinctFiniteSet (X := X) x K).1 : Set (IndexAugmented X))) (hq : q ∈ ((segmentDistinctFiniteSet (X := X) x K).1 : Set (IndexAugmented X))) : ∃ i j : Fin x.length, p = IndexAugmented.mk i.1 (Tuple.entry x i) ∧ q = IndexAugmented.mk j.1 (Tuple.entry x j) ∧ IndexConnected x i j :=

`defn:comparability-components`.

declarations.header: theorem firstOccurrenceList_map_of_injective {α β : Type u} {f : α → β} (hf : Function.Injective f) (l : List α) : firstOccurrenceList (l.map f) = (firstOccurrenceList l).map f :=

declarations.name: firstOccurrenceList_eq_self_of_nodup

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite first-occurrence enumeration helper for the corollary
after `defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: if `a` does not occur in `l`, adjoining `a` as the final
possible new element of a list-union is the same as deduplicating `l` and
then appending `a`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is list bookkeeping only. It supports the thesis'
argument that, in a concatenation of nonempty blocks ordered by first
appearance, the first occurrence of each block label is the first element of
that block.
declarations.header: theorem list_union_singleton_eq_dedup_append_of_notMem {α : Type u} [DecidableEq α] {a : α} {l : List α} (ha : a ∉ l) : l ∪ [a] = l.dedup ++ [a] :=
declarations.name: list_union_singleton_eq_dedup_append_of_notMem

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite first-occurrence enumeration helper for the corollary
after `defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: if a positive-length constant block labelled `a` is
concatenated before a tail that contains no `a`, first-occurrence deletion
keeps exactly one leading `a` and then processes the tail.
declarations.header: theorem firstOccurrenceList_replicate_append_of_pos {α : Type u} {a : α} {l : List α} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (ha : a ∉ l) : firstOccurrenceList (List.replicate n a ++ l) = a :: firstOccurrenceList l :=
declarations.name: firstOccurrenceList_replicate_append_of_pos

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite first-occurrence enumeration helper for the corollary
after `defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: if `a` is not one of the labels in `Ks`, then `a` does
not occur in the flattened list obtained by replacing each `K` by a constant
block labelled `K`.
declarations.header: theorem not_mem_flatten_replicates_of_notMem {α : Type u} {a : α} {Ks : List α} {n : α → ℕ} (ha : a ∉ Ks) : a ∉ ((Ks.map fun K => List.replicate (n K) K).flatten) :=
declarations.name: not_mem_flatten_replicates_of_notMem

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite first-occurrence enumeration helper for the corollary
after `defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: replacing each entry of a duplicate-free label list by a
nonempty constant block and then taking first occurrences recovers the
original label list.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the exact list-level form of the thesis' block-order
argument: the first element of each nonempty connected-segment block is the
first occurrence of that segment after concatenation.
declarations.header: theorem firstOccurrenceList_flatten_replicates_of_nodup {α : Type u} {Ks : List α} {n : α → ℕ} (hKs : Ks.Nodup) (hpos : ∀ K ∈ Ks, n K ≠ 0) : firstOccurrenceList ((Ks.map fun K => List.replicate (n K) K).flatten) = Ks :=
declarations.name: firstOccurrenceList_flatten_replicates_of_nodup

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite block bookkeeping for the corollary after
`defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: in a flattened list of blocks, the parallel flattened
source-label list identifies a block that contains the graph point at the
same position.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is list bookkeeping for the thesis' concatenation
notation. It lets us pass from an abstract source-label shadow back to the
actual sorted graph point occupying the same concatenated position.
declarations.header: theorem exists_label_of_getElem_flatten_blocks {α : Type u} {β : Type v} (Ks : List α) (block : α → List β) {i : ℕ} (hg : i < ((Ks.map block).flatten).length) (hs : i < ((Ks.map fun K => List.replicate (block K).length K).flatten).length) : ∃ K : α, ((Ks.map fun K => List.replicate (block K).length K).flatten)[i] = K ∧ ((Ks.map block).flatten)[i] ∈ block K :=
declarations.name: exists_label_of_getElem_flatten_blocks

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite block bookkeeping for the corollary after
`defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: if a label does not occur in a source-label list, then
filtering a parallel zipped source/value list by that label returns no
values.
declarations.header: theorem map_snd_filter_zip_eq_nil_of_notMem {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α] {K : α} {src : List α} {values : List β} (hK : K ∉ src) : (((src.zip values).filter (fun z : α × β => z.1 = K)).map Prod.snd) = [] :=
declarations.name: map_snd_filter_zip_eq_nil_of_notMem

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite block bookkeeping for the corollary after
`defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

filtering by that same label, and projecting values recovers the value block.
declarations.header: theorem map_snd_filter_zip_replicate_eq {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α] (K : α) (l : List β) : (((List.replicate l.length K).zip l).filter (fun z : α × β => z.1 = K)).map Prod.snd = l :=
declarations.name: map_snd_filter_zip_replicate_eq

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite block bookkeeping for the corollary after
`defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: if a duplicate-free list of labels is expanded into
constant source-label blocks, then filtering a parallel source/value zip by
each label and flattening those filtered value blocks recovers the original
value list.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the generic list form of the thesis' final
contiguous-block argument. It is independent of markets: the only hypotheses
are duplicate-free block labels and matching source/value lengths.
declarations.header: theorem flatten_filter_zip_replicateLabels_eq_values {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α] {Ks : List α} {n : α → ℕ} {values : List β} (hKs : Ks.Nodup) (hlen : values.length = ((Ks.map fun K => List.replicate (n K) K).flatten).length) : ((Ks.map fun K => ((((Ks.map fun L => List.replicate (n L) L).flatten).zip values).filter (fun z : α × β => z.1 = K)).map Prod.snd).flatten) = values :=
declarations.name: flatten_filter_zip_replicateLabels_eq_values

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/2_chapter_market_representations.tex`,
subsection "Sorted Tuples".

Original label: finite block bookkeeping for the corollary after
`defn:minimum-sorting-rule`.

Informal statement: filtering finite positions by a label and then reading
their values is the same as zipping the source-label and value lists,
filtering by that label, and projecting values.
declarations.header: theorem map_filter_finRange_eq_map_snd_filter_zip_ofFn {α : Type u} {β : Type v} [DecidableEq α] {n : ℕ} (s : Fin n → α) (f : Fin n → β) (K : α) : ((List.finRange n).filter (fun i => s i = K)).map f = (((List.ofFn s).zip (List.ofFn f)).filter (fun z : α × β => z.1 = K)).map Prod.snd :=
declarations.name: map_filter_finRange_eq_map_snd_filter_zip_ofFn

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:point-process-tuple`.
The theorem's clauses, consolidated, for the kernel `K_perm` built from a
point process `ξ` and a measurable enumeration `τ` with `m(τ μ) = μ`
(`lem:measurable-enumeration`), on tuple space with its Borel σ-algebra:

1. `K_perm` is a Markov kernel from `Ω` to `T(X)` (probability measure in
`B`, measurable in `ω`);
2. the length of the enumerated tuple is the total mass `N(ω) = ξ(ω)(X)`;
3. `K_perm(ω, B) = (1 / N(ω)!) Σ_{σ ∈ P_{N(ω)}} 1_B(τ(ξ(ω)) ∘ σ)`, the
displayed formula;
4. `K_perm(ω, m⁻¹({ξ(ω)})) = 1`: every reordering induces the same point
measure (`cor:tuple-induced-measure-permutation-invariant`);
5. `K_perm(ω, ·)` is the uniform distribution on the class
`(m^π)⁻¹(ξ(ω))`: each tuple of the class has mass `1 / |class|`
(`prop:finite-equivalence-classes`: every class member is produced by the
same number of permutations);
6. the kernel does not depend on the choice of the enumeration `τ`.

Each clause is the corresponding named lemma of `TupleMeasures`,
`PointProcessAlignment` and this module; the existence statement
`TupleMeasures.pointProcessTuple_markovKernel` is the special case of (1) for
the enumeration `measurableEnumeration`.
declarations.header: theorem pointProcessTuple_kernel_clauses {Ω X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [MeasurableSpace X] [EMetricSpace X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] (ξ : Ω → FiniteIntegerMeasures X) (hξ : Measurable ξ) (τ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X → Tuple X) (hτ : @Measurable (FiniteIntegerMeasures X) (Tuple X) inferInstance (tupleHausdorffBorel (X := X)) τ)
declarations.name: pointProcessTuple_kernel_clauses

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:weak-linear-transport-vector-space-structure`.

Original label: `thm:weak-linear-transport-vector-space-structure`.

Informal statement: `X_φ` carries the transported vector-space structure by
identifying it with the subspace `φ(X)`: `Φ : X_φ → φ(X)` is a bijection, and
the vector-space operations on `X_φ` are the manuscript's
`x + x' = Φ⁻¹(Φ(x) + Φ(x'))` and `α • x = Φ⁻¹(α Φ(x))`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: instead of naming formulas with a set-theoretic inverse
`Φ^{-1}`, Lean constructs an equivalence
`weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ` and transports the algebraic typeclass
instances from the image submodule along that equivalence
(`weakLinearKernelSpace_addCommGroup`, `weakLinearKernelSpace_module`). The
two displayed formulas hold by definition of the transported instances, which
is what the second and third clauses record.
declarations.header: theorem weakLinear_transport_vectorSpace_structure {𝕂 : Type u} {X : Type v} {V : Type w} [Field 𝕂] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕂 V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyLinearOperator 𝕂 X V φ) : Nonempty (WeakLinearKernelSpace φ hφ ≃ weaklyLinearRangeSubmodule φ hφ) ∧ (∀ q r : WeakLinearKernelSpace φ hφ, q + r = (weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ).symm (weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q + weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r)) ∧ (∀ (α : 𝕂) (q : WeakLinearKernelSpace φ hφ), α • q = (weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ).symm (α • weakLinearKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q)) :=
declarations.name: weakLinear_transport_vectorSpace_structure

declarations.docComment:

mapped statement is `weakLinear_transport_vectorSpace_structure`.
declarations.header: theorem weakLinear_transport_vectorSpace_instances {𝕂 : Type u} {X : Type v} {V : Type w} [Field 𝕂] [AddCommGroup V] [Module 𝕂 V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyLinearOperator 𝕂 X V φ) : Nonempty (AddCommGroup (WeakLinearKernelSpace φ hφ)) ∧ Nonempty (Module 𝕂 (WeakLinearKernelSpace φ hφ)) :=
declarations.name: weakLinear_transport_vectorSpace_instances

declarations.header: noncomputable def weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (q : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ) : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ :=
declarations.name: weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication

declarations.docComment: The transported addition has the thesis `Φ^{-1}(Φ q + Φ r)` formula.
declarations.header: theorem weakConvexKernelAdd_image {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) (q r : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ) : ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ q r)).1 : V) = (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 + (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r).1 :=
declarations.name: weakConvexKernelAdd_image

declarations.docComment:
The transported nonnegative scalar operation has the thesis
`Φ^{-1}(α • Φ q)` formula.
declarations.header: theorem weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication_image {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) (α : ℝ) (hα : 0 ≤ α) (q : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ) : ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα q)).1 : V) = α • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 :=
declarations.name: weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication_image

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Corollary `cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Original label: transported cone-closure formula for
`cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Informal statement: under the transported operations on `X_φ`, every
nonnegative linear combination is represented by transporting the corresponding
image-cone combination back along `Φ^{-1}`.
declarations.header: theorem weakConvexKernel_transportedCone_combination_image {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) {α β : ℝ} (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (q r : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ) : ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα q) (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ β hβ r))).1 : V) = α • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 + β • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r).1 :=
declarations.name: weakConvexKernel_transportedCone_combination_image

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Corollary `cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Original label: transported operation package for
`cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Informal statement: the quotient `X_φ` is equipped with the transported
addition and nonnegative scalar multiplication appearing in the thesis, and
these operations realize the convex-cone closure formula through the
quotient-image bijection `Φ`.
declarations.header: theorem weakConvex_transport_convexCone_operations {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) : (∀ q r : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ, ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ q r)).1 : V) = (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 + (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r).1) ∧ (∀ ⦃α : ℝ⦄ (hα : 0 ≤ α) (q : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ), ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα q)).1 : V) = α • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1) ∧ (∀ ⦃α β : ℝ⦄ (hα : 0 ≤ α) (hβ : 0 ≤ β) (q r : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ), ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα q) (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ β hβ r))).1 : V) = α • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 + β • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r).1) :=
declarations.name: weakConvex_transport_convexCone_operations

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Corollary `cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Original label: `cor:weak-convex-transport-convex-cone-structure`.

Informal statement: if `φ` is weakly convex, then the quotient `X_φ` is
identified with the convex cone `φ(X)`, and the transported operations are
the manuscript's `x + x' = Φ⁻¹(Φ(x) + Φ(x'))` and `α • x = Φ⁻¹(α Φ(x))` for
`α ≥ 0`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the manuscript writes explicit transported addition and
nonnegative scalar multiplication using `Φ^{-1}`. The preceding declarations
define those transported operations directly (`weakConvexKernelAdd`,
`weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication`); this theorem records the
image-cone identification used later together with the two displayed
formulas, stated through `Φ` (equivalently, `Φ⁻¹` applied to the right-hand
sides, since `Φ` is a bijection).
declarations.header: theorem weakConvex_transport_convexCone_structure {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommMonoid V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) : ConvexCone (Set.range φ) ∧ Nonempty (WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ ≃ Set.range φ) ∧ (∀ q r : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ, ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ q r)).1 : V) = (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1 + (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ r).1) ∧ (∀ ⦃α : ℝ⦄ (hα : 0 ≤ α) (q : WeakConvexKernelSpace φ hφ), ((weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα q)).1 : V) = α • (weakConvexKernelSpaceEquivRange φ hφ q).1) :=
declarations.name: weakConvex_transport_convexCone_structure

Informal statement: every `v ∈ span φ(X)` is a finite linear combination
`Σ_i α_i φ(x_i)`, and splitting each coefficient as
`α_i = max(α_i,0) - (-min(α_i,0))` writes `v` as a difference of two cone
elements.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is the manuscript's argument
verbatim: `Finsupp.mem_span_range_iff_exists_finsupp` provides the finite
combination, and the two nonnegative parts are cone elements by
`weakConvex_nonnegative_sum_mem_range`.
declarations.header: theorem span_mem_positive_negative_split {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) (v : V) (hv : v ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ)) : ∃ c : X →₀ ℝ, (∑ i ∈ c.support, max (c i) 0 • φ i) ∈ Set.range φ ∧ (∑ i ∈ c.support, (-min (c i) 0) • φ i) ∈ Set.range φ ∧ (∑ i ∈ c.support, max (c i) 0 • φ i) - (∑ i ∈ c.support, (-min (c i) 0) • φ i) = v :=
declarations.name: span_mem_positive_negative_split

declarations.header: theorem grothendieckVectorization_additionOfPairRepresentatives {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) (p q : GrothendieckPair φ hφ) : (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) p) + grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) q)) = (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ p.1 q.1, weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ p.2 q.2) : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ) :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:grothendieck-vector-space-from-convex-cone`.

Original label: `thm:grothendieck-vector-space-from-convex-cone`.

Informal statement: the Grothendieck quotient of a weakly convex operator
carries a real vector-space structure, with the manuscript's displayed
operations on pair classes: `[(x,z)] + [(x',z')] = [(x + x', z + z')]`,
`α [(x,z)] = [(α x, α z)]` for `α ≥ 0`, and `α [(x,z)] = [(|α| z, |α| x)]` for
`α < 0`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the manuscript writes the addition and scalar multiplication
formulas directly on pair classes. Lean obtains the same algebra by first
identifying the quotient with `span φ(X)` and transporting the vector-space
typeclasses along that equivalence `T`
(`grothendieckVectorization_addCommGroup`, `grothendieckVectorization_module`),
so that `a + b = T⁻¹(T a + T b)` and `α • a = T⁻¹(α T a)` hold by definition
(second and third clauses). The equivalence itself is established by the
manuscript's arguments: the relation is an equivalence by the cancellative
transitivity proof (`grothendieckRel_equivalence`), and `T` is onto the span
by the positive/negative coefficient split (`grothendieckToSpan_surjective`).
The last three clauses are the manuscript's pair-class formulas for the
transported operations, written with `T⁻¹(T [p] + T [q])` for `[p] + [q]`
(`grothendieckVectorization_additionOfPairRepresentatives`,
`grothendieckVectorization_scalarMultiplicationOfPairRepresentative_nonnegative`,
`grothendieckVectorization_scalarMultiplicationOfPairRepresentative_negative`).
declarations.header: theorem grothendieck_vectorSpace_from_convexCone {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) : Nonempty (GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ ≃ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ)) ∧ (∀ a b : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ, a + b = (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ a + grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ b)) ∧ (∀ (α : ℝ) (a : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ), α • a = (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (α • grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ a)) ∧ (∀ p q : GrothendieckPair φ hφ, (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) p) + grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) q)) = (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) (weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ p.1 q.1, weakConvexKernelAdd φ hφ p.2 q.2) : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ)) ∧ (∀ ⦃α : ℝ⦄ (hα : 0 ≤ α) (p : GrothendieckPair φ hφ), (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (α • grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) p)) = (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα p.1, weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ α hα p.2) : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ)) ∧ (∀ ⦃α : ℝ⦄, α < 0 → ∀ p : GrothendieckPair φ hφ, (grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ).symm (α • grothendieckVectorizationEquivSpan φ hφ (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) p)) = (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) (weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ |α| (abs_nonneg α) p.2, weakConvexKernelNonnegativeScalarMultiplication φ hφ |α| (abs_nonneg α) p.1) : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ)) :=
declarations.name: grothendieck_vectorSpace_from_convexCone

isometric linear isomorphism onto `span φ(X)`, where
`T([(x,z)]) = Φ(x) - Φ(z)` and the inner product on the vectorization is the
pullback `⟪u, v⟫_𝓥 = ⟨T u, T v⟩` of the ambient inner product.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the witness is
`grothendieckVectorizationLinearIsometryEquivSpan`; the inner-product
instance `grothendieckVectorization_innerProductSpace` is built from the
pulled-back form `grothendieckVectorizationInner`, so both displayed formulas
hold by definition.
declarations.header: theorem grothendieck_vectorization_innerProductSpace_and_isometry {X : Type u} {V : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [Nonempty X] (φ : Operator X V) (hφ : WeaklyConvexOperator X V φ) : ∃ T : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ), (∀ p : GrothendieckPair φ hφ, ((T (Quotient.mk (grothendieckSetoid φ hφ) p) : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ)) : V) = weakConvexKernelImage φ hφ p.1 - weakConvexKernelImage φ hφ p.2) ∧ ∀ u v : GrothendieckVectorization φ hφ, inner ℝ u v = inner ℝ ((T u : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range φ)) : V) (T v : V) :=
declarations.name: grothendieck_vectorization_innerProductSpace_and_isometry

Original label: `prop:function-kernel-quotient-injective-extension`.
The quotient metric has the literal representative distance formula.
declarations.header: theorem functionKernel_dist_class (x y : X) : letI := functionKernelMetricSpace f
declarations.name: functionKernel_dist_class

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:function-kernel-quotient-injective-extension`.
No weak-linearity or convexity hypothesis is needed for this isometry.
declarations.header: theorem functionKernelExtension_isometry : letI := functionKernelMetricSpace f
declarations.name: functionKernelExtension_isometry

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:function-kernel-quotient-injective-extension`.
The metric quotient is isometrically equivalent to the actual image.
declarations.header: def functionKernelIsometryEquivRange : letI := functionKernelMetricSpace f
declarations.name: functionKernelIsometryEquivRange

declarations.docComment:
Alternative route for `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`
(not the mapped proof). The metric space on `T^π(X)` obtained directly from
`sourceEMetricSpace`, i.e. with the uniformity generated by `d_π` itself. The
mapped structure `MatchingTuples.matchingMetricSpace` has the same distance but
carries the (equal) orbit uniformity of `PermutedTuples`.
declarations.header: @[implicit_reducible] def sourceMetricSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : MetricSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) :=
declarations.name: sourceMetricSpace

declarations.header: theorem sourceMetricSpace_edist (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : @edist _ (sourceMetricSpace X).toEDist q r = matchingEDistance q r := rfl
declarations.name: sourceMetricSpace_edist

declarations.docComment:
The cost of matching two fixed-length representatives, including the empty
tuple. The infimum is a minimum because the permutation type is finite.
declarations.header: def fixedMatchingCost {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost

declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_le_one {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x y ≤ 1 :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_le_one

declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_lt_iff {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≤ 1) : fixedMatchingCost x y < ε ↔ ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), coordinateEDistSup x (y ∘ σ) < ε :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_lt_iff

declarations.docComment:
The orbit-Hausdorff distance of `PermutedTuples` below radius one is the
existence of a matching with small coordinate cost. Used only to identify the
matching distance with the truncated orbit distance.
declarations.header: theorem quotient_edist_lt_iff_matching {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≤ 1) : edist (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X)) < ε ↔ ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), coordinateEDistSup x (y ∘ σ) < ε :=
declarations.name: quotient_edist_lt_iff_matching

declarations.docComment: Truncation commutes with the finite coordinate maximum, including length zero.
declarations.header: theorem truncated_coordinateEDistSup {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : min (coordinateEDistSup x y) 1 = Finset.univ.sup (fun i => min (edist (x i) (y i)) 1) :=
declarations.name: truncated_coordinateEDistSup

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
The cost `max_i min(d(x(i), y(σ(i))), 1)` of one candidate matching `σ`.
declarations.header: def matchingCost {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: matchingCost

declarations.docComment: Reindexing `j = σ(i)` does not change a finite maximum.
declarations.header: theorem sup_comp_perm {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℝ≥0∞) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : Finset.univ.sup (fun i => f (σ i)) = Finset.univ.sup f :=
declarations.name: sup_comp_perm

declarations.docComment: The triangle inequality for the truncated ground distance `d̄ = min(d, 1)`.
declarations.header: theorem truncated_edist_triangle {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y z : X) : min (edist x z) 1 ≤ min (edist x y) 1 + min (edist y z) 1 :=
declarations.name: truncated_edist_triangle

declarations.docComment: Symmetry step: the cost of `σ` for `(x, y)` is the cost of `σ⁻¹` for `(y, x)`.
declarations.header: theorem matchingCost_symm {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : matchingCost x y σ = matchingCost y x σ.symm :=
declarations.name: matchingCost_symm

declarations.docComment: Triangle step: the composed matching `σ' ∘ σ` costs at most the sum.
declarations.header: theorem matchingCost_trans_le {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y z : Fin n → X) (σ τ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : matchingCost x z (σ.trans τ) ≤ matchingCost x y σ + matchingCost y z τ :=
declarations.name: matchingCost_trans_le

declarations.docComment:
The manuscript's representative-change calculation before taking minima:
relabelling `x' = x ∘ α`, `y' = y ∘ β` turns the candidate `σ` into
`β ∘ σ ∘ α⁻¹`.
declarations.header: theorem matchingCost_comp_perm {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) (α β σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : matchingCost (x ∘ α) (y ∘ β) σ = matchingCost x y ((α.symm.trans σ).trans β) :=
declarations.name: matchingCost_comp_perm

declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_eq_iInf_matchingCost {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x y = ⨅ σ, matchingCost x y σ :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_eq_iInf_matchingCost

declarations.docComment: The minimum over the finite set `P_n` is attained.
declarations.header: theorem exists_matchingCost_eq_fixedMatchingCost {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : ∃ σ, matchingCost x y σ = fixedMatchingCost x y :=
declarations.name: exists_matchingCost_eq_fixedMatchingCost

declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_le_matchingCost {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : fixedMatchingCost x y ≤ matchingCost x y σ :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_le_matchingCost

declarations.docComment: Taking `σ = id` for two equal representatives gives cost zero.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_self {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x x = 0 :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_self

declarations.docComment:
A zero attained minimum forces `x(i) = y(σ(i))` for every `i`, i.e.
`x = y ∘ σ`, for the minimising matching `σ`; conversely `x = y ∘ σ` gives
cost zero at `σ`. This includes the empty layer without a nonempty-index
assumption.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_eq_zero_iff {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x y = 0 ↔ ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), x = y ∘ σ :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_eq_zero_iff

declarations.docComment: Symmetry via the bijection `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` of `P_n`.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_comm {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x y = fixedMatchingCost y x :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_comm

declarations.docComment:
The triangle inequality via the composed matching `σ' ∘ σ` of two
minimisers.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_triangle {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y z : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x z ≤ fixedMatchingCost x y + fixedMatchingCost y z :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_triangle

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Well-definedness on fixed-length representatives: relabelling either
representative merely relabels the candidate matchings through the bijection
`σ ↦ β ∘ σ ∘ α⁻¹` of `P_n`, so the minimum is unchanged.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_representatives {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) (α β : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) : fixedMatchingCost (x ∘ α) (y ∘ β) = fixedMatchingCost x y :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_representatives

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
The matching distance on representatives: `1` for different lengths and the
minimal matching cost for equal lengths (for length `0` the empty maximum,
i.e. `0`).
declarations.header: def tupleMatchingEDistance {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance

declarations.header: theorem tupleMatchingEDistance_mk_mk {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : tupleMatchingEDistance (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X) = fixedMatchingCost x y :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance_mk_mk

declarations.header: theorem tupleMatchingEDistance_of_length_ne {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {x y : Tuple X} (h : x.1 ≠ y.1) : tupleMatchingEDistance x y = 1 :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance_of_length_ne

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Well-definedness on the quotient, as in the manuscript: if the lengths differ,
so do the lengths of any other representatives and both values are `1`; for
equal lengths `n`, representatives `x ∘ α` and `y ∘ β` give the same minimum
by `fixedMatchingCost_representatives`.
declarations.header: theorem tupleMatchingEDistance_permute {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) (α : FinitePermutation x.length) (β : FinitePermutation y.length) : tupleMatchingEDistance (permute x α) (permute y β) = tupleMatchingEDistance x y :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance_permute

declarations.header: theorem tupleMatchingEDistance_permute_left {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) (α : FinitePermutation x.length) : tupleMatchingEDistance (permute x α) y = tupleMatchingEDistance x y :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance_permute_left

declarations.header: theorem tupleMatchingEDistance_permute_right {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) (β : FinitePermutation y.length) : tupleMatchingEDistance x (permute y β) = tupleMatchingEDistance x y :=
declarations.name: tupleMatchingEDistance_permute_right

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
The permuted-tuple matching distance `d_π` on the quotient: the minimum over
permutations of the truncated maximal coordinate distance for representatives
of equal length, and `1` for different lengths. It is well defined on the
quotient by `tupleMatchingEDistance_permute`.
declarations.header: def matchingEDistance {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance

declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_mk {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : matchingEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) x) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) y) = tupleMatchingEDistance x y :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_mk

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
On two representatives of the same length the matching distance is the
minimum over all permutations of the truncated maximum coordinate cost.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_mk_mk {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : matchingEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X)) = fixedMatchingCost x y :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_mk_mk

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
Distinct length layers have matching distance exactly one.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_of_length_ne {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X} (h : quotientLength q ≠ quotientLength r) : matchingEDistance q r = 1 :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_of_length_ne

declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_le_one {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : matchingEDistance q r ≤ 1 :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_le_one

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
The minimum is attained, so the infimum formulation gives the literal finite
minimum of maximum truncated coordinate distances in the manuscript.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_attained {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : ∃ σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n), matchingEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X)) = Finset.univ.sup (fun i => min (edist (x i) (y (σ i))) 1) :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_attained

declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_self {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : matchingEDistance q q = 0 :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_self

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`.
The distance between the empty classes is zero.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_empty {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] : matchingEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Tuple.empty X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Tuple.empty X)) = 0 :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_empty

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Identity of indiscernibles: distance `0` forces equal lengths, and then the
attained minimising matching `σ` gives `x = y ∘ σ`, so the classes coincide.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_eq_zero {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) (hz : matchingEDistance q r = 0) : q = r :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_eq_zero

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Symmetry: immediate for different lengths, and by `σ ↦ σ⁻¹` otherwise.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_comm {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : matchingEDistance q r = matchingEDistance r q :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_comm

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Triangle inequality: by the composed matching `σ' ∘ σ` for three equal
lengths; otherwise the right-hand side contains a term equal to `1`, which
bounds every matching distance.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_triangle {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r s : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : matchingEDistance q s ≤ matchingEDistance q r + matchingEDistance r s :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_triangle

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
`(T^π(X), d_π)` is an (extended) metric space, with every axiom proved by the
manuscript's verification above. The uniformity carried by this structure is
the one generated by `d_π` itself; `matchingMetricSpace` below replaces it by
the orbit uniformity of `PermutedTuples`, which is the same filter
(`matching_uniformity`), in order to inherit completeness and separability.
declarations.header: def matchingEMetricSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : EMetricSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X)
declarations.name: matchingEMetricSpace

declarations.docComment:
The fixed-length matching cost equals the truncation at `1` of the
orbit-Hausdorff distance of `PermutedTuples` between the two classes.
declarations.header: theorem fixedMatchingCost_eq_min_edist {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : fixedMatchingCost x y = min (edist (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X))) 1 :=
declarations.name: fixedMatchingCost_eq_min_edist

declarations.docComment:
The matching distance is the truncation at `1` of the orbit-Hausdorff
distance of `PermutedTuples`; in particular both induce the same uniformity.
declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_eq_min_edist {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : matchingEDistance q r = min (edist q r) 1 :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_eq_min_edist

declarations.header: theorem matchingEDistance_lt_iff {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X} {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : ε ≤ 1) : matchingEDistance q r < ε ↔ edist q r < ε :=
declarations.name: matchingEDistance_lt_iff

declarations.header: private theorem matching_uniformity (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : (inferInstance : UniformSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X)).uniformity = (matchingEMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace.uniformity :=
declarations.name: matching_uniformity

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
The metric space `(T^π(X), d_π)` of the manuscript: its distance is
`matchingEDistance`, the minimum-over-permutations formula of
`defn:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-distance`, and its axioms are those of
`matchingEMetricSpace`, proved by the manuscript's verifications. The
uniformity is taken to be the orbit uniformity of `PermutedTuples`, which
`matching_uniformity` shows to coincide with the one generated by `d_π`
(because `d_π` is the truncation at `1` of the orbit distance), so that the
completeness and separability clauses below are inherited.
declarations.header: def matchingMetricSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] : MetricSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) :=
declarations.name: matchingMetricSpace

declarations.header: theorem matchingMetricSpace_edist (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] (q r : PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) : @edist _ (matchingMetricSpace X).toEDist q r = matchingEDistance q r := rfl
declarations.name: matchingMetricSpace_edist

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Completeness of `(T^π(X), d_π)` for complete `X`. The uniformity of
`matchingMetricSpace` is the orbit uniformity, so this is the Cauchy-lifting
argument of `PermutedTuples.cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete`: a Cauchy sequence
of classes eventually has constant length, close tuple representatives are
chosen recursively, their limit in the complete tuple space represents the
limit class.
declarations.header: theorem matching_completeSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] [CompleteSpace X] : @CompleteSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) (matchingMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace :=
declarations.name: matching_completeSpace

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.
Separability of `(T^π(X), d_π)` for separable `X`: the classes of a countable
dense set of tuples are dense, as in `PermutedTuples.separableSpace`, whose
topology is that of `matchingMetricSpace`.
declarations.header: theorem matching_separableSpace (X : Type u) [EMetricSpace X] [TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace X] : @TopologicalSpace.SeparableSpace (PermutedTupleQuotientSpace X) (matchingMetricSpace X).toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace :=
declarations.name: matching_separableSpace

declarations.header: def firstRepresentatives (s : Set ι) (f : ι → β) : Set ι :=
declarations.name: firstRepresentatives

declarations.header: theorem firstRepresentatives_injOn (s : Set ι) (f : ι → β) : InjOn f (firstRepresentatives s f) :=
declarations.name: firstRepresentatives_injOn

declarations.header: theorem image_firstRepresentatives (s : Set ι) (f : ι → β) : f '' firstRepresentatives s f = f '' s :=
declarations.name: image_firstRepresentatives

declarations.header: theorem ncard_firstRepresentatives (s : Set ι) (f : ι → β) : (firstRepresentatives s f).ncard = (f '' s).ncard :=
declarations.name: ncard_firstRepresentatives

declarations.header: theorem measurable_firstRepresentatives {s : Ω → Set ι} {f : Ω → ι → β} (hs : Measurable s) (hf : ∀ i, Measurable (fun ω => f ω i)) : Measurable (fun ω => firstRepresentatives (s ω) (f ω)) :=
declarations.name: measurable_firstRepresentatives

declarations.header: theorem measurable_ncard_image {s : Ω → Set ι} {f : Ω → ι → β} (hs : Measurable s) (hf : ∀ i, Measurable (fun ω => f ω i)) : Measurable (fun ω => (f ω '' s ω).ncard) :=
declarations.name: measurable_ncard_image

declarations.header: theorem countablySeparated_of_measurable_injective {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B] [CountablySeparated B] {f : A → B} (hf : Measurable f) (hi : Function.Injective f) : CountablySeparated A :=
declarations.name: countablySeparated_of_measurable_injective

declarations.header: theorem finiteMeasures_countablySeparated (X : Type u) [MeasurableSpace X] [CountablyGenerated X] : CountablySeparated (FiniteMeasure X) :=
declarations.name: finiteMeasures_countablySeparated

declarations.header: def countBelow (s : Set ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (p : ℝ) : ℕ :=
declarations.name: countBelow

declarations.header: theorem countBelow_eq (s : Set ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (p : ℝ) : countBelow s f p = (f '' s ∩ Iio p).ncard :=
declarations.name: countBelow_eq

declarations.header: theorem countBelow_ordered {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ) (hv : StrictMono v) (s : Set ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (hrange : range v = f '' s) (i : Fin n) : countBelow s f (v i) = i.val :=
declarations.name: countBelow_ordered

declarations.header: def orderedValue (upper : ℝ) (s : Set ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (j : ℕ) : ℝ :=
declarations.name: orderedValue

declarations.header: theorem orderedValue_eq [Nonempty ι] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ) (hv : StrictMono v) (upper : ℝ) (s : Set ι) (f : ι → ℝ) (hrange : range v = f '' s) (hupper : ∀ r ∈ s, f r ≤ upper) (i : Fin n) : orderedValue upper s f i.val = v i :=
declarations.name: orderedValue_eq

declarations.header: theorem measurable_countBelow {s : Ω → Set ι} {f : Ω → ι → ℝ} {p : Ω → ℝ} (hs : Measurable s) (hf : ∀ i, Measurable (fun ω => f ω i)) (hp : Measurable p) : Measurable (fun ω => countBelow (s ω) (f ω) (p ω)) :=
declarations.name: measurable_countBelow

declarations.header: theorem measurable_orderedValue (upper : ℝ) (j : ℕ) {s : Ω → Set ι} {f : Ω → ι → ℝ} (hs : Measurable s) (hf : ∀ i, Measurable (fun ω => f ω i)) : Measurable (fun ω => orderedValue upper (s ω) (f ω) j) :=
declarations.name: measurable_orderedValue

declarations.header: theorem permute_eq_self_iff (x : Tuple X) (π : FinitePermutation x.length) : permute x π = x ↔ x.2 ∘ π = x.2 :=
declarations.name: permute_eq_self_iff

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-equivalence-classes`.
The level-set criterion of the source proof: `x ∘ σ = x` holds iff
`x(σ(i)) = x(i)` for every `i`, i.e. iff `σ` maps each level set
`I_a = {i | x(i) = a}` into itself.
declarations.header: theorem permute_eq_self_iff_levelSets (x : Tuple X) (π : FinitePermutation x.length) : permute x π = x ↔ ∀ a : X, ∀ i, x.2 i = a → x.2 (π i) = a :=
declarations.name: permute_eq_self_iff_levelSets

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-equivalence-classes`.
`|S(x)| = m_1! ⋯ m_κ!`: by `permute_eq_self_iff_levelSets` the permutations
fixing `x` are those preserving every level set, and Mathlib's
`DomMulAct.stabilizer_card'` is exactly the bijection of that stabiliser with
the product `∏_a P(I_a)` of the level-set permutation groups, of cardinality
`∏_a |I_a|!` over the distinct entries `a` of `x`.
declarations.header: theorem stabilizing_permutations_card (x : Tuple X) : Nat.card {π : FinitePermutation x.length // permute x π = x} = ∏ a ∈ Finset.univ.image x.2, (Nat.card {i : Fin x.length // x.2 i = a}).factorial :=
declarations.name: stabilizing_permutations_card

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-equivalence-classes`.
`|S(y)| = |S(x)|` for every `y = x ∘ σ₀` in the class: right multiplication
`σ ↦ σ ∘ σ₀⁻¹` (here `Equiv.mulRight`) is a bijection of `P_n` carrying the
fibre over `y` onto the fibre over `x`. This includes repeated values and the
empty tuple.
declarations.header: theorem reordered_tuple_permutations_card (x : Tuple X) (σ : FinitePermutation x.length) : Nat.card {π : FinitePermutation x.length // permute x π = permute x σ} = ∏ a ∈ Finset.univ.image x.2, (Nat.card {i : Fin x.length // x.2 i = a}).factorial :=
declarations.name: reordered_tuple_permutations_card

declarations.docComment: The fibre map `σ ↦ x ∘ σ` from `P_n` onto the class `x^π`.
declarations.header: def toOrbit (x : Tuple X) (σ : FinitePermutation x.length) : permutativeClass x :=
declarations.name: toOrbit

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-equivalence-classes`.
The source's counting identity `n! = |P_n| = Σ_{y ∈ x^π} |S(y)| = |x^π| · m_1! ⋯ m_κ!`:
the fibres of `σ ↦ x ∘ σ` partition `P_n` into `|x^π|` blocks, each of the
common size given by `reordered_tuple_permutations_card`.
declarations.header: theorem orbit_card_mul_multiplicities (x : Tuple X) : (permutativeClass x).ncard * (∏ a ∈ Finset.univ.image x.2, (Nat.card {i : Fin x.length // x.2 i = a}).factorial) = x.length.factorial :=
declarations.name: orbit_card_mul_multiplicities

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `prop:finite-equivalence-classes`.
The exact multinomial cardinality `|x^π| = n! / (m_1! ⋯ m_κ!)`, including
repeated entries and the empty tuple, obtained from the equal-fibre identity
`orbit_card_mul_multiplicities` by dividing out the common fibre size.
declarations.header: theorem orbit_ncard_eq_factorial_div (x : Tuple X) : (permutativeClass x).ncard = x.length.factorial / (∏ a ∈ Finset.univ.image x.2, (Nat.card {i : Fin x.length // x.2 i = a}).factorial) :=
declarations.name: orbit_ncard_eq_factorial_div

Historical relation note: the earlier thesis used the orbit formula:

finite subsets `O(x)` and `O(y)` of tuple space.

declarations.name: permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance

Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Definition the historical orbit-Hausdorff construction.

Original label: representative formula for
the historical orbit-Hausdorff construction.

Informal statement: evaluating the quotient distance on classes represented
by `x` and `y` unfolds to the Hausdorff distance between their finite orbits.
declarations.header: theorem permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance_mk_mk {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] (x y : Tuple X) : permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) x) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) y) = edist (permutativeOrbit x) (permutativeOrbit y) :=

`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Proposition `prop:inverse-permuted-tuple-measure-continuous`.

Original label: final quotient-distance inequality in
`prop:inverse-permuted-tuple-measure-continuous`.

Informal statement: for fixed-length representatives, the permuted tuple
Hausdorff distance between quotient classes is bounded by the largest
coordinatewise distance between those representatives.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis writes
`\mathscr d_\pi(x^\pi,y^\pi) \leq \mathscr d_H(x,y)`. Lean proves the
slightly more concrete fixed-length estimate used in the last step of the
inverse-continuity proof. The proof matches finite permutation orbits point by
point: a permutation of `x` is paired with the same permutation of `y`.
declarations.header: theorem permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance_mk_mk_le_coordinateEDistSup {X : Type u} [EMetricSpace X] {n : ℕ} (x y : Fin n → X) : permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n x : Tuple X)) (Quot.mk (permutativeSetoid X) (Sigma.mk n y : Tuple X)) ≤ coordinateEDistSup x y :=
declarations.name: permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance_mk_mk_le_coordinateEDistSup

declarations.name: permutedTupleHausdorffEDistance_mk_mk_lt_of_forall_edist_lt

Theorem `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.

Original label: metric part of
`thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.

Informal statement: the permuted tuple Hausdorff edistance separates quotient
classes, because the orbit map into finite subsets is injective and the
finite-subset Hausdorff edistance is an extended metric.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this proves the metric-space part of the theorem. The
separability and completeness transfer statements are left as later
topological work, matching the remaining paragraphs of the thesis proof.

`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.

Original label: continuity estimate for the quotient map in the separability
and completeness paragraphs.

Informal statement: if two tuple representatives are within Hausdorff
distance `< 1`, then their permuted-tuple classes are no farther apart than
the original tuple distance.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the proof is the local version needed by the thesis. Below
radius `1`, Chapter 2 identifies the tuple Hausdorff distance with the
fixed-length coordinate supremum; the quotient orbit Hausdorff distance is
bounded by matching each permutation of one tuple with the same permutation of
the other.

`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:permuted-tuple-hausdorff-metric-complete-separable`.

their permuted-tuple classes are within `ε`.

declarations.name: quotientMk_edist_lt_of_tuple_edist_lt_min

Informal statement: if a representative `x` of class `q` is fixed and class
`r` is within quotient Hausdorff distance `< ε` of `q`, then some
representative `y` of `r` is within tuple Hausdorff distance `< ε` of `x`.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: the thesis phrases this using an attained finite minimum. Lean
uses mathlib's finite-Hausdorff lemma
`Metric.exists_edist_lt_of_hausdorffEDist_lt`, which gives the same
representative-selection step in strict epsilon form.

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `lem:disintegration-lemma`.
All four conclusions, including nonempty blocks, their strict maximum-distance
bound, and exact coverage of the nearby measure's atoms.
declarations.header: theorem atomicDecomposition_disintegration_full {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [EMetricSpace X] [OpensMeasurableSpace X] [MeasurableSingletonClass X] {ξ η : FiniteIntegerMeasures X} (dξ : AtomicDecomposition ξ) (dη : AtomicDecomposition η) {ε : ℝ≥0∞} (hε : 0 < ε) (hεγ : ε < atomicDecompositionSeparationGamma dξ) (hρ : prokhorovEDistance ξ.val η.val < ε) : (∀ k, dξ.multiplicity k = ∑ l ∈ nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k) ε, dη.multiplicity l) ∧ (∀ k k', k ≠ k' → Disjoint (nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k) ε) (nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k') ε)) ∧ (∀ k, (nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k) ε).Nonempty ∧ (nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k) ε).sup (fun l => edist (dξ.atom k) (dη.atom l)) < ε) ∧ (∀ l, ∃! k, l ∈ nearbyAtomIndices dη (dξ.atom k) ε) :=
declarations.name: atomicDecomposition_disintegration_full

declarations.docComment:
Original label: `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

declarations.header: theorem atomicDecomposition_unique_of_length_le_one {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] [StandardBorelSpace X] {μ : FiniteIntegerMeasures X} (d e : AtomicDecomposition μ) (hd : d.length ≤ 1) : ∃ hlen : d.length = e.length, ∀ i, e.atom (Fin.cast hlen i) = d.atom i ∧ e.multiplicity (Fin.cast hlen i) = d.multiplicity i :=
declarations.name: atomicDecomposition_unique_of_length_le_one

Informal statement: a sequence of finite measures converges weakly if it
converges against every bounded continuous real-valued test function.

Original label: `defn:weak-convergence-finite-measures`.

Informal statement: the Lean weak-convergence topology on finite measures is
equivalent to the thesis' integral convergence condition for every bounded
continuous real-valued function.

Lean strategy / thesis relation note: this is a direct use of mathlib's theorem

rounding removes the additive error.

declarations.header: noncomputable def finiteAtomicMeasure {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → X) (β : ι → ℕ) : FiniteMeasures X :=

declarations.docComment:
Thesis source:
`1 - theoretical foundations/5_stochastic_markets.tex`,
Theorem `thm:sufficient-decomposition`.

Original label: finite atomic sum `\sum_{k \leq \kappa} \beta_k\delta_{x_k}`.

Informal statement: evaluating a finite atomic measure on a measurable set is
the sum of the multiplicities of atoms lying in that set.
declarations.header: theorem finiteAtomicMeasure_apply {X : Type u} [MeasurableSpace X] {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι] (x : ι → X) (β : ι → ℕ) {B : Set X} (hB : MeasurableSet B) : finiteAtomicMeasure x β B = ∑ i : ι, B.indicator (fun _ : X => (β i : ℝ≥0)) (x i) :=
